speaker: Erethian
text: "I'll speak to thee no more, Avatar!" He ignores you.

speaker: Erethian
text: At your approach, the old man straightens and looking directly at you he says, "Well met, <PLAYER_NAME>. I am called Erethian. Although thou dost not know me, I know thee well."

speaker: Erethian
text: "I have seen thee destroy Mondain's power and so defeat that misguided mage, I have seen thee vanquish the enchantress Minax, I have also seen, in a very unique way, how thou brought low the hellspawn Exodus."

speaker: Erethian
text: He falls silent here and you notice that the old man's eyes are milky white.

speaker: Erethian
text: "Greetings once again, <PLAYER_NAME>. How may I assist thee?" The blind old man looks unerringly in your direction.

speaker: Erethian
text: "I'll never get any work done like this! What do you wish of me?" Erethian seems a little pevish at this point.

speaker: Erethian
text: "Could this possibly be true?" Erethian's blind eyes light up with unabashed glee. "What an opportunity I have here."

speaker: Erethian
text: He once again notices your presence. "Now, do not let any strange ideas of destruction enter thy mind, Avatar. I shan't let thee deprive me of this chance to experience a true wonder of the world. Run along now... Is there not a right to be wronged, somewhere else?"

speaker: Erethian
text: The elderly mage frowns. "I sense no great evil, but then I never did quite get the knack of cosmic awareness. Nevertheless, don't worry thyself over much. These things tend to work themselves out." You feel as if you've just been patted on the head and asked to go play elsewhere.

speaker: Erethian
text: "Ah, yes. I once had a scroll that told of a talisman by that name. If only I could remember where I put it. Dost thou by chance have the parchment entitled Scroll of Infinity with thee?"

speaker: Erethian
text: "If thou dost not have the scroll, I cannot help thee in this matter."

speaker: Erethian
text: "Here we are. Now then, it appears to be written in a strange format. One might even say a code of sorts... I have it! Apparently, the Talisman currently resides in the Great Void. A plane somewhat removed from ours. If thou wishest to gain access to this void, thou shalt need to craft two lenses: one concave, the other convex. Light focused through the properly enchanted lenses will open a conduit between our realm and the void. I believe this treatise speaks of three Talismans of Principle that send out a call to the Infinity Talisman and bring it here. Once here, it would seem that its sole purpose is to coerce a powerful force into the void." A thought hits the mage like lightning strikes a tree. "Oh no, Avatar... Thou shan't gain any more aid from me. I may be blind, but I see through thy sham. I'll not help thee send the Core into the void." Erethian falls silent, and it would appear that he'll speak no more.

speaker: Dark Core
text: Arcadion's voice whispers to you like ripple in still pond, "Fear not, my master. I have some knowledge of these matters."

speaker: Dark Core
text: "Very well. I shall need the scroll to give thee further information."

speaker: Dark Core
text: "Dost thou have the Scroll of Infinity amongst thy possessions?"

speaker: Dark Core
text: "I needs must touch the scroll to glean its meaning. Else I'll not be able to help thee in this matter."

speaker: Dark Core
text: "Here we are. Now then, it appears to be written in a strange format. One might even say a code of sorts... I have it! Apparently, the Talisman currently resides in the Great Void. Thou shan't gain any more aid from me. I may be blind, but I see through thy sham. I'll not help thee send the Core into the void." Erethian falls silent, and it would appear that he'll speak no more.

speaker: Dark Core
text: Arcadion's voice whispers to you like ripple in still pond, "Fear not, my master. I have some knowledge of these matters."

speaker: Dark Core
text: "If thou bringest the scroll to me I can aid the in finding the meaning of the archaic text."

speaker: Dark Core
text: "I once attempted to create a sword of great power." Erethian frowns in concentration then says, "if thou wishest to continue my work, thou shalt have need of some few pieces of forging equipment... And a place to put them... I know just the spot. Come with me and I'll see what I can do to help thee."

speaker: Erethian
text: Erethian nods his head when you tell him of your dilemma with the black sword. "Yes, I can see how the blade would be too clumsy to swing in combat. However, if thou were to bind a magical source of power into the hilt of the blade, thou mightest be able to counteract the unwieldy nature of the sword."

speaker: Hook
text: The little gem sparks up at this turn of the conversation. "I believe that in my current form, I could serve perfectly well as the blade's stabilizing force. In truth, this would allow me to give thee access to some of my more dramatic powers." The daemon sounds excited at this prospect, perhaps a little too excited.

speaker: Erethian
text: Erethian's voice is quiet as he says, "Consider well before thou bindest Arcadion into the sword. For it is true that he will be able to solve the sword's problem of balance, but will he be able to solve his own problems as well?"

speaker: Erethian
text: You wonder if perhaps Arcadion might be able to shed some light on this issue, and as if reading your thoughts, Erethian says, "Beware the daemon. His goals are not those of thine or mine. If he offers to help thee, it is to help himself. Of that thou canst be sure."

speaker: Erethian
text: "This is thy choice to make. Apparently thou hast need to make this sword function, but if the daemon is thy only recourse, I pity thee. For as surely as Arcadion will be bound within the sword, thou wilt be bound to possess it. I can tell thee no more."

speaker: Erethian
text: The mage gives you a half smile, "'Twould seem that thy memory is failing thee, <PLAYER_NAME>. As I have said, my name is Erethian."

speaker: Erethian
text: "I am a follower of the principle of Truth. But unlike those of the Lyceaum, I would prefer to seek out the knowledge instead of waiting for it to come to me."

speaker: Erethian
text: It is this curiosity which has brought me to this island from which Exodus, the spawn of Mondain and Minax, sought to rule the world.

speaker: Erethian
text: "The books and scrolls here have taught me much of Britannia's	history and other... interesting subjects."

speaker: Erethian
text: His clouded eyes sparkle with intelligence. But you can't help wondering how books and scrolls are of any use to a man afflicted with blindness.

speaker: Erethian
text: "If thou art interested, feel free to inspect them. This is no library." As if regretting his gracious gesture, he adds, "However, I trust that thou wilt take utmost care with the older ones." He stops, on the verge of saying more.

speaker: Erethian
text: "Thou art a tiresome child. Leave me be!" He ignores your presence.

speaker: Erethian
text: Erethian scowls, "Now there was a mighty wizard. A bit twisted but then who knows what happens to the human mind when 'tis subjected to the powers he wielded."

speaker: Erethian
text: "'Tis even said his skull alone had the power to destroy enemies... he must have locked a magical matrix upon it, I'll have to research that." He nods his head, seemingly making a mental note, then continues with a wistful look on his aged features,

speaker: Erethian
text: "I	would have loved to study that fascinating Gem of Immortality, but alas, I was born in too late an era."

speaker: Erethian
text: A sad sweet smile comes to the wizard's face, "She was quite a comely lass at one time, with a mind forever searching." His expression darkens, "But then Mondain forced all of the good sense from her."

speaker: Erethian
text: She became a power unto herself, in time. I do not think she quite rivaled her former mentor, Mondain, but she was a force to be reckoned with, nevertheless.

speaker: Erethian
text: "And that thou didst, with the Quicksword, Enilno. That	act will most likely have tales sung about it for the next eon." Under his breath he adds, "Even if Iolo's the only one who sings it."

speaker: Iolo
text: With a look of indignation Iolo says, "Pardon me, sir. But I'll have thee know that ballads of the Avatar still grace all of the finest drinking establishments of Britannia."

speaker: Erethian
text: "And what a dubious distinction that is." The corners of the mage's mouth come up in a delicate smile.

speaker: Iolo
text: An angry retort dies on Iolo's lips as the elderly mage lifts his hands in a gesture of peace.

speaker: Erethian
text: "Please, forgive the offense I have given. Thou shouldst know that I have seen, almost first hand, the Avatar's bravery in the face of adversity."

speaker: Erethian
text: I have nothing but the highest regard for the Destroyer of the Age of Darkness and Harbinger of the Age of Enlightenment.

speaker: Erethian
text: "That being has become a passion of mine, lately." He almost glows with excitement. "Indeed, 'tis what brought me here. While I	was at the Lyceaum, I happened upon a passage in a manuscript that described an Island of Fire."

speaker: Erethian
text: "Upon further research, I found that the entity known as Exodus was not truly destroyed. The interface between its two parts and the world was merely severed."

speaker: Erethian
text: "One part, his psyche we shall call it, was taken by the gargoyles who live below us in a realm on the other side of the world. A truly fascinating culture they have, but I digress..." You begin to wonder just how long this old man has	been out of circulation.

speaker: Erethian
text: He continues, "The other, I have here. I call it the Dark Core, because without the psyche, it is mostly lifeless." His face appears to youthen, and you feel as if you're speaking to a child describing his new toy... or perhaps, pet.

speaker: Erethian
text: "I believe 'twas the removal of the psyche from the Core that caused this island to sink beneath the waves."

speaker: Erethian
text: His expression is unreadable, "The machine that thou destroyed was Exodus' means of communication with and control of the world."

speaker: Erethian
text: When it was destroyed, his psyche could no longer retain its hold on the Dark Core.

speaker: Erethian
text: "I have often wondered if another interface was implemented, would the psyche return, or possibly be regenerated..."

speaker: Erethian
text: As his	idle musings begin to run toward possibly dangerous conclusions, his mouth audibly snaps shut.

speaker: Erethian
text: "Interesting creatures, thou mightest call them balrons, but they are not the beasts that history has made of them."

speaker: Erethian
text: "The larger, winged ones are intelligent and magical by nature,	while the smaller, wingless ones appear to be the work force for the species."

speaker: Erethian
text: He turns his head in your direction with a puzzled expression in his eyes, "I have the oddest feeling that thou hast heard all of this before..." Erethian falls silent.

speaker: Erethian
text: "Eventually, I shall turn my studies to that being. The gargoyles have placed it within a statue, in a shrine they dedicated to their principle of Diligence."

speaker: Erethian
text: "Yes, here it is. It is the cylinder sitting upon yon pedastal." He motions in the direction of the Dark Core.

speaker: Erethian
text: "I have found it to be quite a treasure trove of useful facts. Its sole purpose seems to be the storage of information."

speaker: Erethian
text: Much of the information is trivial, such as the detailed description	of the color of the	sky on a particular day eons ago,

speaker: Erethian
text: while other bits give instructions for the manipulation of the	world.

speaker: Erethian
text: "Within it I even found the knowledge to raise and sustain this island	we stand upon. It is truly a remarkable artifact."

speaker: Erethian
text: He thinks for a moment, then looks nervously in your direction, "Please, do be careful around it. Artifacts seem to have a tendency to, shall we say, disappear around thee."

speaker: Erethian
text: "Ah, now there's a question. I've heard naught of it's existence since the Age of Darkness ended. Would that I knew its location."

speaker: Erethian
text: "It was reputedly a great item of magic. Didst thou find it so?" He cocks his head to one side as he asks the question.

speaker: Erethian
text: "Yes, 'tis a pity to lose such an item of antiquity. Perhaps as time unfolds it will turn up. These things have a way of surfacing at the strangest times."

speaker: Erethian
text: "No? It didst seem to serve thee well enough to dispatch the enchantress Minax. But then I suppose only a poor bard blames his instrument." He winks mischieviously in your general direction.

speaker: Erethian
text: Milky eyes glitter up at you like twin marbles, "Ah, yes. But thou knowest all too well about that little bauble."

speaker: Erethian
text: After all, it was thee who smashed it into the shards which caused thee so much trouble during the regency of Lord Blackthorn.

speaker: Erethian
text: "So much power that even in a shattered state, its magic still flowed. 'Tis sad to lose such an artifact." As if suddenly remembering with whom he is speaking, he ammends, "Much better than having Mondain running about mucking with things, I suppose."

speaker: Erethian
text: "'Twould seem that someone," he pauses dramatically, "let that slip into a volcano..." His wry smile belies his careless tone.

speaker: Erethian
text: "Ah, so thou hast met that old windbag. Truly, I feel that I would do better to free myself of that burdensome beast, but he sometimes proves to be useful. If it weren't for his whining, perhaps he and I would get along better."

speaker: Erethian
text: "'Tis his favorite passtime. He begs, pleads, and threatens me to free him from that stupid mirror. Believe me, if I could I would have done it long ago." Erethian's lined face shows his chagrin.

speaker: Erethian
text: "He wants this special bauble. I once possessed this gem he seeks, and I don't think he'd be very happy once he gets it. I have tried to tell him that 'twould only imprison	him in a more mobile jail, but alas, his head is made of stone."

speaker: Erethian
text: "Quite. Arcadion seeks to have dominion over Britannia and believes that the gem will give him the ability to exert his power here. In truth, the Ether Gem works in the reverse, his power will become accessible to the one who possesses the gem."

speaker: Erethian
text: "The gem was pilfered from me by an ill tempered dragon. She blew her way into this castle, waylayed the golems that protect the Shrine of Principle, then destroyed a perfectly good secret door on her way to the Test of Courage. I'd have liked to see her squeeze through the hole she made, 'tis hardly big enough for a creature of her bulk." The mage's milky eyes twinkle with suppressed mirth.

speaker: Erethian
text: "Mmmm... Yes. This pair of manshaped, magical constucts used to guard the Shrine of Principle, but alas, one fell pray to falling rocks when the dragon assaulted the castle. The other picked up his, ah... brother, for lack of a better word, and carried him off through the portal to the Test of Love."

speaker: Erethian
text: "The shrine lies through the doors at the rear of the main hall. There thou canst find three statues, each one dedicated to a Principle set forth by Lord Britsh at the beginning of the Age of Enlightenment." Conspiratorially he adds, "A bit stuffy, but they make nice cloakracks."

speaker: Erethian
text: "I not had the chance to inspect that oddity yet, however, thou art welcome to peruse it at thy leisure." He smiles like a grandfather giving a present to a child.

speaker: Erethian
text: "I believe 'twas set in motion by Lord British in order to test..." He gestures in your direction, "A virtuous <GENDER_FLAG> fighting ability and courage. The statues in the back of this castle can tell thee more about the tests, though." Erethian grins mysteriously.

speaker: Erethian
text: "So... thou hast made a servant of Arcadion. 'Tis good to be rid of his incessant whining. I hope that thou findest him to be as useful as I didst." You're not sure, but his words might be construed as a curse.

speaker: Hook
text: The gem glows brighter, "'Tis good to see the last of thee, also, old man. Perhaps in another life, I shall be thy master, and thou the slave." The daemon lets out a chilling little laugh.

speaker: Erethian
text: Erethian looks a little shaken at hearing the daemon's voice, but quickly recovers his composure. "I think not, daemon. I'm not at all sure that there is a way for thou to get out of that little gem." The elderly mage's expression is unreadable.

speaker: Erethian
text: "I see that thou didst not heed my warning. Alas, my pity shall be thine eternally. And so, what wouldst thou have of me, Master and Slave of the Shade Blade."

speaker: Erethian
text: "Goodbye and good luck... Thou'lt need it." The old mage snickers under his breath as if enjoying a personal joke, quite possibly at your expense.

speaker: Erethian
text: "Goodbye and good luck..." Erethian sounds truly sympathetic.

speaker: Ferryman
text: The hooded figure in the boat ignores you completely.

speaker: Ferryman
text: Before you stands a tall, skeletal figure in a ghostly boat. He holds out his hand to you, and says in a sepulchral voice, "I am the Ferryman of Skara Brae... Thou must pay two coins... to cross the Misty Channel."

speaker: Ferryman
text: The Ferryman of Skara Brae stands in his spectral boat, holding out his hand for any who would pay his price.

speaker: Ferryman
text: The Ferryman of Skara Brae stands in his spectral boat, holding his pole across his chest. He notices your approach. "You need not pay... to return to the mainland."

speaker: Ferryman
text: He seems a bit disgruntled. "I told you I would be here... until the end of eternity."

speaker: Ferryman
text: "I am... the Ferryman." His voice creaks like the rocking	of the boat.

speaker: Ferryman
text: The Ferryman doesn't respond at first, shaking his head from side to side in puzzlement. "I am... the Ferryman."

speaker: Ferryman
text: "Yes, if you pay me... I can take you across the Misty Channel."

speaker: Ferryman
text: He turns to the side and waves his skeletal hand in a sweeping gesture over the water upon which his boat rests. "This... is the Misty Channel."

speaker: Ferryman
text: He turns all the way around and points across the water to the west. "There... "

speaker: Shamino
text: "Er... <PLAYER_NAME>, art thou sure we need to go over there?"

speaker: Spark
text: "What's the matter, Shamino? Art thou -afraid-?"

speaker: Shamino
text: "Of course not! I just... well, I... oh, never mind! Let's go!"

speaker: Iolo
text: Iolo's eyes narrow as he adopts a patronizing look on his face.

speaker: Iolo
text: "And I suppose thou art without fear?" he says to Spark.

speaker: Spark
text: "No, sir. I am not afraid of a skeleton," he says. As he looks at the ferryman, however, he	gulps.

speaker: Ferryman
text: The gaunt figure looks around as if perplexed. "This... is Skara Brae."

speaker: Ferryman
text: "Wilt thou pay my price... for passage to Skara Brae?"

speaker: Ferryman
text: You place the coins in the shade's palm and his bony fingers close over them. "Step aboard... if thou wouldst go... to the Isle of the Dead."

speaker: Ferryman
text: "I'll not cross... without proper payment."

speaker: Ferryman
text: "Very well." He seems a little disappointed.

speaker: Ferryman
text: "Dost thou wish... to return to the mainland?"

speaker: Ferryman
text: "I may not carry spirits to the mainland." He holds his pole in front of himself, blocking your way onto the boat.

speaker: Ferryman
text: The Ferryman seems to smile beneath his hood as he motions for you to once more board his spectral boat.

speaker: Ferryman
text: You think you see pale flames flicker in the depths of his cowl where his eyes should be. They fade as he sighs, "No matter..."

speaker: Ferryman
text: Just for a moment you think you see a fleeting expression of hope cross the Ferryman's skeletal features, then it's gone. "I must perform my duty... until the end of eternity."

speaker: Ferryman
text: "Do not taunt me... with hopes of release. I must perform my duty... until the end of eternity."

speaker: Ferryman
text: Without acknowledging your goodbye, the Ferryman lowers his head and holds his pole across his chest.

speaker: Palace Guard
text: You see a tough-looking palace guard who takes his job -very- seriously.

speaker: Palace Guard
text: "I am a guard."

speaker: Palace Guard
text: The man looks at you like you are an ignoramus. "I am a guard for the palace, idiot. Thou shouldst go about thy business."

speaker: Palace Guard
text: "Goodbye."
The creature ignores you.
The ape-like creature approaches you cautiously. After a few minutes, it says, "You are greeted, human."
The emp approaches you cautiously. After a few minutes, it says, "You are greeted, human."
"Is more honey had by you?" The Emp asks hopefully.
"No honey is had by you," says the Emp, obviously disappointed.
Obviously disappointed, the Emp says, "That is too bad. What is your wish?"
"Terandan is my name."
"Sendala is my name."
"Tvellum is my name."
"Simrek is my name."
"No job is had by me. Food is gathered by me."
"Fruit, milk, cheese are eaten by Emps."
"Cheese and milk are liked by Emps, but they are hard to find. Only from humans can these foods be found."
"Fruits are found easily in the forest," <PRONOUN> says. "They are what Emps use as food most often."
"Farewell is said to you."

speaker: Carrocio
text: "Now is the time for the young and the old to dig in their pockets and give up the gold. * Dost thou wish to donate a gold piece?"

speaker: Dracothraxus
text: "Well met, seeker. I am Dracothraxus. Thy test, and I fear, thy defeat lies before thee. For thou shouldst know that I am made immortal by the Keeper of Courage. 'Twould take a truly powerful artifact to destroy me... one that does not exist." The great dragon paws the earth in expectation of your imminent battle.

speaker: Dracothraxus
text: Dracothraxus sniffs the air distastefully, "I sense my doom nearby. Perhaps I am to be released at long last. I wish thee good luck mortal. Defend thyself!"  With that, the dragon leaps at you.

speaker: Dracothraxus
text: Dracothraxus sniffs the air distastefully, "I sense my doom nearby. Perhaps I am to be released at long last. I wish thee good luck mortal. Defend thyself!"  With that, the dragon leaps at you.

speaker: Dracothraxus
text: "Thou hast returned to test thy mettle, little one. Thy courage does thee honor, however, I think that thou shalt take thine honor to the grave with thee."

speaker: Dracothraxus
text: The dragon lets out a searing sigh, "Released at last. I go now to seek my reward, for this has been a test of my courage as well as thine. Thy reward lies beyond the door to the north. Enter the blue gate and the Amulet of Courage will be thine."

speaker: Dracothraxus
text: "Well done, little human. Thou art as powerful as thou art courageous. Do not think that thou hast destroyed me, thou hast merely bested me. And for this wonderous feat, I think thou dost deserve a reward. I have a truly magnificent gem that I would give to thee, if thy courage can but continue for a bit." Dracothraxus opens her mouth wide. Within, you can see a multitude of teeth, each one needle sharp. Also, near the back, you see a small but brilliant blue gem. Do you reach in and take it?

speaker: Dracothraxus
text: As you place your hand in the furnace that is the dragon's maw, you can't help but wonder if a small gem is worth the risk.

speaker: Dracothraxus
text: Nevertheless, you persevere and retrieve the lovely little gem.

speaker: Dracothraxus
text: Just as you are about to pluck the gem literally from the jaws of death, the dragon gently places it within her nest. Dracothraxus closes her mouth and winks at you. "'Twas merely a test of thy courage, little one."

speaker: Dracothraxus
text: "Tis a pity thy courage goes only so far as bravery in battle, and not to trust of an honorable opponent. However, thou hast earned thy reward, and here it is." The dragon pushes the gem forward with her tongue, and removes it from her mouth. She then places it gently within her nest.

speaker: Dracothraxus
text: "I go now to rest, but I shall return. The door will not open until thou hast found a way to best me for good and for all. Farewell, little mortal."

speaker: Batlin
text: Batlin watches Hook's death with icy resignation. Time seems to slow as he turns to you. "This battle is not done, Avatar. Dost thou imagine thyself an immortal? The Guardian is far more. Return to your precious Earth and rest."

speaker: Batlin
text: "Sleep, that he may visit your dreams with countless visions of death in the belly of the Great Sea Serpent."

speaker: Batlin
text: "As for me, I shall begone! Thou shalt never find me! Farewell, Avatar!"

speaker: Time Lord
text: "Congratulations, Avatar, on destroying the Sphere. I am free from my celestial prison. I thank thee. But I regret to inform thee that The Guardian engineered the Sphere such that its destruction has permanently disabled the Moongates, and thine Orb of the Moons as well. Thou canst not return to thine home by way of a red Moongate."

speaker: Time Lord
text: "Thine only hope of leaving Britannia at the conclusion of thy quest is to use The Guardian's own vehicle for entering the land -- The Black Gate."

speaker: Time Lord
text: "The Guardian's followers are building The Black Gate of blackrock and will be using magic and natural elements to activate it. The Guardian plans to enter Britannia during the upcoming Astronomical Alignment, which is imminent. That is the only time when the elements will work well enough for The Black Gate to be permeable and active. Thou wilt need a device which has the ability to vanquish blackrock. If thou hast not already encountered such a device, thou canst find something to help thee in the workshop of Rudyom the Mage, in Cove."

speaker: Time Lord
text: "Before thou canst locate The Black Gate, there is one more generator which must be destroyed. It is the device used to transmit The Guardian's voice to his followers and charm them into obeying his wishes. Look in the area near Serpent's Hold for a dungeon containing this generator. It is most likely shaped like a Cube. It could very well be on The Fellowship's island east of Serpent's Hold."

speaker: Time Lord
text: "When thou hast completed this task, concentrate thine efforts in Buccaneer's Den. Thou mayest find clues there as to the location of The Black Gate."

speaker: Time Lord
text: "Shouldst thou wish to speak with me again, simply use the hourglass. Goodbye."

speaker: Time Lord
text: "Avatar! The Astronomical Alignment is almost at hand! Time is running out! The Guardian must be prevented from coming through The Black Gate!"

speaker: Time Lord
text: "The Cube will help thee find the location of The Black Gate. With it in thy possession, those under the influence of The Guardian will be more receptive to speaking the truth to thee."

speaker: Time Lord
text: "Go to Buccaneer's Den. Search for the one called 'Hook'. Talk to the so-called Fellowship. Thou shouldst have no trouble ascertaining his whereabouts there. I am sure that thou wilt eventually find the location of The Black Gate! Good luck!"

speaker: Time Lord
text: You see a vaguely familiar but intimidating figure enclosed in some kind of cylindrical cell. He looks at you intently.

speaker: Time Lord
text: "It has been many years since we met during the time of Exodus! I have never wanted to see thee again as badly as most recently! It is about time thou shouldst arrive! I do not have eras to waste whilst I wait for thee! There is a crisis and Britannia needs thine help! I need thine help! The entire universe needs thine help!"

speaker: Time Lord
text: "Hast thou decided if thou wilt help me?"

speaker: Time Lord
text: The Time Lord looks relieved.

speaker: Time Lord
text: "Then I have a mission for thee."

speaker: Time Lord
text: "Then away with thee!"

speaker: Time Lord
text: "How may I help thee, Avatar?" the Time Lord asks.

speaker: Time Lord
text: "I am known as the Time Lord."

speaker: Time Lord
text: "I ensure that time flows smoothly through space." He shrugs his shoulders. "Do not ask me to explain this. It is beyond mortal beings' comprehension."

speaker: Time Lord
text: "It was I who sent the red moongate to thine homeland to lure thee to Britannia! It took every bit of my strength to make it functional, and still something went wrong. Thou didst arrive in Trinsic, which was not mine intention. It has therefore taken thee much longer to reach me than I anticipated."

speaker: Time Lord
text: "Once thou didst arrive in Britannia, the only other way I could contact thee was via the Wisps. After the considerable rest I had since creating the red moongate, I managed to repair the one Orb of the Moons location that would bring thee to me. I cannot roam freely through time and space, doing my work, whilst I am trapped here."

speaker: Time Lord
text: "The land is under attack by a powerful and malicious being from another dimension, and thou art the only one who can stop him! I have been trapped here by a trick, due to a sorcery which The Guardian has performed. The Guardian has put a wrinkle in the space-time continuum by creating a powerful 'generator' which has made the Moongates and thine Orb of the Moons mostly inoperable."

speaker: Time Lord
text: "Thou -must- free me and we must work together in battling The Guardian. The fate of thy people depends upon it. Dost thou accept?"

speaker: Time Lord
text: "Then I have a mission for thee."

speaker: Time Lord
text: "Then thou shalt be doomed to never finish thy quest. Art thou sure? I give thee one more chance. Dost thou want to help?"

speaker: Time Lord
text: "Then I have a mission for thee."

speaker: Time Lord
text: "Then farewell, Avatar. Leave now. Thou wilt come back when thou dost realize it is thy destiny to help me."

speaker: Time Lord
text: "I knew thou wouldst not let me down."

speaker: Time Lord
text: "Go at once to the Serpent's Spine area. Search for the entrance to a dungeon somewhere northwest of Britain. I believe it may be called 'Dungeon Despise'. This will lead thee to the generator causing the problem. If mine hunch is correct, it will resemble a large Sphere."

speaker: Time Lord
text: "Thou may have already seen it."

speaker: Time Lord
text: "Thou must find a way to destroy it."

speaker: Time Lord
text: "It may have a defense mechanism. If thou canst not conquer it, return here and describe the defense to me. Perhaps I can help thee more. It might be wise to use the spells Mark and Recall to save thyself the trouble of finding thy way through the entire dungeon a second time, should thou have to travel there again."

speaker: Time Lord
text: "Its defense, as thou dost know, is an unusual Moongate."

speaker: Time Lord
text: "Oddly aloof creatures. They have made good messengers in the past."

speaker: Time Lord
text: "He is an embodiment of supreme evil. He must be stopped. He thrives on domination and control."

speaker: Time Lord
text: "It is a magic generator that The Guardian was able to send from his world. Its purpose is to disable the Moongates. Thou must break its outer defense and enter the structure, taking the smaller Sphere floating inside. Keep the small Sphere, as it will be useful later."

speaker: Time Lord
text: "The Sphere's outer defense sends thy party back to a specific position in space. Until this defense is broken, thou canst not enter the generator. Thou must find Nicodemus' hourglass."

speaker: Time Lord
text: "If I am correct in mine hypothesis, the Sphere's inner defense will involve Moongates. Look for a visual pattern to help thee solve this mystery."

speaker: Time Lord
text: "It is an enchanted hourglass which will help thee if it is used at the site of the Sphere. Once I am free of the power of the generator, thou canst summon me by using the hourglass."

speaker: Time Lord
text: "It is of no use to thee now, unless thou dost want to summon me again."

speaker: Time Lord
text: "He is a mage that lives west of the forest of Yew."

speaker: Time Lord
text: The Time Lord thinks a moment.

speaker: Time Lord
text: "The ether must be repaired before the mages in Britannia can use magic again. I suggest that thou seest Penumbra in Moonglow. She may be able to help thee with this problem."

speaker: Time Lord
text: "Magic must be functioning properly now, Avatar. Use it wisely."

speaker: Time Lord
text: "It is a magic generator that The Guardian has sent from his world. It is controlling the ether which is depended upon by the mages to perform magic. Like the Sphere, thou must penetrate its outer defense, enter the structure, and take the smaller Tetrahedron floating inside."

speaker: Time Lord
text: "It is not surprising that the Tetrahedron has such a defense. Penumbra in Moonglow should be able to help thee with that. It is obvious now that the Tetrahedron must be destroyed before thou canst destroy the Sphere."

speaker: Time Lord
text: "I am not sure what kind of inner defense the Tetrahedron may hold. It may be dangerous. Be sure to be well-armed when entering it."

speaker: Time Lord
text: "She is an elderly mage who lives in Moonglow."

speaker: Time Lord
text: "It is a magic generator which The Guardian has sent from his world. From what thou dost say, it sounds to me like the device he uses to 'speak' to his followers and charm them into submitting to his wishes. I am afraid that before thou canst destroy it, thou must take care of the other magic generators which The Guardian has placed in Britannia."

speaker: Time Lord
text: "It is the third and final magic generator which The Guardian has sent from his world. It is the device he uses to 'speak' to his followers and charm them into submitting to his wishes. Tis in a dungeon near Serpents Hold. Thou must destroy its outer defense, enter it, and take the smaller Cube floating inside."

speaker: Time Lord
text: "This outer defense can be conquered by using special helmets which cover your ears. The helmets must be made from a rare mineral called 'Caddellite'. It is present in meteors. Seek out Brion, at the Observatory near the Lycaeum. He can give thee more advice on finding this mineral."

speaker: Time Lord
text: "The inner defense will most likely involve The Guardian himself. Do not listen to what he might tell thee."

speaker: Time Lord
text: "Farewell, Avatar. Good luck to thee."

speaker: Iolo
text: "<PLAYER_NAME> dost thou notice the unique Iolo trademark on these bolts?  They are designed for maximum performance with genuine IOLO crossbows, available at a location near Yew."

speaker: Spark
text: "Thou dost need a blacksmith to do that. I wager my dad could do it... I mean, could have... if he were still alive..."

speaker: Horance
text: As the Soul Cage dissolves into dust, a great transformation comes upon the Liche. Where the evil spirit was caged you see the form of a familiar person. It's Horance! He's a ghost, but he much more resembles a man than an undead terror.

speaker: Batlin
text: The wand glows faintly. Batlin smirks. "Not yet, Avatar."

speaker: Guard
text: You see a tough-looking guard who takes his job -very- seriously.

speaker: Guard
text: "My name is not important."

speaker: Guard
text: "I keep villains and knaves out of Trinsic and keep a record of all who leave. Thou must have a password to leave."

speaker: Guard
text: "What is the password?"

speaker: Guard
text: "Very well, thou mayest pass."

speaker: Guard
text: "Thou dost not know the password. Sorry. The Mayor can give thee the proper password."

speaker: Guard
text: "Goodbye."

speaker: Shrine
text: "Our gratitude is thine, Avatar. Thou hast saved Britannia from what might have become a second Age of Darkness. Again, thou dost prove thy worthiness to be the instrument of Lord British."

speaker: Shrine
text: "Salutations, Avatar. I can assist thee no more, but remember my words: the Psyche returns to the Core..."

speaker: Shrine
text: Suddenly, your mind is filled with the crystal-clear resonance of an authoritative voice.

speaker: Shrine
text: "Greeting to thee. I am the keeper of Truth. Dost thou seek the wisdom and boon of Truth?"

speaker: Shrine
text: The Shrine of Truth speaks. "Greetings, seeker. Once again I ask thee, Dost thou seek my enlightenment?"

speaker: Shrine
text: "Very well. Prepare thyself." The voice falls silent.

speaker: Shrine
text: "I wish thee well, then."

speaker: Shrine
text: "Thy Love for life is boundless. Thine heart-felt actions are a shining example to all of Britannia."

speaker: Shrine
text: "Welcome, Avatar. I can help thee no further, save to offer the advice I gave before: A great evil stirs in Britannia..."

speaker: Shrine
text: An unearthly beautiful voice sighs gently into your conciousness. "Greetings, Avatar. I represent the embodiment of Love. If thou dost seek enlightenment , thou must take the Test of	Love. Its path lies through the glowing, blue portal to the south."

speaker: Shrine
text: "I welcome thee again, seeker. I cannot aid thee until thy successful completion of the Test of Love."

speaker: Shrine
text: "Thine onus is abated and Britannia is free of Exodus' grasp once more. Thy deeds will long be rembered as the most courageous in the history of this land."

speaker: Shrine
text: "Hail, mighty Avatar! Thou must not fail in thy quest to find the Talisman of Infinity. Remember: the scroll that will unlock its secret lies within this castle."

speaker: Shrine
text: A strong, vibrant voice rings out in your mind. "Greetings seeker! I am the Keeper of Courage. If thou hast the will to seek my reward, thou must enter the portal to the south."

speaker: Shrine
text: "Again I say to thee, my path lies through the portal to the south. Enter if thou hast the Courage, seeker..."

speaker: Shrine
text: "Thou hast mastered the Test of Truth, and so a boon of great intellect and magical ability will be bestowed upon thee. Use -- and respect -- thy powers well, Avatar."

speaker: Shrine
text: "My heart is gladdened to learn that Love is a Principle thou dost hold dear, evident by thy successful completion of the Test of Love. Now, then, shall a blessing of quickness and skill be thine."

speaker: Shrine
text: "Well done, mighty warrior! The unsurpassed Courage which flows through thy veins could be none other than that of the Avatar. Thou hast proven thyself worthy of the reward of Courage with Valor, Sacrifice, Honor, and Spirituality... Receive it now	in Humility."

speaker: Shrine
text: "Thou hast now experienced the full meaning of the Principle of Truth. The value of such is beyond measure, for truth shall guide thee throughout thy life's endeavors."

speaker: Shrine
text: The statue's voice takes on a warning tone. "Know this Truth: the Psyche returns to the Core..." With that said, the statue becomes quiet once more.

speaker: Shrine
text: "Now hast thou earnestly experienced all that is Love. 'Tis a benefit never to be taken lightly, for Love is a formidible motivator. Remember always the lessons in Compassion, Sacrifice, and Justice thou hast mastered."

speaker: Shrine
text: The voice of the Keeper of Love fills with compassion as she speaks. "Do have a care, Avatar. For a great evil stirs within Britannia, I know not the source."

speaker: Shrine
text: Urgency breaks into the voice of the statue. "I lay upon thee a geas, and as thou art the Avatar, thou art bound to respond. Thy quest is to seek the Talisman of Infinity. Within this castle there lies a scroll which can tell thee of its use. Go now, for time grows short."

speaker: Palace Guard
text: You see a tough-looking guard who takes his job -very- seriously.

speaker: Palace Guard
text: "I am a guard."

speaker: Palace Guard
text: The man looks at you like you are an ignoramus. "I am a guard, idiot. Thou shouldst go about thy business."

speaker: Palace Guard
text: "Goodbye."

speaker: Avatar
text: You feel as if your mind is being probed, delicately at first, then with more insistance. Images of long past memories flit before your eyes and old emotions resurface. At one point, the images pause as you remember the words Love, Sol, Moons, and Death then a strange sense of deja vu comes over you as the vision comes up to the current time. The images cease and a vast wave of power overwhelms you. A wall of darkness falls...

speaker: Avatar
text: Your mind is quickly probed, then cast aside, leaving you feeling slightly ill and filled with an irrational sense of forboding.

speaker: Bollux
text: "Hast thou in thy possesion the book on the Stone of Castambre?"

speaker: Bollux
text: "His eyes reveal his hope. As he takes the book from you, it almost appears as if he is smiling."

speaker: Bollux
text: "That is, indeed, a pity," he says, shaking his head in sadness.

speaker: Bollux
text: "Greetings to thee, honorable one. I can but assume that my presence here was thy doing." It becomes quickly apparent that this creature possesses a greater	capability for speech than his fallen companion.

speaker: Bollux
text: The recently raised golem stares down at the prone, lifeless body of Bollux. Quickly he looks up at you.

speaker: Bollux
text: "Wh-what has happened?"

speaker: Bollux
text: "Now thou must excuse me, for I am off to find my fellow sentry."

speaker: Bollux
text: "Hail, friend. I hope that I may assist thee in some way."

speaker: Bollux
text: "Art thou here to aid me in healing my brother?"

speaker: Bollux
text: "Very good. I am pleased to call thee friend."

speaker: Bollux
text: "Then begone, for I have work to do!"

speaker: Iolo
text: A rather large, familiar man looks up and sees you. The shock that is evident from his dumbfounded expression quickly evolves into delight. He smiles broadly.

speaker: Iolo
text: "<PLAYER_NAME>! If I did not trust the infallibility of mine own eyes, I would not believe it! I was just thinking to myself, 'If only the Avatar were here!' Then..."

speaker: Iolo
text: "Lo and behold! Who says that magic is dying! Here is living proof that it is not!"

speaker: Iolo
text: "Dost thou realize, <PLAYER_NAME>, that it hath been 200 Britannian years since we last met? Why, thou hast not aged at all!"

speaker: Iolo
text: Iolo winks conspiratorially. He whispers, "Due no doubt to the difference in the structure of time in our original homeland and that of Britannia?"

speaker: Iolo
text: He resumes speaking aloud. "I have aged a little, as thou canst see. But of course, I have stayed here in Britannia all this time."

speaker: Iolo
text: "Oh, but Avatar! Wait until I tell the others! They will be happy to see thee! Welcome to Trinsic!"

speaker: Petre
text: The distraught peasant interrupts Iolo. "Show <PRONOUN> the stables, milord. 'Tis horrible!"

speaker: Iolo
text: Iolo nods, his joy fading quickly as he is reminded of the reason he was standing there in the first place.

speaker: Iolo
text: "Ah, yes. Our friend Petre here discovered something truly ghastly this morning. Take a look inside the stables. I shall accompany thee."

speaker: Iolo
text: Iolo takes you aside and whispers, "Avatar, for the sake of our mutual sanity, I strongly suggest that thou shouldst purchase a mouse."

speaker: Iolo
text: "I am sorry, I do not join thieves."

speaker: Iolo
text: "All right, I suppose thou hast learned thy lesson. I shall rejoin."

speaker: Iolo
text: "Yes, my friend?" Iolo asks.

speaker: Iolo
text: Your friend snorts. "What, art thou joking, <HONORIFIC>? Thou dost not know thine old friend Iolo?"

speaker: Iolo
text: "Thou must see for thyself, <PLAYER_NAME>. Brace thyself, my friend. 'Tis truly a horrible sight."

speaker: Iolo
text: "Why, right now 'tis adventuring with that most courageous of all legendary heroes, the Avatar!"

speaker: Iolo
text: "Why, there is no doubt -thou- art the Avatar, <PLAYER_NAME>! However, thou mayest have some trouble convincing those who do not know thy face."

speaker: Iolo
text: "Of course, thou -shouldst- be safe around thy friends!"

speaker: Iolo
text: "Well, after all, thou hast been gone for 200 years! Most of those who would recognize thee are long gone! Sorry to be blunt and all, my friend, but there it is."

speaker: Iolo
text: "Ugly, is it not? From what I have heard, neither Christopher nor Inamo deserved so grisly a death. Thou shouldst certainly ask everyone in town about it."

speaker: Iolo
text: "I wish thee luck in determining what is going on. I haven't a clue!" Iolo grins broadly, patting you on the back.

speaker: Iolo
text: "Well, between thee and me, I think that he hath aged much more than I!"

speaker: Iolo
text: "Full of information, that chap. But he never seems to leave Britain anymore."

speaker: Iolo
text: "My liege will be enormously pleased to see thee. We should travel to Britain post haste. I am sure he can give thee some valuable information and update thee on much of what thou hast missed in the 200 years of thine absence."

speaker: Iolo
text: "Certainly. LB is always a repository of the most amazing facts, eh? Probably something to do with listening and not always talking."

speaker: Iolo
text: "Right, Shamino?"

speaker: Iolo
text: Shamino grunts and turns away as Iolo grins mischievously.

speaker: Iolo
text: "Speaking of information, reminds me of something! I have a little item which might be useful to thee. 'Tis an abacus. Use it to tally up all of our gold."

speaker: Iolo
text: "Thou must mean Shamino and Dupre."

speaker: Iolo
text: "Why, he is right there, <HONORIFIC>."

speaker: Dupre
text: "I am right here, <HONORIFIC>."

speaker: Iolo
text: "See? I told thee!"

speaker: Iolo
text: "I am sure we shall find him somewhere. Last I heard, he was in Jhelom. Didst thou know he was knighted?"

speaker: Iolo
text: "Hard to believe, is it not?"

speaker: Iolo
text: "It's true! Lord British knighted him recently. Why he did so, I cannot imagine!"

speaker: Iolo
text: "Why, he is right there, <HONORIFIC>."

speaker: Shamino
text: "I am right here, <HONORIFIC>."

speaker: Iolo
text: "See? I told thee!"

speaker: Iolo
text: "Thy best bet in finding that rascal is to look in Britain. He has a girlfriend employed as an actress at the Royal Theatre."

speaker: Iolo
text: "The town has changed little, has it not? Everyone seems a little defensive, though. When we ran into each other, I was passing through and had stopped to visit my friend Finnigan."

speaker: Iolo
text: "I think it best for thee to speak with them thyself. There have been many changes since last thou didst visit, Avatar. I think thou wilt feel at times a bit... well, old-fashioned."

speaker: Iolo
text: "It has grown since thou last saw it. Paws is now a virtual township of Britain! It dominates the east coast of Britannia."

speaker: Iolo
text: "Lord British's castle is still the overwhelming feature."

speaker: Iolo
text: "It still lies between Britain and Trinsic, but it has grown further into Britain itself."

speaker: Iolo
text: "He is a good man. The Mayor of Trinsic, he is. I have known him for years."

speaker: Iolo
text: "I did not know him, <HONORIFIC>."

speaker: Iolo
text: "I never spoke with him. It is truly a shame. There are not many gargoyles living amongst the humans. This will only discourage the practice even more."

speaker: Iolo
text: Iolo looks hurt. "Thou dost really want me to leave?"

speaker: Iolo
text: "Dost thou want me to wait here or dost thou want me to go home to Yew?"

speaker: Iolo
text: "Very well. I shall wait here until thou dost return and ask me to rejoin."

speaker: Iolo
text: "Farewell, then. I shall always rejoin if thou dost so desire." Iolo turns away from you.

speaker: Iolo
text: "Whew. Thou didst frighten me!"

speaker: Iolo
text: "I was waiting until thou didst ask me!"

speaker: Iolo
text: "It seems that thou hast enough members travelling with thee already! I shall wait until someone leaves the group."

speaker: Iolo
text: "Since thou wert last in Britannia, the Gargoyles have begun to integrate with the humans. Most of them live on Sutek's old island, which was renamed 'Terfin'. However, thou mayest see one here and there throughout the land."

speaker: Iolo
text: "I do not know much about them, except that they originated about twenty Britannian years ago. They seem to do good deeds and are looked at with favor by most everyone. They have branch offices all over Britannia. I have not personally had any dealings with them."

speaker: Iolo
text: "He is just an acquaintance."

speaker: Iolo
text: "'Tis always a pleasure to speak with thee, my friend."

speaker: Spark
text: You see a boy who appears to be a young teen. He is dirty and unkempt. He looks as if he has been crying, but he sits up straight and looks sharp when he sees you.

speaker: Spark
text: "Who art thou and what dost thou want?" You realize the boy has a sling in hand.

speaker: Spark
text: You face the boy and tell him who you are.

speaker: Spark
text: "So? What makes thee so special?"

speaker: Spark
text: "The last time I heard -that- one I fell off a prehistoric creature from Eodon!"

speaker: Iolo
text: "Boy, this is the Avatar! "

speaker: Iolo
text: "Upon my word he is! He has come to help thee!"

speaker: Iolo
text: "Upon my word she is! She has come to help thee!"

speaker: Spark
text: Then the boy narrows his eyes, studying you. He slowly lowers his weapon, ready to act in case it's a trap. You admire the boy's obvious experience in dealing with strangers.

speaker: Spark
text: You and Spark stare at each other. He is not sure what to do. Finally, he nods his head. "All right. I believe thee. Thou dost look like paintings I have seen. I am sorry, <HONORIFIC>."

speaker: Spark
text: "Yes, <PLAYER_NAME>?" Spark asks. "What dost thou want?"

speaker: Spark
text: "I have always been called Spark."

speaker: Spark
text: "I have no job. I am only fourteen, so I am just learning how to best help Father in the smithy," he says, proudly. But then he suddenly realizes something which terrifies him. "And now that Father is dead, I am an orphan!"

speaker: Spark
text: "Father was the best blacksmith in Britannia. People were always coming from everywhere to get him to make this and that."

speaker: Spark
text: "My mother died a long time ago. I can just barely remember her."

speaker: Spark
text: "I cannot believe Father is dead. And poor Inamo, too. It is so strange. I -dreamed- it was happening. Well, in a way."

speaker: Spark
text: "Last night I was having a nightmare about Father. I dreamed that he screamed, and it woke me up. I looked around the house, but he was not in his bed. I was wide awake, so I went out to find him."

speaker: Spark
text: "I am sure thou canst find the man who killed Father!"

speaker: Spark
text: "Dost thou want me to repeat everything I know about the murder?"

speaker: Spark
text: "What dost thou want to know about?"

speaker: Spark
text: "All right."

speaker: Spark
text: "I am not sure if it's the same one, but I think I saw Father with a scroll just like the one in the chest one or two days ago. I know he was making something special for someone. I am fairly certain it was at his shop. As for the medallion, he usually wore it. I do not know why it was in the chest. And the gold-- I have never seen so much gold in my life. I cannot imagine why father had it."

speaker: Spark
text: "Thou shouldst try opening the chest."

speaker: Spark
text: "It is so strange. I -dreamed- it was happening. Well, in a way."

speaker: Spark
text: "Last night I was having a nightmare about Father. I dreamed that he screamed, and it woke me up. I looked around the house, but he was not in his bed. I was wide awake, so I went out to find him."

speaker: Spark
text: "I know it sounds witless, but... I dreamed that a big red-faced man was watching down on everything and... He looked down... And he noticed Father... That is all I remember."

speaker: Spark
text: "No, I did not find him. At least, not right away. But I did see something."

speaker: Spark
text: "I was in front of the stables. I saw a man and a wingless gargoyle running from behind the building. They ran toward the dock. Then I went inside and found... Father."

speaker: Spark
text: Spark's voice falters, and he begins to sob a little.

speaker: Spark
text: "All I saw of him was that the man had a hook for a right hand."

speaker: Spark
text: "I cannot tell one gargoyle from another. I could not identify him, except that he had no wings."

speaker: Spark
text: "Wilt thou go find the Man with the Hook? Let me help thee!" the boy pleads. His tears cease, and his face takes on a determined, forceful look.

speaker: Spark
text: "Take me with thee! Please! I must avenge Father's death! If thou dost not take me with thee, I will follow thee anyway!"

speaker: Spark
text: The boy is all excited now. "I am an expert with a slingshot! I can strike sewer rats with almost every shot! And I am small -- I do not eat much! Please take me! Please ask me to join thee!"

speaker: Iolo
text: Iolo whispers to you. "I do not know about taking a child on the road with us, <HONORIFIC>."

speaker: Spark
text: Suddenly, Spark lets his sling fly. His target, a small fly hovering above Iolo's head, is smacked out of the air. You laugh as Iolo	yelps, jumps away, curses and runs his fingers through his hair.

speaker: Spark
text: Suddenly, Spark lets his sling fly. His target, a small fly hovering above your head, is smacked out of the air.

speaker: Spark
text: "I told thee I am good! May I join?"

speaker: Spark
text: "Hooray!" the boy leaps with delight.

speaker: Spark
text: "Fine." The boy looks angry. "But I'll follow thee anyway."

speaker: Spark
text: "I know thou wilt find that man."

speaker: Spark
text: "I know thou wilt find that man."

speaker: Spark
text: "'Tis about time thou didst ask again!"

speaker: Spark
text: "Hooray!"

speaker: Spark
text: "Well, on second thought, it looks like too big of a crowd. I do not like crowds."

speaker: Spark
text: "Don't make me go!" Spark cries. "Dost thou really want me to go?" He looks at you with puppy-dog eyes.

speaker: Spark
text: "Well, should I just wait here or dost thou want me to go home to Trinsic?"

speaker: Spark
text: "All right. I shall wait here until thou dost return and ask me to rejoin."

speaker: Spark
text: Spark bows his head and murmurs, "Goodbye, then."

speaker: Spark
text: "Thou wilt not be sorry!"

speaker: Spark
text: "Father was the blacksmith. I cannot believe that he has been murdered! He had no enemies that I know of. Unless it was The Fellowship."

speaker: Spark
text: "Well, at first they harassed Father and me when they came around asking us to join. I suppose they do good things. Many people like them. Father eventually joined the group after he went to Britain and took one of their tests."

speaker: Spark
text: "I do not know anything about them. I never took one. Maybe thou shouldst ask the man at the Fellowship Branch. Klog."

speaker: Spark
text: "The Fellowship has branches all over Britannia."

speaker: Spark
text: "He is the head of the Fellowship Branch here in Trinsic. He and Father got into an argument a week ago when Klog and two of his friends came over to talk with Father."

speaker: Spark
text: "I don't know what it was about. Perhaps thou shouldst ask Klog."

speaker: Spark
text: "I do not remember what they look like. I did not recognize them.	They were most likely some other members of The Fellowship."

speaker: Spark
text: "That key opened my Father's chest, did it not?"

speaker: Spark
text: "That looks like the key to Father's chest. I wondered where it was!"

speaker: Spark
text: "What key? Dost thou have the key to Father's chest? Where is it?"

speaker: Spark
text: The boy's eyes widen. "I had no idea that Father had that much money hidden away!"

speaker: Spark
text: "I suppose I could give it to thee if thou art going to look for those who killed my Father!"

speaker: Spark
text: "Father was a member of The Fellowship. I don't know why the medallion was in the chest -- he usually wore it."

speaker: Spark
text: "I am not sure if it's the same one, but I think I saw Father with a scroll just like that one or two days ago. I know he was making something special for someone. I am fairly certain it was at his shop."

speaker: Spark
text: "It's in the southwest corner of town."

speaker: Spark
text: "He was a very nice gargoyle. He helped Father a lot and did tasks in the stables. I cannot think why anyone would want to kill him!"

speaker: Spark
text: "All right, I will speak with thee later."

speaker: Shamino
text: "I am sorry, I do not join thieves."

speaker: Shamino
text: "All right, I suppose thou hast learned thy lesson. I shall rejoin."

speaker: Shamino
text: Your old friend Shamino stands before you and you marvel that he has finally progressed into what some might call 'middle age'.

speaker: Shamino
text: "Yes, <PLAYER_NAME>?" Shamino asks.

speaker: Shamino
text: Your friend looks at you like you have lost your head. "'Tis Shamino. -Sha-mi-no-."

speaker: Shamino
text: "I should hope 'twould be adventuring with thee! I am weary of loitering about Britain. There is much we could be accomplishing! Where hast thou been, anyway?"

speaker: Shamino
text: "But please tell me what brings thee here!"

speaker: Shamino
text: "Well, I do not know if thou art aware, but we are having many problems with magic in general, and with the Moongates."

speaker: Shamino
text: "Yes, I have been in Britain as of late, attempting to find work. Thou dost know that adventuring comes around too infrequently. One must find -other- diversions. Which reminds me... I have thy pocketwatch."

speaker: Shamino
text: "Thou didst leave it when thou didst last visit Britannia. Here	it is."

speaker: Shamino
text: Shamino hands you the pocketwatch.

speaker: Shamino
text: "Oops. Thine hands are too full to take it. Ask me about it later."

speaker: Shamino
text: "I already gave thee the pocketwatch, <PLAYER_NAME>. I hope thou didst not lose it again!"

speaker: Shamino
text: "The usual. I do not see our old friends often, and Lord British rarely finds work for me. I certainly have no time	for wenching or drinking -- I have grown up a bit."

speaker: Iolo
text: "Ahem, I have heard something about an actress, no?"

speaker: Shamino
text: "What dost thou know of it?"

speaker: Iolo
text: "<PLAYER_NAME>, ask him about 'Amber'."

speaker: Shamino
text: "Thou art a swine, Iolo."

speaker: Shamino
text: "I suggest that thou proceed immediately to see him!"

speaker: Shamino
text: "I am glad I do not look as aged as -he- does!"

speaker: Shamino
text: "Thou dost mean Iolo and Dupre, I presume?"

speaker: Shamino
text: "Dost thou mean that miserable excuse for an archer?"

speaker: Iolo
text: "Watch what thou dost say, scoundrel!"

speaker: Shamino
text: "Yes, that's Iolo!"

speaker: Shamino
text: "Surely he is around somewhere. Where didst thou last leave him?"

speaker: Shamino
text: "Dost thou mean that incorrigible wencher and drunkard?"

speaker: Dupre
text: "Do not forget that my mere thumb can squash in thy face like a marshmallow."

speaker: Shamino
text: "Yes, that's Dupre!"

speaker: Dupre
text: "That's -Sir- Dupre to thee!"

speaker: Shamino
text: "Sir Dupuke? Didst thou say Sir Dupuke?"

speaker: Dupre
text: "Du-pre-!"

speaker: Shamino
text: "Pardon -me-, Sir Dupuke!"

speaker: Dupre
text: "I'm not going to listen to this anymore."

speaker: Shamino
text: "I believe he is in Jhelom."

speaker: Shamino
text: "He must be around somewhere!"

speaker: Shamino
text: Shamino looks relieved. "I am -so- glad thou didst ask me that." He gathers his gear and prepares to follow you.

speaker: Shamino
text: "Hmmm. I do not like big crowds. I shall wait until thy group is smaller before joining."

speaker: Shamino
text: "Hmmm. Dost thou merely want me to wait here or dost thou want me to go home?"

speaker: Shamino
text: "Very well. I shall await thy return."

speaker: Shamino
text: "I really hate to, but if thou dost insist." Shamino	grudgingly gathers his belongings.

speaker: Shamino
text: Shamino listens as you tell him the story. "I would be honored to join and help thee in investigating this matter."

speaker: Shamino
text: "I am confounded by their inability to function properly."

speaker: Shamino
text: "'Tis a pity that thou art marooned here."

speaker: Shamino
text: "Magic all over Britannia seems to be disturbed. Say, dost thou remember Nicodemus in the great forest? He has gone mad and is terribly silly. Perhaps we should visit him."

speaker: Shamino
text: "It does not work well. I do not understand it."

speaker: Shamino
text: "It will probably work extremely well now, <PLAYER_NAME>."

speaker: Shamino
text: You see a light shine in Shamino's eyes as you mention her name. He is obviously smitten.

speaker: Shamino
text: "She is an actress I know."

speaker: Shamino
text: "That woman! She cannot understand that I must have mine adventuring! I cannot settle down. -Yet-! Soon maybe."

speaker: Shamino
text: Shamino looks concerned. "I have grown up. A bit."

speaker: Shamino
text: Shamino bows slightly.

speaker: Dupre
text: "I am sorry, I do not join thieves."

speaker: Dupre
text: "All right, I suppose thou hast learned thy lesson. I shall rejoin."

speaker: Dupre
text: You see the familiar face of your good friend, Dupre. While somewhat older, he still seems full of his usual casual good humor.

speaker: Dupre
text: "How may I assist thee, <PLAYER_NAME>?" asks Sir Dupre.

speaker: Dupre
text: "Why, dost thou not recognize me? It is I, Lord British!" he laughs. "Dost thou not know thy friend Dupre when thou seest him, <PLAYER_NAME>?"

speaker: Shamino
text: "Do not be so modest, Sir Dupre. Thou shouldst tell the Avatar that thou hast been knighted since last you met."

speaker: Dupre
text: Sir Dupre looks quite embarrassed. "Well, yes, I would have gotten around to that."

speaker: Iolo
text: "Do not be so modest, Sir Dupre. Thou shouldst tell the Avatar that thou hast been knighted since last you met."

speaker: Dupre
text: Sir Dupre looks quite embarrassed. "Well, yes, I would have gotten around to that."

speaker: Dupre
text: "I have not seen our old friends in some time. Currently I am conducting a study of all of the various drinking establishments of Britannia. At present I am about halfway through. But it is nothing that could keep me from adventuring with thee, <PLAYER_NAME>."

speaker: Dupre
text: "My job is currently to try and keep thee and thy friends out of trouble as much as possible!" He winks and gives you a good-natured grin.

speaker: Dupre
text: "Our old friends -- Iolo and Shamino."

speaker: Dupre
text: "It would be both an honor and a pleasure to join thee on thine adventures once again."

speaker: Dupre
text: "Hmm. Too crowded for my liking. Come back if thou shouldst diminish thy group by a member or two."

speaker: Dupre
text: "Dost thou want me to wait here or dost thou truly want me to leave and go home?"

speaker: Dupre
text: "Very well. I shall await thy return."

speaker: Dupre
text: "I shall depart thy company if that is truly thy wish. If thou shouldst ever need me again, thou hast only to ask." He turns away from you, obviously disappointed.

speaker: Dupre
text: "It is something like the old times of Britannia, during the days of thy last visit, only more bloodthirsty. The local sport in Jhelom is duelling."

speaker: Dupre
text: "These people still believe that any problem can be solved by hitting something or stabbing someone. They remind me of a more primitive but less complicated time. Perhaps that is why people live here-- to escape their modern problems."

speaker: Dupre
text: "Right now the town is buzzing about three local fighters, all of whom have challenged another man to a duel. The challenged one's name is Sprellic."

speaker: Dupre
text: "Perhaps now that several of Jhelom's local ruffians have been well smited things in that town will calm down. Although I doubt they will for long."

speaker: Dupre
text: "Perhaps since thou hast shown the town that disagreements can be settled without bloodshed things will calm down for a while in Jhelom. But I doubt it."

speaker: Dupre
text: "I feel a bit sorry that we never did intercede on behalf of that innkeeper fellow, Sprellic. He did need our help, desperately." Dupre eyes look a bit sad.

speaker: Dupre
text: "I doubt he has ever held a sword in his life. When I bet I usually bet on the underdog, but not even I am so foolhardy with my money as to bet on him. The man is no fighter, he is the innkeeper!"

speaker: Dupre
text: "Thou didst save the life of that poor little man Sprellic. He certainly got himself in a lot of trouble." Dupre cannot keep himself from grinning. "Still, all's well that ends well."

speaker: Dupre
text: "To this Sprellic fellow, foolhardy would be a compliment! He looks like he has never been in a fight in his entire life. I do not know why he would provoke someone into a duel. It is a puzzlement."

speaker: Dupre
text: You tell Dupre what Sprellic told you. "Hmmm. I suppose I judged the man too harshly. I think thou, er, we shouldst do something about this!"

speaker: Dupre
text: "I know not the specifics of his story but thou mayest ask him for thyself. He went back to his house about an hour ago and has not come out. He must be having a very hard time finding something."

speaker: Dupre
text: "The poor man has been hiding in his house and will not come out."

speaker: Dupre
text: "Terrible what happened to our poor friend Iolo. We must try and get his body to a healer while there may still be time to revive him. I do miss him so."

speaker: Dupre
text: "<PLAYER_NAME>, there is a strange old man following thee, and he bears a vague resemblance to Iolo! It is most odd."

speaker: Iolo
text: "Thy drinking must have blurred thy vision, Sir Dupre."

speaker: Dupre
text: "Then thou hadst better join me for one later. It will give thee the chance to catch up to me."

speaker: Dupre
text: "We should find that rascal Iolo and have him join us as well."

speaker: Dupre
text: "Two men and a woman. Their names are Timmons, Vokes, and Syria. Respectively."

speaker: Dupre
text: "A sad fate to befall our fine comrade Shamino. He will be sorely missed. We must try and get his remains to a healer. Perhaps he may still be revived."

speaker: Dupre
text: Sir Dupre snorts, "From what I had heard Shamino was all but settled down and retired from the adventuring life."

speaker: Shamino
text: "I still have a few wild oats left to sow, thank thee very much."

speaker: Dupre
text: "Then it is good to see another member of our old sowing circle once again!"

speaker: Dupre
text: "Let us go and find Shamino and make this a proper reunion!"

speaker: Dupre
text: Sir Dupre stares at the Fellowship medallion around your neck for a long moment. "Thou must be joking," he snorts.

speaker: Dupre
text: "I still cannot believe that thou hast joined The Fellowship. If thou didst wish to prove that thou wouldst do anything, no matter how ridiculous to fulfill thy quest, then thou hast succeeded."

speaker: Dupre
text: "Spark, the poor brave lad, is no longer with us. We should endeavor to get his body to a healer so he may be revived."

speaker: Dupre
text: Dupre points a thumb at Spark. "He is joining us, as well?" He mutters at you, "Art thou trying to make me feel old, <PLAYER_NAME>?"

speaker: Dupre
text: "I shall speak with thee later, then."

speaker: Jaana
text: You are surprised to see your old companion Jaana, looking only slightly aged since your last visit.

speaker: Jaana
text: "Yes, <PLAYER_NAME>?" Jaana asks.

speaker: Jaana
text: "Why, I am Jaana. Thou shouldst remember me!"

speaker: Jaana
text: "I have been the Cove Healer for some time now, and can provide thee with mine healing services. Since magic is not reliable, I have been yearning to join a party of adventurers, such as mine old friends. I miss the old life!"

speaker: Jaana
text: "I am sorry, I must wait a while before I can heal again."

speaker: Jaana
text: "Our old friends -- Iolo, Shamino, and Dupre. The men who conquer evil in the name of Lord British!"

speaker: Jaana
text: "I would be honored to join thee, <HONORIFIC>!"

speaker: Jaana
text: "I do believe thou dost have too many members travelling in thy group. I shall wait until someone leaves and thou dost ask me again."

speaker: Jaana
text: "Dost thou want me to wait here or should I go home?"

speaker: Jaana
text: "Very well. I shall wait until thou dost return."

speaker: Jaana
text: "I shall obey thy wish. I would be happy to re-join if thou shouldst ask. Goodbye."

speaker: Jaana
text: "My magic has been affected by something in the air, but I have found that my senses are still with me. Hast thou noticed that the mages in the land are afflicted in the head? It is most disconcerting. Nevertheless, I can manage to cast a spell or two most of the time."

speaker: Jaana
text: "I feel that the ether is flowing smoothly now. Magic is alive again!"

speaker: Jaana
text: Jaana blushes. "Yes, I have been seeing our Town Mayor for some time now."

speaker: Lord Heather
text: "I see that thou art leaving Cove for a while, my dear?"

speaker: Jaana
text: "Yes, milord. But I shall return. I promise thee."

speaker: Lord Heather
text: "I shall try not to worry about thee, but it will be difficult."

speaker: Jaana
text: "Do not worry. I shall be safe with the Avatar."

speaker: Lord Heather
text: "I do hope so." The Mayor embraces Jaana.

speaker: Jaana
text: "Where is he? 'Twould be good to see him!"

speaker: Jaana
text: "He looks the same to me! Perhaps he has a little more waistline than before... but that is to be expected if one stays away from adventuring for too long!"

speaker: Iolo
text: "What dost thou mean? 'Little more waistline' indeed!"

speaker: Jaana
text: "No offense intended, Iolo!"

speaker: Jaana
text: "Oh, I would love to see him. I wonder where he might be."

speaker: Jaana
text: "Shamino, thou dost not look like a 'kid' anymore! What didst happen? Didst thou reach the venerable age of thirty?"

speaker: Shamino
text: "Hmph. I am still a kid at heart."

speaker: Jaana
text: "That is a relief." She grins cheekily.

speaker: Jaana
text: "I miss having a drink or two with that rogue! Let's go find that knight!"

speaker: Jaana
text: "For someone recently knighted, he has retained his good looks and boyish charm, hasn't he?"

speaker: Dupre
text: "Thou dost mean 'mannish' charm, dost thou not?"

speaker: Jaana
text: "Oh, pardon -me-, sir. Thine immaturity confused me for a moment."

speaker: Dupre
text: "Art thou going to let her get away with that, <PLAYER_NAME>?"

speaker: Dupre
text: Dupre is speechless and turns away in a huff.

speaker: Jaana
text: "Good!" Jaana winks at you from behind his back.

speaker: Jaana
text: "I have not seen our liege in many years."

speaker: Jaana
text: "Goodbye, <HONORIFIC>."

speaker: Trellek
text: The creature ignores you.

speaker: Trellek
text: The ape-like creature peers at you intently for a few minutes. Then, shrugging, it walks cautiously up to you. "I am Trellek. Your name is?"

speaker: Trellek
text: The Emp peers at you intensely for a few minutes. Then, shrugging, it walks cautiously up to you. "I am Trellek. Your name is?"

speaker: Trellek
text: "You are greeted."

speaker: Trellek
text: "You are greeted, <PLAYER_NAME>."

speaker: Trellek
text: "My name is still Trellek."

speaker: Trellek
text: He gives you a puzzled look.

speaker: Trellek
text: "The meaning of `job' is not clear to me. Is `work' the word meant by you?"

speaker: Trellek
text: "I am a gatherer of food."

speaker: Trellek
text: "No job is had by me."

speaker: Trellek
text: "All Emps are food-gatherers. Mainly fruits are sought by us."

speaker: Trellek
text: "Fruits are pleasant-tasting, like the honey you gave us!"

speaker: Trellek
text: "I am an Emp. Saralek is an Emp. Salamon is an Emp. You," he smiles, "are a human."

speaker: Trellek
text: "Saralek is my bonded-one. `Wife' is what you would call her. My home is her home."

speaker: Trellek
text: "Silverleaf trees are our homes," he nods.

speaker: Trellek
text: "Silverleaf trees cannot be explained by me in human terms. I am sorry. Another human should be asked by you?" he shrugs, imitating the human gesture rather well.

speaker: Trellek
text: "Salamon is the wisest Emp. Humans have been met by her. -Many- things have been seen by her. She is very experienced and knowledgeable."

speaker: Trellek
text: "Wisps are known to me," he nods. "Wisps are found in the woods. What is your concern?"

speaker: Trellek
text: "For you to talk to wisps is still your wish? Then helping you is my goal. A whistle can be made by me."

speaker: Trellek
text: "Correct was my bonded-one. A whistle can be made by me."

speaker: Trellek
text: "The residence of the wisps is a stone building in a mountain in the middle of the forest."

speaker: Trellek
text: "A whistling sound is made by Emps when talking is done by us. An imitation of that sound can be created by a special whistle," he says enthusiastically.

speaker: Trellek
text: He begins quickly searching around for a dead, hollow, fallen tree branch. Shortly he finds one that meets his satisfaction. Apparently embarrassed, he turns his back to you, and makes motions similar to one twisting a cork from a flagon.

speaker: Trellek
text: After a few minutes of this, he turns around and presents the whistle to you.

speaker: Trellek
text: "Here is your whistle."

speaker: Trellek
text: "Fewer items must be carried by you to take this whistle."

speaker: Trellek
text: "Your statement is a mystery. For me to talk to wisps is what you want?"

speaker: Trellek
text: He looks around, apparently surveying the area.

speaker: Trellek
text: "No wisps are here for conversation."

speaker: Trellek
text: "Your want is not conveyed to me." He shrugs.

speaker: Trellek
text: "Julius was a good human. His great deed was saving Emp family from big fire years ago." He stares at you directly.

speaker: Trellek
text: "But, his story is sad, being about his death from too much smoke in his body. His body is in the cemetery near the Abbey. He is one human that Emps call 'hero'."

speaker: Trellek
text: "Your wish is for me to travel with you?"

speaker: Trellek
text: "My wish is that also. But that is not the wish of Saralek, my wife. Permission from her must first be gained."

speaker: Trellek
text: "You are very odd, <PLAYER_NAME>."

speaker: Trellek
text: "Good luck is hoped for you."

speaker: Sentri
text: You see a dashing, slender man, stylishly dressed, with a lot of flair.

speaker: Sentri
text: "How may I help thee, <PLAYER_NAME>?" Sentri asks.

speaker: Sentri
text: "Thou dost not remember me? I am Sentri! We have gone adventuring together in the past!"

speaker: Sentri
text: "When I am not adventuring with old friends, I am a trainer in Britain. I specialize in combat involving swordsmanship. I am quite good at that, as thou dost remember."

speaker: Sentri
text: "But I would drop everything to join thy group if thou art not too encumbered."

speaker: Sentri
text: "I do not see our old friends Iolo, Shamino, or Dupre much."

speaker: Sentri
text: Sentri draws his sword so quickly it is like a flash of lightning. He does a few fancy moves, slashing the air with the blade. "No foe shall stand after I am finished with him!"

speaker: Sentri
text: Sentri bows. "I am very pleased to join thy group."

speaker: Sentri
text: "I like small crowds, Avatar. Thou art travelling with a group too large for my tastes. If thou shouldst lose someone along the way, return and I shall be happy to join thee."

speaker: Sentri
text: "Dost thou want me to wait here or go home?"

speaker: Sentri
text: "Very good. I shall wait here until thou dost return."

speaker: Sentri
text: "Farewell, <PLAYER_NAME>. If thou dost need my services again, I shall be only too happy to comply."

speaker: Sentri
text: "I am becoming weary of the place. It is having growth pains of which the bourgeoisie are unaware. All is not as serene as the noblemen present it."

speaker: Sentri
text: "Well, for example, try going to one of the smaller towns, say, Paws. It is a poor man's place. It reeks, too. And 'tis only just beyond the Britain town limits. More money should be put into improving the land as a whole, not just in building new buildings in the capitol city. I do not know what Lord British is thinking!"

speaker: Sentri
text: "My fee is 30 gold for a training session. Is this all right?"

speaker: Sentri
text: "Then I shall rob someone else!" Sentri laughs aloud.

speaker: Sentri
text: "I am afraid I must adhere to my policy of training only during my business hours. This applies to -all- of my friends."

speaker: Sentri
text: "Since I am a member of thy group, I shall train thee for free!"

speaker: Sentri
text: "How art thou, friend? Thou dost look like thou couldst use a little training thyself!"

speaker: Iolo
text: "What is this? Everyone doth make fun of my physique!"

speaker: Sentri
text: "I am not making fun, Iolo. I am serious!" Sentri laughs.

speaker: Sentri
text: "I miss that fellow!"

speaker: Sentri
text: "Say, Shamino, art thou still spending thy time dressing in women's clothes?"

speaker: Sentri
text: "Or art thou wasting away thy life in a healer's den, now that thou art in thy middle ages?"

speaker: Shamino
text: "Careful, friend. Those are fighting words!"

speaker: Sentri
text: Sentri punches Shamino good-naturedly. "And that is all they are, my dear friend. Words! 'Tis good to see thee!"

speaker: Sentri
text: "'Twould be good to share a joke or two with him!"

speaker: Sentri
text: "Ah, my good friend Dupre! Hast thou some good ale on thee?"

speaker: Dupre
text: "Art thou joking? I -always- have ale!"

speaker: Sentri
text: "Then we should have some before someone else does!"

speaker: Dupre
text: "'Twould be a pleasure. However, I must be prudent and save the ale for when we need it."

speaker: Sentri
text: Sentri feels of Dupre's head. "Art thou feeling all right, Dupre? Or has knighthood done something to thy brain?"

speaker: Sentri
text: "No, but I would be glad to stop in a pub and share a few pints with thee!"

speaker: Sentri
text: "Mmmm! Sounds good to me! Next time we pass a place, let us stop!"

speaker: Sentri
text: "I want to see that no-good trouble-maker! He is a knight now, I hear! Sir Dupre indeed!"

speaker: Sentri
text: "I never see him much. He stays in that castle of his all the time. He never gets out. No wonder he hasn't a clue what is going on in this country."

speaker: Sentri
text: "Until later."

speaker: Julia
text: You see Julia, a member of your party of adventurers from one of your previous visits to Britannia.

speaker: Julia
text: "It is good to speak with thee again, <PLAYER_NAME>," Julia greets you.

speaker: Julia
text: "Has it really been that long, <PLAYER_NAME>? 'Tis I, Julia!"

speaker: Julia
text: "Since accompanying thee on thine adventures when thou wast last in Britannia, I have become the tinker of Minoc. I repair things for the people of the town. But my duties and obligations are not so pressing as to prevent me from joining thee again shouldst thou wish it. After all, when thou art in Britannia, thou hast usually come to repair very important things and help put the world to rights."
