speaker: Julia
text: "Now is not the proper time for a joyous reunion, <PLAYER_NAME>. This town has been touched by a mysterious evil. There have been murders committed in Minoc."

speaker: Julia
text: "It is not really what I wish to do with the rest of my life. I do not have the patience to be a proper tinkerer. If thou didst ask me, I would say I have sacrificed enough!"

speaker: Julia
text: "Well... All right. But I did not like thee telling me to leave!"

speaker: Julia
text: "Aye! It would be my pleasure!"

speaker: Julia
text: "I believe thou hast enough travellers for one group."

speaker: Julia
text: "Art thou sure thou dost want me to leave?"

speaker: Julia
text: "Dost thou want me to wait here or should I go home?"

speaker: Julia
text: "Very well. I shall wait here until thou dost return."

speaker: Julia
text: "Well! Fine, if that is thy wish, I shall leave!"

speaker: Julia
text: "Then I shall stay."

speaker: Julia
text: "'Tis a terrible thing to be happening in our town, these murders. Minoc was once a safe and quiet place."

speaker: Julia
text: "Well, at least safe, if not necessarily quiet. Especially with all the commotion caused by Owen and his monument."

speaker: Julia
text: "Owen is our local shipwright. Frankly, I think he is something of a fool."

speaker: Julia
text: "The Fellowship wanted to build a statue of Owen. That way they can use him as an example of the success of the Fellowship philosophy. It would also increase Owen's business to the point of upsetting the local economy and driving the Artist's Guild out of business!"

speaker: Julia
text: "And it would have worked if thou hadst not put a stop to their plans."

speaker: Julia
text: "Frederico and Tania were killed at the Minoc sawmill in a manner most gruesome."

speaker: Julia
text: "Frederico was the leader of the Gypsies, and Tania was his wife. They lived outside of town. I know nothing more about them."

speaker: Julia
text: "The manner in which Frederico and Tania were murdered suggests a ritual killing. From what I have been hearing it is similar to one that thou hast run across in Trinsic	and one that occurred in Britain a while ago. 'Tis a most puzzling mystery."

speaker: Julia
text: "May I see them?" She examines every line of the plans carefully. "These designs are unsound. Ships built to these specifications will easily capsize and sink. Thou shouldst show these plans to the Mayor."

speaker: Julia
text: "Karl has the plans to the ships Owen built that sank?! I would very much like see them. Perhaps I could help discover why those tragedies occurred."

speaker: Julia
text: "Perhaps we should go find Iolo and have him join us as well."

speaker: Julia
text: "Hello, Iolo."

speaker: Iolo
text: "'Tis a pleasure to see thee again, Julia."

speaker: Julia
text: "Perhaps we should go find Shamino and have him join us as well."

speaker: Julia
text: "Hello, Shamino!"

speaker: Shamino
text: "Oh, Julia! Good of thee to be joining us again!"

speaker: Julia
text: "Perhaps we should go find Sir Dupre and have him join us as well."

speaker: Julia
text: "Once again our paths cross, Sir Dupre!"

speaker: Dupre
text: "Julia! I was just wondering if we would ever see thee again!"

speaker: Julia
text: "Well, thou canst wonder no more, Dupre."

speaker: Dupre
text: "<PLAYER_NAME>, just between thou, myself and the lamppost, thou hadst better watch Julia. She hath a temper."

speaker: Julia
text: "And who is this fine young lad?"

speaker: Spark
text: "My name is Spark, milady."

speaker: Julia
text: "He is a cute one! And so well-mannered!"

speaker: Spark
text: Spark turns beet red.

speaker: Julia
text: "Goodbye, <PLAYER_NAME>."

speaker: Katrina
text: You see your old companion Katrina looking only slightly older than when you saw her during your last visit.

speaker: Katrina
text: "Hello again, <PLAYER_NAME>!" Katrina greets you with a smile.

speaker: Katrina
text: "Why," she blinks at you, "I know it has been a long time, but surely thou cannot have forgotten me. I am Katrina. One of thine old companions."

speaker: Katrina
text: You share a friendly laugh at your reunion.

speaker: Katrina
text: "Ah, yes, Iolo, Shamino, and Dupre."

speaker: Katrina
text: "Although there is a vast difference in how time passes in our world and in this one, I am certain I have aged at least a bit," she says pleasantly.

speaker: Katrina
text: "Why, after last accompanying thee on thine adventures I settled down to the peaceful life of a shepherd in New Magincia."

speaker: Katrina
text: "If thou dost have need of me I could join thy party again."

speaker: Katrina
text: "Following thee around, <HONORIFIC>! I shall never miss New Magincia!"

speaker: Katrina
text: "I watch over my flock, and the townspeople as well, when they need me."

speaker: Katrina
text: "It would be an honor, <HONORIFIC>!"

speaker: Katrina
text: "I prefer smaller crowds, Avatar. Perhaps later."

speaker: Katrina
text: "Dost thou want me to wait here or shall I go on home?"

speaker: Katrina
text: "I shall be happy to wait here until thou dost return."

speaker: Katrina
text: "If thou dost think it best, I shall. If thou dost need me again thou dost have but to ask."

speaker: Katrina
text: "We are isolated here. We get no news from the world outside. Life is much the same as it was the last time thou didst visit Britannia two hundred years ago. I have many friends here."

speaker: Katrina
text: "That is the way we like it here. Now we have three other strangers on the island -- besides thee. Of course, thou couldst hardly be called a stranger. This is the largest number of visitors we have had in years."

speaker: Katrina
text: "But, never fear, <PLAYER_NAME>, I am seldom lonely."

speaker: Katrina
text: "I have many friends here. When I am lonely, I speak with Alagner the Sage, Russell the shipwright, or Henry the peddler."

speaker: Katrina
text: "He is a wise man who knows many things and tells wonderful stories. Alagner came here to retreat from the outside world. I know not why."

speaker: Katrina
text: "He has a sailor's heart, an artist's soul and a craftsman's hands. He never lived his dream of sailing the world. His ships do that for him."

speaker: Katrina
text: "Henry has been a very dear friend for years. He is a simple but good man who does not have an ounce of hate in his heart for anyone. I am so fond of him that I gave him a valuable heirloom."

speaker: Katrina
text: "Since he does not have much money, I gave Henry my gold locket so he could present it to his sweetheart Constance. I have not talked to him lately, but I must confess I am worried about him."

speaker: Katrina
text: "Soon after Henry left carrying the locket, I saw the three strangers on the island, wandering off in the same direction."

speaker: Katrina
text: "The three visitors come from Buccaneer's Den. I met them shortly after their arrival and we spoke briefly. Robin is the one dressed like a gambler and the other two, Battles and Leavell, appear to be bullies."

speaker: Katrina
text: "Iolo should be in our party adventuring with us."

speaker: Katrina
text: "How hast thou been keeping thyself all these years, Iolo?"

speaker: Iolo
text: "The years have not been as kind to me as they obviously have been to thee, milady."

speaker: Katrina
text: "Ha! I see thou art still a scallywag, Iolo."

speaker: Katrina
text: "Shamino should be here with us."

speaker: Katrina
text: "Is that a gray hair I see in thine hair, Shamino?"

speaker: Shamino
text: "It is not! Where?"

speaker: Katrina
text: "Perhaps it is but a trick of the light."

speaker: Katrina
text: "I cannot help but miss Dupre a little. I have not seen him since he was knighted."

speaker: Katrina
text: "Sir Dupre, hast thou finished thy studies yet?"

speaker: Dupre
text: Dupre looks confounded. "My studies, milady?"

speaker: Katrina
text: "Of all the various drinking establishments in Britannia!"

speaker: Dupre
text: "Oh, yes, of course, my studies! Continuing mine education has always been of the utmost importance to me."

speaker: Katrina
text: "Pleasant days, <PLAYER_NAME>."

speaker: Tseramed
text: "We need not be concerned about these bees, so long as we have a number of my trusty arrows."

speaker: Tseramed
text: "Greetings, traveller<VAR>."

speaker: Tseramed
text: "I am Tseramed the woodsman. Thou art a <VAR>."

speaker: Tseramed
text: "I am called Tseramed. Art thou Fellowship members? How art thou called?"

speaker: Tseramed
text: "The Avatar! This is a strange chance. Tell me Avatar, by what name art thou called?"

speaker: Tseramed
text: "Well met, <PLAYER_NAME>"

speaker: Tseramed
text: Thy demeanor is noble.

speaker: Tseramed
text: "Perhaps thou couldst introduce me to thy companions?"

speaker: Tseramed
text: "I do not trust The Fellowship, and most especially <VAR>."

speaker: Tseramed
text: "I have no love for The Fellowship. We shall speak of it when I know thee better."

speaker: Tseramed
text: "Yes. Perhaps I am addressing the illustrious <VAR>?"

speaker: Tseramed
text: "Not long ago The Fellowship began to spread its influence throughout Britannia."

speaker: Tseramed
text: "In their early days they attracted many bright and enthusiastic young people, among them my love, Lady M."

speaker: Tseramed
text: A woman so intelligent could not help but rise in their ranks. Her direct superior was <VAR>.

speaker: Tseramed
text: One black evening she fell gravely ill. According to friends of mine, <VAR> forbade her to visit the local healer. By the time I learned of this, she had already passed away.

speaker: Tseramed
text: "She rests now forever in the Yew graveyard, may her sleep be peaceful. I searched the land for <VAR>, but never found my quarry. In fact, it seems that every time I near my prey, they have already vanished! My search shall never be truly over."

speaker: Tseramed
text: "Knave, <VAR> I have not forgotten thy wrong doing, nor the evil crime that followed it."

speaker: Tseramed
text: "Oh soul as black as pitch!"

speaker: Tseramed
text: "Youth is hers forever."

speaker: Tseramed
text: "I travel with thee, <VAR>, to aid thee with my wood craft."

speaker: Tseramed
text: "I am but a humble woodsman. I garner my living from the forest and find knowledge in its depths."

speaker: Tseramed
text: "I have explored all this region."

speaker: Tseramed
text: "As I said, my woodcraft encompasses all this forest, even the caves in the mountain."

speaker: Tseramed
text: "<VAR>"

speaker: Tseramed
text: "The forest is a wild place, but tamed somewhat in recent years. Within, <VAR>, thou mayest still find creatures spoken of only in legend."

speaker: Tseramed
text: "North of my hut is a deep bore-hole into the mountains. Within live bees of a size to rival sheep, or hounds. Their wings stir up leaves as they fly, and they humm with a noise to make men flee in fear."

speaker: Tseramed
text: "Some have entered, never to return. Perhaps they are there still... Death is greedy, and holds a fate for those of like intent."

speaker: Tseramed
text: "Many years have I dwelt by the mountains. Many spans have vanished under my roaming feet. Into the depths of the dark swamp I have gone, and to the heights of the mountains. I know the trees of the forest, and the secret places in the earth."

speaker: Tseramed
text: "North of the mountain spur is a dense swamp. Killing slime [lurk within, guarding a clear spring. All about the water is foul and noisome."

speaker: Tseramed
text: Into thy boots the foul concoction will seep, bringing on nausea and dizziness. The wise traveller wears swamp boots in such places.

speaker: Tseramed
text: "East, North, and West that mire is drained. Through Yew and past the Abbey the westward river flows. The others both bend north into the sea."

speaker: Tseramed
text: "Empath Abbey is its proper name <HONORIFIC>. They practice ancient arts there, the eldest being the fermentation and distillation of spirits. Demand for their products is high in Yew."

speaker: Tseramed
text: "Citizens of a reclusive nature feel at peace there. Within the forest lie its buildings, many so grown-over as to seem a part of the wood."

speaker: Tseramed
text: "East of my dwelling the wood is thick, but a woodcrafty traveller may find the houses there."

speaker: Tseramed
text: "The sea!  Its waves sooth a rough mood, but its fury is unrivaled. Ask those who live upon it! A gift it is, to live by it and reap its natural harvest. I cast in a line when I may."

speaker: Tseramed
text: "Dost thou wonder what mysteries the sea must hold?"

speaker: Tseramed
text: "I also wonder. But the doings of those who travel upon it are more familiar to me. I have seen pirates land upon the northern coast."

speaker: Tseramed
text: "Perhaps thou art not as fond of the sea as I..."

speaker: Tseramed
text: "Perhaps they land to cache their booty in the forest. I have never followed them."

speaker: Tseramed
text: "Vaulting in from the coast looms a narrow spine. Dangerous and sharp rear the crags of those mountains. Caves there hold danger, and death for the unwary."

speaker: Tseramed
text: "Death for the greedy. Death for any who steal from the dwellers in the caves."

speaker: Tseramed
text: "Aye. Such as would devour the unwary and pick bones dry. In the forest are harpies, and slime on the margins of the swamp, and bees in the caves."

speaker: Tseramed
text: "Good game live also in the forest: Foxes and the like."

speaker: Tseramed
text: "Harpies! To battle! Let us slay them at once!"

speaker: Tseramed
text: "A malformed flying horror. Thou wouldst not want to meet one."

speaker: Tseramed
text: "A dangerous organism is the greenish slime. Acidic to touch, it will hurl pseudopods at its prey from three paces."

speaker: Tseramed
text: "Never sleeping, it has no mind and is composed in the main of	poisonous substances. It engulfs and devours hapless animals voraciously."

speaker: Tseramed
text: "Attack it with flame! Slime has no defense against it."

speaker: Tseramed
text: "Cunning is the fox, and shy of humans. We shall never belong to the forest as they do.<VAR>"

speaker: Tseramed
text: "Bees such as these may be tamed with my special arrows!"

speaker: Tseramed
text: "Such bees as thou hast never seen! Large as a wolf they are, with wings stretching over a span in length."

speaker: Tseramed
text: "A creature stung by them will pass into a deep, death-like sleep."

speaker: Tseramed
text: "I have hunted them on many occasions, for I use their poison on my arrows. And I like their honey. Perhaps together we might journey into the cave for some?"

speaker: Tseramed
text: "I fashion my arrows from the stingers of giant bees. With them one may put a foe to sleep."

speaker: Tseramed
text: <VAR>

speaker: Tseramed
text: "Use them with care, for even a scratch may put one to sleep!" he says, handing you <VAR> arrow<VAR>.

speaker: Tseramed
text: "Perhaps when thou art carrying less I can give them to thee."

speaker: Tseramed
text: "Very well, <HONORIFIC>."

speaker: Tseramed
text: "I would be honored, <HONORIFIC>."

speaker: Tseramed
text: "'Twould appear, <HONORIFIC>, that thou already hast more than enough travelling companions."

speaker: Tseramed
text: "Dost thou want me to wait here or should I go home?"

speaker: Tseramed
text: "Very well! I shall wait for thee!"

speaker: Tseramed
text: "Very well, <HONORIFIC>. Fare thee well."

speaker: Tseramed
text: "Speaking of caves and mountains, there are some who dwell near, or perhaps in, the cave of bees. They are hermits."

speaker: Tseramed
text: "One day I glimpsed a man and a woman deep within the cave as I was hunting. Since then I have seen them twice. I believe they are former citizens of Yew, though I do not know how they live in harmony with the bees."

speaker: Tseramed
text: "These are the people I saw!"

speaker: Tseramed
text: "These people are the hermits I spoke of before."

speaker: Tseramed
text: "Perhaps those hermits are still living in the cave."

speaker: Tseramed
text: "This puts me in mind of a story. Wouldst thou like to hear it?"

speaker: Tseramed
text: "One day while walking along the edge of the swamp I happened upon a strange sight. A fox was held at bay on a small hillock in the midst of the swamp, and all about the hillock writhed green slime."

speaker: Tseramed
text: Slowly the slime crept up toward the fox, when suddenly the fox trotted directly across the surface of the ooze!

speaker: Tseramed
text: "Unharmed, the fox dashed off into the wood, leaving the slime writhing behind. By this I guess that the victims of slime are those caught sleeping, or unaware."

speaker: Tseramed
text: "Perhaps another time."

speaker: Tseramed
text: "Thy pardon, <HONORIFIC>, but thy visage brings to my mind a statue that I once saw.  'Twas a likeness of the ancient hero known as the Avatar."

speaker: Tseramed
text: "Art thou not that same honorable soul?"

speaker: Tseramed
text: "Noble hero, it is an honor to make thine aquaintance. <VAR>"

speaker: Tseramed
text: "I must be mistaken. Farewell."

speaker: Tseramed
text: "^<HONORIFIC>, if it pleases thee, I would be honored to travel with thee. I have skill in arms, and I can offer my knowledge and wood craft to thee..."

speaker: Tseramed
text: "'Til next time, <HONORIFIC>."

speaker: Petre
text: The peasant looks at you as if he has seen a ghost! "Iolo! This <VAR> did appear from thin air! Help me!"

speaker: Petre
text: You see a distraught peasant. "Art thou really the Avatar?"

speaker: Petre
text: Petre bows before you. "^<HONORIFIC>."

speaker: Petre
text: Petre looks confused. "Thou shouldst not make fun of me!" He turns away.

speaker: Petre
text: "What is it, <HONORIFIC>?" Petre asks.

speaker: Petre
text: "Look in the stables! 'Tis horrible! I will answer thy questions, but first look in the stables!"

speaker: Petre
text: "I am called Petre," the man sniffs.

speaker: Petre
text: "I am the stables caretaker."

speaker: Petre
text: "I have worked here for years. I can sell thee a nice horse and carriage if thou dost want one. The animal and the carriage are located in a small shelter just outside the north gate of the town."

speaker: Petre
text: "Right now the place gives me the creeps!"

speaker: Petre
text: His eyes are wild with fright.

speaker: Petre
text: "The Mayor did not let me clean in there until twenty-four hours after thou didst leave Trinsic. He thought we had to keep the place of the crime unsullied. Well, if thou dost ask me, I can tell thee that it still stinks like the end of the world in there!"

speaker: Petre
text: "I discovered poor Christopher and Inamo earlier this morning. I did not touch a thing. Made me sick, it did!"

speaker: Petre
text: "Nice man. He made the shoes for mine horses."

speaker: Petre
text: "He worked for very little money. Did basic chores around the stables and the pub. I let him sleep in the little back room. He must have been in the wrong place at the wrong time."

speaker: Petre
text: "The horse and carriage combination sells for 60 gold. Dost thou want a title?"

speaker: Petre
text: "Very good. Nothing like a little business transaction to take my mind off the ghastly scene in the stables."

speaker: Petre
text: "Oh, my. Thine hands are too full to take the title!"

speaker: Petre
text: "Oh. Thou dost not have enough gold to buy the title."

speaker: Petre
text: "Some other time, then."

speaker: Petre
text: "They doth lead out the back way, yes? They must be the tracks of the murderer!"

speaker: Petre
text: His eyes widen a bit more.

speaker: Petre
text: "Or... murderers!"

speaker: Petre
text: "I do not want to join them, but they seem all right."

speaker: Petre
text: "I do not know the man too well. I have no dealings with him."

speaker: Petre
text: "That be Christopher's son. Nice lad."

speaker: Petre
text: Petre ruffles the boy's hair.

speaker: Petre
text: "This here is Christopher's son. He's a good lad, is Spark, when he's not pilfering things from honest shopkeepers."

speaker: Petre
text: "Goodbye," the man sniffs.

speaker: Finnigan
text: "Hast thou properly searched the stables?"

speaker: Finnigan
text: "What didst thou find?"

speaker: Finnigan
text: "Hmmm, a key. Perhaps if thou dost ask Christopher's son about it, he may know what it is for."

speaker: Finnigan
text: "Ask Spark about it. He may know something."

speaker: Finnigan
text: "I know that! What ELSE didst thou find? Thou shouldst look again, Avatar!"

speaker: Finnigan
text: "Yes, obviously it is filled with poor Christopher's own blood. But surely there was something else that might point us in the direction of the killer or killers - thou shouldst look again, Avatar."

speaker: Finnigan
text: "Thou shouldst look again, 'Avatar'!"

speaker: Finnigan
text: "Well, do so, then come speak with me!"

speaker: Finnigan
text: "Hmmm. Hast thou reconsidered mine offer to investigate the murder?"

speaker: Finnigan
text: "Splendid. Then thou must really be the Avatar after all!"

speaker: Finnigan
text: "Then leave our people to work it out for themselves."

speaker: Iolo
text: "Avatar! I am ashamed of thee! Thou shouldst reconsider!"

speaker: Finnigan
text: You see a middle-aged nobleman.

speaker: Finnigan
text: "Iolo! Who is this stranger?"

speaker: Iolo
text: "Why, this is the Avatar!" Iolo proudly proclaims. "Canst thou believe it? May I introduce thee? This is Finnigan, the Town Mayor. And this is <PLAYER_NAME>, the Avatar!"

speaker: Iolo
text: "I simply cannot believe she is here!"

speaker: Iolo
text: "I simply cannot believe he is here!"

speaker: Finnigan
text: The Mayor looks you up and down, not sure if he believes Iolo or not. He looks at Iolo skeptically.

speaker: Iolo
text: "I swear to thee, it is the Avatar!"

speaker: Finnigan
text: "I have heard that thou art the Avatar. I am not certain that I believe it."

speaker: Finnigan
text: The mayor looks at you again as if he were studying every pore on your face. Finally, he smiles.

speaker: Finnigan
text: "Welcome, Avatar."

speaker: Finnigan
text: But just as suddenly, Finnigan's face becomes stern.

speaker: Finnigan
text: "A horrible murder has occurred. If thou art truly the Avatar, perhaps thou canst help us solve it. I would feel better if thou takest this matter into thine hands. Thou shalt be handsomely rewarded if thou dost discover the name of the killer. Dost thou accept?"

speaker: Finnigan
text: "Petre here knows something about all of this."

speaker: Petre
text: The peasant interjects. "I discovered poor Christopher and the Gargoyle Inamo early this morning."

speaker: Finnigan
text: "Petre, the stables caretaker, discovered poor Christopher and Inamo early this morning."

speaker: Finnigan
text: The Mayor continues. "Hast thou searched the stables?"

speaker: Finnigan
text: "Well, thou could not be the real Avatar then!"

speaker: Finnigan
text: "Yes, Avatar?" Finnigan asks.

speaker: Finnigan
text: "My name is Finnigan."

speaker: Finnigan
text: "I am the Mayor of Trinsic and have been since I arrived here three years ago."

speaker: Finnigan
text: "Trinsic was once the city of Honor. I suppose it still is. Our Rune of Honor was taken many years ago <VAR> I believe it now resides in the Royal Museum in Britain, yet the empty pedestal still remains in the center of town. I feel this is symbolic of the town itself. It is rather empty -- of people, of life, and of honor. 'Tis sad, really."

speaker: Finnigan
text: "Then there is this murder, of course. We have temporarily closed the gates of the city and require a password to get in or out."

speaker: Finnigan
text: "Of course, <PLAYER_NAME>. Here is thy gold."

speaker: Finnigan
text: "Oh, I am sorry, <PLAYER_NAME>. Thou still cannot carry this amount. Thou must return to me later."

speaker: Finnigan
text: "Here thou art."

speaker: Finnigan
text: "A crime like this has never happened in Trinsic before. I cannot believe this happened to Christopher and Inamo. Please -- explore the town! I would appreciate it if thou wouldst bring me a report on thy progress. Be sure to ask everyone in town about the murder. After speaking with Christopher's son, thou mightest next want to speak with Gilberto, the guard on watch at the dock last night."

speaker: Finnigan
text: The mayor hesitates, then leans in to speak quietly.

speaker: Finnigan
text: "Actually, I have seen something like this before. It was about four years ago, in Britain."

speaker: Finnigan
text: "I hope thou art progressing on the murder investigation."

speaker: Finnigan
text: "'Twas before I came to Trinsic. There was a murder with strikingly similar aspects. A body was found mutilated exactly like poor Christopher. It appeared to be a ritualistic killing. I would wager that whoever was responsible for that murder is the culprit behind this one."

speaker: Finnigan
text: "Christopher's son is called Spark. Their house is in the northwest area of town."

speaker: Finnigan
text: "He was struck from behind early this morning and was knocked senseless. Johnson, the morning watch, found him unconscious. He is recuperating at Chantu the Healer's house on the west side of town."

speaker: Finnigan
text: "He is our town healer. He hath been here for years. Nice fellow."

speaker: Finnigan
text: "I am satisfied with thy report. Please carry on thine investigation, Avatar."

speaker: Finnigan
text: "Art thou ready to answer some questions concerning the investigation?"

speaker: Finnigan
text: "Oh. Well, carry on with thine investigation."

speaker: Finnigan
text: "Shall we continue thy report?"

speaker: Finnigan
text: "Oh. Well, carry on with thine investigation."

speaker: Finnigan
text: "Why, they are an extremely helpful group. Their branch office is just east of mine. Very optimistic group of people."

speaker: Finnigan
text: "He is the Fellowship branch leader. Kind man."

speaker: Finnigan
text: "He is probably at the dock right now."

speaker: Finnigan
text: "Christopher was the local blacksmith. He lives, or rather -lived-, with his son in the northwest part of town. The blacksmith's shop is in the southwest corner. Christopher was not a rich man by any means -- he barely kept himself and his son alive. But he certainly enjoyed his work."

speaker: Finnigan
text: "The Gargoyle Inamo slept in the stables, as I understand it. I believe he emigrated here from Terfin a few months ago. It seems that he was merely a chance victim of someone intent on violence."

speaker: Finnigan
text: "Oh, dost thou want the password now?"

speaker: Finnigan
text: "Excellent! I have no doubts now that thou art the one true Avatar!"

speaker: Finnigan
text: "Oh-- I almost forgot! The password to leave or enter the town is `Blackbird'!"

speaker: Finnigan
text: "Hmmm. I am afraid that I still have my doubts about thou being the Avatar. My public duty disallows me to give thee the password. I am sorry."

speaker: Finnigan
text: The Mayor shrugs and looks at you as if you were mad.

speaker: Finnigan
text: "I will give thee the password when thou hast given me a report on the progress of thine investigation."

speaker: Finnigan
text: The Mayor nods his head at you and goes on about his business.

speaker: Gilberto
text: You see a grumpy fellow with a bloody bandage on his head.

speaker: Gilberto
text: "Dost thou need something else?" Gilberto asks. You notice his wound is healing nicely.

speaker: Gilberto
text: "I am Gilberto."

speaker: Gilberto
text: "I have the night watch at the dock gate."

speaker: Gilberto
text: "It must have occurred shortly before I was knocked out."

speaker: Gilberto
text: "It was just about sunrise. I was looking out to the sea. All of a sudden, I felt a blow on the back of mine head."

speaker: Gilberto
text: He winces in pain.

speaker: Gilberto
text: Gilberto still seems a little wobbly, but his gesture indicates that he does not desire your aid.

speaker: Gilberto
text: "My skull is still ringing, but I shall be all right momentarily."

speaker: Gilberto
text: "The next thing I knew, I was on the ground. Johnson, the guard for the next watch, was shaking me. I had been out about ten minutes. I knew that because the sun had just peeked over the horizon. And 'The Crown Jewel' had gone and sailed!"

speaker: Gilberto
text: "Did I forget to say? That is a ship that was docked here all night. I believe it was about to sail for Britain. Thou couldst ask Gargan the Shipwright to make sure. Anyway, I did not see mine attackers," the guard grumbles.

speaker: Gilberto
text: "Hmmm. I wonder if they jumped onto the ship! They could be all the way to Britain by now!"

speaker: Gilberto
text: "He is a good man but thou mayest not wish to stand too close to him. Thou mayest catch something."

speaker: Gilberto
text: "If thou dost want a ship, thou must get a deed from the shipwright. Thou must also have the password to leave town."

speaker: Gilberto
text: "What is it?"

speaker: Gilberto
text: "All right. Thou mayest pass."

speaker: Gilberto
text: "Thou mayest not pass."

speaker: Gilberto
text: "Thou dost not know the password. The Mayor can give thee the proper password."

speaker: Gilberto
text: "He takes the morning watch at the dock."

speaker: Gilberto
text: He shrugs.

speaker: Gilberto
text: "Thou art asking the wrong man. I suppose they are all right. I have never had trouble with them."

speaker: Gilberto
text: The guard thinks a moment.

speaker: Gilberto
text: "No. I cannot say that I saw a man with a hook."

speaker: Gilberto
text: "I have not had many dealings with him."

speaker: Gilberto
text: "Goodbye. Watch thy back."

speaker: Johnson
text: "I will speak with thee after the Fellowship meeting."

speaker: Johnson
text: "I must get to the Fellowship meeting! I am late! May we speak tomorrow?"

speaker: Johnson
text: You see an alert and no-nonsense guard.

speaker: Johnson
text: "What is it?" Johnson asks, sternly.

speaker: Johnson
text: "Johnson."

speaker: Johnson
text: "I have the morning watch guarding the dock. I authorize the comings and goings of every ship."

speaker: Johnson
text: "I did hear of this. When I arrived at my post at sunrise, I found Gilberto lying felled on the ground. If thou art asking if I saw anything -- I did not. No one hath passed by me since I arrived at the dock."

speaker: Johnson
text: "The boat left just after sunrise. It did sail to Britain, I believe. Thou canst ask Gargan the Shipwright about that."

speaker: Johnson
text: "Yes, I am a member. Wouldst thou like to join?"

speaker: Johnson
text: "Then thou shouldst go to see Batlin in Britain."

speaker: Johnson
text: "'Tis thy loss."

speaker: Johnson
text: "Good man. He is our branch leader here in Trinsic."

speaker: Johnson
text: "If thou dost want a ship, thou must get a deed from the shipwright. Thou must also have the password to leave town."

speaker: Johnson
text: "What is it?"

speaker: Johnson
text: "Very well, thou mayest pass."

speaker: Johnson
text: "Thou mayest not pass."

speaker: Johnson
text: "Thou dost not know the password. I am sorry. The Mayor may give thee the proper password."

speaker: Johnson
text: "A man with a hook? No, I saw no one all night or all morning."

speaker: Johnson
text: "Thou canst purchase that from Gargan the Shipwright."

speaker: Johnson
text: "Good day."

speaker: Eiko
text: You see a stunningly attractive oriental woman. She is armed to the teeth.

speaker: Eiko
text: "Thou dost wish to speak with me again?" asks Eiko.

speaker: Eiko
text: "My name is Eiko."

speaker: Eiko
text: "I have no job. I have a quest. My quest is shared with mine half-sister, Amanda."

speaker: Eiko
text: "We are leaving this dungeon now that our quest is over."

speaker: Eiko
text: "Eighteen years ago my father was murdered by a cyclops called Iskander Ironheart. Mine half-sister Amanda and I are his only surviving kin and we have vowed to avenge him."

speaker: Eiko
text: "Our father was a mage named Kalideth. He was working to find a cause of the disturbances of the ethereal waves that have been preventing magic from working for the past twenty years and more, as well as the madness that has afflicted all mages since then."

speaker: Amanda
text: "Our father was a wise and kind man. His death was a loss for all of Britannia." She sniffs.

speaker: Amanda
text: "His killer deserves to die."

speaker: Eiko
text: "Neither one of us knew that the other existed until after the death of our father."

speaker: Amanda
text: "I had always felt like I had a sister somewhere. But I attributed those feelings to the natural loneliness a child feels upon losing a father. Learning about each other has been the only good thing that has happened to me since father's death."

speaker: Eiko
text: "Yes, I know I am not pronouncing it correctly. I understand he has a more human nickname that is actually a translation from the ancient cyclops language. But I do not know what it is."

speaker: Eiko
text: You explain to Eiko what you have learned. Kalideth had gone mad when he fought with Iskander and the source of what is causing the problems with magic and the mage's minds was the thing that really killed Kalideth!

speaker: Eiko
text: "Then if thou hast discovered the true force that killed my father, my vengeance against Kalideth would be unjust."

speaker: Amanda
text: "How canst thou say that? I thought that thou wert my sister? Thou art a traitor!"

speaker: Eiko
text: "Farewell."

speaker: Klog
text: This man exudes kindness and geniality. "Ah, Avatar! I recognized thee at once! Word has moved through town quickly. I had heard thou wert here."

speaker: Klog
text: "Hello again, <PLAYER_NAME>," Klog asks. "How may I help thee?"

speaker: Klog
text: "My name is Klog."

speaker: Klog
text: "I am the Trinsic branch leader for The Fellowship. I work here with my wife Ellen."

speaker: Klog
text: The Cube vibrates. "Hook did a splendid job, did he not? Too bad	I missed it. Had to keep up appearances and remain at home.	Had to have an alibi."

speaker: Klog
text: "Well," the man says, reflecting, "I was home all night, and my wife Ellen will certainly verify that. But, as we say in The Fellowship, 'Worthiness Precedes Reward'. Christopher must have done something bad. And the poor gargoyle Inamo! 'Tis a pity."

speaker: Klog
text: "The Fellowship meets here at the branch office in Trinsic every night at nine. Thou art welcome to attend."

speaker: Klog
text: "Why, thou shouldst know all about our little family by now!"

speaker: Klog
text: "She is my wife and bookkeeper for our branch."

speaker: Klog
text: "Christopher was a valued member of The Fellowship for some time. Unfortunately, we got into a petty argument last week."

speaker: Klog
text: "I did not know the gargoyle. It sounds as if he was in the wrong place at the wrong time. 'Tis a pity."

speaker: Klog
text: "Last week Christopher stated that he wanted to leave The Fellowship! Canst thou imagine? Well, we simply attempted to speak with him and alter his decision. The man verbally assaulted me and my companions with no provocation!"

speaker: Klog
text: "Batlin in Britain will be happy to administer our test to thee. Thou shouldst certainly take it. Who knows? Thou mayest find something within thee that needs improving."

speaker: Klog
text: "They have gone to Fellowship Headquarters in Britain. They were here delivering Fellowship funds. Their names are Elizabeth and Abraham."

speaker: Klog
text: The Cube vibrates. "That was payment for delivery of the plans for the Black Gate pedestals."

speaker: Klog
text: "I do not know what thou art talking about."

speaker: Klog
text: "All I know is that it is being built on the Isle of the Avatar."

speaker: Klog
text: "Christopher had expressed interest in leaving The Fellowship. Perhaps he had stored it for safekeeping."

speaker: Klog
text: The Cube vibrates. "Christopher received his reward prior to showing his worthiness. He reneged on delivery of	the plans for the pedestal. It was merely a warning."

speaker: Klog
text: "I do not know anything about that."

speaker: Klog
text: The Cube vibrates. "That is Hook's ship."

speaker: Klog
text: "I do not know that ship."

speaker: Klog
text: The Cube vibrates. "He is the one who was assigned to kill Christopher. I do not know where he is now."

speaker: Klog
text: "I am afraid I do not know a man of that description."

speaker: Klog
text: "If there is anything else I may help thee with, <PLAYER_NAME>, let me know."

speaker: Chantu
text: You see a solemn fellow in healer's robes.

speaker: Chantu
text: "Hello, again," Chantu says. "How may I help thee?"

speaker: Chantu
text: "My name is Chantu," he says with a slight bow.

speaker: Chantu
text: "I am the Trinsic healer. I can perform a heal, a poison cure, or a resurrection on any of thy friends. Or on thee, of course."

speaker: Chantu
text: "'Tis a sad state for Britannia when events such as these happen. Christopher was a good man. I hope that the villain is caught."

speaker: Chantu
text: The healer frowns. "The Fellowship does not appreciate the efforts of healers in Britannia. Although they do admirable things, The Fellowship is short-sighted when evaluating the need for healers. They believe that our work can be done through their so-called 'Triad of Inner Strength'."

speaker: Chantu
text: Chantu notices your medallion and his eyes widen.

speaker: Chantu
text: "Excuse me, <HONORIFIC>, I did not mean to offend thee."

speaker: Chantu
text: The healer shrugs. "He does his duty as he sees fit. And I do mine."

speaker: Chantu
text: "Goodbye."

speaker: Dell
text: Dell frowns at you for distracting him during the Fellowship meeting.

speaker: Dell
text: "I do not have time to talk with thee! I must get to the meeting of The Fellowship! Come to my shop tomorrow!"

speaker: Dell
text: You see a stern shopkeeper who might once have been a strong fighter.

speaker: Dell
text: "Thou hast entered my shop, so thou had best buy something."

speaker: Dell
text: "Who might I be addressing?"

speaker: Dell
text: "Hmph. My name is Dell."

speaker: Dell
text: "Oh, art thou really? I did not know there were so many of thee! Why, only last week did an 'Avatar' come through here! He took me for 20 gold, too! An expert trickster, he was!"

speaker: Dell
text: Dell looks you up and down. "Avatar, indeed! I do not like Avatars. But never mind that. I am called Dell. What dost thou want?"

speaker: Dell
text: "How may I help thee?" Dell asks.

speaker: Dell
text: "My name is Dell. Did I not say that already?"

speaker: Dell
text: Dell looks disgruntled. "I sell weapons, armour, and provisions when I am not doing work for The Fellowship."

speaker: Dell
text: "If thou art not going to buy anything, then get thy face out of my sight!"

speaker: Dell
text: "I am afraid I know nothing about it save for what is being said in the street, so do not ask me. If thou art not going to buy anything, then thou art wasting my time. Go away."

speaker: Iolo
text: Iolo whispers to you, "Pleasant chap, is he not?"

speaker: Dell
text: "Certainly, <HONORIFIC>. What type of ware wouldst thou wish to see?"

speaker: Dell
text: "Come to my shop during business hours."

speaker: Dell
text: "Hmpf."

speaker: Dell
text: "Spend more money next time thou dost come in."

speaker: Apollonia
text: You see a gorgeous and voluptuous woman in her thirties.

speaker: Apollonia
text: "Hello again!" Apollonia says, her eyes twinkling.

speaker: Apollonia
text: "My name is Apollonia," she says, <VAR>

speaker: Apollonia
text: "Why, I run the Honorable Hound Pub and Inn," she purrs.

speaker: Apollonia
text: "Wouldst thou like a room? Or wouldst thou like something to eat or drink? Just say so and I shall try and please thee with my delicacies."

speaker: Apollonia
text: You realize she is flirting with you.

speaker: Apollonia
text: "I shall be happy to serve thee during business hours!"

speaker: Apollonia
text: "I can think of no better place in all of Trinsic to lay thine head to rest or to nibble upon treats to satisfy thine appetite."

speaker: Apollonia
text: Apollonia shuts her eyes and shakes her head as if she had just bitten into a very sour lemon. "Oooh. That was so... hideous! How could anyone do something so horrible? Art thou searching for information? I do hope thou dost find the person responsible."

speaker: Apollonia
text: "We serve the finest meat, fish, and cake. Our specialty is a Silverleaf meal. If thou wouldst like to buy something, please say so!"

speaker: Apollonia
text: "I can offer thee mead, wine and ale."

speaker: Apollonia
text: "Our rooms are cheap. Only 6 gold per person per night. Want a room?"

speaker: Apollonia
text: "Oh dear. Thou art carrying too much to take the room key."

speaker: Apollonia
text: "Here is thy room key. It is good only until thou dost leave."

speaker: Apollonia
text: "Thou dost not have enough gold, <HONORIFIC>."

speaker: Apollonia
text: "Some other night, then."

speaker: Apollonia
text: "Mmmm. What a delicacy! It is the most wonderful delicacy that thou shalt ever eat! It is worth every gold piece spent."

speaker: Apollonia
text: Apollonia blushes and bats her eyelashes. "Oh, <PLAYER_NAME>! I would wager that thou dost say that to all the barmaids!"

speaker: Apollonia
text: Apollonia blows a kiss at you. "Do come again!"

speaker: Apollonia
text: Apollonia waves at you. "Do come again!"

speaker: Markus
text: You see a solid-looking but seemingly bored fighter.

speaker: Markus
text: "Yes?" Markus asks.

speaker: Markus
text: "I am Markus the trainer."

speaker: Markus
text: "I am a trainer here in Trinsic," he says gruffly. "If thou dost wish to increase thy skill in combat I can help thee."

speaker: Markus
text: "I heard about it, but I assure thee I know nothing of the details." Markus yawns.

speaker: Markus
text: The fighter shrugs. "The town is all right." He sniffs.

speaker: Markus
text: "The cost to train with me is 20 gold. Too costly, right?"

speaker: Markus
text: Markus yawns. "Very well."

speaker: Markus
text: "Please come to my place of business during normal daylight hours."

speaker: Markus
text: "Goodbye," the fighter bows.

speaker: Gargan
text: You see a salty old sailor who reeks of tobacco.

speaker: Gargan
text: "Yes, matey?" Gargan asks, coughing.

speaker: Gargan
text: "My name is Gargan."

speaker: Gargan
text: He sniffs loudly.

speaker: Gargan
text: "I am the Trinsic shipwright. If thou wouldst like to know about a ship or a sextant, just say so."

speaker: Gargan
text: Gargan coughs.

speaker: Gargan
text: "Thou dost want to buy a ship?" the old man asks, smiling. (Apparently not too many folks buy ships these days.)

speaker: Gargan
text: "My ships are sturdy and well built. They may not be built by Owen, but they are fine vessels! But thou must first purchase a deed."

speaker: Gargan
text: Gargan wipes his runny nose on his sleeve.

speaker: Gargan
text: "Well, ye'll have to come to the shop when it is is open."

speaker: Gargan
text: "I sell sextants for 80 gold. Want one?"

speaker: Gargan
text: Gargan clears his throat.

speaker: Gargan
text: "Here ye are!"

speaker: Gargan
text: "Thine arms are too full to carry the sextant!"

speaker: Gargan
text: Gargan sneezes.

speaker: Gargan
text: "Thou dost not have enough gold, sailor."

speaker: Gargan
text: Gargan sneezes.

speaker: Gargan
text: "Suit thyself."

speaker: Gargan
text: Gargan sneezes.

speaker: Gargan
text: "Thou hast not heard of Owen? Finest shipwright in the land. He lives in Minoc."

speaker: Gargan
text: Gargan coughs.

speaker: Gargan
text: "Well, ye'll have to come to the shop when it is open."

speaker: Gargan
text: "I already sold thee the deed to 'The Scaly Eel'! It was the only ship I had!"

speaker: Gargan
text: Gargan coughs loudly.

speaker: Gargan
text: "The deed I can sell thee is for the ship 'The Scaly Eel.' It goes for 600 gold. Interested?"

speaker: Gargan
text: "All right, then!" the sailor replies. He hands you the deed and takes your gold.

speaker: Gargan
text: Gargan sneezes.

speaker: Gargan
text: "Thou'rt already carrying enough to sink a galleon, <HONORIFIC>! If thou wilt leave something behind, mayhaps thou wilt be able to sail, and I will be glad, indeed, to sell thee the deed."

speaker: Gargan
text: Gargan sneezes.

speaker: Gargan
text: "Sorry, matey," Gargan says. "Thou dost not have enough gold!"

speaker: Gargan
text: Gargan sneezes.

speaker: Gargan
text: "Some other time, then," the sailor shrugs, disappointed.

speaker: Gargan
text: Gargan sneezes.

speaker: Gargan
text: "I heard about that. Terrible thing to happen. Can't say I saw or heard anything, though."

speaker: Gargan
text: Gargan coughs, clears his throat loudly, then spits.

speaker: Spark
text: "Ooooh, yuck!"

speaker: Gargan
text: "Yes, that ship was docked overnight." He consults his log. "She sailed for Britain at sunrise. I do not recall seeing anyone get on or off."

speaker: Gargan
text: Gargan snorts and coughs a couple of times.

speaker: Gargan
text: "Matey, I have always seen pirates and sailors with peglegs and hooks. If thou hast seen one, thou hast seen another." But the man suddenly frowns. "Hmm. Now that thou dost mention it, I -did- see a man with a hook late last night after sundown. I was leaving the shop and saw him outside. There was a wingless gargoyle with him. They were walking east."

speaker: Gargan
text: Gargan sneezes, then coughs a couple of times.

speaker: Spark
text: "I told thee! It was him!"

speaker: Gargan
text: "I am too old to pay attention to them."

speaker: Gargan
text: Gargan wipes his runny nose on his sleeve.

speaker: Gargan
text: "May thy day have smooth sailing," the sailor starts to say, but a coughing spasm interrupts him.

speaker: Caroline
text: Caroline asks you to keep your voice down. The Fellowship meeting is in progress.

speaker: Caroline
text: "Oh! I cannot stop to speak with thee now! I am late for the Fellowship meeting!"

speaker: Caroline
text: You see a young woman with a bright smile.

speaker: Caroline
text: "Hello again!" Caroline says brightly.

speaker: Caroline
text: "My parents named me Caroline," she says proudly.

speaker: Caroline
text: "I have no 'job' per se. I have devoted mine energies to helping The Fellowship. I hope to recruit new members."

speaker: Caroline
text: She looks concerned. "'Tis awful! Christopher was a nice man. Didst thou know he was one of our members? I cannot believe he is dead..."

speaker: Caroline
text: "Of The Fellowship. We meet every night at the hall. Thou shouldst visit!"

speaker: Caroline
text: "Every night at nine o'clock we have a meeting in the Fellowship hall. Thou mayest consider thyself invited to attend."

speaker: Caroline
text: "Goodbye!"

speaker: Lord British
text: "Fool!! What possessed thee to cast that damned Armageddon Spell? I knew it was dangerous! Thou didst know it was dangerous!! Now look at us! We are all alone on the entire planet! Britannia is ruined! What kind of Avatar art thou!?! Now, with no Moongates working, we are both forced to spend eternity in this blasted wasteland!"

speaker: Lord British
text: "Of course, it could be viewed as a clever solution to all of our problems. After all, not even this so-called Guardian would want Britannia now!"

speaker: Lord British
text: "I felt the passing of the remains of Exodus from this realm. It has lifted a great weight from my shoulders. And so Avatar, I cannot let this accomplishment go unrewarded. Please kneel, my friend." Lord British holds out his hands as you obey his command.

speaker: Lord British
text: You see your old friend Lord British, looking a bit older than when you last saw him. His eyes gleam at the sight of you.

speaker: Lord British
text: "Welcome, my friend," he says, embracing you. "Please. Tell me what brings thee to Britannia! Or, more importantly, what 'brought' thee here?"

speaker: Lord British
text: "Yes, <PLAYER_NAME>?" Lord British asks.

speaker: Lord British
text: Lord British laughs. "What, art thou joking, Avatar? Dost thou not recognize thine old friend?"

speaker: Lord British
text: Lord British rolls his eyes. "Must we go through this formality?" He laughs, shaking his head.

speaker: Lord British
text: "Very well. As thou well knowest, I am sovereign of Britannia and have been for some time now. Even though I come from thine homeland, I have chosen to live my life here."

speaker: Lord British
text: "I know that it has been many a year since I visited our Earth, but surely thou dost remember that the two of us hail from the same time and place? And, as brothers in origin, thou shouldst also remember that thou canst ask me for aid at any time thou mightest require it."

speaker: Lord British
text: "Do not forget, Avatar, that I have the power to heal thee. That is one bit of magic that still seems to work for me. And I could probably provide thee with some equipment and a spellbook."

speaker: Lord British
text: "The state of the land could not be more prosperous. Dost thou realize that thou hast been away for 200 Britannian years?" Lord British wags a finger at you.

speaker: Lord British
text: "I am certain that thy friends have rued thine absence. 'Tis a shame thou didst stay away so long! But... I am so very happy to see thee. Britannia is prosperous and abundant. Look around thee. Explore the newly refurbished castle. Travel the land. Peace is prominent in all quarters."

speaker: Lord British
text: "Yes, Britannia has never been better. Well, almost never."

speaker: Lord British
text: "Well, 'things' are indeed fine. It is the 'people' I am concerned about."

speaker: Lord British
text: "There is something wrong in Britannia, but I do not know what it is. Something is hanging over the heads of the Britannian people. They are unhappy. One can see it in their eyes. There is nothing that is unifying the population, since there has been peace for so long."

speaker: Lord British
text: "Perhaps thou couldst determine what is happening. I implore thee to go out amongst the people. Watch them in their daily tasks. Speak with them. Work with them. Break bread with them. Perhaps they need someone like the Avatar to take an interest in their lives."

speaker: Lord British
text: You relate the story of how a red Moongate appeared behind your house and mysteriously took you to Trinsic.

speaker: Lord British
text: Lord British's brow creases as you speak. Finally he says, "I did not send the red Moongate to fetch thee. Someone or something must have activated that Moongate. And that is strange indeed, because we have been having a bit of trouble with Moongates as of late. In fact, we have been having trouble with magic in general!"

speaker: Lord British
text: "Mine has not worked since the troubles with magic began. In fact, none of the Moongates have been working reliably for quite a while!"

speaker: Lord British
text: "Didst thou bring thine Orb of the Moons?"

speaker: Lord British
text: "Really? Where is it? Thou dost not have it on thee! "

speaker: Lord British
text: "I see. "

speaker: Lord British
text: "Hmmm. Thou might be stranded in Britannia. Here. Why not try mine? I shall let thee borrow it. Perhaps it will work for thee. Be careful, though. The Moongates have become dangerous."

speaker: Lord British
text: Lord British hands you his Orb of the Moons.

speaker: Lord British
text: "Thine hands are too full to take the Orb!"

speaker: Lord British
text: "Yes, it has been redecorated since thy last visit. The architects and workers did a splendid job."

speaker: Lord British
text: The ruler leans toward you with a sour look on his face.

speaker: Lord British
text: "The only mar in the entire complex is that damn nursery!"

speaker: Lord British
text: "I will not go near the place! Kings and dirty diapers do not mix. The Great Council talked me into implementing the nursery after several of my staff started having families. Although it was probably a necessity, I shall pretend it does not exist!"

speaker: Lord British
text: "I have not been down there in many years. Has something happened there?"

speaker: Lord British
text: "Indeed. Then it seems that Trinsic has not changed much since I saw it last." His eyes twinkle.

speaker: Lord British
text: "Murder? In Trinsic?" The ruler looks concerned.

speaker: Lord British
text: "I have heard nothing about it. Art thou investigating it?"

speaker: Lord British
text: "Very good. It pleases me that thou art concerned about my people."

speaker: Lord British
text: "Ah, but perhaps thou shouldst!"

speaker: Lord British
text: The king pauses a moment. "Now that thou dost mention it, I have had reports of other similar murders in the past few months. In fact, there was one here in Britain three or four years ago. The body was mutilated in a ritualistic fashion. Apparently there is a maddened killer on the loose. But I have no doubt that someone such as thee, Avatar, can find him!"

speaker: Lord British
text: "I do not recall many details. Thou shouldst ask Patterson, the town mayor, about it. He may remember more."

speaker: Lord British
text: "That is, of course, only an assumption on my part. But that is all we have had to work with. Unless thou hast already uncovered some useful information?"

speaker: Lord British
text: "They are an extremely useful and productive group of citizens. Thou shouldst most certainly visit the Fellowship Headquarters here in Britain and speak with Batlin. The Fellowship has done many good deeds throughout Britannia, including feeding the poor, educating and helping those in need, and promoting general good will and peace."

speaker: Lord British
text: "Yes, it is not far from the castle, to the southwest. It is just south of the theatre."

speaker: Lord British
text: "He is a druid who began The Fellowship about twenty years ago. He is highly intelligent, and is a warm and gentle human being."

speaker: Lord British
text: "A man with a hook?" The king rubs his chin.

speaker: Lord British
text: "No, I do not recall ever meeting a man with a hook."

speaker: Lord British
text: "I am afraid I cannot possibly know of every ship that comes through our ports. Thou shouldst check with Clint the Shipwright if thou hast not done so."

speaker: Lord British
text: "Thou must mean Iolo, Shamino, and Dupre, of course."

speaker: Lord British
text: "I have seen our friend rarely over the years. I understand he has been spending most of his time in Trinsic."

speaker: Lord British
text: "Hello, Iolo! How art thou?"

speaker: Iolo
text: "I am well, my liege! 'Tis good to see thee!"

speaker: Lord British
text: "That rascal does not come around very often, though I understand he spends most of his time in Britain these days!"

speaker: Lord British
text: "What dost thou have to say for thyself, Shamino?"

speaker: Shamino
text: "Mine apologies, milord," Shamino says.

speaker: Lord British
text: "What's this I hear of a woman? An actress? Hmmmm?"

speaker: Shamino
text: Shamino blushes and shuffles his feet.

speaker: Lord British
text: "I suspected as much!" the ruler says, laughing.

speaker: Lord British
text: "I have not seen that one since I knighted him. Typical -- I do the man a favor and he disappears! I heard he might be in Jhelom."

speaker: Lord British
text: "Where hast thou been, Sir Dupre?"

speaker: Dupre
text: "Oh, here and there, milord," the fighter replies.

speaker: Lord British
text: "I have very few friends from our homeland here in Britannia. Thou must make a point to visit more often! Especially since thou art a knight!"

speaker: Dupre
text: "If thou dost wish it, milord," Dupre says, bowing.

speaker: Lord British
text: "A rather violent place, by all accounts. I have not had the pleasure of a visit in quite a while."

speaker: Lord British
text: "Something is awry. Magic has not been working for the longest time. I even have trouble creating food with magic! It must be something to do with the magical ether."

speaker: Lord British
text: "There are those who say that magic is dying, what with the trouble with the Moongates and the situation with Nystul. I am beginning to suspect that they might be right!"

speaker: Lord British
text: Lord British studies you a moment.

speaker: Lord British
text: "Perhaps magic will work much better for thee. Thou hast not been in Britannia long. It is possible that whatever has affected magic has not made its mark upon thee yet. Please try it. A spellbook is stored with the rest of thine equipment."

speaker: Lord British
text: "Er... try talking to him."

speaker: Lord British
text: The king lowers his voice.

speaker: Lord British
text: "He is acting oddly, isn't he? Something has happened to his mind. He doesn't seem to be able to concentrate on magic anymore."

speaker: Lord British
text: "He is beginning to act much more normally."

speaker: Lord British
text: "The Moongates are not functioning! We cannot use them as we have in the past. Not only are they dysfunctional, they are, in fact, dangerous! One of my trusted sages used mine own Orb of the Moons to travel to the Shrine of Humility, and his body did shatter upon entering the gate! If only that mage in Cove hadn't gone mad!"

speaker: Lord British
text: The ruler leans forward and speaks quietly.

speaker: Lord British
text: "There is a mad mage in Cove by the name of Rudyom. Dost thou remember him? Rudyom was working with a magical substance called 'blackrock'. Before he went mad, he claimed that this mineral could solve the problems of the Moongates. I suggest that thou shouldst go to Cove and find him. Try to learn what it was he was doing with this blackrock material. It could be our only hope."

speaker: Lord British
text: "He was a brilliant and respected mage. But something happened to him in recent years. He seemed to go completely senile."

speaker: Lord British
text: Suddenly, something jars Lord British's memory. "I wonder if there is a connection with what happened to Rudyom and what has befallen Nystul!"

speaker: Lord British
text: "Surely thou dost remember Cove. It is a very pleasant town to the east of Britain. Quite relaxing."

speaker: Lord British
text: "I do not know of a 'Guardian'. Art thou sure he really exists? Thou shouldst investigate further."

speaker: Lord British
text: "Yes, I have a spellbook stored away with the rest of the equipment."

speaker: Lord British
text: "Thou art welcome to any of mine equipment. I keep it in a locked storeroom here in the castle. Thou wilt find the key in my study."

speaker: Lord British
text: "I am sure thou canst find it."

speaker: Lord British
text: The ruler smiles slyly. "Consider it something of a game!"

speaker: Lord British
text: "'Tis in the western end of the castle."

speaker: Lord British
text: Lord British listens to your story about Weston. He looks concerned.

speaker: Lord British
text: "I do not recall this case. Let me check... Hmmm..." He quickly scans a large scroll.

speaker: Lord British
text: "Imprisoned for the theft of one apple from the Royal Orchards... Ludicrous! Someone must have usurped mine authority. Thou mayest consider this man pardoned. An investigation will commence immediately into the circumstances surrounding his arrest, and into this fellow, Figg. My thanks to thee, Avatar."

speaker: Lord British
text: Lord British looks at you gravely, "The foundation of Britannia was shaken with the rising of an island. This event was no random disaster, it was one of sorcerous intent."

speaker: Lord British
text: "Yes, <PLAYER_NAME>. I felt a great disturbance in the ether when this island arose from the sea. The island is none other than the Isle of Fire where thou defeated the Hellspawn Exodus."

speaker: Lord British
text: "<PLAYER_NAME>, thou shouldst know that when I created the shrines of the Virtues, I also set upon this island three great shrines, dedicated to the Priciples of Truth, Love, and Courage."

speaker: Lord British
text: They reside within the walls of the Castle of Fire. I never revealed this to thee before as I thought them forever lost when the Isle of Fire mysteriously sank beneath the waves.

speaker: Lord British
text: The shrines are meant for the use of an Avatar only, and therefore a talisman will be necessary to use one.

speaker: Lord British
text: "The talismans are guarded by tests that thou shouldst have no problem passing if thou wishest to seek thier counsel."

speaker: Lord British
text: "Thy battle with that strange mixture of machine and spirit is now legendary. Do be careful if thou art going to the isle, for the remains of that being now reside in one of the chambers of the Castle of Fire."

speaker: Lord British
text: "Goodbye, <PLAYER_NAME>. Do come back soon."

speaker: Lord British
text: "I congratulate and thank thee, <PLAYER_NAME>. Thy deeds continue to speak well of thee."

speaker: Nystul
text: You see your old friend Nystul, now a decrepit old man in mage's robes. He seems lost in thought, far away.

speaker: Nystul
text: "Do I know thee?" Nystul asks.

speaker: Nystul
text: "Yes, Avatar?" Nystul asks.

speaker: Nystul
text: The mage looks confused a moment. "My name is Nystul? Yes, that is it!"

speaker: Nystul
text: "Why, 'tis Nystul!"

speaker: Nystul
text: "Well, I used to perform quite a bit of magic," he says apologetically. "At least... I -think- I used to do so. There is a man named Lord British, I think. I work for him."

speaker: Nystul
text: "I am Lord British's personal mage!"

speaker: Nystul
text: "Sometimes the magic works, sometimes it doth not." He waves his hand, and drops his wand. "Oops!" he cries, as he bends to pick it up.

speaker: Spark
text: "Art thou sure this man is not really the jester?"

speaker: Nystul
text: "Anyway, as I was saying, uhm, what was I saying? Oh yes. Magic. I can still sell thee some spells or reagents if thou wouldst like."

speaker: Nystul
text: "The magic is much better now. My spells all work very nicely. I thank thee, Avatar, for clearing the ether. Interested in any spells or reagents?"

speaker: Nystul
text: "Dost thou wish to buy some spells?"

speaker: Nystul
text: "Oh. Never mind, then."

speaker: Nystul
text: "Dost thou wish to buy some reagents?"

speaker: Nystul
text: "Oh. Never mind, then."

speaker: Nystul
text: "Lord who? Dost thou mean that old man who sometimes sits on the throne?"

speaker: Nystul
text: "He is the greatest ruler this land has ever known and I am proud to serve him."

speaker: Nystul
text: "Are we going somewhere?"

speaker: Nystul
text: "Goodbye, Avatar. Do come see us again soon."

speaker: Chuckles
text: You are wary of conversing with that trickster Chuckles, but decide to anyway.

speaker: Chuckles
text: "I will speak if thou dost play The Game, friend," Chuckles says.

speaker: Chuckles
text: "I must not say my name, lest I break the rule of The Game!"

speaker: Chuckles
text: "I was, am, and shall be the Court...Fool! I could give thee a clue if I wish, but for now my job is to play The Game."

speaker: Chuckles
text: "Art thou sure thou canst play The Game?"

speaker: Chuckles
text: "Thou must play The Game to get the clue!"

speaker: Chuckles
text: "Oops. I did give thee one!"

speaker: Chuckles
text: "Thou must play The Game if thou dost want to speak with me."

speaker: Chuckles
text: "Thou must just learn The Game and then jump in and play it!"

speaker: Chuckles
text: "Then just play it!"

speaker: Chuckles
text: "Of what thou wouldst like."

speaker: Chuckles
text: "Why dost thou want to speak of me? Canst thou not think of a thing much more fun of which to speak?"

speaker: Chuckles
text: "I do not think I can tell a good joke whilst I play The Game! 'Twould be hard! Hmm. Ah! I have one! Why did the hen cross the road? To get to the side she was not on!"

speaker: Chuckles
text: "There be a lot of fine girls in our fair town! Or is it 'fair girls in our fine town'?" Chuckles shrugs his shoulders.

speaker: Chuckles
text: "There is good food at the pub! As for me, I like to eat on the floor of my room!"

speaker: Chuckles
text: "Thou canst get a good meal there! But I could give thee a good -clue-!"

speaker: Chuckles
text: "So long, my friend! Do not forg... I mean, do not lose how to play The Game!"

speaker: Chuckles
text: "Bye for now!"

speaker: Batlin
text: Batlin's eyes narrow to red slits as he peers practically through you.

speaker: Batlin
text: "Thou hast the Cube! Thou cannot use it against -me-!"

speaker: Batlin
text: With that, Batlin turns with a flourish, and vanishes before your eyes!

speaker: Batlin
text: Batlin looks at you and his gaze returns to the Armageddon winter storm. "Many years ago, Avatar, I went to Skara Brae, the ghost city. The way the world is now reminds me of that dead place. In Skara Brae I had a spiritual experience so profound that I have never spoken of to another soul. I would like to share that experience with thee now, Avatar."

speaker: Batlin
text: "There at Skara Brae I saw a man who was called The Tortured One. I asked this dead man, pray tell, what is the answer to the question of Life and Death? He gave me no reply, and I asked him again. I beseeched him to impart some small parcel of wisdom upon me. What is the answer to the question of Life and Death?! He said nothing, but in his eyes... In his eyes I could see, Avatar, that he could not answer me for there was no answer to give. No answers to the question of Life and Death! It was then I understood. No meanings! No virtues! No values!!!... I commend thee, Avatar, for reaching that same liberating illumination!"

speaker: Batlin
text: "Art thou ready to answer questions from the Book of Fellowship?"

speaker: Batlin
text: "Excellent, Avatar!"

speaker: Batlin
text: Fighting a tremble of hesitation you take a long deep drink from the goblet. Batlin steps up to you. "May the news spread far and wide that our newest member is none other than the Avatar!"

speaker: Batlin
text: The other Fellowship members cheer with pleasure.

speaker: Batlin
text: "Very good, Avatar."

speaker: Batlin
text: "Allow me to present thee with thy Fellowship medallion." Batlin gives you the medallion. "Please -- wear thy medallion at all times for it shall be a symbol to all who see it that thou dost walk with the Fellowship. Ready it to thy neck immediately! Oh, and... welcome to The Fellowship, Avatar."

speaker: Batlin
text: "Thou art too encumbered to receive thy Fellowship medallion. Thou must lighten thy load."

speaker: Batlin
text: "My dear Avatar. Thou must realize that thou must know everything there is to know about The Fellowship before I can induct thee. Please study thy Book of Fellowship and return to me."

speaker: Batlin
text: "Your mind seems unclear. I would not be surprised if thou dost not understand	another soul with whom thou dost speak."

speaker: Batlin
text: "Come back when thou art ready."

speaker: Batlin
text: You see a rotund older gentleman, who is at once humble yet dignified. His gentle eyes exude caring for his fellow person.

speaker: Batlin
text: The man's eyes focus on the Fellowship medallion around your neck.

speaker: Batlin
text: "My dear friend, thou art falsely impersonating a Fellowship member! Remove that medallion at once!"

speaker: Batlin
text: "I shall not speak to thee unless thou dost remove that Fellowship medallion. Thou art falsely impersonating a Fellowship member!"

speaker: Batlin
text: "<PLAYER_NAME>, my dear, dear friend! How wonderful to see thee again!" says Batlin.

speaker: Batlin
text: "My name, good friend, is Batlin. And indeed it is truly a privilege to meet the Avatar in the flesh."

speaker: Batlin
text: "I was once a druid. Now I am the leader and the originator of The Fellowship. It is rapidly growing throughout Britannia and keeps me very busy, as thou canst well imagine. Ha! Ha! Ha!"

speaker: Batlin
text: "The Fellowship was formed twenty years ago with the full approval and support of Lord British. It is a society of spiritual seekers who strive to reach the highest levels of human potential and to share this knowledge freely with all people."

speaker: Batlin
text: "The Fellowship advances the philosophy of sanguine cognition, a way to apply a positive order of thought to one's life through what is called the Triad of Inner Strength."

speaker: Batlin
text: "We strive to avoid the mistakes made by mystics and sages since the dawn of time. They apply the standards of the past, such as the virtues, for example, to qualify the present, and thus they do not perceive it correctly. We seek to examine our present lives each on our own terms and see the world the way it is."

speaker: Batlin
text: "They are perfectly adequate for those who feel that they still need them for whatever reason. But no one, not even thyself, thou must admit, Avatar, can fulfill them perfectly. Therefore they are a philosophy that is ultimately based upon failure. We have never claimed that our teachings are a substitute for the virtues. However, ours is a belief that is based upon success, not failure."

speaker: Batlin
text: "The Triad of Inner Strength is simply three basic values that, when applied in unison, enable one to be more creative, satisfied and successful in life."

speaker: Batlin
text: "The three values of the Triad of Inner Strength are Strive For Unity, Trust Thy Brother and Worthiness Precedes Reward."

speaker: Batlin
text: "When we say Strive For Unity, it is simply our way of expressing how the people of Britannia should all cooperate and work together. A worthwhile sentiment, I am certain thou wouldst concur."

speaker: Batlin
text: "What The Fellowship means by this is that people are all the same and the world is, generally speaking, a supportive, nurturing place. The trust we place in each other is like the pinions that hold our society together. Quite true, wouldst thou not say?"

speaker: Batlin
text: "Allow me to explain the meaning of Worthiness Precedes Reward. Each one of us seeks something which we desire from life and we must strive to be worthy of that which we seek. It would be difficult for thee to disagree I am quite sure."

speaker: Batlin
text: "Ah, my good colleagues Elizabeth and Abraham were just here. They left this morning for Minoc on Fellowship business. They deal with the distribution and collection of funds."

speaker: Batlin
text: "I have not seen my colleagues since they were last here. They are busy folk."

speaker: Batlin
text: "I have not seen my colleagues since they were last here. They are busy folk."

speaker: Batlin
text: Batlin smiles and shakes his head. "Thou art not having much luck tracking them down, art thou? They were here, having done some work in Jhelom, but now they have gone to Vesper to see about starting a branch there."

speaker: Batlin
text: "I have not seen my colleagues since they were last here. They are busy folk."

speaker: Batlin
text: "But thou art already a member, Avatar! One can only join once!"

speaker: Batlin
text: "Thou hast not completed thy tasks. Remember that Worthiness Precedes Reward. Once thou hast completed the missions, thou mayest join."

speaker: Batlin
text: "Ah! I do hope thine hands are not too full to take the package."

speaker: Batlin
text: "Excellent! Here it is. Thou must now be on thy way!"

speaker: Batlin
text: "Avatar! I am tired of this! Please make room in thine inventory for the package!"

speaker: Batlin
text: "Congratulations, Avatar, and our thanks to thee for successfully delivering our package to Elynor of Minoc. Now we have another task at hand before thou canst join The Fellowship. Because thou didst deliver the package thou hast proven thyself worthy of performing another mission."

speaker: Batlin
text: "Avatar, didst thou deliver the package to Elynor of Minoc?"

speaker: Batlin
text: "Didst thou open the package?"

speaker: Batlin
text: "Thou knew that thou wast instructed not to open it. We put trust in thee to carry out our instructions to the letter and that trust was broken."

speaker: Batlin
text: "That is not what Elynor of Minoc tells us. We put trust in thee to carry out our instructions to the letter and that trust was broken."

speaker: Batlin
text: "I understand that the contents of the package were missing as well, and this is very serious indeed!"

speaker: Batlin
text: "I am afraid that thou must carry out a mission for us as a test of trust if thou art to begin truly walking with The Fellowship."

speaker: Batlin
text: Batlin's eyes open wide in surprise.

speaker: Batlin
text: "What has happened? Hast thou lost the package?"

speaker: Batlin
text: "Tsk. Tsk. Tsk. That is most unfortunate. We put trust in thee to deliver the package and that trust was broken. I am afraid that thou must carry out a mission for us as a test of trust if thou art to begin truly walking with The Fellowship."

speaker: Batlin
text: "Please deliver our package, Avatar. We have more business to discuss once thou art finished."

speaker: Batlin
text: "Thou shalt visit the dungeon of Destard, which is in the mountains just west of Trinsic. Do not worry, it is completely deserted. There thou shalt find a chest of Fellowship funds which was hidden for safekeeping just a few days ago. Thou wilt know the chest because it will contain not only gold but two Fellowship medallions. The site is also most likely marked with a Fellowship staff. Bring these funds back to us without losing a single coin and thou wilt have successfully completed thy mission. No need to bring the chest, just the gold. Now, thou must be on thy way!"

speaker: Batlin
text: "Ah yes, thou hast returned from Dungeon Destard! But wait! I do not see the Fellowship funds that thou wast to bring back! What has happened?!"

speaker: Batlin
text: "Why, thy tale is outlandish! I refuse to believe it!" Batlin sniffs in irritation.

speaker: Batlin
text: "Monsters! There are monsters lurking in dungeon Destard?! Well then, I do apologize for thine inconvenience."

speaker: Batlin
text: "Surely thou canst do better than that! If thou simply dost not wish to answer my question why dost thou not say so?"

speaker: Batlin
text: Batlin slowly rolls his eyes. "Thou ought to have been a bard, thou dost regale me with such stories!"

speaker: Batlin
text: "Allow me to present thee with thy Fellowship medallion." Batlin gives you the medallion. "Please -- wear the medallion at all times. Ready it to thy neck immediately! Oh, and... welcome to The Fellowship, Avatar."

speaker: Batlin
text: "Thou cannot receive thy Fellowship medallion. Thou art too encumbered!"

speaker: Batlin
text: "While thou art here, please feel free to enjoy an apple. The finest in all of Britannia, I am certain thou wilt find. They are provided to The Fellowship by the Royal Orchards."

speaker: Batlin
text: "Once a person has walked with The Fellowship long enough and applied the Triad of Inner Strength to his life, he has cleared his mind of all conflicting, counterproductive thoughts to the point where he may actually hear his internal voice of reason. This voice of reason is the core of thine inner mind which guides thee through pure instinct, wisdom and irreproachable logic. Once one starts to listen to it and follow its guidance, one has achieved the height of enlightenment. Perhaps thou shalt hear it one day."

speaker: Batlin
text: "Only active or potential Fellowship members are privy to the concept of 'the voice'. I can tell thee more when thou dost take the Fellowship test."

speaker: Batlin
text: "Oh, art thou ready to join The Fellowship?"

speaker: Batlin
text: "Until thou art ready to join, I cannot tell thee any more about the test."

speaker: Batlin
text: "It is a retreat from the pressures and distractions of everyday life where new members of The Fellowship may go and study the philosophies of The Fellowship. It is located on an island east of Serpent's Hold."

speaker: Batlin
text: "Until we meet again, Avatar."

speaker: Raymundo
text: You can see the creativity literally flowing in abundance from this fellow. He looks at you with interest.

speaker: Raymundo
text: "Yes, yes?" Raymundo snaps. "What dost thou want? I'm busy!"

speaker: Raymundo
text: "I am Raymundo."

speaker: Raymundo
text: "Why, I am famous throughout the land! Hast thou not heard of me?"

speaker: Raymundo
text: "I told thee so!"

speaker: Raymundo
text: "-Really-!? I am surprised! But never mind..."

speaker: Raymundo
text: "I am the Director of the Royal Theatre here in Britain. I am also Playwright-in-Residence. I compose a tune now and then as well. I sometimes act, but it is not wise to act in something that one directs."

speaker: Raymundo
text: "We are working on a play at the moment."

speaker: Raymundo
text: "Come by the theatre during the day and watch the rehearsals for our play."

speaker: Raymundo
text: "It's a little something I wrote entitled 'The Trials of the Avatar'. It's about a legendary figure in Britannian history." The artist looks you up and down.

speaker: Raymundo
text: "Hmmm. Thou dost have a certain quality... hast thou ever acted on stage?"

speaker: Raymundo
text: "I thought so!"

speaker: Raymundo
text: "Well, it does not matter. I am sure thou couldst quickly adapt."

speaker: Raymundo
text: "Officially, auditions have closed and the play is already cast. However, we need someone to understudy the role of the Avatar. Wouldst thou like to audition?"

speaker: Raymundo
text: "Excellent! What thou needest to do is to visit Gaye's Clothier Shoppe and purchase an Avatar costume. I can audition thee once I see thee in -proper- attire. Run along and do that, quickly now, I'm a busy man."

speaker: Raymundo
text: "No? Thou hast never dreamed of performing on the stage? Seeing thy name in torches? Donning the olde grease paint and wig? Bowing to thunderous applause? Well, begone then, I have not the time for chatting with the public."

speaker: Raymundo
text: "'Tis a wonderful space, dost thou not think? 'Twas opened only last year, thanks to the sponsorship of a few wealthy citizens of our great city."

speaker: Raymundo
text: "The construction of the actual theatre building was paid for by the Royal Mint, but the theatre company relies solely on the support of individuals such as thyself. Wouldst thou like to make a modest contribution of, say, ten gold pieces to our theatre company?"

speaker: Raymundo
text: "I thank thee. Thou hast shown thyself to be a true patron of the arts and a person of culture and refinement."

speaker: Raymundo
text: "Thine unconvincing performance gave thy game away! Thou dost not have ten gold pieces!"

speaker: Raymundo
text: "Give a man a loaf of bread and thou hast fed him for a day, give a man a play and perhaps thou hast fed his soul for a lifetime! Once thou hast seen one of our productions I am certain thou shalt reconsider."

speaker: Raymundo
text: "I see thou art ready? Very well. Take center stage, wouldst thou?"

speaker: Raymundo
text: "Where is thy costume? Thou cannot audition without a costume!"

speaker: Raymundo
text: "Come to the theatre during rehearsal hours, wouldst thou?"

speaker: Raymundo
text: Raymundo takes a deep breath and smiles.

speaker: Raymundo
text: "Ah, lovely woman. 'Tis a pity she is more interested in politics than the stage. But I must say that we get along famously!"

speaker: Raymundo
text: "He is quite a character, is he not?" Raymundo's face fills with pride.

speaker: Raymundo
text: "Takes after his old man, I must say. He is sure to be a great actor. Or writer. Or director. Or producer."

speaker: Raymundo
text: "Well, I am really not at liberty to divulge the names of our patrons. But most of them belong to The Fellowship."

speaker: Raymundo
text: "These are people who contribute to our theatre. They come from all walks of life and have little in common besides a love of fine theatre."
