speaker: Raymundo
text: "For non-artists, they have given generous contributions to the theatre. They are -fine- people in my book!" He rubs his hands with glee.

speaker: Raymundo
text: "I am not a member, though."

speaker: Raymundo
text: "Leaving? Sorry, I do not give autographs."

speaker: Jesse
text: This is a tall, skinny actor with knobby knees.

speaker: Jesse
text: He wears a woman's wig and is dressed in drag.

speaker: Jesse
text: Jesse clears his throat. "Hello again!"<VAR>

speaker: Jesse
text: The actor speaks in falsetto.

speaker: Jesse
text: "I am Jesse and I am a star."

speaker: Jesse
text: He slaps his own face and speaks in a normal register, "Oops, sorry! I am so entrenched in the role that I sometimes forget that I am not a woman!"

speaker: Jesse
text: "I work at the Royal Theatre as an actor. I have played -all- the great roles in my career. I now have the chance to play the part of a lifetime -- the Avatar!"

speaker: Jesse
text: "Because it must cater to the masses, we never have the opportunity to do experimental works -- only the traditional gruel of mediocrity. But 'tis a wonderful space and it has marvelous acoustics."

speaker: Jesse
text: "People like to see tales of heroic adventures, knights in armour, beautiful princesses, wise kings, wizards, evil monsters. All that rot."

speaker: Jesse
text: "The role is very challenging. I have a plethora of lines and I had to work with a trainer for weeks to prepare for the enormous amount of activity required. This role will make 'Jesse' a household name!"

speaker: Jesse
text: "It is easily the most ambitious theatrical production ever conceived. There is over a hundred hours of play time. That is a long time for an audience."

speaker: Jesse
text: "My biggest lines are:"

speaker: Jesse
text: "Name!"

speaker: Jesse
text: "Job!"

speaker: Jesse
text: "Bye!"

speaker: Jesse
text: "My favorite piece is something Raymundo wrote for me entitled 'Three on a Codpiece'. I stand on stage and invite the audience to join me in tearing an undergarment into tiny pieces, after which they are placed in funeral urns and mixed with wheat paste. The pieces of cloth, not the audience members. Then the audience may glue the pieces anywhere on my body that they wish."

speaker: Jesse
text: "Goodbye. Be sure to come to the show when it opens!"

speaker: Stuart
text: This actor has much stage presence and a booming voice.

speaker: Stuart
text: Stuart looks down his nose at you. "Yes?"

speaker: Stuart
text: "My real name is Stuart. My stage name is Laurence."

speaker: Stuart
text: "I am the greatest actor who ever lived," he proclaims with absolutely no modesty. "I am playing the character 'Iolo' in the new play."

speaker: Stuart
text: "'Tis the name of a particular hero of mine."

speaker: Stuart
text: Stuart's feathers are obviously ruffled. "Yes. I have been cast as second banana yet again! I am much more suited to play the Avatar, but did Raymundo cast me? Noooo!"

speaker: Iolo
text: "But thou art nothing like me!"

speaker: Stuart
text: "And who art thou, pray tell?"

speaker: Iolo
text: "Why, I am the -real- Iolo!"

speaker: Stuart
text: "Of course thou art. And I am really Lord British. Thou must take me for an ass to think I would believe that."

speaker: Iolo
text: Your friend whispers to you. "These actor types. A touchy bunch, eh?"

speaker: Stuart
text: "I suppose he's a good director. He never casts me in the right roles, though. And to think I went to school with him! We were on our first stage crew together!"

speaker: Stuart
text: Stuart whispers to you, "Jesse is all wrong! Why, -thou- wouldst make a better Avatar than he! And -thou- probably couldst not act thy way out of a reagent bag! That is not a reflection on thee, but on Jesse."

speaker: Stuart
text: "Acting is the highest form of art. It allows one to step outside oneself and become another person. 'Tis like a game!"

speaker: Stuart
text: "Goodbye. Be sure to come to the show when it opens!"

speaker: Amber
text: This lovely actress is dressed in a mouse costume.

speaker: Amber
text: "Hello, there!" Amber says.

speaker: Amber
text: "I am Amber."

speaker: Amber
text: "I am an actress at the Royal Theatre. I am playing the role of Sherry the Mouse in the new play."

speaker: Amber
text: "'Tis a lovely space in which to perform. I have dedicated my life to acting, thou knowest."

speaker: Amber
text: "Raymundo himself had a hand in the design of the theatre."

speaker: Amber
text: "Actually, this will be my debut theatrical performance. I have been working as a barmaid waiting for my first chance to be in the theatre."

speaker: Amber
text: "Between thee and me, methinks the play stinks." She winks at you.

speaker: Amber
text: "Canst thou imagine such drivel? I do not believe there ever was a Sherry the Mouse. Who ever heard of a mouse that could talk! Especially these lines! I would rather play a queen. Much more fitting for me, I would say."

speaker: Amber
text: "I have to memorize this preposterous children's story called 'Hubert's Hair-Raising Adventure'."

speaker: Amber
text: "I asked Raymundo about this and he threw a tantrum. He said that it would not be historically accurate. Ha! As if that were something of any significance!"

speaker: Amber
text: "Poo Poo Head!" she cries. She then rushes to him and kisses him full on the mouth. Shamino turns red and shuffles his feet.

speaker: Shamino
text: "Not in front of the Avatar, Poo!"

speaker: Amber
text: "To blazes with the Avatar!" She kisses him again. "The Avatar is the last one who will convince thee to settle down."

speaker: Amber
text: "Dost thou know my beau? He is probably drowning his sorrows at the Blue Boar. The lazy knave! I will not let him go about adventuring. It is time for him to settle down. Thou canst tell him I said so!"

speaker: Amber
text: "Adieu!"

speaker: Kristy
text: This is a cute toddler holding a baby doll.

speaker: Kristy
text: "Hi!" Kristy exclaims.

speaker: Kristy
text: "Kwisty."

speaker: Nanna
text: "Kristy, like Nicholas, is one of our orphans. She was found in an abandoned home in Paws by one of the Great Council members."

speaker: Kristy
text: "Tag! Playing tag!"

speaker: Kristy
text: The toddler runs off in search of a nursery-mate.

speaker: Kristy
text: Kristy looks confused. "Sing. Horsey. Rosa. Winner."

speaker: Kristy
text: Kristy is more than happy to do so. "A-B-C-D-E-F-G! H-I-K-M-M-M-O-P! Q-T-W-Y-X-Z!" She is proud of her song, although she didn't get it quite right.

speaker: Kristy
text: "I love horsey!" She rocks hard on the rocking horse.

speaker: Kristy
text: Kristy hugs her baby doll tight. "Rosa!"

speaker: Kristy
text: "I am winner!" she proclaims loudly.

speaker: Nanna
text: "She keeps saying that. I am not sure what it means. Something to do with a competition."

speaker: Kristy
text: "Bye bye!"

speaker: Max
text: This toddler is full of energy and is playing hard when he sees you. He stops what he is doing.

speaker: Max
text: "Hi!" Max grins at you.

speaker: Max
text: "Makth."

speaker: Nanna
text: "He says his name is Max."

speaker: Max
text: "Playing tag!"

speaker: Max
text: The boy runs away from you to catch another child.

speaker: Max
text: "I'm a funny boy!" Max laughs hysterically. "Makth sing too!"

speaker: Max
text: "Thou funny boy, -too-!" Max laughs madly as he throws his pacifier at you. He points at it and says, "Binky!"

speaker: Max
text: Max nods furiously. "Binky! Get Binky! Get Binky!"

speaker: Max
text: You realize that the boy wants you to pick it up. Apparently it is some kind of game that only toddlers understand. You pick it up and hand it to him. He immediately plugs it into his mouth.

speaker: Max
text: Max stands upright and bellows, "Old Lord British had a farm, -e-i-e-i-o-! On this farm he had a drake, -e-i-e-i-o-! With a -roar- -roar- here, a -roar- -roar- there, here a -roar-, there a -roar-, everywhere a -roar- -roar-!    Old Lord British had a farm, -e-i-e-i-o-!"

speaker: Max
text: "Bye bye!"

speaker: Nicholas
text: You see a child that has recently grown into toddlerhood.

speaker: Nicholas
text: "Whee! Yoooo!" intones Nicholas.

speaker: Nanna
text: "His name is Nicholas."

speaker: Nicholas
text: "Nick-las".

speaker: Nicholas
text: The toddler is obviously deeply engaged in a game of tag and will not stop to speak.

speaker: Nanna
text: "Why, his job is to wet his diaper! Is that not right, Nicholas?" Nanna says in baby-talk.

speaker: Nicholas
text: "Whee! Dia-per!"

speaker: Nanna
text: "Nicholas is one of our orphans. He was left in front of the castle one morning. 'Tis a sad state of affairs when this kind of thing happens."

speaker: Nicholas
text: "Whee! Dia-per!"

speaker: Nicholas
text: You notice that Nicholas' diaper is wet.

speaker: Nanna
text: "Oh, my. He's wet, is he not? Couldst thou be a dear and change him for me? I would appreciate it!"

speaker: Nicholas
text: "Yeeee! Dia-per! Geeee!" Nicholas says happily.

speaker: Nanna
text: "The diapers are there on that table. If thou wouldst just use one	on Nicholas...."

speaker: Nicholas
text: Nicholas points to the diapers on the table.

speaker: Nicholas
text: "Bye bye!"

speaker: Nanna
text: Nanna gives you a stern look for bothering her during The Fellowship meeting, much like the look of an elementary school teacher you once had.

speaker: Nanna
text: "I cannot imagine where Batlin may be. He has never missed a Fellowship meeting!"

speaker: Nanna
text: "Oh! Hello! I must not stop to speak now. I am on my way to The Fellowship meeting!"

speaker: Nanna
text: You see a working-class elderly woman who exudes sweetness.

speaker: Nanna
text: "Yes, may I help thee?" Nanna asks.

speaker: Nanna
text: "Oh, everyone simply calls me 'Nanna'."

speaker: Nanna
text: "I watch over the Royal Nursery. I am the nanny of these wonderful children."

speaker: Nanna
text: "There have been a great number of babies born in Britannia in recent years, so Lord British established this nursery. It is nice that the noblemen and noblewomen have this luxury so that they may attend to their daily duties."

speaker: Spark
text: "Whew! Dost thou smell what I smell, Avatar?"

speaker: Iolo
text: "I believe that is the smell of diapers, boy. When thou art a father one day, thou wilt come to know that smell quite well."

speaker: Nanna
text: "Well, I feed them and change their diapers and read aloud all the books thou dost see lying around. Luckily, I have Sherry to help me."

speaker: Nanna
text: "Lord British brought them from his homeland. They are very foreign to us here in Britannia, but the children enjoy them just the same."

speaker: Nanna
text: "Sherry is a special mouse who has lived here in the castle for many, many years. She recites stories for the children."

speaker: Nanna
text: "They are lovely, are they not? Every day they seem to learn more and more. Most of the time they are a joy." Nanna whispers to you conspiratorially, "And other times I could happily throw them out with the bathwater!"

speaker: Nanna
text: "The children must be outside playing with Sherry now."

speaker: Nanna
text: "Yes, I suppose it really is a luxury. The poorer people in Britannia certainly do not have such a service for caring for their children. The rich do have an advantage." You detect a hint of bitterness in her voice.

speaker: Nanna
text: "I do not mean to complain by any means. I adore my work. But contrary to the thinking of many of the noblemen and women, a class structure exists in Britannia more than ever before. Taxes are unbearable. The rich get richer, and the poor get poorer, as the saying goes."

speaker: Nanna
text: "The Britannian Tax Council drains us all dry. Especially the lower and middle classes."

speaker: Nanna
text: "Well, look around! There are rich men who live in opulent castles. And right outside are poor people who live in hovels. Thou dost know how there are winged gargoyles and wingless gargoyles? Well, it seems the human race is getting to be just as divided. There is no unity in the land anymore. It is why I have joined The Fellowship."

speaker: Nanna
text: She notices your medallion. "But thou dost know all that already!"

speaker: Nanna
text: "Thou shouldst really come to a meeting. Thou wouldst learn a lot!"

speaker: Nanna
text: "Good day! Do come back and visit again soon!"

speaker: Csil
text: You see a healer who looks wise and honest.

speaker: Csil
text: "I have been looking forward to thine arrival, Avatar. Word spreads quickly. I am pleased to meet thee!"

speaker: Csil
text: "Hello again, Avatar!" Csil says with a smile.

speaker: Csil
text: "I am Csil the Healer, although in a past life I was known as Abrams. I became Csil when I was advanced."

speaker: Csil
text: "I am Britain's healer, and have been for many years. If thou wishest to employ my services, please say so. I shall be only too happy to help."

speaker: Csil
text: "When my name was Abrams, I lived on the island of New Magincia and did mine apprentice work there. My practice grew, and soon I was travelling by ship to Moonglow to see patients there."

speaker: Csil
text: "Soon I had patients on three islands. It was then that Lord British received word of my practice."

speaker: Csil
text: "My practice grew swiftly. I am a modest man, but I do not mind saying that I was a popular healer."

speaker: Shamino
text: "He is probably the best healer in all Britannia. Why, he cured a, er, particular problem I had in no time at all."

speaker: Iolo
text: "Oh? What problem was that?"

speaker: Shamino
text: "Never mind. The whole world does not need to know about it."

speaker: Csil
text: "Well, Lord British himself was struck down with some sort of malady. He sent for me. I arrived at the castle as soon as I could leave my patients, and I examined the king. It appeared to me that something had infested his blood. I have a theory about it, which I am convinced is correct. Others, however, do not share my view."

speaker: Csil
text: "I believe that most sicknesses are caused by tiny living things. We cannot see these things with the naked eye. However, I am working on developing an instrument which -can- see these creatures. I believe that someday, healing will not depend on magic at all, but on some form of treatment which makes one less vulnerable to these living creatures. Since these animals are biological, I call this theorized treatment 'antibiotics'. What dost thou think, Avatar? Am I on the right track?"

speaker: Csil
text: "Good. I thought so."

speaker: Csil
text: "No? Hmmm." Csil looks concerned. "Well, I cannot believe in the archaic tradition of bleeding a person until the sickness has left his body. There must be another way..."

speaker: Csil
text: Csil looks at his notes, worried that his theory is invalid.

speaker: Csil
text: "There is a group of people who do not encourage my studies. We do not get along at all. I think they have something against healers which goes beyond simple distrust. Dost thou know whom I mean?"

speaker: Csil
text: Csil nods. "I thought so. The Fellowship is not... quite what they seem."

speaker: Csil
text: "No?" Csil lowers his voice. "The Fellowship."

speaker: Csil
text: "They have a doctrine which outlines their beliefs. They believe if one is faced with pain, then he has no choice but to go through it in order to be a 'better person'. I do not agree with this. No one should ever go through needless pain. But... they are entitled to their own opinions."

speaker: Csil
text: "Goodbye, Avatar."

speaker: Zella
text: You see a lean, young fighter with a rather dashing flair.

speaker: Zella
text: "Hello again!" Zella says.

speaker: Zella
text: "My name is Zella."

speaker: Zella
text: "I am a trainer. I specialize in hand-to-hand combat. After all, a fighter never knows when he might encounter an adversary and suddenly realize he is unarmed. I call it 'boxing'. Boxing is not only a method of fighting -- it is an art."

speaker: Zella
text: "The field of battle contains many arenas. Almost any situation could arise. Every fighter should be knowledgeable and adept at many forms of combat. I have mine own theory of fighting."

speaker: Zella
text: "All the various arenas of combat, all the various styles one may learn in fighting with various weapons, are not fighting in its purest form. To truly be a great fighter one must go to the source of all fighting knowledge."

speaker: Zella
text: "Just as a castle is built from the foundation up, so must a fighter. One cannot simply begin by learning to fight with weapons. Weapons are merely an extension of a person's extremities. A true fighter learns by using those extremities first."

speaker: Zella
text: "Make no mistake. Fighters are made, not born. All the natural talent in the world will avail thee naught if one does not have the heart and the will to win. Part of that will is the courage to seek out thine own limitations and strive to better them."

speaker: Zella
text: "Thine arms. Thy legs. Thy fists. This is what makes 'boxing'."

speaker: Zella
text: "My price for training is 45 gold. Is this all right?"

speaker: Zella
text: "Then mayest thou find more inexpensive training elsewhere."

speaker: Zella
text: "Be so kind as to return during normal training hours, wouldst thou?"

speaker: Zella
text: "Good day to thee."

speaker: Lucy
text: You see an attractive woman in her fifties. She has a warm smile. "Welcome! Who art thou, stranger?"

speaker: Lucy
text: "Well, hello, <PLAYER_NAME>."

speaker: Lucy
text: "Whoa! Hey everyone! This here is the Avatar!"

speaker: Lucy
text: Everyone in the Blue Boar laughs.

speaker: Lucy
text: "And I'd bet thou dost need a drink, right?"

speaker: Dupre
text: "Damn! How did she know?"

speaker: Lucy
text: "Oh, really?" she says in mock surprise. "Why, I have always wanted to meet the Avatar!"

speaker: Lucy
text: "What will it be, <PLAYER_NAME>?" Lucy asks.

speaker: Lucy
text: "What can I do for thee, <PLAYER_NAME>?" Lucy asks.

speaker: Lucy
text: "I'm Lucy!"

speaker: Lucy
text: "I run The Blue Boar. Oldest tavern in Britannia."

speaker: Lucy
text: "If thou dost want anything to eat or drink, just say so!"

speaker: Lucy
text: She addresses Dupre. "How about thou, handsome? Want something to eat?" She bats her eyelashes.

speaker: Dupre
text: "My dear, thou wouldst make any man hungry!"

speaker: Lucy
text: "I like thy friends, <PLAYER_NAME>."

speaker: Lucy
text: "I shall be happy to serve thee something if thou dost come to the pub during open hours!"

speaker: Lucy
text: "Smashing place for a revel! It hath been here for ages! I inherited it from my grandfather. I enjoy it because I love to cook. And eat." She laughs. "And drink!" She laughs again.

speaker: Lucy
text: "But mostly I like it because I meet so many interesting people. Just like thee, <PLAYER_NAME>!"

speaker: Lucy
text: "Thou dost look like the kind of person who doth enjoy a fair bit of revelry!"

speaker: Lucy
text: "Come back to the pub in the evening to hear our house band, The Avatars!"

speaker: Lucy
text: "Our house band The Avatars is performing in the other room!"

speaker: Lucy
text: Lucy laughs. "Revelry! Singing! Dancing! Eating! Drinking! All in a time and place where one may stop and enjoy life! I can see it hath been too long since thou hast sampled the simple pleasures of life in Britannia!"

speaker: Lucy
text: "They are a popular local singing group. I am sure thou wilt like them, <PLAYER_NAME>!"

speaker: Lucy
text: "Oh, I so enjoy meeting men who like to go out and 'kill' things!"

speaker: Lucy
text: "Everything I serve is delicious. I highly recommend that thou tasteth the Silverleaf dish. Worth every gold piece spent!"

speaker: Lucy
text: "I serve Britain's finest ale and wine."

speaker: Lucy
text: "It's made from the root of a very rare tree. Quite superb, it is!"

speaker: Lucy
text: "Talk to thee later!"

speaker: Greg
text: You see a gleeful-looking merchant with an enthusiastic voice and manner.

speaker: Greg
text: "Why, what can I do for thee, <HONORIFIC>?" asks Greg.

speaker: Greg
text: "Why, my name is Greg. It is good to see thee."

speaker: Greg
text: "Why, I run the Provisioner's Shop here in Britain. A second home to the intrepid, it is."

speaker: Greg
text: "Why, thou dost look to be a person to whom adventure is no stranger. Whether thou art climbing a mountain, sailing the ocean, crossing a desert, exploring a dungeon or sleeping under the stars I have just what thou mayest need."

speaker: Greg
text: "I have moved my store here as a service to Lord British, who uses me exclusively to outfit all of his various expeditions. It is true!"

speaker: Greg
text: "I used to have my shop in Paws. But no one in Paws has the money to buy much of anything."

speaker: Greg
text: "What every adventurer needs is good luck! There is just something about this shop, about the items bought here, something about me and my shop that is simply very lucky. I can give thee an example of what I mean."

speaker: Greg
text: "A fighting man named Gorn once bought a shovel from me and he told me that it saved his life."

speaker: Greg
text: "Perhaps thou knowest of Gorn. He speaks with a most peculiar accent!"

speaker: Greg
text: "Gorn wanted to dig for some buried treasure somewhere, when he heard some noises behind him. Upon turning, he was horrified to see a swarm of undead skeletons rushing toward him! In his haste to dig up the treasure, he had unbuckled his belt and laid down his sword. The only thing in his hands was the shovel. He immediately began swinging it and ended up knocking all the skeletons to bits! He now considers it his 'lucky shovel'!"

speaker: Greg
text: "This is Lord British's favorite provisionary shop. He told me so himself. All sorts of famous adventurers pass through these doors. Why, just last week, we had the Avatar himself in this, my very own store!"

speaker: Greg
text: "Why, now that I mention it, he was dressed a lot like thou art. Yes, he was."

speaker: Greg
text: "Why, I seem to remember that Avatar was also wearing a Fellowship medallion like the one thou dost possess. Hmmmm. And he nearly robbed me blind. I shall have to keep a careful eye on thee, I will."

speaker: Greg
text: "Well, he said he was the Avatar. But then it is not all that unusual encountering some loon or fool who claims to be the Avatar!" He looks at you and for a moment appears a little embarrassed.

speaker: Greg
text: "He was dressed like the Avatar, similarly to how thou art presently attired. At first I thought it was Jesse, the actor who is playing the Avatar in the play by that director... What is his name again?"

speaker: Greg
text: "Oh, well. It was not him."

speaker: Greg
text: "Thou wouldst think that one who appears to be like the Avatar would be worthy of trust. But, no. In this day and age there is no telling what to expect!"

speaker: Greg
text: "My customers are all people who go out and perform dangerous feats of bravery and derring-do. But most keep returning to buy more provisions time and again. With all the dangerous things my customers do, it is a wonder I have not lost them all and gone out of business!"

speaker: Greg
text: "I am dreadfully sorry but the Provisioner's Shop is currently closed. Do return at noon when it shall be open once again."

speaker: Greg
text: "As I say, we have everything thou dost need to have a jolly splendid adventure!"

speaker: Greg
text: "Good day to thee, <HONORIFIC>."

speaker: Neno
text: Neno is busy performing with The Avatars and cannot speak at the moment.

speaker: Neno
text: "I must get to my performance at The Blue Boar! The Avatars are playing tonight!"

speaker: Neno
text: You see a handsome and flamboyant musician.

speaker: Neno
text: "Hello," Neno says.

speaker: Neno
text: The musician nods at you. "I am Neno."

speaker: Neno
text: "I am studying to be the greatest bard that Britannia has ever known. I probably already -am- the greatest bard Britannia has ever known." You note that Neno is not at all modest.

speaker: Neno
text: "It is a great honor to be a bard. Thou art someone who gives pleasure to other people, while at the same time fulfilling a creative urge within thyself. It is truly magical. I know this from mine experience playing with The Avatars."

speaker: Neno
text: "The Music Hall provides a great environment for study. Judith is a wonderful teacher, and the opportunities here are of the highest quality. One day I shall travel the world and entertain the common folk and nobles alike."

speaker: Neno
text: "It is my dream to be famous throughout the land. I shall tour the country every year, and play in the largest pubs in every town." He winks at you. "I shall be assured of wooing the women, dost thou not think?"

speaker: Neno
text: "'Tis a singing group I play with. We play at The Blue Boar every evening. Please, come listen to us." Neno leans in to whisper, "But I plan to begin performing alone very soon. I am obviously the most talented member of the quartet."

speaker: Neno
text: "Farewell! Thou must watch the postings for our performance dates!"

speaker: Judith
text: Judith is busy performing with The Avatars and cannot speak at the moment.

speaker: Judith
text: "I must run! I am late for my performance with The Avatars! I shall talk with thee later!"

speaker: Judith
text: You see an attractive middle-aged woman with music in her eyes.

speaker: Judith
text: "Hello!" Judith says.

speaker: Judith
text: "I am Judith. And I already know who thou art!"

speaker: Judith
text: "I teach music at The Music Hall. I also fatten my purse a bit by playing with The Avatars!"

speaker: Judith
text: "Music is my life. I know I will never be a famous bard, but I receive great pleasure from playing and performing. I enjoy teaching as well."

speaker: Judith
text: "Lord British appointed me music teacher a couple of years ago. It is a wonderful job!"

speaker: Judith
text: "We are a singing group. We play at the Blue Boar every evening. Please come and hear us! My pupil, Neno, is in the group. We hope to tour the country next year, if we can raise the funds."

speaker: Judith
text: "It fulfills my life's purpose to teach others. It also gives me time away from home."

speaker: Judith
text: "Oh, I do not want to speak about mine home. Mine husband and I... well, we are not altogether... happy."

speaker: Judith
text: "Thou mightest know him. He is Patterson, the Town Mayor. He is an intelligent and honest man, but we have our differences."

speaker: Judith
text: "I do not know why I am telling thee all of this!"

speaker: Judith
text: "Well, for one thing, he is a member of that group, The Fellowship. Another thing is that he does not spend too much time at home. I cannot believe he works so much."

speaker: Judith
text: "They seem to have taken over our lives. They seem to have taken over our country!"

speaker: Judith
text: "He is always saying he has to work late. Some nights he comes home before dawn. Other nights he is out the entire night."

speaker: Judith
text: "Well, I must not think about it. I only become saddened. I must concentrate on my music."

speaker: Judith
text: Judith goes back to her instrument after a smile and a wave.

speaker: Candice
text: Candice is listening intently to the Fellowship meeting.

speaker: Candice
text: "Hast thou seen Batlin? He has not shown up for the Fellowship meeting!"

speaker: Candice
text: "Oh! I must not stop to speak with thee! I am late for a Fellowship meeting!"

speaker: Candice
text: This is a bright woman who looks much younger than she actually is.

speaker: Candice
text: "Well! Thy reputation precedes thee! The Avatar in person! Word has spread that thou wert in Britain!"

speaker: Candice
text: Candice looks guilty about something. She gives you a little wave, but says nothing. She looks at Patterson, hoping that he will do the talking.

speaker: Candice
text: "Yes, Avatar?" Candice says.

speaker: Candice
text: "Yes, Avatar?" Candice says.

speaker: Candice
text: "My name is Candice," she says brightly. "I must say I am honored to meet the Avatar!" She curtsies.

speaker: Candice
text: "I am the curator of the Royal Museum."

speaker: Candice
text: "Feel free to ask about any of the exhibits."

speaker: Candice
text: "I hope to see thee there when the museum is open."

speaker: Candice
text: "I spend the rest of my time working with The Fellowship."

speaker: Candice
text: "It has been in Britain for many, many years. It contains historical artifacts, as well as works of art."

speaker: Candice
text: "We have just opened a special section in which thou might be interested -- an exhibit of 'Avatar artifacts'!"

speaker: Candice
text: "Come to the museum when it is open!"

speaker: Candice
text: "There are relics from early Britannia and even from the Three Ages of Darkness -- back when Britannia was known as Sosaria."

speaker: Candice
text: "Well, thou surely must recognize them. They are supposed to be authentic! Things like the Silver Horn and the eight stones. I understand the stones were used for teleportation, and if mages were not so sick in the head these days, they could cast a 'Recall' spell on them to teleport to specific places around Britannia. I believe if one casts a 'Mark' spell on one, thou canst re-assign the teleportation location! But I suppose none of that works anymore."

speaker: Iolo
text: Iolo whispers to you, "Er, Avatar, thou dost know that I do not condone stealing. But, er, I do believe these stones may be useful to us. Perhaps we should come back later when the museum is closed, if thou dost know what I mean? After all, these items technically belong to thee!"

speaker: Candice
text: "Britannia is proud of the artists who donate their works to the museum. Thou wilt see pieces all over the country by Britannian artists Watson, Richard Fox, Randi Frank, Glen Johnson, and Denis Loubet."

speaker: Candice
text: "We meet every evening at the Hall. Thou must come and visit!"

speaker: Candice
text: "Thou must know all about it by now! I hope to see thee at an evening meeting!"

speaker: Candice
text: "The Fellowship has given me a great purpose in life. I have made new friends, and have even found love!" She giggles. "Ooops! I gave away my secret! I must not speak of it. Do forget I said that, please?"

speaker: Candice
text: "I want to attain a higher level of acceptance in The Fellowship. I want to hear the 'voice'. That is mine one true goal."

speaker: Candice
text: "Dost thou not know? The longer one is a member of The Fellowship, the greater the chances that one will hear the 'voice'. Supposedly, it is a man's voice that thou wilt hear -- perhaps in thy dreams, perhaps while thou art concentrating on something else -- it is a voice that tells thee things, suggests things. I do not know, really. I have not heard it yet, so I am only speaking of what I have heard from others more fortunate than I."

speaker: Candice
text: "What secret? I do -not- have a secret! It was a slip of the tongue. I cannot really speak to anyone about it. Why, if word got out that the Mayor and I... I mean, uhm, -may- I... er, ask thee to forget that I said anything?"

speaker: Candice
text: Candice turns beet red and turns away.

speaker: Candice
text: "Good day, Avatar."

speaker: Cynthia
text: You see a helpful and efficient-looking woman.

speaker: Cynthia
text: "How may I help thee?" asks Cynthia.

speaker: Cynthia
text: "My name is Cynthia."

speaker: Cynthia
text: "I am the teller at the Mint. I am also a member of the Britannian Tax Council."

speaker: Cynthia
text: "Here at the Mint we store gold, oversee production of coins and keep an accurate count of how much money the kingdom has available for such things as farming, building the roads, developing sources of fresh water, seeing to the health of the citizenry, maintaining the estates of nobles, raising the guard militia and carrying out the decrees of Lord British."

speaker: Cynthia
text: "The Britannian Tax Council is in charge of the accounting, assessment and collection of the taxes. If thou wilt be earning any money here in Britannia thou wilt need to take this paper."

speaker: Cynthia
text: "Fill it out and return it here at the end of the year when thou dost come back to pay thy taxes."

speaker: Cynthia
text: "Thou art carrying too much. Come back and I will give thee thy paper when thou art not so greatly encumbered."

speaker: Cynthia
text: "In order to keep the standard of money constant, we also operate as an exchange for those who possess quantities of gold."

speaker: Cynthia
text: "We supply the equivalent value of their gold in spendable coin of the realm and then transform the gold we receive into more money. So, as thou canst see, it is a very efficient system."

speaker: Cynthia
text: "As I am certain thou dost know, the seven year drought, which thankfully ended several years ago, has left much of the farming in the Kingdom in disarray. That is why the cost of food is so expensive. But without the support of the Royal Treasury, the prices would be even higher."

speaker: Cynthia
text: "The increased use of wagons has caused many of the roads throughout Britannia to rapidly deteriorate. It costs a lot of money to build new roads and keep them all repaired."

speaker: Cynthia
text: "It is of the utmost importance to the Kingdom to insure its populous a clean water supply, and that requires a regular supply of new and fresh wells."

speaker: Cynthia
text: "As Britannia's population has greatly increased in the last two hundred years, so has the risk of infectious diseases, such as the mysterious skin deterioration that afflicts those who partake in the venom of the silver serpent. The number of healers that the Kingdom needs has risen dramatically."

speaker: Cynthia
text: "The local Lords and Mayors all have residences that are maintained through the auspices of the Kingdom."

speaker: Cynthia
text: "The military training is conducted at Serpent's Hold, where the guards that protect all of the towns and cities of Britannia are instructed. 'Tis funded by the Royal Treasury."

speaker: Cynthia
text: "It not only applies to gold but it also applies to all minerals. We oversee the sale and rate of exchange for precious ores extracted by the Britannian Mining Company. But we do not handle the sale of gems. There is a jeweler in town who handles that."

speaker: Cynthia
text: "Dost thou have some gold that thou wouldst like to exchange?"

speaker: Cynthia
text: "I can see thou hast no nuggets or bars of gold. Whatever gold thou mayest possess is already the coin of the realm. I cannot help thee anymore than that."

speaker: Cynthia
text: "We can exchange thy gold nuggets and bars into spendable coin for thee. I will give thee ten gold coins for each gold nugget and one-hundred gold coins for each gold bar."

speaker: Cynthia
text: "Oh, my. Thou canst not possibly carry that many gold coins. Thou must return when thou dost have more space in thy pack."

speaker: Cynthia
text: "And here are <VAR> gold coins for thee in return, <HONORIFIC>. I thank thee for thy business."

speaker: Cynthia
text: "Very well. Mayhaps another time."

speaker: Cynthia
text: "Please come to The Mint during regular daytime hours."

speaker: Cynthia
text: "James is mine husband and I am very worried about him. I know he is feeling very unhappy lately and he dislikes his job. If thou dost speak to him please tell him that even though we have not been speaking very much lately, that I am still thinking of him and that I still care about him."

speaker: Cynthia
text: "Good day, <HONORIFIC>."

speaker: Patterson
text: Patterson is concentrating on the Fellowship meeting and does not wish to speak.

speaker: Patterson
text: "I wonder where Batlin could be! 'Tis not like him to miss a meeting."

speaker: Patterson
text: "I cannot stop to speak right now. I am late for the Fellowship meeting!"

speaker: Patterson
text: You see a nobleman in his forties who looks like either a politician or a well-dressed merchant.

speaker: Patterson
text: "Avatar! I was just alerted of thy presence in our fair city! I have been expecting thee!"

speaker: Patterson
text: "Avatar! Er, uhm, how art thee? Oh, dost thou know Candice, the curator at the Royal Museum? She is a 'brother' at The Fellowship. I was, er, just seeing her home!"

speaker: Iolo
text: "Hmmm. And does thy wife know thou art seeing Candice home?"

speaker: Patterson
text: You ask if Judith knows about this.

speaker: Patterson
text: "Why, she doth not need to know! It does not matter! 'Tis nothing, really!"

speaker: Patterson
text: The Mayor is sweating profusely. He looks at you with beady eyes. He knows he has been found out. His body slumps. He is mortified and ashamed.

speaker: Patterson
text: "Thou hast discovered my... our secret. Please do not tell Judith. I... will end this. I swear. Candice -- we must stop meeting. I... I'm sorry."

speaker: Patterson
text: You decide to leave Patterson and Candice to work out what has happened, and you hope that the Mayor has learned something about honesty.

speaker: Patterson
text: "How may I help thee?" Patterson asks.

speaker: Patterson
text: "How may I help thee?" Patterson asks.

speaker: Patterson
text: "I am Patterson. Named after my father." He holds his hand out, takes yours, and shakes it firmly. "It is such a pleasure to meet the Avatar!"

speaker: Patterson
text: "Why, I am the Town Mayor! The Town Mayor of Britain, that is! I would have thee know that mine election was an overwhelming victory! Mine opponent never had a chance!"

speaker: Patterson
text: "I am also President of the Britannian Tax Council."

speaker: Patterson
text: "It was held two years ago. I received 84 percent of the votes. It was an impressive victory, I must admit."

speaker: Patterson
text: "Of course, when one has a group like The Fellowship behind them..."

speaker: Patterson
text: "He was an old farmer named Brownie. Didn't have much money to put into a campaign. Even the peasants didn't support him."

speaker: Patterson
text: "My life has improved greatly since I joined. I find that mine honesty is impeccable, my leadership is unchallengeable, and my love for my wife is irreproachable."

speaker: Patterson
text: "Thou shouldst consider attending one of our meetings in the evening."

speaker: Patterson
text: "I would wager that thy life has improved as well!"

speaker: Patterson
text: "Did I say that? I certainly did not mean it. There is no class system in Britain anymore, nor in the entire country, for that matter! What I meant is that the 'peasantry', that is, those people who are not of superior lineage -- which is the type of man Brownie is -- -they- did not support him either. They knew who would be the best leader!"

speaker: Patterson
text: "Did I say that? I do not think I really meant that the way it sounded. What I meant to say was that there are people who come from families of better standing than others. And Brownie is not one of them! But do not misunderstand me -- I still maintain that the class system in Britannia has been abolished!"

speaker: Patterson
text: "She said what? Well, she's wrong! And to think she is a 'brother'. One of The Fellowship! I shall have to speak to Batlin about her."

speaker: Patterson
text: You notice that Patterson seems ill-at-ease.

speaker: Patterson
text: "I am obviously the most honest person in Britain! Perhaps I should move to Moonglow! Ha!"

speaker: Patterson
text: "Her name is Judith. She's the music teacher at The Music Hall. Perhaps thou hast met her. We have a wonderful relationship."

speaker: Patterson
text: "The land must have some way of generating income. Taxes are the only solution. Every merchant and farmer is taxed. Anyone who works for a living is taxed."

speaker: Patterson
text: "The Britannian Tax Council has its main office in the Royal Mint."

speaker: Patterson
text: "Why, I do not know what she is talking about! I work late, that is all!"

speaker: Iolo
text: Iolo whispers to you, "This man seems very defensive, dost thou not think? I say we should observe him and see where he goes after The Fellowship meeting tonight."

speaker: Patterson
text: Patterson's eyes widen and for a moment looks very nervous. But very quickly he regains his composure.

speaker: Patterson
text: "Candice? Why, she is a friend! A 'brother' at The Fellowship! That is all!"

speaker: Patterson
text: You relate what Lord British said about the murder in Britain a few years ago. Patterson nods.

speaker: Patterson
text: "I remember it well. Quite gruesome, it was. There was a man named Finster who was running for public office. He was quite outspoken in his opinions, and I suppose this got him into trouble."

speaker: Patterson
text: "He was trying to make many social changes. He wanted more power for the Great Council and the Britannian Tax Council, and he wanted to disband The Fellowship. Finster was a nobleman with too much ambition. Anyway, his beliefs must have provided him with a few enemies."

speaker: Patterson
text: "How should I know? Anyway, his body was found in an abandoned building which is no longer standing. It used to be a storehouse of some kind, up near the castle. It was torn down a couple of years ago. The body was mutilated beyond belief. It was as if someone tied the poor man down with stakes and cut off all of his limbs. Finster was then beheaded. It was almost... what is the word... ritualistic!"

speaker: Patterson
text: "And that is all I remember. No one was ever arrested for the crime."

speaker: Patterson
text: Patterson nods his head at you.

speaker: Carrocio

speaker: Carrocio
text: "In a wink, in a word,"

speaker: Carrocio
text: "I do greet thee, Milord."

speaker: Carrocio
text: "To greet thee, On this day,"

speaker: Carrocio
text: "'Tis my pleasure, Milady."

speaker: Carrocio
text: "From out the dawn, when sun doth rise,"

speaker: Carrocio
text: "Until next morn when moon must go,"

speaker: Carrocio
text: "I answer to thy beck and cries,"

speaker: Carrocio
text: "thine humble servant, Carrocio!"

speaker: Carrocio
text: "The puppet's curtain I unfurl,"

speaker: Carrocio
text: "And from mine hands the story's told,"

speaker: Carrocio
text: "For pleasure of a boy or girl,"

speaker: Carrocio
text: "To see doth cost one coin of gold."

speaker: Carrocio
text: "To take good measure of thy power,"

speaker: Carrocio
text: "Forged in fire of virtue's heart,"

speaker: Carrocio
text: "To ring the bell this very hour,"

speaker: Carrocio
text: "Do test thy strength 'til thy muscles smart."

text: "And perhaps impress thine own sweetheart!" Carrocio winks at you.

text: "Or dost thou wish to be a king?"

text: "Yonder sticks a sword in stone."

speaker: Carrocio
text: "If thou canst only pull it out"

text: "My childhood's eye spied father's toil,"

speaker: Carrocio
text: "A puppet's show of splendor royal."

text: "Time's breeze has blown, My father's gone,"

speaker: Carrocio
text: "His child has grown, Regrets anon,"

text: "Gears and wheels move the moppets now, in need of no one,"

text: "Come to the	grounds to test thy fitness"

text: "Take the hammer in thine hands and strike a blow upon the ground,"

text: "If thine arms be possessed of might then thou shalt hear a ringing sound."

speaker: Carrocio
text: "Once thou hast struck if thou hearest naught then thou dost know thy strength is flagging."

speaker: Carrocio
text: "But if thou dost win the strength test game thou shalt receive a stuffed dragon."

speaker: Carrocio
text: "I fear an end to my family craft, where the show is run by human heart,"

speaker: Carrocio
text: "But bones do age, not so machines, and we cannot simply replace a part."

speaker: Carrocio
text: "I carry on as best I can, A machine to play my father's role,"

speaker: Carrocio
text: "Control the marionettes unseen, struggling to imbue them with a soul."

speaker: Carrocio
text: "The faces pressed before me, fleeting moments chance of glee, From the lowly mongrel beggar to the resident of throne,"

speaker: Carrocio
text: "Each know their place and gave me chase to find the one for me, Woman whom my life may share, this heart that waits alone."

speaker: Carrocio
text: "A beggar man called Snaz will come to watch my show, "

text: "Thine ignorance doth make me skittish,"

text: "The awakening of mine heart's idyll,"

text: "Perchance through destiny a marriage made."

speaker: Carrocio
text: Carrocio looks as if he is lost in a memory. After a moment he returns to reality.

speaker: Carrocio
text: "I would not be a gentleman if I spoke of this more, Forgive me the candor of mine heart's open door."

speaker: Carrocio
text: He appears somewhat embarrassed and clears his throat loudly several times.

speaker: Carrocio
text: "My coins are arrows rushing to make good,"

speaker: Carrocio
text: "'Til the day when the jeweller sells his ring,"

speaker: Carrocio
text: "For my sure heart is not but carved from wood,"

speaker: Carrocio
text: "And she doth tend to the bed of a king."

speaker: Carrocio
text: Carrocio gives you a shocked look and drops to his knees before you. "I beseech thee, <HONORIFIC>, "

speaker: Carrocio
text: "Keep still thy tongue,"

speaker: Carrocio
text: "My Nell has ne'er harmed anyone,"

speaker: Carrocio
text: "It would cause grievous injury to her reputation,"

speaker: Carrocio
text: "Through the town's wagging lips our secret to spread,"

speaker: Carrocio
text: "'Twould make a permanent end of mine occupation,"

speaker: Carrocio
text: "And kill our hope of a happy life dead." He looks you in the eyes, pleadingly. "In thee I must place mine hope and trust,"

speaker: Carrocio
text: "Part, parcel and whole."

speaker: Carrocio
text: "To ne'er again speak of the spoils of my lust, "

speaker: Carrocio

speaker: Figg
text: Figg is too intent on listening to the Fellowship meeting to acknowledge your attempts to converse with him.

speaker: Figg
text: "Hast thou seen Batlin? Where is he? He needs to lead our meeting!"

speaker: Figg
text: "My goodness! It is nine o'clock! Excuse me, I must get to tonight's Fellowship meeting."

speaker: Figg
text: You see a man whose wrinkled face forms a caricature of grumpiness.

speaker: Figg
text: "Thou dost wish words with me, <HONORIFIC>?" asks Figg.

speaker: Figg
text: "I am Figg."

speaker: Figg
text: "I am the caretaker of the Royal Orchards here in Britain."

speaker: Figg
text: "My responsibilities include caring for the trees, watching over the pickers at harvest time and protecting the Royal Orchard from thieves."

speaker: Figg
text: "Apple trees require constant care. I must make sure the trees all have enough water but not too much. I must keep all trees properly trimmed and be watchful so that the crop does not get infested by bugs or worms. I am also required to pick up all of the fallen apples, which is a job in itself."

speaker: Figg
text: "Most of them are migrant farmers from Paws. Because they were once farmers, they are convinced they know more about the upkeep of the orchard than I! Of course that is preposterous. Also the pickers do not take orders very well."

speaker: Figg
text: "They would rob us down to the last twig if I gave them the chance! I should be awarded a medal from Lord British himself the way I risk my very life and limb protecting this orchard. Why, I just caught another thief recently. His name was Weston."

speaker: Figg
text: "Here are grown the finest apples in all of Britannia. I would let thee sample one but it would be against the law as thou art obviously not of noble stock."

speaker: Figg
text: "He now resides in the prison, thanks to me! I knew what he was up to from the moment I saw him! He had the look of a hardened apple thief so I had him nicked by the town guard."

speaker: Figg
text: "Yes, Weston is now living in our local prison. If thou dost not believe me, thou canst go there and see for thyself!"

speaker: Figg
text: "Oh, he came here with some sob story. But when one is as astute an observer of human behavior as I am, one can tell the true intent of people, which is often contrary to what they will say to thee!"

speaker: Figg
text: "I do not recall, exactly. Something about his impoverished wife and family starving to death in Paws or some load of rubbish."

speaker: Figg
text: "Yes, I do consider myself to be a more than passable judge of character. And dost thou know how I became so?"

speaker: Figg
text: "Oh, then art thou not the clever one!"

speaker: Figg
text: "Then I shall tell thee! I am a member of The Fellowship!"

speaker: Figg
text: "I am a member of the Fellowship, yes. But it would be a crime for me to give apples from the Royal Orchard to The Fellowship, and it would be a violation of my sacred duty. While selling apples is also a violation, I was only trying to do this man Weston a favor. And I suppose these accusations are the thanks I get? Hmph!"

speaker: Figg
text: He leans in close to you and speaks lower. "Thou art also a member of The Fellowship, after all. Am I not thy brother? Shouldst thou not trust me?" He gives you a crooked wink.

speaker: Figg
text: "Thou seest? I am thy brother!" He hands you an apple.

speaker: Figg
text: "I would give thee an apple to show thee my sincerity, but it seems thou art too encumbered."

speaker: Figg
text: "But enough of these desperate accusations from a known criminal."

speaker: Figg
text: "I can do thee a favor as well. Wouldst thou like to buy one of these beautiful apples for the merest pittance of five gold coins?"

speaker: Figg
text: Figg takes an apple from a nearby basket. After polishing it slightly on his shirt, he hands it to you.

speaker: Figg
text: "Thou cannot take thine apple! Thou art carrying too much!"

speaker: Figg
text: "Thou dost not even have enough gold to buy one apple! Thou hast wasted the time of the King's Caretaker of the Royal Orchard. Away, peasant! Away before I call the guard!"

speaker: Figg
text: "Very well. But thou art passing up an opportunity that few are offered. In fact, eh, I would appreciate it if thou wouldst not mention our little chat to anyone. Agreed?"

speaker: Figg
text: "Ah, I knew thou wert a good 'un."

speaker: Figg
text: "No! Well, fine, then."

speaker: Figg
text: "I can see that thou shouldst be on thy way."

speaker: James
text: You see a sour-faced innkeeper who looks at you as if all of his problems were your fault.

speaker: James
text: "What must I do for thee now, <HONORIFIC>?" asks James.

speaker: James
text: "My name is James."

speaker: James
text: "I am the proprietor of the inn."

speaker: James
text: "It is just another way of saying that I am the man who is the desk clerk. Which thou mayest think is an easy job although it is not, I can assure thee."

speaker: James
text: "This place is called the Wayfarer's Inn. It has a long and substantial history in Britain. If thy grandparents ever came to town this is probably where they stayed."

speaker: James
text: "Of course, being desk clerk is not all I do. I must spend all day listening to people talk about their problems as if I am supposed to solve them!"

speaker: James
text: "That is correct, <HONORIFIC>. So if thou dost have a problem, allow me the courtesy of not having to hear all about it. Now what was it that I was saying again?"

speaker: James
text: "Maybe solving people's problems is an easy task for other innkeepers, but, not only am I bad at it, I have mine own problems as well."

speaker: James
text: "I do not like my job! I never wanted to be an innkeeper, I just wanted to keep the place going after my father passed on. Now that I am married to Cynthia, I am more tied down than ever!"

speaker: James
text: "Instead of being an innkeeper I always secretly wanted to be a pirate! When I was not sailing the seas I would be living in Buccaneer's Den."

speaker: James
text: "As I understand it they have an excellent House of Games there as well as opulent baths. Or at least so I have heard from Gordon, the man who sells fish and chips."

speaker: James
text: "Do not mistake my words, <HONORIFIC>. I love Cynthia with all mine heart. But there are I times I feel I am too young to be married. Besides, I know I cannot be a good husband for her."

speaker: James
text: "Thou knowest for certain that few if any people would pour their troubles out to pirates. If I were a pirate I could get this bad foot replaced with a peg, too!"

speaker: James
text: "How can I make Cynthia happy on the pittance an innkeeper makes when all day long she is counting all that money in the mint? I know I cannot."

speaker: James
text: "I know the nature of the heart, my good friend. After being exposed to such large sums of money she shall begin to covet it. As I cannot provide it, she shall leave me to give her heart to a wealthy man. Perhaps a merchant or a nobleman. The thought of it makes my blood boil."

speaker: James
text: "When one is an innkeeper one must run around all day long. If anyone wants anything thou art the one who must take care of it for them!"

speaker: James
text: "I spend so much time running around that I have gotten a bad foot."

speaker: James
text: "Already I can sense she is worried about our marriage. I know that there is something wrong between us."

speaker: James
text: "Oh, I suppose thou wouldst like a room now! There, that is just what I mean! It is ten gold pieces per person for a night. Thou dost want a room, dost thou not?"

speaker: James
text: "Thou art carrying too much to take the room key!"

speaker: James
text: "Here is thy room key. It is only good until thou leavest the inn."

speaker: James
text: "Thou dost not have enough gold to get a room here. Now I suppose thou shalt be telling me all about how such a sorry state befell thee. Well, I shall not listen to thee!"

speaker: James
text: James wipes his brow. "Phew! That was a close call!"

speaker: James
text: "Please, <HONORIFIC>. Do allow me some time to myself! Presently I am not doing the business of the inn and I do wish to keep it that way. Thou must attend to the inn during business hours."

speaker: James
text: You repeat the words that Cynthia had said to you about him. A smile comes across his face. "Aww, who wants to be a pirate anyway? I would hate that!" With that he goes back to wiping the bar, but you notice that the smile is still there.

speaker: James
text: "Oh, thou shalt just come back again wanting something else from me! I just know it!"

speaker: Jeanette
text: This young, lovely tavern wench is sexy and sweet.

speaker: Jeanette
text: "Hello again!" bubbly Jeanette says.

speaker: Jeanette
text: "Jeanette, at thy service!"

speaker: Jeanette
text: "I work for Lucy at the Blue Boar. I serve food and drinks."

speaker: Jeanette
text: "If there is anything thou wouldst like, please say so! And, er, I shall give thee a discount if thou dost buy from me!"

speaker: Jeanette
text: "Why, Sir Dupre! How good to see thee again!"

speaker: Dupre
text: "Hello milady! I thought I might re-sample The Blue Boar's fine beverages!"

speaker: Jeanette
text: "Any time, milord! Any time!"

speaker: Jeanette
text: "I work during the day and evening hours. Thou shouldst come by the pub then and we shall talk more!"

speaker: Jeanette
text: "Lucy is a good cook. I recommend everything. Especially Silverleaf."

speaker: Jeanette
text: "Wonderful dish. Try it!"

speaker: Jeanette
text: "Thou dost look like thou dost need a good drink!"

speaker: Jeanette
text: "He spoke of me, did he? Well, he may think again! I cannot bring myself to socialize with the upper class. Those bourgeoisie rich men are obnoxious and egotistical. Besides, I am in love with another."

speaker: Jeanette
text: "They are all alike. They work in castles and have piles of gold and can have any woman they want! On the other hand, a humble merchant is the perfect man."

speaker: Jeanette
text: "'Tis Willy the Baker! But he does not know it yet!" she giggles.

speaker: Lucy
text: "A moment, Jeanette! Thou hast it all wrong! Charles is a -servant-! Thou art an ignoramus! Charles is not 'upper class'! He is as working class as thee! 'Tis Willy who is the rich merchant! If thou dost ask me, 'tis Willy who is obnoxious and egotistical. Charles is a dream!"

speaker: Jeanette
text: You point out to Jeanette that Charles is a servant.

speaker: Jeanette
text: Jeanette thinks about what was said. "Thou art right! I cannot believe I have been so blind! Oh, Charles! I can actually consider Charles! And he is... so handsome!" Jeanette squeals with delight. "I shall have to flirt with him in earnest next time he is in the pub!"

speaker: Jeanette
text: "Farewell!"

speaker: Amanda
text: You see an attractive woman dressed in armour and carrying a small arsenal of weapons with her.

speaker: Amanda
text: "How may I help thee?" asks Amanda.

speaker: Amanda
text: "My name is Amanda."

speaker: Amanda
text: "Mine half-sister and I have no job at this time. We are journeying to seek inner peace, now that our quest has been aborted."

speaker: Amanda
text: "Mine half-sister and I have no job but to serve our quest."

speaker: Amanda
text: "Mine half-sister is Eiko. She, like myself, is a warrior trained by Karenna in the ways of combat. We studied long and hard together to master the skills that <VAR> required to achieve our vengeance."

speaker: Eiko
text: "The two of us had not even met before our father's death. But we bonded like sisters in the rigorous disciplines we learned from our trainer, Karenna of Minoc."

speaker: Amanda
text: "Yes. Our lives have been dedicated to vengeance for so long that we feel adrift, aimless without it. We must find a new reason for living."

speaker: Amanda
text: "We are considering joining The Fellowship, as they offer guidance for lost souls. But we must consider this longer. We are still unsure."

speaker: Amanda
text: "We are on the trail of our father's murderer."

speaker: Amanda
text: "Our father was slain in a most violent manner by a vicious and terrible cyclops. He was impaled on a spear. It took several hours for him to die."

speaker: Amanda
text: She looks up, eyes glittering. "Hast thou ever watched anyone die from a belly wound, <HONORIFIC>? The agony cannot be imagined."

speaker: Amanda
text: "We have been tracking this creature for years, ever since we completed our training. We have followed him from one end of Britannia to another. Sometimes he was just one step ahead of us. But now we know that we are nearer to him than we have ever been before."

speaker: Eiko
text: "When we find him there shall be no escape. We want vengeance and we mean to have it!"

speaker: Amanda
text: "Our father fought bravely for his life. He did not die easily. He died a hero's death. Although we may both die in the effort, we intend to give his murderer a death fit for a true villain."

speaker: Eiko
text: Eiko smiles wickedly.

speaker: Amanda
text: You explain to Amanda what you have learned. Kalideth had gone mad when he fought with Iskander and the source of what is causing the problems with magic and the mage's minds - the thing that really killed Kalideth - has been destroyed.

speaker: Amanda
text: "Thou hast robbed me of my rightful vengeance! How dare thee!"

speaker: Eiko
text: Eiko sighs, and her shoulders slump. "Come now, sister. With the matter of our father's untimely death now settled we can at last let it go. Now we can devote our lives to ourselves rather than remain trapped in the past. It is for the best, thou must trust me."

speaker: Amanda
text: Amanda shakes her head, dazed and confused. "Perhaps thou art correct, Eiko. I must think."

speaker: Amanda
text: Amanda turns and slams her fist into the wall, then collapses onto it with a sob. After a moment, she straightens, but does not turn to face you.

speaker: Amanda
text: "Have no fear that I will continue my vengeance against the cyclops. I am not so far gone that I would kill a creature for acting in self-defense."

speaker: Amanda
text: "But I must have some time to myself now. Please, go. I must think."

speaker: Amanda
text: "Good journey to thee, <HONORIFIC>."

speaker: Denby
text: You see a fighter with intense eyes and a serious disposition.

speaker: Denby
text: "Yes, Avatar?" Denby asks.

speaker: Denby
text: "I am Denby."

speaker: Denby
text: "I am a trainer. I specialize in a form of combat which relies on one's ability to use intelligence and physical ability to activate minor magical effects. But I am not a mage. I am a fighter."

speaker: Denby
text: "For example, I simply teach a combination of physical and mental exercises which increases one's intelligence. This, in turn, gives one an advantage if one desires to practice magic."

speaker: Denby
text: "Thou shouldst be aware, however, that magic is not working in Britannia these days. It is a dying phenomenon. No one understands why. Nevertheless, my training should increase any magic user's primary chances for casting a spell, as well as their fighting skill."

speaker: Denby
text: "Although I am a fighter, I have dedicated my life to peace. There has been too much fighting in the world as it is. Let history take care of the adversarial qualities which exist in man. I believe in using my skills as a deterrent."

speaker: Denby
text: "My fee for training is 75 gold. Does this meet with the approval of thy purse strings?"

speaker: Denby
text: Denby bows. "I am sorry my fee is too high for thee. Perhaps at another time thou wilt realize the value of my services."

speaker: Denby
text: "Please return during daylight hours if thou dost wish to train."

speaker: Denby
text: Denby puts his palms together and bows.

speaker: Fred
text: You see a friendly-looking farmer who waves at you as you approach.

speaker: Fred
text: "Hello again, <HONORIFIC>." says Fred.

speaker: Fred
text: "My name is Fred."

speaker: Fred
text: "I sell meats here at the Farmer's Market in Britain."

speaker: Fred
text: "They are the tastiest meats that thou canst buy. Do thyself a favor and try some."

speaker: Fred
text: "Here at the Farmer's Market we sell vegetables bought from the farmers just outside of town, as well as meats from the slaughterhouse in Paws."

speaker: Fred
text: "It is run by a man named Morfin, a very successful merchant from Buccaneer's Den."

speaker: Fred
text: "Morfin is an unusual character. If I did not know any better I would say he was involved with a number of shady business activities."

speaker: Fred
text: "Morfin left that place because he saw all of the commerce that was developing there as competition to his own business activities and moved to Paws."

speaker: Fred
text: "Paws is a good place to go to buy things for low prices. Many of the people are rather poor, I am sorry to say. There is little active commerce there, however. In Paws, one must deal with people on a more personal level."

speaker: Fred
text: "Thou must return when the Farmer's Market is open."

speaker: Fred
text: "Wouldst thou like to buy some meats?"

speaker: Fred
text: "We have a fine selection of meats for thee today, <HONORIFIC>."

speaker: Fred
text: "Come back when thou art hungry and we shall serve thee then."

speaker: Fred
text: "Goodbye, <HONORIFIC>."

speaker: Kelly
text: You see a sturdy-looking farmer's wife. She gives you a hospitable smile before returning to her chores.

speaker: Kelly
text: "What brings us the pleasure of having thee back on this day, <HONORIFIC>?" says Kelly.

speaker: Kelly
text: "I am called Kelly, <HONORIFIC>."

speaker: Kelly
text: "Mine husband Fred and I run the Farmer's Market."

speaker: Kelly
text: "My Fred is one of the most respected merchants in Britain. He sells the eggs and vegetables grown by Brownie and Mack, as well as exotic imported fruits."

speaker: Kelly
text: "The Farmer's Market is where most of Britain buys its food. Why even the people in Paws will come here to buy eggs and vegetables. Fred has never raised the price of anything since opening this market many years ago."

speaker: Kelly
text: "Farmer Mack's chickens lay plenty of eggs. It is a good thing the people here have such healthy appetites!"

speaker: Kelly
text: "We sell those mostly to older people. Thou dost know, I am sure, how children do not like to eat their vegetables. Some people do not want to keep a lot of fruit in their home as they are afraid of attracting fruit flies."

speaker: Kelly
text: "Brownie is a good man. I do hope he runs for the mayorship again. If he does thou must be sure to vote for him."

speaker: Kelly
text: "I do believe that poor old Mack has been cooped up with his chickens for too long. He is a good person. Do not be put off by the strange stories he doth tell. He rarely ever sleeps as he spends most of the night staring at the sky. Of course his rooster crows at dawn and no farmer can afford to sleep past the dawn. So his mind is a bit ragged."

speaker: Kelly
text: "Oh, in Britain they look for quality produce. I see the people who buy here look over every egg for cracks and every vegetable for any sign of spoilage."

speaker: Kelly
text: "The people of Paws are always short of money. Mine heart goes out to them. They are always looking to buy the least expensive items for it is all they can afford."

speaker: Kelly
text: "The market is now closed. Thou must return when we are open for business."

speaker: Kelly
text: "Wouldst thou like to buy some eggs, fruits or vegetables? We have plenty of delicious fresh eggs here for thee. And our vegetables are sure to keep thee in good health."

speaker: Kelly
text: "I am sure we have something here that will be to thy liking."

speaker: Kelly
text: "Perhaps another time then."

speaker: Kelly
text: "Good day to thee, <HONORIFIC>."

speaker: Willy
text: You see a very clean-looking, portly young man who waves at you frantically.

speaker: Willy
text: "Ah, hello there! Good to see thee again!" says Willy.

speaker: Willy
text: "My given name is Wilhelm, although no one calls me that. I prefer to be addressed as Willy. Thank thee very much."

speaker: Willy
text: "I am the baker here in Britain and I make the sweetest bread thou hast ever tasted! "

speaker: Willy
text: "Hast thou had a chance to sample any of my bread yet?"

speaker: Willy
text: "Ah, then thou dost agree it is the sweetest, dost thou not?"

speaker: Willy
text: "Ha! Thou dost see, then? Everyone agrees! That should be proof enough!"

speaker: Spark
text: "I want some!"

speaker: Willy
text: "Here thou art, laddie." Willy hands Spark a pastry and the boy devours it in one gulp.

speaker: Spark
text: "Mmmmm! I say, <PLAYER_NAME>, I think we need a lot of this for the road. We had best buy some, all right?"

speaker: Willy
text: "Thou dost not?! Why, do not be ridiculous! Of course thou dost!"

speaker: Willy
text: "Then here, thou must have some!" He tears a piece of bread off of one of several loaves he is carrying and stuffs it into your mouth. "There! Is it not the sweetest bread thou hast ever tasted? It is, is it not?!" You chew as fast as you can in order to answer him.

speaker: Willy
text: He grabs your face by the cheeks and plants a big kiss on your forehead. "Thou art truly a person of good palate and refined taste!"

speaker: Willy
text: Dejectedly Willy looks down at the loaf of bread he is carrying. He sniffs at it twice and tosses it out of sight.

speaker: Willy
text: "Please come to the bakery when it is open in daytime hours and thou shalt sample some!"

speaker: Willy
text: He nods. "Yes, I am a baker and I have many secret recipes passed down to me by my father and mother. Why, there are even those who say I am a master baker!"

speaker: Willy
text: "And there are those who call me a... doughnut," he says with a frown.

speaker: Willy
text: "Oh, dear. Do not tell me that thou art yet another person who is trying to pry one of my secret recipes out of me! If that is what thou art after then thou wilt just be disappointed!"

speaker: Willy
text: Willy wipes away a tear. "Gone. Both of them. Gone to join mine ancestors in that great kitchen in the sky. I will never be able to cook as they did. Still I plod along, trying to keep the family name alive, and that is why I am a baker. But I suppose it is not the only reason."

speaker: Willy
text: "Yes, many people tell me that. Now thou dost say it, too. If thou dost say so, then it must be true!"

speaker: Willy
text: Willy takes a bite of his own bread. "Mmmm. I -am- a master baker!"

speaker: Willy
text: He gives you a long puzzled look. After a moment he takes one of his loaves of bread and swats you over the head with it.

speaker: Willy
text: "Actually, there is a very good reason why I am a baker."

speaker: Willy
text: "Because the way to a woman's heart is through her stomach. Why, I have two women in love with me right now and I did not even have to pursue either one."

speaker: Willy
text: He sighs. "If thou must know, their names are Jeanette and Gaye."

speaker: Willy
text: "Jeanette is a pleasant enough girl, but to be honest I cannot see myself with a tavern wench. She thinks I have not noticed how she feels about me. Frankly, I wish she would just leave me alone."

speaker: Willy
text: "Gaye, who runs the costume shoppe, is of more interest to me. But she is a Fellowship member and I have no wish to become one. I hope that it does not prevent us from courting."

speaker: Willy
text: "My bread is the finest in Britannia. It is renown for both its pleasant taste and its very reasonable price. But it is a lot of work making enough to satisfy the constant demand for it. I need to hire someone to help me."

speaker: Willy
text: "I not only have bread for sale, but pastries, cakes and rolls as well. The most delicious baked goods thou couldst ever wish to pop into thy mouth! Wouldst thou like to buy some?"

speaker: Willy
text: "If thou wert a person of truly refined taste, thou wouldst buy some!"

speaker: Willy
text: "I am afraid the bakery is closed. Please come back during normal business hours."

speaker: Willy
text: "Thou couldst work for me here in the shoppe making bread. Or I will buy sacks of flour from thee. Thou couldst buy them wholesale in Paws, and I will pay thee 4 gold per sack."

speaker: Willy
text: "Dost thou wish to work here in the shoppe for me?" Willy asks hopefully.

speaker: Willy
text: "Excellent! Thou canst start work immediately! I shall pay thee 5 gold for every five loaves of bread thou dost make. All right?"

speaker: Willy
text: "First thou must make dough from the flour. Simply spread some flour out on the table, add some water to make it thick and, well, doughy. Then use the dough in the oven to bake it. Wait a bit, then-- voila! Thou dost have bread!"

speaker: Willy
text: "Very well. But I warn thee that employment is hard to obtain in these times!"

speaker: Willy
text: "'Tis a pity thou art unavailable. Thou dost look like one who doth know their way around a kitchen."

speaker: Willy
text: "I would be happy to talk with thee about employment at my shoppe during normal business hours."

speaker: Willy
text: "Good day to thee, <HONORIFIC>, and bon appetit!"

speaker: Gaye
text: Gaye is watching the Fellowship meeting. She turns to you brusquely and puts a finger to her lips, gesturing for you to be silent.

speaker: Gaye
text: "I cannot imagine where Batlin is. I am worried about him..."

speaker: Gaye
text: "I cannot speak now! I am on my way to the Fellowship meeting at the Hall!"

speaker: Gaye
text: You see a woman who oozes partially sincere friendliness.

speaker: Gaye
text: "Hello again, and what may I do for thee today?" asks Gaye.

speaker: Gaye
text: "My name is Gaye."

speaker: Gaye
text: "I oversee the clothier's here in Britain when I am not pursuing the teachings of The Fellowship."

speaker: Gaye
text: "At our clothier's shop we have the finest silks and garments to buy that thou hast ever seen, imported from every corner of Britannia to cater to all tastes."

speaker: Gaye
text: "I am so sorry, the clothier's shop is closed. Please return during our regular business hours. We are open from nine until six every day."

speaker: Gaye
text: "Do not tell me! Raymundo sent thee to get an Avatar costume! They cost thirty gold coins. Dost thou want one?"

speaker: Gaye
text: She looks you up and down. "Yes, I think we might be able to find something for thee."

speaker: Gaye
text: After several minutes of rummaging through the store, Gaye returns. "Here it is! Not many left-- we have had a run on them recently!"

speaker: Gaye
text: "Um. Perhaps thou couldst return when thou dost have enough gold." She lays the costume down and smiles.

speaker: Gaye
text: "Oh. Thou canst not carry this with what thou art already carrying. Mayhaps thou couldst dispose of something and return for the costume."

speaker: Gaye
text: "It is, indeed, a pleasure to do business with thee, O great Avatar!" She grins and hands you the costume.

speaker: Gaye
text: "'Tis strange! I thought for certain that thou wert the theatrical type!"

speaker: Gaye
text: "Wouldst thou like to buy some clothing today?"

speaker: Gaye
text: "We have many nice clothes to choose from."

speaker: Gaye
text: "Thou mayest look around for thyself. If thou dost change thy mind be sure to let me know."

speaker: Gaye
text: "Thou wouldst want to attend the Fellowship meeting tonight at nine o'clock. It is always a moving experience to hear the words of Batlin, our founder."

speaker: Gaye
text: "Yes, he is a very amusing fellow. I am quite taken with him and I do see him against my better judgment. He does not seem like the type to join The Fellowship, though. Since The Fellowship is my whole life, I do not know if there is a place in it for him. I have not made up my mind about that yet."

speaker: Gaye
text: "Good day, <HONORIFIC>."

speaker: Coop
text: Coop is onstage with The Avatars. He sees you and says, "Uhm, there is someone special listening tonight, and this next tune is dedicated to them."

speaker: Coop
text: He signals to his partners and they begin to play. He sings the following lyrics:

speaker: Coop
text: "Across the country we do fly -- "

speaker: Coop
text: Best to heed our battle cry!

speaker: Coop
text: "We fight for virtues, far and wide, "

speaker: Coop
text: "And we cause the damsel's sigh."

speaker: Coop
text: Then Neno and Judith join in on the chorus:

speaker: Coop
text: "Oh, Avatars are we "

speaker: Coop
text: And virtuous we doth be!

speaker: Coop
text: "Beware ye ogre and ye beast "

speaker: Coop
text: Lest thou be served at our next feast!

speaker: Coop
text: "We rescue damsels, oh so fair, "

speaker: Coop
text: And battle pirates on a dare!

speaker: Coop
text: "No evil liche doth daunt or sway! "

speaker: Coop
text: Against them all we win the day!

speaker: Coop
text: "We are the Av-atars! "

speaker: Coop
text: We are the Av-atars!

speaker: Coop
text: "We are the Aaaa-Vaaa-Taaars!"

speaker: Coop
text: The applause is tumultuous.

speaker: Iolo
text: "Hmmm. They must have seen thee coming, <HONORIFIC>."

speaker: Coop
text: "Must not stop to speak now! I am late for a performance of The Avatars! Come and hear us play at The Blue Boar!"

speaker: Coop
text: You see a young, wiry teen.

speaker: Iolo
text: "Hello, lad! This is <PLAYER_NAME>, the Avatar! This is my young apprentice, Coop. How go things, Coop?"

speaker: Coop
text: "Not too badly, milord. I sold a triple crossbow this morning."

speaker: Iolo
text: "Lovely! Lovely! Keep that gold coming in, that's what I always say!"

speaker: Coop
text: "Hello!" Coop says.

speaker: Coop
text: "My name is Coop."

speaker: Coop
text: "I am the manager of Iolo's Bows! Master Iolo has entrusted me with this responsibility!"

speaker: Coop
text: "If there is anything thou dost want in the way of bows and arrows, please say so!"

speaker: Coop
text: "Thou must come by the shoppe when it is open!"

speaker: Coop
text: "Iolo opened this shoppe many, many years ago. He opened Iolo's South in Serpent's Hold more recently. He is becoming quite an entrepreneur!"

speaker: Coop
text: "I sell many goods but I also plan to perpetuate the good name of Iolo by becoming a master archer! Iolo has taught me well!"

speaker: Iolo
text: "Yes, the lad is good! He was good before I taught him the first lesson."

speaker: Coop
text: "What I would not give to join thy group and go adventuring! But, then there would be no one to run the shoppe. So I cannot go. But someday... Anyway, I please myself in the evenings by singing with a musical group."

speaker: Coop
text: "Hello, boss!"

speaker: Iolo
text: "Greetings, lad. Thou art looking well."

speaker: Coop
text: "The same to thee, milord!"

speaker: Coop
text: "My group is called... well, it is called 'The Avatars'. I hope that does not offend thee."

speaker: Coop
text: "The band is just me and two musicians from The Music Hall. We play at the Blue Boar every night. I sing and write lyrics. The other two play the instruments. Please come to hear us!"

speaker: Coop
text: "We sell all kinds of bows, along with arrows and bolts. If thou dost wish to buy something, please say so!"

speaker: Coop
text: "Goodbye!"

speaker: Grayson
text: Grayson shushes you, as you are disturbing the Fellowship meeting.

speaker: Grayson
text: "Now where could that Batlin be? I suppose we shall have to have the meeting without him!"

speaker: Grayson
text: "I must run! I must run! I must! I must! I am late for the Fellowship meeting!"

speaker: Grayson
text: You see a shrewd-looking man who smiles as if he has just seen his next customer.

speaker: Grayson
text: "Hello again, my good friend," says Grayson.

speaker: Grayson
text: "I am Grayson, <HONORIFIC>. A humble and honest man."

speaker: Grayson
text: "Why, here in Britain I sell the best armour and weapons that money can buy. In my spare time, I do deeds for The Fellowship."

speaker: Grayson
text: Grayson looks you up and down. "Dost thou truly believe that thou art sufficiently protected in what thou art wearing? In truth I fear for thy safety if thou shouldst become involved in combat. Are thou interested in buying something today?"

speaker: Grayson
text: "Another time, then."

speaker: Grayson
text: After looking at you, Grayson says, "I can see that thou art in sore need of weaponry. Dost thou want to buy something today?"

speaker: Grayson
text: "Another time, then."

speaker: Grayson
text: "I sell a complete line of armour and weapons."

speaker: Grayson
text: "Which wouldst thou care to inspect?"

speaker: Grayson
text: "Please come to the shop when it is open."

speaker: Grayson
text: "I see that thou art a member of The Fellowship!"

speaker: Grayson
text: "It has been very beneficial in my life. I was on the verge of going out of business before I joined and now I am more prosperous than ever before."

speaker: Grayson
text: "I was never sufficiently forward or aggressive enough to be successful as a merchant but The Fellowship changed all that for me."

speaker: Grayson
text: "By applying the values of the Triad of Inner Strength to my life I have accomplished what I have set out to do with my life. Mine armour and weapon shop is successful and I have a place where I belong in The Fellowship."

speaker: Grayson
text: "Thou dost see, I am convinced that my failures were all due to my bad attitude. It took the teachings of The Fellowship to change the way I used my mind and to turn me in the proper direction."

speaker: Grayson
text: "Goodbye and farewell, <HONORIFIC>."

speaker: Diane
text: You see a pleasant-looking young peasant woman.

speaker: Diane
text: "Greetings to thee, <HONORIFIC>," says Diane.

speaker: Diane
text: "My name is Diane."

speaker: Diane
