text: "My job is to oversee the stables here in Britain and sell thee a horse and carriage if thou dost want one."

speaker: Diane
text: "Here thou wilt find a selection of the finest horses produced by Lord British's personal horse breeder. If thou dost wish to buy one, I am sure we can come to some sort of arrangement. They come with a carriage, of course."

speaker: Diane
text: "Britain is such a grand city, but it can be somewhat disconcerting if thou dost not know anyone. Fortunately, I know many people here."

speaker: Diane
text: "The horse and carriage combination sells for 120 gold. Thou shalt find it in a small shelter just south of the stables, across the street. Dost thou want a title?"

speaker: Diane
text: "Very good. Here is thy title."

speaker: Diane
text: "Oh, my. Thine hands are too full to take the title!"

speaker: Diane
text: "Oh. Thou dost not have enough gold to buy the title."

speaker: Diane
text: "Some other time, then."

speaker: Diane
text: "I have many friends in Britannia. Among them are Greg, James, Brownie and Mack."

speaker: Diane
text: "Greg runs a shop that sells provisions. If thou art planning any sort of expedition he is just the person to see. He seems to be lucky. Perhaps some of it will rub off on thee."

speaker: Diane
text: "James, who runs an inn not far from here, wanted a life of adventure. His family wanted him to run the inn after his father died and he has been discontent ever since. Still, I think he fancies Cynthia who works at the Mint."

speaker: Diane
text: "Brownie is a decent and honest man who would have made a much better mayor than Patterson if thou dost want mine opinion. He uses our horses to plow his fields in the spring."

speaker: Diane
text: "One word of warning about Mack. Do not let him start talking about the sky. Other than that he is perfectly fine, I can assure thee."

speaker: Diane
text: Diane notices your Fellowship medallion. "It is odd. If thou dost not mind me saying so, thou dost not seem like a Fellowship member. There is something about thee. I cannot place it."

speaker: Diane
text: "Good day to thee, <HONORIFIC>."

speaker: Clint
text: Before you stands an old sailing man whose determined face appears to have weathered many a storm.

speaker: Clint
text: "And what be thy business with me this time, <HONORIFIC>?" says Clint.

speaker: Clint
text: "I be Clint."

speaker: Clint
text: "In my youth I was a sailor who sailed across the sea in tall ships. Now I must content myself solely with selling ships and sextants to others."

speaker: Clint
text: "Of course this was in the day when it took mighty men to be a sailor. Nowadays those who set out to sea would not have lasted a day. But I suppose it is the nature of the universe that everything slowly becomes more tame."

speaker: Clint
text: "Soon all the monsters will die off and the whole world will join together in trust and worthiness and unity like all those Fellowship people say. Bah! The world was a better place when everybody fought everybody else, I say."

speaker: Clint
text: "No offense intended, of course. I did not realize that thou art a member." Clint reacts as if he has just touched a leper.

speaker: Clint
text: "It is always the best thing to make thine own way in the world and not listen to what thou art told to believe. Thou hast better remember that!"

speaker: Clint
text: "If thou art in need of a ship I hold the deed to a fine one. Thou wilt also need a sextant to help steer her true."

speaker: Clint
text: "My business is now closed. Return another time and I will be happy to serve thee, <HONORIFIC>."

speaker: Clint
text: "I do believe I sold thee the deed to 'The Beast'! What happened to it? Hast thou lost the ship? If so, then thou must find another shipwright!"

speaker: Clint
text: "The deed to the ship 'The Beast' costs eight hundred gold pieces. Dost thou wish to purchase her?"

speaker: Clint
text: "Here is thy deed, <HONORIFIC>."

speaker: Clint
text: "I would give thee thy deed but thou art carrying too much to take it from me!"

speaker: Clint
text: "Thou dost not have enough gold to buy a ship!"

speaker: Clint
text: "If thou dost need a ship be sure to come back here."

speaker: Clint
text: "A sextant costs one hundred gold pieces. Does thou wish to buy one?"

speaker: Clint
text: "Here is thy sextant. She shall steer thee true, to be sure."

speaker: Clint
text: "I would give thee thy sextant, but thou art carrying too much to take it from me."

speaker: Clint
text: "Thou dost not have enough money to buy a sextant!"

speaker: Clint
text: "If thou shouldst ever need a sextant be sure to come back."

speaker: Clint
text: "The Crown Jewel came to Britain? Not anytime recently. Most certainly not. I remember the Crown Jewel and it has not been to Britain for a long time."

speaker: Clint
text: "As I have told thee before, the Crown Jewel has not been here in a long time."

speaker: Clint
text: "May thy travels do well."

speaker: Gordon
text: Gordon is too involved in listening to the Fellowship meeting to hear you.

speaker: Gordon
text: "Where oh where is Batlin? He is late for the meeting!"

speaker: Gordon
text: "Oh, my! I must leave immediately! I am late for the Fellowship meeting!"

speaker: Gordon
text: You see a friendly face looking back at you.

speaker: Gordon
text: "How art thou this fine day, <HONORIFIC>?" asks Gordon.

speaker: Gordon
text: "My name is Gordon."

speaker: Gordon
text: "I sell fish and chips from my wagon."

speaker: Gordon
text: "Come back later when I am open for business."

speaker: Gordon
text: "I have the best fish and chips thou shalt taste in all of Britannia. My price is only 8 gold coins per serving. Wouldst thou like to have some?"

speaker: Gordon
text: He hands you a plate.

speaker: Gordon
text: "They are indeed the best fish and chips in all of Britannia."

speaker: Gordon
text: "Thou art carrying too many things to take thy fish and chips from me!"

speaker: Gordon
text: "Thou dost not have enough gold to get any fish and chips. Sorry!"

speaker: Gordon
text: "Come back again when thou art hungry and I am sure thou shalt change thy mind."

speaker: Gordon
text: "I just painted my wagon recently. It receives more attention. Business is much better now. I am saving my money to travel to Buccaneer's Den."

speaker: Gordon
text: "Ever since I became a member of The Fellowship, business has been increasing steadily. I have refined and improved the recipe for my fish batter and it has since become a favorite meal of nearly everyone in Britain. I have even served my fish and chips to Lord British himself."

speaker: Gordon
text: "Thou dost know-- the bloke who wears a crown and acts like a king."

speaker: Gordon
text: "I am glad to see that thou art a member. Will I see thee at the next meeting?"

speaker: Gordon
text: "Then I shall see thee at nine o'clock sharp!"

speaker: Gordon
text: "Thou shouldst apply thyself more stringently to the ways of The Fellowship! Our meeting is at nine o'clock. I can see thou dost certainly need to attend."

speaker: Gordon
text: "I wish to win some money at Buccaneer's Den. It is a pirate resort and they have a fabulous House of Games there."

speaker: Gordon
text: "As I am certain thou knowest, Buccaneer's Den was once a den of thieves and villains. As such, it held a romantic appeal for those who longed for a taste of such an adventurous existence. I confess, I am one of those people. When thou dost spend thy life selling fish from a wagon, thou art in need of excitement. The pirates eventually realized just how much they are secretly envied, and so they have turned their island into a place of thrilling amusements."

speaker: Gordon
text: "It is said they have several games of chance there! Gold can be won wagering on the outcome of a race of fine stallions."

speaker: Gordon
text: "I saw thee receive thy medallion. I can certainly say the Fellowship has done wonders for my life and I know it will be the same for thee as well." He gives thee a knowing grin.

speaker: Gordon
text: "Have a pleasant day, <HONORIFIC>."

speaker: Sean
text: Sean is deep in concentration, listening to the Fellowship meeting.

speaker: Sean
text: "I cannot imagine where Batlin is. He never misses Fellowship meeting!"

speaker: Sean
text: "I must not stop to speak now! I am late for the Fellowship meeting!"

speaker: Sean
text: You see a man whose boyish face is set with scrutinizing eyes that look as if they have seen much.

speaker: Sean
text: "And what may I do for thee, <HONORIFIC>?" asks Sean.

speaker: Sean
text: "My name is Sean."

speaker: Sean
text: "When not tending to Fellowship affairs, I am a jeweller here in Britain. If thou dost wish to buy something, say so!"

speaker: Sean
text: "It is very delicate work. It requires a special touch that only a few have. Thou must know precisely how to handle precious materials. Only the finest of craftsmen become jewellers and they receive the highest compensation."

speaker: Sean
text: "I constantly require new materials with which to create my very special jewelry. I am always in the market to buy gems. If thou dost ever come across any, I am the man to come to if thou shouldst want to sell them and make money."

speaker: Sean
text: "As I have told thee, only the finest of craftsmen become jewellers, and I am the finest of jewellers. Does that not tell thee something?" Sean sniffs. "My business makes more money than the mint!" He laughs forcibly.

speaker: Sean
text: "The jeweller's shop is currently closed for business. Come back later!"

speaker: Sean
text: "Dost thou have a gem for sale?"

speaker: Sean
text: "I will pay thee 30 gold coins per gem. Is that price agreeable?"

speaker: Sean
text: "Dost thou think me a fool?! This little blue bauble is worthless!"

speaker: Sean
text: Sean's face tightens. "This gem is small and dark as the heart of an unholy Liche. Away with it!"

speaker: Sean
text: "Thou dost have no gems! Thou art a liar! I will do no business with thee!"

speaker: Sean
text: "I see that thou has one gem."

speaker: Sean
text: "I see that thou hast <VAR> gems."

speaker: Sean
text: "Here is thy payment."

speaker: Sean
text: "Thou art carrying too much to take thy payment!"

speaker: Sean
text: "It seems we have little left to discuss then."

speaker: Sean
text: "If thou dost have no gems for sale then do not even waste my time by mentioning it!"

speaker: Sean
text: "I see thou art a member!" Sean suddenly looks at you with a bit more respect. "I am sure The Fellowship will do thee a world of good in the future." He smiles condescendingly.

speaker: Sean
text: "Even thou mayest join The Fellowship and I can tell thee more about it."

speaker: Sean
text: "I can tell thee about The Fellowship's philosophy if thou dost wish."

speaker: Sean
text: "Thou art really interested in hearing more?"

speaker: Sean
text: "I thought I was wasting my breath on thee."

speaker: Sean
text: "I moved mine entire business here to Britain to be near the main branch of The Fellowship. Thou hast no idea how much my business improved after I joined The Fellowship."

speaker: Sean
text: "Wouldst thou like to buy something?"

speaker: Sean
text: "Then please browse if thou dost like."

speaker: Sean
text: "Please come to the shop during normal business hours."

speaker: Sean
text: "I am sure thou must be on thy way." Sean smiles.

speaker: Brownie
text: You see a farmer who, despite showing considerable wear from hard work, appears energetic, cheerful and friendly.

speaker: Brownie
text: "Hello again, <HONORIFIC>," Brownie greets you.

speaker: Brownie
text: "I am Brownie."

speaker: Brownie
text: "Well, I ran for the office of Mayor of Britain once, but I lost. Now I am back doing what I have been doing since I was a boy. Working the farm."

speaker: Brownie
text: "Patterson won the election. He spent a lot of money on his campaign. Most of it to buy votes. But I am not bitter. I was just not meant to be Mayor."

speaker: Brownie
text: "Patterson courted the support of The Fellowship. They forced a vote from all their members. Once word spread, my support drained away. No one wants to be on the losing side." Brownie sighs.

speaker: Brownie
text: "I do not really have any wish to succeed in politics. It just made me ill seeing all of the people with riches mistreat all of the people who are poor, and then have to listen to them talk about how the class system has been abolished."

speaker: Brownie
text: Brownie gestures toward your medallion. "Frankly, I do not know what thou seest in that group."

speaker: Brownie
text: "If thou art not with The Fellowship thou art against them. I think they saw me as a potential enemy that had to be stopped."

speaker: Brownie
text: "Of course, I could have won the election if I had wanted to. I had information about Patterson that would have ruined any chances of him winning."

speaker: Brownie
text: "I could have revealed a secret about Patterson but if I did it would have hurt someone close to him very much. I did not want to be mayor that badly."

speaker: Brownie
text: "Patterson does little to hide his secret. If thou dost keep an eye on him thou wilt surely learn of it sooner or later."

speaker: Brownie
text: "I feel more at home on the farm growing vegetables. There is another farmer named Mack who works a farm near Britain as well. He raises chickens."

speaker: Brownie
text: "I like him. He even voted for me. But to tell thee the truth about Mack, he is a lunatic."

speaker: Brownie
text: "I raise pumpkins. But I am in a bind at the moment and need some help."

speaker: Brownie
text: "I strained my back the other day lifting heavy pumpkins. I cannot so much as lift a small one today! And I need help with the harvest of pumpkins so that I can get them to the market."

speaker: Brownie
text: "There are piles of pumpkins at the north end of the field. I need them brought down near my farmhouse. If thou wilt help me by bringing the pumpkins to me, I will gladly pay thee for thy work. How does one gold coin for every pumpkin carried sound?"

speaker: Brownie
text: "How nice! A helper! Please, feel free to start work at any time!"

speaker: Brownie
text: "Perhaps some other time, then."

speaker: Brownie
text: "Thou shouldst simply go to the north end of the field and bring back as many pumpkins as thou can carry!"

speaker: Brownie
text: "Good day, <HONORIFIC>."

speaker: Mack
text: You see a farmer with wild eyes widened in excitement.

speaker: Mack
text: "Avatar! Thou hast returned!" exclaims Mack.

speaker: Mack
text: "I am Mack."

speaker: Mack
text: "I am a farmer, though most folks just call me a lunatic."

speaker: Mack
text: "On my farm I raise chickens and grow vegetables. If thou dost need work, talk to me!"

speaker: Mack
text: "Thou dost also think so, eh? But I tell thee what I say is true! There are creatures visiting us from another place in the stars! I have seen them!"

speaker: Mack
text: "They are big mean ugly liontigers! Or is that tigerlions? They are ferocious and they want to eat us!"

speaker: Mack
text: "All I can say is that there are certainly no such creatures in this world! Nor is their ship like any that has ever been seen anywhere in Britannia."

speaker: Mack
text: "With mine own eyes I have seen a star creature and the inexplicable conveyance which enabled it to travel to Britannia! I swear to thee! I am completely sane! I have proof!"

speaker: Mack
text: "Go and look behind my farm in the middle of the field. Take a look for thyself and thou shalt see my proof."

speaker: Mack
text: "I told thee I was not a looney! Didst thou see the proof?"

speaker: Mack
text: "Thou must go and look at what is in my field! Then come back here, for I must talk about this with someone who knows that I am not a looney!"

speaker: Mack
text: "Did I not tell thee that I am no loonie? Still, my story of how I did come across this thing is beyond belief."

speaker: Mack
text: "I like to stay up late. Sometimes I see bright lights flash across the sky. No one else ever pays them any mind. But one night I see this bright light come crashing down and it lands in my field."

speaker: Mack
text: "I have been looking every night for another sign of those things but I have not seen any since that last time I told thee about it."

speaker: Mack
text: "I always watch for moving bright lights in the night sky. That is part of why people in the town say I am a loonie. But is what I do so different from what they do in the orrery?"

speaker: Mack
text: "After the explosion and crash I ran out to my field. There I saw the strange machine that thou hast seen, only it was glowing hot. I was terrified. But then the top of the machine started to open."

speaker: Mack
text: "It resembled a bird, but it was not a bird!"

speaker: Mack
text: "I could not move from the spot as I saw the strange ship open. From out of the top came the vicious tigerlion. There was a savage hunger in its eyes."

speaker: Mack
text: "In other words, it looked like it might eat me!"

speaker: Mack
text: "It came at me like a predator comes after prey. It was so fast that I could not even move. I thought I was going to be killed for certain. It reached me in a second. It looked into mine eyes, and then it died."

speaker: Mack
text: "What it and I had failed to notice was that I was holding mine hoe. It had once been accidentally enchanted by a passing mage, and it works wondrously in the fields. I use it for everything! The tigerlion had run itself through upon it. As it died, the thing spoke."

speaker: Mack
text: "It said two words. "Kill Wrathy." I do not know who this Wrathy person is, or why the tigerlion wanted me to kill him. But I do know I sure get worried now whenever I see moving lights in the night sky."

speaker: Mack
text: "I am sure thou dost know about the plague of looniness that has come to afflict all of the mages in the world. It was several years ago that I brought my broken hoe to a mage called Mumb. Fixing things was all he was good for anymore. There was also some fighter who wanted Mumb to enchant his sword, turning it into "The Sword of Death". It appears poor Mumb got confused and that fighter came back and killed him because the man wound up with a sword that was only good for cutting weeds. I could never figure out exactly what happened. It appears that old Mumb made mine hoe into the Hoe of Destruction! Unfortunately, the hoe is lost."

speaker: Mack
text: "Well, 'tis not really lost. It is locked up in my shed. It is the key to the shed that is lost! I think I might have accidentally used it as a fishhook when I was fishing on the banks of Lock Lake. So now I cannot get into my shed. One would think I -am- a looney!"

speaker: Mack
text: "I am quite certain that was it, or something like that. Anyway the tigerlion itself proved to be quite delicious."

speaker: Mack
text: "I need someone to work for me and help gather all the eggs being laid by the chickens! When that big thing came crashing down it scared them all so much that they cannot stop laying eggs! Wilt thou work for me? I will pay thee 1 gold per egg."

speaker: Mack
text: "Fine! Thou wilt find the chickens out back. Thou must feel around in the nest to find the eggs that are there. But there is a limit to how many they will produce in one day, of course."

speaker: Mack
text: "Ask me again if thou dost change thy mind."

speaker: Mack
text: "I thank thee for thy decency and consideration."

speaker: Snaz
text: You see a filthy beggar who flashes you a grin as though you were his best friend in the whole world.

speaker: Snaz
text: "Hello again, <HONORIFIC>," says Snaz.

speaker: Snaz
text: "I am called Snaz."

speaker: Snaz
text: "I have no job for I am a beggar. For a gold coin I shall tell thee a joke."

speaker: Snaz
text: "When I was just a little boy I was made an orphan and left homeless and penniless. That was a joke life played on me. 'Tis a funny joke, eh?"

speaker: Snaz
text: "But I would not charge thee a gold piece for that one."

speaker: Snaz
text: "Dost thou wish to hear one?"

speaker: Snaz
text: "All right, here is one..."

speaker: Snaz
text: "If thou dost want to hear a joke, thou must pay me, <HONORIFIC>. Come back when thy pockets are full. The richer thou art, the funnier I get!"

speaker: Snaz
text: "Have a heart, I pray thee! I have a wife and six hungry children to feed." He feels your stare upon him. "Oh, very well. Wouldst thou believe I have a cat and it just had kittens?"

speaker: Snaz
text: "I was discussing philosophy with a Fellowship member the other day and he asked me, 'What, in thine opinion, is the height of stupidity?'"

speaker: Snaz
text: "So I said, 'I do not know. How tall art thou?'"

speaker: Snaz
text: "No, really, I make sport of The Fellowship, but I mean it sincerely..."

speaker: Snaz
text: "That is what I dearly love about The Fellowship. They could always take a joke!"

speaker: Snaz
text: "And from what I hear they play funny jokes themselves! Like the joke they played in Trinsic!"

speaker: Snaz
text: "For a gold coin I will tell thee another. Dost thou wish to hear it?"

speaker: Snaz
text: "I see I have reached the limits of thy sense of humor."

speaker: Snaz
text: "I was at the castle of Lord British the other day and I noticed he has three large pools. So I asked why he doth have three of them."

speaker: Snaz
text: "He pointed to the first one and said the first was to swim in cool water. "

speaker: Snaz
text: "The second was for friends to swim in warm water."

speaker: Snaz
text: "I noticed that the third pool was empty and I asked him why."

speaker: Snaz
text: "He said that it was for people who could not swim!"

speaker: Snaz
text: "Thou art more destitute than I! If I tell thee any more jokes now thou mayest steal mine act!"

speaker: Snaz
text: "Poor Lord British! When faced with a gigantic menace that threatens his entire kingdom he is an extremely capable ruler."

speaker: Snaz
text: "But what happens when there are a myriad of smaller things that all threaten the welfare of his people indirectly?"

speaker: Snaz
text: "There is a riddle for thee to solve!"

speaker: Snaz
text: "For a gold coin I will tell thee another. Dost thou wish to hear it?"

speaker: Snaz
text: "Very well. If thou didst not get the first two there is no good reason for me to continue now."

speaker: Snaz
text: "A man named Weston came to me deep in perplexity."

speaker: Snaz
text: "He told me he wanted to steal some apples from the Royal Orchards but if he did he would feel bad about it in the morning."

speaker: Snaz
text: "So I gave him this advice -- sleep until noon!"

speaker: Snaz
text: "Thy pockets are empty, <HONORIFIC>. Perhaps it is time to stop laughing and start worrying!"

speaker: Snaz
text: "Weston now sits in the castle prison, where he shall most certainly rot for the rest of his life. Heh-heh-heh! "

speaker: Snaz
text: "Try as I might, I cannot best that little jest!"

speaker: Snaz
text: "For a gold coin I will tell thee another. Dost thou wish to hear it?"

speaker: Snaz
text: "Thou art wise. Thou shouldst save thy gold to pay a healer to cure that ache in thy side."

speaker: Snaz
text: "Whilst travelling on the road I came across a mage."

speaker: Snaz
text: "He looked as if he had not eaten for days and complained of a terrible pain in his stomach."

speaker: Snaz
text: "So I told him his stomach was empty. If he put something in it he would feel better."

speaker: Snaz
text: "Later he complained to me of a headache. I said his headache was caused by a similar	problem as his stomach."

speaker: Snaz
text: "No doubt it did hurt him so because, being a mage, there was nothing left in it!"

speaker: Snaz
text: "Now thou art playing a joke on me. Thou art broke!"

speaker: Snaz
text: "All of the mages have gone daft or mad! What other proper response is there in a world that is so terrifically funny?!"

speaker: Snaz
text: "Thou art a brave Avatar! Dost thou wish to hear another?"

speaker: Snaz
text: "Aha! Not as brave as I thought!"

speaker: Snaz
text: "Didst thou knowest that the notorious Sullivan the Trickster recently became a father?"

speaker: Snaz
text: "It is true! They say the baby has his father's eyes and his mother's nose, but they made the baby give them back."

speaker: Snaz
text: "Thou mayest be laughing but surely thy purse is not, for it is empty."

speaker: Snaz
text: "Yes, I know the man they call Sullivan the Trickster! In fact thou dost remind me of him!"

speaker: Snaz
text: "Or does he remind me of thee?"

speaker: Snaz
text: "He is so tricky that just talking about him has caused me to trick myself! Heh-Hee-Haa!"

speaker: Snaz
text: "I have amused thee so far! Wouldst thou like to hear another? It is a joke about gold!"

speaker: Snaz
text: "Thank thee very much! Now, goodbye!"

speaker: Snaz
text: "Dost thou get it? Ha! Ha! Ha! Ha! If not, it would be my pleasure to repeat it."

speaker: Snaz
text: "Wouldst thou like to hear the gold joke again?"

speaker: Snaz
text: "Now listen carefully..."

speaker: Snaz
text: "Oh, I am so sorry. I cannot tell thee the joke again for thou art out of money."

speaker: Snaz
text: "I see thou art becoming wise to the ways of show business, <HONORIFIC>. Good day to thee!"

speaker: Snaz
text: "I can see thou art so poor that thou cannot even afford a sense of humor!"

speaker: Snaz
text: "Oh, it is a pity that thou dost not wish to hear it! It is the funniest one yet and my personal favorite!"

speaker: Snaz
text: "I do hope I did amuse thee."

speaker: Millie
text: Millie ignores your attempts to get her attention and goes back to intently watching the Fellowship ceremony.

speaker: Millie
text: Millie looks perturbed. "Batlin has never missed a meeting before. What does he expect? Does he want -me- to run the meeting?"

speaker: Millie
text: "Sorry, I cannot speak with thee now! I am late for the Fellowship meeting!"

speaker: Millie
text: You see a cute-looking woman who beams with a huge smile when she notices you looking at her.

speaker: Millie
text: "It is good to speak with thee, again," says Millie.

speaker: Millie
text: "My name is Millie," she giggles coyly.

speaker: Millie
text: "I suppose I have no job, but is that really so bad? I am a member of The Fellowship and I talk to people about them all day long."

speaker: Millie
text: "I see we have the same job!" She laughs at her own joke. "Dost thou spend all thy time talking to people about The Fellowship? For if that is what thou dost do, thou must get thyself another corner!" Millie's face wrinkles in displeasure.

speaker: Millie
text: "Dost thou know what The Fellowship is?"

speaker: Millie
text: "Oh, I think thou dost not really know!"

speaker: Millie
text: "If thou dost wish, thou mayest attend tonight's meeting at the Fellowship Hall. It begins at nine o'clock sharp. Just tell them that thou art my guest. I shall see thee there, I hope." Millie giggles and looks away shyly.

speaker: Millie
text: "I spend all my time trying to recruit, er... spread the word of The Fellowship. It is better than having a job! I learned how to do this at the Meditation Retreat."

speaker: Millie
text: "'Tis located on an island in south Britannia near Serpent's Hold. Most new Fellowship members spend some time down there learning the tenets of the group. One can also learn to hear 'the voice' at the retreat."

speaker: Millie
text: "Fellowship members have an inner voice which speaks to them. I have not heard it yet, but I am working toward it. I may need to spend another few days at the Meditation Retreat in order to do so. Batlin tells me not to be discouraged, though. He says I will hear it when I have made myself worthy."

speaker: Millie
text: Millie rolls her eyes. "Thou hast met my brother? Thou poor thing! He is really a candidate for the asylum, I wouldst say! He believes The Fellowship kidnapped me and charmed me into following them. Well, I joined of mine own free will, without a second thought, and it was a pure lark! No one coerced me! Thad can go hang! Mama always said he was the impulsive one in the family!"

speaker: Millie
text: "I shall see thee later! Maybe even at tonight's Fellowship meeting!"

speaker: Geoffrey
text: You see your former companion and friend, Geoffrey, Captain of the Guard.

speaker: Geoffrey
text: "Yes, <PLAYER_NAME>?" Geoffrey asks.

speaker: Geoffrey
text: Geoffrey chuckles. "Art thou joking? I am Geoffrey!"

speaker: Geoffrey
text: "These days I remain in my position as Captain of the Guard. I am Lord British's personal bodyguard, and I am in charge of security at the castle. I do not have much time or use for adventuring now."

speaker: Geoffrey
text: "I have aged a bit over the last 200 years. I am afraid I shall not be joining thee this time. But my thoughts are with thee, and if I may offer some assistance, I shall be glad to do so."

speaker: Geoffrey
text: "Yes, it has been a long time by Britannian reckoning since I have seen mine homeland. When thou hast finished with thy business, do come back and tell me news of what is happening in our homeworld."

speaker: Geoffrey
text: "Mine advice to thee is to build up thine experience and skills as soon as possible. Thou hast been away from Britannia for a long time. Thou mightest not be in the same shape thou wert in at the end of thy last adventure here."

speaker: Geoffrey
text: "It is apparently another difference in our two worlds. Whenever thou shalt return it is as if thy physical body has arrived here for the first time. It is the reason why many of	thine own companions have chosen to stay here even though they have aged in Britannian time."

speaker: Geoffrey
text: "Go and search for monsters. Vanquish them. Take their gold! Gain experience! Use that experience when thou dost visit trainers. Increase thy strength, dexterity, and intelligence, as well as thy combat skill and ability to perform magic. Thou wilt be lost without this necessary evolution of experience!"

speaker: Geoffrey
text: "He is quite looney. If thou dost ask me, I believe all the mages in the land are afflicted. Take a look and find out for thyself."

speaker: Geoffrey
text: "He is much better now!"

speaker: Geoffrey
text: "Have courage. Have faith. Be strong. Be wise."

speaker: Wislem
text: You see an impressive winged gargoyle with a stately demeanor.

speaker: Wislem
text: "To greet thee again," Wislem says.

speaker: Wislem
text: "To be known as Wislem."

speaker: Wislem
text: "To be the word for `wise man.'"

speaker: Wislem
text: "To be advisor to Lord British, and act as representative for my race here in Britain. To be honored to be in long line of advisors to the king."

speaker: Wislem
text: "To make sure the gargoyle race is heard in the castle. To have been a long road to acceptance and integration into Britannian society."

speaker: Wislem
text: "To tell you that, not long after your last visit, the gargoyles settled upon Terfin, an island to the southeast. To have moved, little by little, onto the mainland."

speaker: Wislem
text: "To be accepted in most places. To feel sad, however, that there are still towns that do not accept us. But our Lord and King, Draxinusom, is still alive and is doing a magnificent job. To know and help all gargoyles who are alive."

speaker: Wislem
text: Wislem listens to your story about the murders in Trinsic. "To be sad to hear this. To suggest that you visit Lord Draxinusom in Terfin and tell him about Inamo. He will know who Inamo's parent gargoyle is. To recommend you relay this news as soon as possible."

speaker: Wislem
text: "To go soon and tell Draxinusom about Inamo?"

speaker: Wislem
text: "To know you are reliable."

speaker: Wislem
text: "To be concerned that Inamo's parent shall never know what happened." He appears saddened.

speaker: Wislem
text: "To bid farewell."

speaker: Sherry
text: You see a very large mouse with an air of superior intelligence.

speaker: Sherry
text: "Avatar!" she exclaims. "I cannot believe thou art here, <PLAYER_NAME>!"

speaker: Sherry
text: "Hello, <PLAYER_NAME>!" Sherry the Mouse exclaims.

speaker: Sherry
text: "Why, dost thou not remember Sherry, <PLAYER_NAME>?"

speaker: Sherry
text: "I am trying to keep up with these children! We are playing tag through the castle! I must run! Talk to me later in the nursery!"

speaker: Sherry
text: "I mainly assist Nanna in the Royal Nursery during the day. I watch the children alone in the evenings while Nanna has dinner and goes to her Fellowship meeting. Other times I run around the castle looking for mouse food!"

speaker: Sherry
text: "The children are so much fun. I like to read them their favorite story. It happens to be Lord British's favorite children's story, too! He read it to me oh, those many years ago."

speaker: Sherry
text: "If thou hast not had the chance yet, do look around and meet them. They are most wonderful and amusing."

speaker: Sherry
text: "It is much the same as it was when thou wert last here. There has been a bit of remodeling. After all, it has been 200 years since thou wert last here! I believe Lord British has a storeroom with quite a bit of equipment inside."

speaker: Sherry
text: "Well, cheese is my favorite. If thou dost ever have cheese to give away, I will gladly eat it. But I will generally eat most anything. Dost thou have any cheese for me?"

speaker: Sherry
text: "Want to give me some?"

speaker: Sherry
text: "Thank thee, <PLAYER_NAME>!"

speaker: Sherry
text: "I am unable to take thy cheese at the moment, <HONORIFIC>."

speaker: Sherry
text: "Well! I thought thou wert my friend!"

speaker: Sherry
text: "But thou hast not got any cheese!"

speaker: Sherry
text: "Too bad! If thou dost find any, please keep me in mind!"

speaker: Sherry
text: "Dost thou want to hear the story? It is called 'Hubert's Hair-Raising Adventure'."

speaker: Sherry
text: Sherry stands on her hind legs, takes a deep breath, and then recites -- from memory -- very, very fast:

speaker: Sherry
text: "Some other time, then!"

speaker: Sherry
text: "Farewell, <HONORIFIC>!"

speaker: Boots
text: This is an elderly woman who epitomizes 'grandmotherly'.

speaker: Boots
text: "Hello, again!" Boots says.

speaker: Boots
text: "All my brothers and sisters called me 'Boots' when I was a baby, and it hath remained my name ever since."

speaker: Boots
text: "Why, I am Lord British's personal cook! I prepare meals for the entire castle."

speaker: Boots
text: "Just go to the dining room at breakfast or supper time and mine husband Bennie will serve thee!"

speaker: Boots
text: "For breakfast I usually prepare a dish that my Liege brought with him from his homeland. Here we call it Eggs British. It is served with assorted fruits and tea, of course. It is the King's favorite."

speaker: Boots
text: "This meal is usually whatever meat or game or fish Lord British requests, accompanied by several additional courses and a fine dessert."

speaker: Boots
text: "He's a dear, but he has become a little absent-minded in his later years. He never remembers to bring enough meat from the slaughterhouse in Paws. In fact, we are short this week!"

speaker: Boots
text: "Last week I asked him to put a little garlic into some soup. He put in the garlic and then forgot about it. So he went and put some more in. Then he forgot he did that. So he put in more. Well, thou canst imagine the look on Lord British's face when he finally did taste that soup! It is a good thing we live and work in the castle of such a just ruler."

speaker: Boots
text: "That is right, we do not have enough. If thou couldst bring me mutton from the slaughterhouse, I will pay thee 5 gold for every portion thou canst bring. All right?"

speaker: Boots
text: "Good, I will be awaiting thy return!"

speaker: Boots
text: "Oh dear. Well, I know thou art busy. Some other time, then."

speaker: Boots
text: "Splendid! Let's see, we agreed on 5 gold per portion, if I remember correctly."

speaker: Boots
text: "Bye now!"

speaker: Bennie
text: You see an elderly man with good humor and a warm smile.

speaker: Bennie
text: "Yes, Avatar?" Bennie asks with authority.

speaker: Bennie
text: "All my friends call me Bennie."

speaker: Bennie
text: "I am the Head Servant at the castle. My job consists of keeping the other servants in line and serving the meals."

speaker: Bennie
text: "Yes, I have been Head Servant for many years. Mine entire family works for Lord British. My son is the king's gentleman's gentleman. My daughter is the Royal Chambermaid. My wife is Head Cook. We are pleased to work for Lord British."

speaker: Bennie
text: "My wife, Boots, is the head cook. Her specialty is roast beef. She makes wonderful pastries, too. Enough of those will give thee a very un-Avatar-like figure!"

speaker: Bennie
text: "Wouldst thou like to order a meal?"

speaker: Bennie
text: "For thee, it is free!"

speaker: Bennie
text: Bennie serves you and your party a delicious meal of beef and pastry.

speaker: Bennie
text: "Return tomorrow and thou canst have another free meal."

speaker: Bennie
text: "Thou art carrying too much to take the beef and pastry!"

speaker: Bennie
text: "I am sorry, <PLAYER_NAME>, but I am allowed to serve thee only once per day. Return tomorrow for a meal."

speaker: Bennie
text: "Oh. Well, thou must return when thou art hungry."

speaker: Bennie
text: "Come to the dining room during breakfast or dinner and I will be most honored to serve thee!"

speaker: Bennie
text: "Yes, I suppose I am. I am also becoming a little hard-of-hearing. When thou hast seen as many years as I have, one's faculties are no longer perfect."

speaker: Bennie
text: "Safe journeys, <PLAYER_NAME>."

speaker: Weston
text: You see a thoroughly disheartened young man who is miserably languishing behind bars.

speaker: Weston
text: "Hello again, <HONORIFIC>," says Weston.

speaker: Weston
text: "I am Weston."

speaker: Weston
text: "I have none so long as I am left to rot here in this prison."

speaker: Palace Guard
text: "Thy job is to pay for the crime thou hast committed."

speaker: Weston
text: "My crime was stealing apples from the Royal Orchards. This I did and I admit it freely. If given the same set of circumstances I would do it again."

speaker: Palace Guard
text: "A-ha! Not only an unrepentant criminal but also a potential professional thief! Looks like this one has ended in the right place and just in the nick o' time."

speaker: Weston
text: "I had offered to buy them first, but Figg, the caretaker of the orchard, set an exorbitant price which I am certain he would have pocketed for himself. So, yes, I admit to stealing them."

speaker: Palace Guard
text: "See how the common criminal blames his type of immoral behavior on others, all the while denying it in himself! This one is irredeemable, he is."

speaker: Weston
text: "He gives baskets of fruit free to The Fellowship without Lord British's consent, I am quite certain."

speaker: Palace Guard
text: "Thou shouldst not listen to this obvious slander, <HONORIFIC>! It is hearsay!"

speaker: Weston
text: "Mine only regrets are that I did not try to steal something bigger and that	I did not get away with it."

speaker: Weston
text: "I am not from Britain, <HONORIFIC>. I am from Paws and it is another reason why they believe I can be trifled with."

speaker: Palace Guard
text: "This prisoner is from Paws! I bloody knew it! To his credit he was in town nearly an entire day before he stole something. For a citizen of Paws that is as honest as they come!"

speaker: Weston
text: "Paws is a town where thou mayest feel the icy grip of poverty about thine heart."

speaker: Palace Guard
text: "Oh bloody 'ell! Now I suppose he is going to go and tell us his whole pathetic life's story! Couldst thou wait until I get out mine handkerchief so I do not interrupt thee with all my wailing!"

speaker: Weston
text: "Not so long ago Paws was a thriving rustic coastal village. But as Britain grew larger most of our local businesses moved there. We became a farming town and the seven year drought gave us a lashing that we have yet to recover from."

speaker: Weston
text: "I do not wish to bemoan my fate, but my family lives in Paws -- my wife Alina and my child Cassie. They were starving and I came to Britain to get food for them."

speaker: Palace Guard
text: "Oh, now! Do not go and bring up poverty as an excuse as to why thou hast turned to crime! My father was so poor he and his family had to eat dirt. But he still raised me proper. Beat the stuffings out of me if he ever so much as imagined I did anything wrong, I can tell thee that!"

speaker: Weston
text: "I do not want any mercy for myself. I have admitted my guilt. But my life does not only belong to myself. It belongs to my wife and family as well. Without me they will suffer unbearable hardships, such as they might not survive."

speaker: Weston
text: "Although there are fools who will speak otherwise, the people of Britannia are being crushed by the vicious tyranny of the class system. While a few have more than they could ever enjoy, there are many who go to sleep hungry every night. My wife and daughter to name two of them."

speaker: Palace Guard
text: "Oh, that reminds me it is nearly time for my meal break! The trout is supposed to be delicious today at the Farmer's Market."

speaker: Weston
text: "Fools like our good friend the guard would have us believe that nothing has changed in Britannia for over two hundred years. That we can live our lives as if all of our problems do not exist. I say to thee that it is people like that who cause our problems in the first place."

speaker: Weston
text: "While I am certain Lord British is a just and fair ruler, he must be quite unaware of all that goes on in his kingdom. Surely he would not tolerate such inequity."

speaker: Palace Guard
text: "All right! That is enough noise out of thee! All day long yakkata-yakkata about the awful terrible class system! Why, the next thing thou knowest thou shalt be sayin' society is to blame for thy crimes. Not a word from anybody about any appreciation for keeping the laws and order. No, of course not! But all the pity in the world for the dangerous lawbreakers who are the real threat to society."

speaker: Weston
text: "Wouldst thou speak with Lord British about me? I would bet that he is completely unaware of my case! Please! Wilt thou speak with him?"

speaker: Weston
text: "Oh, I thank thee, Avatar! My fate and the fates of my wife and daughter are in thine hands!"

speaker: Weston
text: Weston lowers his head. "Then why art thou speaking with me? Go away and leave me to my misery."

speaker: Weston
text: "I thank thee for visiting me."

speaker: Miranda
text: This is a lovely, earthy woman with a warm smile.

speaker: Miranda
text: "Word has spread quickly of thine arrival, Avatar! Welcome!"

speaker: Miranda
text: "Hello, <PLAYER_NAME>," Miranda says. "Nice to see thee again."

speaker: Miranda
text: "I am Miranda."

speaker: Miranda
text: "I serve on the Great Council. Today we are working on a bill of law. When I am not here in the castle, I am kept busy with a young child."

speaker: Miranda
text: "The Great Council supports Lord British in the legislation of Britannia's laws. I am honored to be one of the three women serving on the Council."

speaker: Miranda
text: "I am particularly concerned about women's duties and privileges and their available opportunities in the land. Our history has been kind to women in general, but there is still room for improvement."

speaker: Miranda
text: "More women could hold public office, for one thing. And I would personally like to be rid of those scantily-clad women in heroic fantasy paintings."

speaker: Miranda
text: Miranda smiles. "Yes, my son's name is Max."

speaker: Miranda
text: "He is probably in the Royal Nursery."

speaker: Miranda
text: "He's right here! Say hello to the Avatar, Max."

speaker: Max
text: "Hi. I'm a funny boy!"

speaker: Miranda
text: "He's quite precocious."

speaker: Miranda
text: "I wonder where he could be..."

speaker: Miranda
text: "He is quite obviously his father's son. Perhaps thou hast met him? Raymundo -- the director of the Royal Theatre. We believe Max will be quite a performer when he's older."

speaker: Miranda
text: "Inwisloklem and I are drafting a bill which would make illegal any distribution of waste products in Lock Lake, near Cove. The lake is quite defiled."

speaker: Miranda
text: "I would like to speak with thee about the new bill we are drafting. Please come to the Council Chamber during normal working hours and we shall talk."

speaker: Miranda
text: "Art thou travelling to Cove?"

speaker: Miranda
text: "That is good news! Perhaps thou couldst do us a great favor. We need this bill delivered to Lord Heather in Cove. He must read it and give us his approval by signing it. I know thou hast far more important things to do than running errands, but it would be greatly appreciated. Wilt thou do it?"

speaker: Miranda
text: "Wonderful! Here is the bill. Please bring it back to me when it is signed. And we thank thee."

speaker: Miranda
text: "Thine hands are too full to take the bill!"

speaker: Miranda
text: "Oh. All right. We know that thou art very busy. We shall find another way to deliver the bill. Thank thee anyway."

speaker: Miranda
text: "Thou wilt not be travelling to Cove at all? Well, all right then. Never mind."

speaker: Miranda
text: "Didst thou have Lord Heather sign the bill?"

speaker: Miranda
text: "Excellent! Let me see it."

speaker: Miranda
text: "It looks in order! We thank thee, Avatar!"

speaker: Miranda
text: "Wait, where is it? Thou dost not have it. I hope thou hast not lost it. Thou shouldst go and find it. 'Tis an important document!"

speaker: Miranda
text: "Wait! Where is it? Thou dost not have it. I hope thou hast not lost it. Thou shouldst go and find it. 'Tis an important document!"

speaker: Miranda
text: "But thou hast not had the bill signed! Please do so, as soon as possible, if thou wouldst."

speaker: Miranda
text: "Oh. Well, the next time thou art in Cove, perhaps thou wilt find time to see him."

speaker: Miranda
text: "We shall see thee again soon, I hope, Avatar."

speaker: Inwisloklem
text: A winged gargoyle looks at you with interest and obvious intelligence.

speaker: Inwisloklem
text: "To welcome thee to Britain, Avatar!"

speaker: Inwisloklem
text: "To greet thee again, Avatar!" Inwisloklem smiles.

speaker: Inwisloklem
text: "To be called Inwisloklem."

speaker: Inwisloklem
text: "To mean `interpreter' in your language."

speaker: Inwisloklem
text: "To be, indeed, an interpreter in my homeland. To be now on the Great Council to serve our most noble ruler, Lord British. To be honored as one of the two gargoyles on the Council."

speaker: Inwisloklem
text: "To be one of the surviving gargoyles, and to preserve our heritage is my life work. To tell you our race emigrated to Britannia many, many years ago. To have settled on the island known as Terfin."

speaker: Inwisloklem
text: "To be so many of my people killed two hundred years ago in the War of the False Prophet. To be the war that you ended by bringing peace between our races."

speaker: Inwisloklem
text: "To be a lonely place. To be desolate. To be not what humans call `homey'. To desire to establish a new way of life for gargoyles in Britannia, and to eliminate the hatred and misunderstanding of our race in humans. To know that ignorance breeds bigotry. To be one of those who are correcting this."

speaker: Inwisloklem
text: "To desire a world where humans and gargoyles could live together in peace as equals in Britannian society."

speaker: Inwisloklem
text: "To be called The Fellowship."

speaker: Inwisloklem
text: "To be dedicated to promoting good will and trust in the land. To be thinking of joining the group soon!"

speaker: Inwisloklem
text: "To create the laws of the land. To inform you that my colleague, Miranda, can tell you more of what we are doing now. To be unfortunate that most of the Council is away now."

speaker: Inwisloklem
text: "To inform you that Miranda is an intelligent woman who has great concern for the well being of all of Britannia's citizens. To be one of Lord British's most trusted advisors."

speaker: Inwisloklem
text: "To be on holiday at the moment. To have only Miranda and myself present to enact this new law."

speaker: Inwisloklem
text: "To tell you to ask Miranda about it, for she knows more than I."

speaker: Inwisloklem
text: "To say farewell."

speaker: Nell
text: Nell will not speak to you.

speaker: Nell
text: You see a servant girl who looks at you in wonder. "Thou dost look familiar. Who art thou?"

speaker: Nell
text: "Oh. Hello. I am Nell."

speaker: Nell
text: "I thought so! I have seen thy portrait before. And I had heard that thou wouldst be visiting! I'm Nell."

speaker: Nell
text: "Hello, <PLAYER_NAME>."

speaker: Nell
text: "I told thee my name is Nell."

speaker: Nell
text: "I am a chambermaid. I am responsible for keeping the castle tidy. Just a servant girl, really."

speaker: Nell
text: "It is very large. Keeps me very busy. Thou wouldst not believe how dusty it gets."

speaker: Nell
text: "I suppose I'll always be a servant. My parents are servants. My brother is a servant. My fiance is a servant. My child will probably be a servant."

speaker: Nell
text: "They work in the castle as well. Boots is my mother. Bennie is my father. They have been here for years. I was born in this castle and played in the nursery."

speaker: Nell
text: "Thou mightest run into him. He is also a servant in the castle. Charles. Other than not being as smart as I am, he is all right. For a bumbling ass, that is!" She laughs.

speaker: Nell
text: "That would be Carrocio, that dear man who runs the Punch and Judy Show. He writes the loveliest love poetry. We are getting married as soon as Carrocio can afford a wedding ring."

speaker: Nell
text: Nell looks worried. "Shhh! I do not want anyone to know. 'Tis not showing yet, is it? Carrocio and I are getting married as soon as possible. He -is- the father. I think. Then again, it could be... no, probably not him. Or could it be...? Hmmm. That would be interesting! Wait! What am I saying? The father is most definitely Carrocio! Please do not tell anyone. 'Twould be embarrassing. All right?"

speaker: Nell
text: "I know I can trust thee, <PLAYER_NAME>."

speaker: Nell
text: "But thou wouldst ruin my reputation! Please -- a servant girl needs all the self-esteem she can get without that burden!" Nell turns away from you.

speaker: Nell
text: "Goodbye, <PLAYER_NAME>."

speaker: Charles
text: You see a young peasant with a tray of wine glasses.

speaker: Charles
text: "Hello, Avatar."

speaker: Charles
text: "I am Charles."

speaker: Charles
text: "I am a servant in Lord British's castle. I serve as a gentleman's gentleman, among other things. Right now I am serving wine."

speaker: Charles
text: "My family has been employed by Lord British for many years. My father, Bennie, once held the position I now hold. He is the head servant. I shall be head servant one day, I suppose. Then perhaps my sweetheart will love me."

speaker: Charles
text: "Thou wilt encounter them. My mother cooks in the kitchen. My prudish sister is the chambermaid."

speaker: Charles
text: Charles sighs. He is clearly smitten. "She is Jeanette. She works in the Blue Boar. But I am afraid I am not 'up to her standards'. I believe she has her eye set on someone else. I do not know what to do about it."

speaker: Charles
text: "She does not love me, I know. She would rather marry a rich man. I have not a chance."

speaker: Charles
text: You tell Charles what Jeanette said.

speaker: Charles
text: "Really? Thou dost mean I have a chance?" Charles becomes so excited he nearly drops his tray. "Oh, I thank thee, Avatar, for giving me this hopeful news! I must run and send her flowers or some gift! I must declare my love!" He turns away from you, obviously walking on clouds.

speaker: Charles
text: "She is engaged to the carousel manager. It is hard to get used to. I have always been overly protective of my little sister. I would wager she has never even been kissed! Not even by Carrocio! That is mainly because I have looked after her all this time. I would smite anyone who laid a hand on her! Besides, Nell has always been chaste and prudish. She would never think to allow a man to kiss her."

speaker: Charles
text: You remember what Nell told you about her 'condition'. Do you mention it to Charles?

speaker: Charles
text: You tell Charles what Nell revealed in confidence.

speaker: Charles
text: Charles is wide-eyed and shocked. "Why, that hussy! My sister! She is nothing more than a tramp! And wait until I get mine hands on Carrocio!"

speaker: Charles
text: Charles turns away. There is murder in his eyes.

speaker: Charles
text: Your conscience rests easy, knowing that you resisted the temptation to carry tales.

speaker: Charles
text: "Wouldst thou like some wine?"

speaker: Charles
text: "'Tis on the house." Charles hands you and your friends glasses of wine.

speaker: Charles
text: "Oops. Thou art carrying too much. Ask me again when thou dost not have thine hands full!"

speaker: Charles
text: "Some other time, then."

speaker: Charles
text: Charles nods his head at you, then goes about his business.

speaker: Rudyom
text: This elderly mage looks older and more senile than when you last saw him.

speaker: Rudyom
text: "Who art thou?" Rudyom asks. "Oh -- I remember."

speaker: Rudyom
text: "Hello again, Avatar!" Rudyom says, beaming.

speaker: Rudyom
text: "That I know. My name is Rudyom."

speaker: Rudyom
text: "I am not sure anymore. I was a powerful mage at one time! Now nothing works. Magic is afoul! I suppose I could sell thee some reagents and spells if thou dost want. And mind the carpet -- it does not work!"

speaker: Rudyom
text: "I am a powerful mage! Magic is my milieu! I can sell thee spells or reagents."

speaker: Rudyom
text: "I do not understand what is wrong. My magic does not work so well anymore."

speaker: Rudyom
text: "The ether is flowing freely! Magic is with us once again!"

speaker: Rudyom
text: "The big blue carpet. 'Tis a flying carpet. It does not work like it should."

speaker: Rudyom
text: Rudyom looks around and scratches his head.

speaker: Rudyom
text: "Funny. It was here a while ago. Oh! I remember now. Some adventurers borrowed my flying carpet a few weeks ago. When they returned they said they had lost it near Serpent's Spine. Somewhere in the vicinity of the Lost River. I suppose	if thou didst want to go and find it, thou couldst keep it. It did not work very well. Perhaps thou canst make it work. I did not like the color, anyway!"

speaker: Rudyom
text: "Dost thou wish to buy some spells?"

speaker: Rudyom
text: "Oh. Never mind, then."

speaker: Rudyom
text: "Dost thou wish to buy some reagents?"

speaker: Rudyom
text: "Oh. Never mind, then."

speaker: Rudyom
text: "Do not mention that foul mineral's name to me! It hast caused me much frustration! Before my mind lost me I was conducting experiments with the infernal material. But now I cannot for the life of me remember what it was I was trying to do."

speaker: Rudyom
text: "They are a nuisance, are they not? I do believe that blackrock is the solution to the problem. I wish my mind had not lost me, or I could continue my work..."

speaker: Rudyom
text: "I understand they are gone for good. Do not blame thyself, Avatar. The disaster will only pave the way for a new era in experimentation and discovery. I hope."

speaker: Rudyom
text: "I wrote them all down in my notebook, which is somewhere around here. Thou art welcome to look at it. But stay away from that damned transmuter -- 'tis dangerous!"

speaker: Rudyom
text: "I used it to record mine experiments with blackrock and the blackrock transmuter."

speaker: Rudyom
text: "'Tis that wand-like thing. It was supposed to magnetize and magically transmute blackrock, but it doth not work correctly. Try pointing it at a piece of blackrock and thou wilt see what I mean. But do not stand too close! Thou art welcome to take it if thou dost want a piece of garbage!"

speaker: Rudyom
text: "Leaving so soon? Deary me. I hope I remember thee if thou dost come back."

speaker: Rudyom
text: "Goodbye, Avatar."

speaker: Nastassia
text: This is an attractive young woman who seems sad.

speaker: Nastassia
text: Emotion immediately grips your heart to see such a beautiful young woman seem so sad.

speaker: Nastassia
text: She looks up as you introduce yourself.

speaker: Nastassia
text: "Hello again, <PLAYER_NAME>!" Nastassia says.

speaker: Nastassia
text: "I am Nastassia."

speaker: Nastassia
text: She thinks a moment. "I suppose my job is to keep the Shrine of Compassion pristine, though it is not an official position."

speaker: Nastassia
text: "The Shrine of Compassion has been here for many generations, as have all the shrines in Britannia. My great-great-grandmother Ariana made a request in her will that her family line take care of this particular shrine."

speaker: Nastassia
text: "Many of the shrines have fallen into disuse or have been overgrown to the point of being lost. It is sad."

speaker: Nastassia
text: "I am afraid that thou mightest find the other shrines in poor condition. I keep this one... well, nice. And I do it not only to keep alive my great-great-grandmother's tradition, but... for other reasons, too."

speaker: Nastassia
text: "Some people may think it odd that a young person would cling to the old ways so. But it is something that gives me great comfort. It gives me the feeling that there is something in this world that I belong to."

speaker: Nastassia
text: "I... I'd rather not say. Please do not ask."

speaker: Nastassia
text: "Thou dost know the reasons."

speaker: Nastassia
text: "Yes, she was my great-great-grandmother. I understand that she actually met the Avatar and <PRONOUN> made a profound impact on her life."

speaker: Nastassia
text: "It is odd, but thou dost resemble the portraits I have seen of the Avatar."

speaker: Nastassia
text: "Thou dost know of my father? I suppose the townsfolk have been talking again. I wish I had known him. There is something within me that yearns for some news of him. Anything at all."

speaker: Nastassia
text: "My mother. She died horribly, and by her own hand. That is the true reason I pay homage to this Shrine. I hope someday to provide her with the means to rest in peace."

speaker: Nastassia
text: "My father died in the Great Forest there. Some wild animal or something killed him. Art thou perhaps travelling to Yew?"

speaker: Nastassia
text: "Oh, <PLAYER_NAME>, I do wish thou wouldst try to find out something about my father. How did he die? What happened? Please! Wilt thou search for the truth and come back and tell me?"

speaker: Nastassia
text: "Bless thee! I shall be waiting here for thee."

speaker: Nastassia
text: "I know we have a strong kinship now. We shall be like sisters."

speaker: Nastassia
text: Unexpectedly, Nastassia pulls your head down to hers and kisses you on the mouth.

speaker: Nastassia
text: Nastassia turns away and looks as if she might cry. "Very well. Please leave me alone."

speaker: Nastassia
text: "No? Well, let me know if thou art in the future. Perhaps thou couldst help me."

speaker: Nastassia
text: You kiss Nastassia and she moans.

speaker: Nastassia
text: The two of you rush into each other's arms and your mouths meet. You had forgotten how good her lips felt against yours.

speaker: Nastassia
text: You kiss Nastassia's lovely mouth again. She responds.

speaker: Nastassia
text: "No man hath done that as well as thee."

speaker: Nastassia
text: She looks at you with wide eyes.

speaker: Nastassia
text: "Do it again, milord."

speaker: Nastassia
text: You kiss Nastassia yet again. This time your bodies press together tightly, and you know this promises to be more than a fleeting fling with some tavern wench.

speaker: Nastassia
text: You kiss Nastassia and she moans.

speaker: Nastassia
text: Nastassia studies your features.

speaker: Nastassia
text: "Somehow I knew it. It hath been said that thou wouldst return."

speaker: Nastassia
text: You tell Nastassia what you learned from Trellek. She closes her eyes and it seems a great weight has lifted from her shoulders.

speaker: Nastassia
text: The woman raises her arms to the sky and cries out, "Didst thou hear that, mother? Thine husband was only trying to provide for his family! And he died... a hero! He was not a vagabond! Dost thou hear? Thou canst rest thy tortured soul now. Please, mother, forgive him. Do so, so that I can now forgive thee."

speaker: Nastassia
text: She wipes the tears from her face and looks at you.

speaker: Nastassia
text: "I thank thee, <PLAYER_NAME>. Thou hast made me very happy. I shall always remember thee."

speaker: Nastassia
text: She kisses you once lightly. "Thank thee, <PLAYER_NAME>. Thou hast made me very happy. Shouldst thou become weary of adventuring, I shall be waiting here for thee. Thou art welcome to live and share thy life with me. Go now. Finish the job thou must needs do. But keep me in thy thoughts."

speaker: Nastassia
text: "Goodbye." She kisses you again, and then turns so that she will not see you leave.

speaker: Nastassia
text: "Goodbye, <PLAYER_NAME>."

speaker: Nastassia
text: "Goodbye, <PLAYER_NAME>."

speaker: Rayburt
text: You startle a fighter who seems lost in thought.

speaker: Rayburt
text: His dog seemed to be meditating as well.

speaker: Rayburt
text: "Hello again," Rayburt says.

speaker: Rayburt
text: "I am Rayburt."

speaker: Rayburt
text: He turns to the dog. "And this is Regal."

speaker: Rayburt
text: "I am a trainer. I specialize in a style of combat that relies on concentration and meditation. It shall boost thy dexterity and intelligence, as well as thy combat skill."

speaker: Rayburt
text: "He is an exceptionally smart animal. He understands the meditative way of life."

speaker: Rayburt
text: Rayburt throws the dog a cookie, which is snarfed up in the blink of an eye. "He is cute, too," Rayburt says with complete seriousness.

speaker: Rayburt
text: You see a hint of a smile on Rayburt's face. "She and I are one person."

speaker: Rayburt
text: "Most of all combat occurs in the mind before the first blow is ever struck. The key to victory is to first win the inner battle in the mind. Winning that inner battle is what I help my students to learn."

speaker: Rayburt
text: "I charge 60 gold for a session, but thou wilt benefit greatly. Is this agreeable?"

speaker: Rayburt
text: "It is not the first time I have been accused of being too expensive."

speaker: Rayburt
text: "Please come to my studio during business hours if thou wishest to train."

speaker: Rayburt
text: Rayburt bows.

speaker: Lord Heather
text: This regal gentleman epitomizes a well-liked politician.

speaker: Lord Heather
text: "Hello! Lord British sent word that thou might come to visit us. Welcome to Cove, Avatar!"

speaker: Lord Heather
text: "Hello again, Avatar!" Lord Heather proclaims.

speaker: Lord Heather
text: "I am Lord Heather. And I recognize thee, Avatar!"

speaker: Lord Heather
text: "I am the Town Mayor of Cove, home of the Shrine of Compassion."

speaker: Lord Heather
text: "It's a small place, I know. Many of our residents have moved away to the larger towns, especially Britain. But we have maintained a small core of loyal Covites."

speaker: Lord Heather
text: "We are proud of our Shrine. One of our residents takes good care of it. Thou must try and visit the Shrine if thou hast not already. It is a monument to all the lovers in town."

speaker: Lord Heather
text: "Britain may be the city of Compassion, but Cove has become the city of Passion. Everyone here seems to fall in love rather easily. Thou wilt find that everyone loves someone. Almost everyone, that is."

speaker: Lord Heather
text: "Well, let's see... I am in love with Jaana, our healer.	And she is in love with me, of course. Then there is Zinaida, who runs the Emerald. She has an interest in De Maria, our local bard. And vice versa. Rayburt, our trainer, is courting Pamela, the innkeeper."

speaker: Iolo
text: "Sounds like bad theatre to me!"

speaker: Spark
text: "Any wenches mine own age around here?"

speaker: Lord Heather
text: "I see that thou art leaving Cove for a while, my dear?"

speaker: Jaana
text: "Yes, milord. But I shall return. I promise thee."

speaker: Lord Heather
text: "I shall try not to worry about thee, but it will be difficult."

speaker: Jaana
text: "Do not worry. I shall be safe with the Avatar."

speaker: Lord Heather
text: "I do hope so." The Mayor embraces Jaana.

speaker: Lord Heather
text: "Except for Nastassia."

speaker: Lord Heather
text: "She is a lovely young woman who is always melancholy. De Maria can tell thee more about her. I suggest thou seekest him at the Emerald. 'Tis a sad but compelling tale."

speaker: Lord Heather
text: "I do hope thou canst help her. She needs <VAR> to bring her out of her depression."

speaker: Lord Heather
text: "'Tis about time that the government did something about the awful stench coming from that lake! I shall be happy to sign thy bill of law! Take it back to the Great Council post haste!" Lord Heather signs the bill and hands it back to you.

speaker: Lord Heather
text: "But thou dost not have a bill of law!"

speaker: Lord Heather
text: "I thought I already signed that bill!"

speaker: Lord Heather
text: "It has gotten so putrid that on hot summer days the stink is suffocating. I believe that the Britannian Mining Company in Minoc is the source of the problem. Mining waste is being deposited in the Lake. Thou shouldst be glad it is nearly winter!"

speaker: Lord Heather
text: "Do come and visit again, Avatar!"

speaker: Pamela
text: You see a friendly woman in her thirties.

speaker: Pamela
text: "Greetings, again!" Pamela says.

speaker: Pamela
text: "I am Pamela!"

speaker: Pamela
text: "I am the Innkeeper at the Out'n'Inn."

speaker: Pamela
text: "If thou wouldst like a room, just say so!"

speaker: Pamela
text: "Please come by if thou wouldst like to rest thy weary feet for the night!"

speaker: Pamela
text: "The room is quite inexpensive. Only 8 gold per person. Want one?"

speaker: Pamela
text: "Thou art carrying too much to take the room key!"

speaker: Pamela
text: "Here is thy room key. It is good only until thou leavest."

speaker: Pamela
text: "Thou dost not have enough gold, eh? Too bad."

speaker: Pamela
text: "Another night, then."

speaker: Pamela
text: "Well... Cove is the city of Love and Passion, didst thou not know? Thou must be careful. If thou dost stay too long in Cove, thou wilt fall in love with someone! Mark my words!"

speaker: Pamela
text: "Oooh, he is such a wonderful man, dost thou not think? He is so intense and serious. Handsome, too! Oh, and	I like Regal as well."

speaker: Pamela
text: "As far as dogs go, he is handsome, too!"

speaker: Pamela
text: "See thee soon!"

speaker: Zinaida
text: This beautiful, earthy woman in her forties gives you a friendly smile.

speaker: Zinaida
text: "Hello," Zinaida says.

speaker: Zinaida
text: "I am Zinaida," she says with a curtsey.

speaker: Zinaida
text: "I am the owner and manager of The Emerald."

speaker: Zinaida
text: "If I can help thee with food or drink, please say so. I have never had a dissatisfied customer."

speaker: Zinaida
text: "Please come to the pub when it is open and I shall be happy to serve thee!"

speaker: Zinaida
text: "The Emerald is pleased to serve thee the finest cuisine this side of Britain. Thou mightest wish to try the special -- Silverleaf."

speaker: Zinaida
text: She winks at you. "Some say it is a powerful aphrodisiac... It is delicious, regardless. It comes from the root of an exotic tree growing somewhere in Britannia."

speaker: Zinaida
text: "The Emerald serves only the best wine and ale. I cannot recommend the water, however. Thanks to Lock Lake."

speaker: Zinaida
text: "He is the light of my life. A finer man does not exist." She beams.

speaker: Zinaida
text: "The stench has made our water taste terrible. That mining company must cease pouring their sewage into what was once a fine lake!"

speaker: Zinaida
text: "Come again soon!"

speaker: De Maria
text: This flamboyant bard exudes a festive aura.

speaker: De Maria
text: "I have sung about thee in many a song! And here thou art in the flesh! I recognized thee immediately." The man bows. "Welcome, Avatar!"

speaker: De Maria
text: "Greetings again, Avatar!" De Maria bows.

speaker: De Maria
text: "I am De Maria, the Bard."

speaker: De Maria
text: "I spin tales and sing songs!"

speaker: De Maria
text: "I also know a good deal about the folks in Cove."

speaker: De Maria
text: "What if I combine all three? Shall I sing a song which is a tale about the people of Cove?"

speaker: De Maria
text: "Very well, then!"

speaker: De Maria
text: "'Tis thy choice... and thy mistake!"

speaker: De Maria
text: "Ah, dear Nastassia. Wouldst thou like to hear her tale?"

speaker: De Maria
text: "Very well, then!"

speaker: De Maria
text: "Oh. I thought thou wert curious. Never mind then."

speaker: De Maria
text: "My love! My flower! Mine angel! The provider of the sweetest nectar my mouth has ever known! She is the light of my day! The notes of my songs! The flesh of my..."

speaker: Zinaida
text: "Enough, my love. I think the Avatar dost know thy meaning!"

speaker: De Maria
text: De Maria stops his reverie, sighs, and smiles at you. "Thou dost apprehend my meaning..."

speaker: De Maria
text: "Do take care of thyself!"

speaker: Elynor
text: "It is time for the ceremony to begin." says Elynor.

speaker: Elynor
text: You see a woman whose cultured manner is tinged with a suggestion of arrogance.

speaker: Elynor
text: "Art thou speaking to me, <HONORIFIC>?" Elynor asks.

speaker: Elynor
text: She straightens her shoulders and looks you in the eye.

speaker: Elynor
text: "I am Elynor."

speaker: Elynor
text: "I am the head counselor of the Fellowship branch here in Minoc. We are a society of spiritual seekers, dedicated to achieving our highest potential, advancing worthiness, unity and trust in our brothers."

speaker: Elynor
text: "Perhaps thou wouldst wish to join our Fellowship?"

speaker: Elynor
text: "This is indeed a great day for The Fellowship! Seek out Batlin in Britain.	He is our founder. Such a great honor as the acceptance of the Avatar into The Fellowship should properly	be reserved for him alone."

speaker: Elynor
text: "I can see by the look in thine eyes that thou dost lack the courage to take this vital step in thy life. Perhaps one day soon thou shalt be ready."

speaker: Elynor
text: She looks down her nose at you. "We shall see..."

speaker: Elynor
text: "Ah-- but thou dost know all of this."

speaker: Elynor
text: "I now recall a message Batlin sent to me. I have been expecting thee. Thou has been sent to deliver our package. Thou mayest relinquish it now."

speaker: Elynor
text: Elynor notices your medallion. "I do not think thou shouldst be wearing the medallion yet. Thou hast not been properly inducted into The Fellowship! I am afraid I must inform Batlin of thy falsehood!"

speaker: Elynor
text: "Thou hast picked a most inappropriate time to engage in such casual conversation. Perhaps thou wouldst be interested knowing that there have been two murders discovered in this sawmill!"

speaker: Elynor
text: "We should strive to put this business of the murders behind us. Minoc will soon be known throughout Britannia as a city where majestic ships are built. There	is even going to be a statue erected in the center of town honoring our shipwright, Owen. He is a skilled and valued member of our community and, of course, a Fellowship member."

speaker: Elynor
text: "Ours is not a great city, such as Britain, but it is widely known as a center of commerce and for its mine. The slight embarrassment of the legacy of Owen will fade in time."

speaker: Elynor
text: "I am saddened at the loss of life but cannot say I am surprised. Frederico and Tania were antagonistic people. The same may be said of most gypsies. I have nothing against them personally, of course."

speaker: Elynor
text: You produce the package and hold it before Elynor. Her eyes shift from you to the package and then back to you.

speaker: Elynor
text: "Surely thou hast been instructed not to open	the package. Hast thou opened it nonetheless?"

speaker: Elynor
text: "Thou knowest well that thou wert instructed to deliver the package unopened. As a Fellowship member, thou dost understand that we must be worthy of the rewards we seek. As thou hast violated Batlin's trust, any payment is forfeited. He will be informed of this indiscretion, and he will not be pleased."

speaker: Elynor
text: She takes the box from your	hands.

speaker: Elynor
text: "Nonsense. The package is still perfectly sealed." She stares at you suspiciously.

speaker: Elynor
text: "I know not why thou didst choose to claim that it was opened, but thou must learn better to trust thy brother. As the box is still intact, thou wilt receive thy reward, but thine actions will be reported. Be careful, my brother."

speaker: Elynor
text: She hands you 50 gold coins.

speaker: Elynor
text: "Thou cannot carry thy reward! My, thy travels have indeed been successful. Well, then, thou must endure a further test. Return the sealed box to me when thou canst tote the extra gold, and thou wilt be paid what thou dost deserve."

speaker: Elynor
text: She inspects the inside of the box.

speaker: Elynor
text: "Ah, good. The contents, at least, are still intact. The guilty one was only a victim of his own curiosity, and not truly a thief."

speaker: Elynor
text: She looks you up and down. "It is quite possible that thou wilt still learn to be a worthy member of our illustrious Membership. We shall see."

speaker: Elynor
text: She inspects the inside of the box.

speaker: Elynor
text: "I see that the contents of the box are missing. Either thou art a thief, or, at the least, not very diligent in thy duty as a messenger. One way or the other, <HONORIFIC>, the box hath been robbed!"

speaker: Elynor
text: She looks you up and down. "Batlin will be informed of this... development."

speaker: Elynor
text: Elynor takes the package from your hands.

speaker: Elynor
text: "Thou hast done very well. Now as promised, here is thy payment."

speaker: Elynor
text: "Thou cannot carry thy reward! My, thy travels have indeed been successful. Well, then, thou must endure a further test. Return the sealed box to me when thou canst tote the extra gold, and thou wilt be paid what thou dost deserve."

speaker: Elynor
text: Elynor takes the package from you. Examining it, she immediately notices that it has been opened.

speaker: Elynor
text: "^<HONORIFIC>! The box is open! Certainly, one as diligent as thee could not have been robbed?"

speaker: Elynor
text: She inspects the inside of the box.

speaker: Elynor
text: "Ah, good. The contents, at least, are still intact. The guilty one was only a victim of his own curiosity, and not truly a thief."

speaker: Elynor
text: She looks you up and down. "It is quite possible that thou wilt still learn to be a worthy member of our illustrious Membership. We shall see."

speaker: Elynor
text: She sniffs. "This will, of course,	be reported to Batlin."

speaker: Elynor
text: Peering inside, she is beset by a fit of anger. "It would appear thou hast been robbed. Obviously, as thou hast failed in the responsibility entrusted to thee by Batlin, thou shalt not receive any payment."

speaker: Elynor
text: "Batlin will be informed of this indiscretion."

speaker: Elynor
text: "Dost thou not have it with thee at this time? Thou wilt not be paid until thou dost deliver it unto mine own hand. I do hope thou hast secreted it in a safe place."

speaker: Elynor
text: "He is a classic example of The Fellowship making a vast difference in a person's life. Before he joined The Fellowship, he was without confidence and ready to put aside his trade. Now he stands on the verge of being recognized as the finest at his craft in the world."

speaker: Elynor
text: Elynor rolls her eyes. "Oh, please!" she says, sounding exasperated. "I do not concern myself with ones such as him these days."

speaker: Elynor
text: "Frederico and Tania treated all members of our Fellowship as if we were diseased. Frederico particularly would often bully our members. Thou dost know, it is common knowledge that we are pacifists. He had a reputation for cruelty, even among his own people. It is not surprising he came to a violent end."

speaker: Elynor
text: "The Fellowship is highly regarded in Minoc. Why, even the Mayor himself is a member. I brought him into The Fellowship myself. He was the first new member of our local branch. Gregor, the head of The Fellowship here, directs the Britannian Mining Company. Many Fellowship members pass through Minoc."

speaker: Elynor
text: "Thou hast just missed them! They were here collecting funds. They have moved on to Paws to visit our Shelter there."

speaker: Elynor
text: "I have not seen Elizabeth or Abraham since they were here last."

speaker: Elynor
text: The Cube vibrates. "Hook lives somewhere on Buccaneer's Den. I do not know where."

speaker: Elynor
text: "A man with a Hook? I am certain I would remember having seen anyone like that, and I am positive that does not match the description of any Fellowship member this branch has ever come in contact with."

speaker: Elynor
text: The Cube vibrates. "That is Hook's ship. I have not seen it in some time."

speaker: Elynor
text: "Many ships come and go in our busy port. I do not know of any one specific ship. Perhaps thou shouldst ask Owen."

speaker: Elynor
text: "Thou dost dare to spy upon Gregor and I as we share our moments together?! Dost thou have no decency?! Gregor and I have a right to privacy the same as do any lovers!"

speaker: Elynor
text: The Cube vibrates. "The candelabra was left at the murder site by mistake. Hook and Forskis are getting careless."

speaker: Elynor
text: "Yes, The Fellowship commissioned Xanthia to create a candelabra which thou dost describe. Its design incorporates our three tenets: 'U' for Unity, 'T' for Trust, and 'W' for Worthiness."

speaker: Elynor
text: You tell Elynor that it was found at the murder site. Elynor registers surprise.

speaker: Elynor
text: "I cannot imagine why it was there. Someone must be trying to implicate The Fellowship!"

speaker: Elynor
text: She thinks a moment.

speaker: Elynor
text: "If thou didst ask it of me, I would wager that Frederico and Tania were murdered by their own people, and another gypsy placed the candelabra at the site to implicate us. Those gypsies would kill their own mother if it meant gaining a bit of gold!"

speaker: Elynor
text: "They have set up camp southeast of town. Near the sawmill. That is suspicious, dost thou not think?"

speaker: Elynor
text: "I have a feeling that we shall see each other again."

speaker: Gregor
text: Gregor is busy concentrating on the Fellowship meeting and cannot talk now.

speaker: Gregor
text: "No time for idle chatter! I must get to the Fellowship Meeting! I am late!"

speaker: Gregor
text: You see an old man whose domineering disposition matches the hardened physique of his aged body.

speaker: Gregor
text: "Art thou addressing me?" Gregor scowls.

speaker: Gregor
text: "My name is Gregor."

speaker: Gregor
text: "I am in charge of the Minoc branch of the Britannian Mining Company."

speaker: Gregor
