text: "Art thou fevered, <HONORIFIC>? Dost thou not realize why we have gathered at this spot? 'Tis shameful, thine unaffected manner in the presence of such tragedy!"

speaker: Gregor
text: "Our town is a major center of trade in Britannia, and it is a place of social change."

speaker: Gregor
text: "The Britannian Mining Company produces a wide variety of minerals that are essential to the continuation of progress in	Britannia."

speaker: Gregor
text: "Here in Minoc we have one of the largest mining operations in Britannia, a sawmill, an inn, the Artist's Guild, and a shipwright."

speaker: Gregor
text: "Here in Minoc we are erecting a monument to our good shipwright Owen, a master craftsman whose name will soon be known throughout Britannia. We also have a very active Fellowship branch."

speaker: Gregor
text: "A long-standing and profitable business. A shame it will become more renowned for the murders that were committed there than for any of the fine work it does."

speaker: Gregor
text: "The Checquered Cork is famous for its rustic character and atmosphere. It is a fine place. Do not be put off by its apparent uncleanliness."

speaker: Gregor
text: "The Artist's Guild is a small collection of craftspeople who have huddled together to sell their little trinkets. They pride themselves on being the local dissenters of everything."

speaker: Gregor
text: "I may have already mentioned Owen, the shipwright. He builds the finest ships that have ever set sail."

speaker: Gregor
text: "I helped to organize things with Mayor Burnside to get the monument built."

speaker: Gregor
text: "It will be huge and made of the finest ore from our mine."

speaker: Gregor
text: "They have done immeasurable good for Minoc, helping to counter the disunity that can plague a town such as ours where so many people are fixated upon monetary gain."

speaker: Gregor
text: "It is terrible! The gypsies Frederico and Tania have been found murdered in William's sawmill!"

speaker: Gregor
text: "Leave us in peace, damn thee! Elynor and I are in love and we wish to be alone together! Find thy cheap excitations elsewhere!"

speaker: Gregor
text: "Be on thy way then."

speaker: Margareta
text: You see a young, bewitching gypsy woman with wise, soul-peering eyes.

speaker: Margareta
text: "Thou vishest to speak vith me again?" Margareta asks.

speaker: Margareta
text: "Very vell."

speaker: Margareta
text: "Very vell."

speaker: Margareta
text: "Margareta at thy service," she speaks slowly.

speaker: Margareta
text: The gypsy woman smiles slightly. "To tell thy destiny."

speaker: Margareta
text: "I knew it vould happen. I varned Frederico. He vouldn't listen."

speaker: Margareta
text: "He vas my brother-in-law. His death makes me very sad."

speaker: Margareta
text: "She vas Frederico's vife, but thou dost know that already, no? She vas a good voman."

speaker: Margareta
text: Margareta is silent a moment.

speaker: Margareta
text: "He has been led astray. It is unfortunate that he vill realize his mistake only as a result ov the death ov his parents."

speaker: Margareta
text: "There are many, many others like Sasha who have been led astray. For them, I see no future."

speaker: Margareta
text: "Thou dost know vhat I mean."

speaker: Margareta
text: "Thou art a member thyself."

speaker: Margareta
text: "The Fellowship."

speaker: Margareta
text: Margareta sees your medallion and raises her eyes.

speaker: Margareta
text: "I see thou art vearing vone ov their medallions, but thou art not truly a member, art thou? Bevare -- there are those in The Fellowship that vill see through thy deception."

speaker: Margareta
text: "Thou vilt soon be enlightened about their true nature."

speaker: Margareta
text: "Thou shalt learn more about them in due time."

speaker: Margareta
text: "Jergi is mine husband, ov course. Now he has the veight ov guiding the gypsy race in these	troubled times."

speaker: Margareta
text: "Fairvell. Go in peace."

speaker: Sasha
text: You see a young gypsy lad. He is wearing a Fellowship medallion. His eyes look down and his expression is one of extreme sorrow.

speaker: Sasha
text: Sasha looks up. "Good day to thee, <HONORIFIC>."

speaker: Sasha
text: "My name is Sasha."

speaker: Sasha
text: "I am too young to have a job. I am a gypsy as my parents vere gypsies. I am also a member of The Fellowship."

speaker: Sasha
text: "My parents - Frederico and Tania - vere murdered. I do not know vhy anyone vould vant to harm them." The words choke out of the boy. Suddenly he is overwhelmed by grief and is unable to speak further.

speaker: Sasha
text: "It happened at the sawmill in Minoc."

speaker: Sasha
text: "For the past veek I have been avay from home doing vork for The Fellowship."

speaker: Sasha
text: "I have returned to be vith Margareta and Jergi to grieve for my parents. They did not approve of my joining The Fellowship but I know that they vere concerned out of their love for me, just as I loved them."

speaker: Sasha
text: "She is very vise and knows many things but vhen I asked her if I should go back to The Fellowship or stay with them she did not answer me."

speaker: Sasha
text: "He vas my father's brother. He is a good man and vise. Now he is the leader of our people. He vill do what is right for us."

speaker: Sasha
text: "Perhaps thou shouldst talk vith him."

speaker: Sasha
text: The lad stoically nods and turns away.

speaker: Gladstone
text: You see a handsome craftsman with an intense, piercing gaze.

speaker: Gladstone
text: Gladstone shakes your hand and you can feel just a trace of sculptor's clay clinging to his palm. Although he hardly knows you, he treats you like an old friend.

speaker: Gladstone
text: "My name is Gladstone, <HONORIFIC>. At thy service."

speaker: Gladstone
text: "I am a glassblower and a sculptor. I make mostly bottles and bowls. But in my time I have constructed all manners of statuary out of glass as well."

speaker: Gladstone
text: The man's eyes study you for a moment. "Thou dost not know what has happened? William, our local Sawyer found two gypsies murdered in his sawmill."

speaker: Gladstone
text: "There is active commerce here in Minoc sufficient to keep the Artist's Guild financially solvent. But in recent weeks I have come to fear we may not keep it going for very much longer. Unlike The Fellowship or Owen's monument, we do not have much political power. Now other events make our troubles seem less important."

speaker: Gladstone
text: "The Artist's Guild is taxed mercilessly by the Britannian Tax Council. Even in our best year it is a struggle to make ends meet. It seems that we are not considered important enough to be given an even chance."

speaker: Gladstone
text: "Surely thou hast heard about the murders of Frederico and Tania?!"

speaker: Gladstone
text: "The Artist's Guild is a group of local craftsmen. We sell our wares here in Minoc. While we are organized as a guild of equal members, I am tentatively the Guild head."

speaker: Gladstone
text: "I shudder to think such foul deeds are so freely committed in our fair town. Art thou investigating it? I wish thee all success in tracking the culprit. I barely knew Frederico or Tania, but I did meet their son Sasha once."

speaker: Gladstone
text: "He befriended Seara and stayed the night with us once. He seemed like a nice young man, but misguided."

speaker: Gladstone
text: "We do not get along very well with those people. I believe we have been unofficially marked as enemies of The Fellowship ever since all of the members of the Artist's Guild refused Elynor's invitation to join. They dislike us because they consider us to be indisposed toward Unity."

speaker: Gladstone
text: "Dost thou think of us as thine enemy?"

speaker: Gladstone
text: "Then get out of my sight! I do not wish to speak with thee!"

speaker: Gladstone
text: "Then I shall give thee the benefit of the doubt for now. But know that I do what I must to protect our Guild."

speaker: Gladstone
text: "Owen the shipwright is commissioning a statue of himself to be built in the center of town. The Artist's Guild decided to have nothing to do with this foolishness, of course. But just the word of this statue has spread and now orders are coming in from all over Britannia. Merchants want to have a ship built by the 'famous' Owen, master shipwright of Minoc."

speaker: Gladstone
text: "Oh, yes, that reminds me! I cannot speak for long, I'm afraid. There is, after all, that barren slab in the center of town with nothing for it now. The Mayor has commissioned us to create something to fill the empty space. I don't want to say anything about it other than it's going to be wonderful. It will not be ready for quite a while but once it is, I hope thou wilt be able to return to Minoc then and see it. In better times perhaps. Farewell, then."

speaker: Gladstone
text: "I fear we have grievously miscalculated by thinking that if we boycotted the statue, it would not be built. It seems all the talk of it has made Owen into some sort of bizarre legend around this area, and the bloody statue hasn't even gone up yet! But that, I fear, is not the worst of the situation."

speaker: Gladstone
text: "Once the statue is built, orders for ship-building are bound to increase even more! It won't take long before all local commerce will become affected by it. Owen will be purchasing more of the local resources, which will cause prices to rise, especially at the sawmill, and that will surely force the Artist's Guild into bankruptcy."

speaker: Gladstone
text: "I regret that I do not have any of my work for sale at present. Like our other artists I have a backlog of orders that will keep me busy for the foreseeable future. But there are several examples of my work, of which I am most proud, in the Guild Hall on display. If thou art interested, please have a look at them."

speaker: Gladstone
text: "Good journey, my friend."

speaker: Xanthia
text: You see a cheerful woman with bright eyes and blonde hair.

speaker: Xanthia
text: "Hello again, <HONORIFIC>." says Xanthia.

speaker: Xanthia
text: "Hello, my name is Xanthia."

speaker: Xanthia
text: "I am a member of the Artist's Guild in Minoc. I make and sell candelabras."

speaker: Xanthia
text: "If thou wouldst not mind, we can perhaps get to know each other during a more sociable occasion! Two people have been recently murdered over at William's sawmill! This is hardly the time to get to know someone!"

speaker: Xanthia
text: "We are a guild of artists and craftspeople united for the common good and dedicated to the advancement of the arts, as well as showing other artists that it is possible to exist solely by thine own efforts without sacrificing thy creativity."

speaker: Xanthia
text: "I make simple candelabras, but sometimes I will do commissioned work, making more specific ones. I was hired by The Fellowship to make the candelabras for all of their Fellowship halls."

speaker: Xanthia
text: "Elynor, the head of the local Fellowship branch, showed me a picture of the Fellowship symbol and I based the design for my candelabra on that."

speaker: Xanthia
text: "Yes, she's quite a recruiter. Why, she got Burnside, our Mayor, to join, as well as Gregor, the local head of the Britannian Mining Company, and Owen, our shipwright. He is soon to be famous, I am sorry to say. She has never asked me to join, thank goodness."

speaker: Xanthia
text: You describe the candelabra found at the murder scene to Xanthia. Her eyes widen with recognition. "Yes, that is one of the candelabras I made. 'Twas in the sawmill at the murder site?"

speaker: Xanthia
text: Xanthia looks shocked. "How horrible! I swear I do not know how it could have gotten there! Thou shouldst certainly ask Elynor about it!"

speaker: Xanthia
text: She gives you a slightly cross look. "Well, I hope that thou didst not steal it from Elynor."

speaker: Xanthia
text: "With the success of the mine, Minoc is a prosperous city. Not a place where one is used to having murders happen. A good place for our Artist's Guild to do well. But things have always been hard for us here. Now I fear they may get worse."

speaker: Xanthia
text: "That is what Gladstone says. Thou hadst better ask him about it."

speaker: Xanthia
text: "It is so terrible! I never knew Frederico or Tania personally, but I did meet their son, Sasha, once. He was a nice boy, if somewhat misguided. He spent the night with us once at the Artist's Guild, as a guest of Seara."

speaker: Xanthia
text: "They are to build a monument to Owen for some reason or another. Owen and Elynor refuse to use anyone from the Guild to help build it! Rather rude of them, dost thou not think?"

speaker: Xanthia
text: "Farewell, <HONORIFIC>. I hope I was of some assistance to thee."

speaker: Zorn
text: You see a man whose long hours of difficult, smouldering work have frozen his face into a rigid expression with eyes like hot coals.

speaker: Zorn
text: "How may I serve thee?" says Zorn.

speaker: Zorn
text: "I am Zorn."

speaker: Zorn
text: "I am the blacksmith of Minoc."

speaker: Zorn
text: "Dost thou have no respect for the dead? Indeed, trying to solicit at a terrible time like this! When people have been found murdered over at William's sawmill!"

speaker: Zorn
text: "I make weapons and armour."

speaker: Zorn
text: "Minoc is quite a city. Money changes hands here. But it does not keep people happy. They find something to squabble over. And now these terrible murders have everyone afraid."

speaker: Zorn
text: "All of the weapons and armour I sell are made by mine own hand. They would serve thee well."

speaker: Zorn
text: "Perhaps we could speak more of these things another time. Say, perhaps during the business hours of my shop?"

speaker: Zorn
text: "The smithy is currently closed for outside business. Thou shalt have to return some other time."

speaker: Zorn
text: "I have an assortment of very lethal weapons to show thee."

speaker: Zorn
text: "The smithy is currently closed for outside business. Thou shalt have to return some other time."

speaker: Zorn
text: "Thou mayest buy fine armour from me."

speaker: Zorn
text: "This noise over Owen's monument, for instance. People ought to tend to their own business and let others handle their own, foolish or not."

speaker: Zorn
text: "He is our town shipwright. He is a man who has an exceedingly high opinion of himself."

speaker: Zorn
text: "Owen is building a monument to himself. It is forty feet tall, depicting him holding up a roll of plans. Pigeons will have a place to sit, forevermore. Why argue over something as unimportant as that?"

speaker: Zorn
text: "No one in this town ever really hated the gypsies, at least not that I have ever been aware of. Who could have done such a thing?"

speaker: Zorn
text: You present the Caddellite to Zorn. "This is amazing! Why I thought that the only place to find Caddellite was the lost island of Ambrosia. What should I make with this?"

speaker: Zorn
text: You describe the sort of helmet that you require, one that can block out the dangerous sound from the cube generator. Zorn nods. "Yes, I can make some for thee. I shall start work immediately."

speaker: Zorn
text: "But thou dost not have any Caddellite chunks with which to make helmets!"

speaker: Zorn
text: "Thou hast <VAR> in thy party. I am afraid thou does not have enough Caddellite for me to make that many helmets."

speaker: Zorn
text: Zorn takes the Caddellite from you and begins his work.

speaker: Zorn
text: "Thou hast <VAR> Caddellite chunks. That is how many helmets I can make for thee."

speaker: Zorn
text: Zorn takes the Caddellite from you and begins his work. You watch in fascination as the master blacksmith softens the ore in the fire, then molds it into	shape. Zorn quickly takes the necessary measurements, then makes some adjustments with the hot material. Finally, it is done.

speaker: Zorn
text: Zorn dips the helmet in water to cool it.

speaker: Zorn
text: Zorn dips the helmets in water to cool them.

speaker: Zorn
text: "Here, I have met thy request to thy precise specifications."

speaker: Zorn
text: He hands you the helmet.

speaker: Zorn
text: He hands you the helmets.

speaker: Zorn
text: "Thou art too encumbered!"

speaker: Zorn
text: "Goodbye, <HONORIFIC>."

speaker: Seara
text: You see a handsome, creative-looking young man.

speaker: Seara
text: "Greetings, <HONORIFIC>," says Seara.

speaker: Seara
text: "I am called Seara, <HONORIFIC>. A pleasure to meet thee."

speaker: Seara
text: "I am a member of our local Artist's Guild here in Minoc."

speaker: Seara
text: "Please, <HONORIFIC>, now is not the time to speak in such a casual way! Why, not far from this very spot there have been not one, but two murders committed!"

speaker: Seara
text: "Yes, we have an Artist's Guild here in Minoc. I am a member. The other members are Xanthia and Gladstone. Thou canst purchase some of the finest crafts available anywhere in Britannia there. I, for example, make clocks."

speaker: Seara
text: "Xanthia is a very talented young woman. She makes very elaborate and distinctive candelabras."

speaker: Seara
text: "Gladstone is a sculptor and a glassblower. He also is in charge of most of the business decisions for the Guild."

speaker: Seara
text: "I make all types of clocks and watches that tell the time reliably to the second. I would be happy to sell thee one but right now I have a two year backlog to fill."

speaker: Seara
text: "Until the monument was to be built and now these murders I believed this town to be a good place to live."

speaker: Seara
text: "It is horrible. Frederico and Tania were looking for their son, Sasha. He had run away to join the Fellowship. How could this have happened to them?" Seara slowly shakes his head.

speaker: Seara
text: "I met him a few weeks ago when he came to town looking for the local Fellowship branch. I once let him stay the night at the Guild Hall. He said his father would beat him if he knew he was thinking of joining The Fellowship and I believed him. Sasha's father could be a cruel man. He is basically a good lad, just looking for the truth like a lot of us are. Unfortunately, he is looking in the wrong place."

speaker: Seara
text: "I have not seen or heard of Sasha since we last spoke of him. I do not know if he ever joined The Fellowship."

speaker: Seara
text: "Their camp is just outside of town. There are not too many of them left. I understand that Sasha's aunt, Margareta, is an amazing fortune teller. For a few gold coins, she can tell thee many things that may be very useful to thee."

speaker: Seara
text: "No offense intended to thee, but I do not share thy beliefs. In fact I think few of the members of thy Fellowship are sincere in all their talk of unity, trust and worthiness. But Sasha is old enough to make up his mind for himself, though I regret not sending him home that night."

speaker: Seara
text: "No, I am not a member or anything like that, but I have heard the basic speech from Sasha so many times that I have it memorized. I never tried to dissuade him from joining The Fellowship even though I have no belief in it. I think Sasha is old enough to start making his decisions for himself. Now I truly regret not sending him home the moment I saw him."

speaker: Seara
text: "That shipwright Owen is a self-righteous fool. His statue will be nothing more than a monument to all the hurtful bad feelings he has caused in this town. I cannot believe that such a meaningless and obvious charade	could jeopardize our Guild's future."

speaker: Seara
text: "Thou hadst best ask Gladstone about that."

speaker: Seara
text: "A pleasant day to thee, <HONORIFIC>. Do come see us again."

speaker: Karl
text: You see a mountain man who appears to have been in the wilderness a long time. He gives you a long look, then he snorts and looks away.

speaker: Karl
text: "What dost thou want? Leave me alone!"

speaker: Karl
text: "I am not in the habit of speakin' to strangers but seein' as how thou dost not appear to be very intelligent, I shall humor thee for now. My name is Karl, formerly of Minoc."

speaker: Karl
text: "Job?! Art thou mad, <HONORIFIC>?! Firstly, if thou dost wish to offer me employment I have no interest in it. Secondly, if thou dost wish to hire my services for anything for any reason, then I reject thine offer most enthusiastically. Thirdly, if thou dost wonder what my job is, then wonder no more for I have not one.	Fourth and lastly, if thou dost wonder why I have no job then stop it right now because it is none of thy business!"

speaker: Karl
text: "Do not ask me of Minoc, the filthy little town of Fellowship fools, casual murders and monuments to incompetence. I do not even live here and I would not if thou didst pay me!"

speaker: Karl
text: "Hmmph. Why should that be any concern of mine? People kill each other every day. Oh, thou art investigating the crime! Well, do not let me keep thee from it. After thou dost catch the murderer thou canst build a statue of him."

speaker: Karl
text: "Gads! Thou dost want me to join! Away from me, thou dolt!"

speaker: Karl
text: "Do I look like a member of The Fellowship to thee? I do not even know what The Fellowship is! And I do not care!"

speaker: Karl
text: "Owen, the shipwright, dost deserve to have a monument built to him. It should be in the shape of a gallows and it should have him hanging from it."

speaker: Karl
text: "My brother - mine only family in the world - served aboard a ship built by Owen. The ship was one of several that sank three years ago during the first storm it ever encountered. My brother went down with it and was never seen again."

speaker: Karl
text: "I confronted Owen with this and he denied that it had anything to do with his workmanship. I returned that night and stole the plans he had drafted, so at least no other ships would ever be built like them again. But it left me so angry at the world that I knew I could not live among people ever again. I went away to live up in the mountains. The only times I ever come back are to fetch a few supplies and maybe have a drink of Rutherford's fine ale once in a while."

speaker: Karl
text: "Three other ships that were built from Owen's basic designs all sunk within the first year of their launch. Over a dozen lives were lost due to that vainglorious bastard!"

speaker: Karl
text: "If not for Rutherford's fine ale, there would no purpose to the existence of civilization."

speaker: Karl
text: "I still have those plans up in my cabin. Every once in a while I try to figure them out. I suspect no one in town, save for Owen himself, could understand them. Maybe Julia, the tinker, would be able to shed some light on them. But she would never listen to an old mountain man like me."

speaker: Julia
text: "Yes I would, Karl! Thou dost have too low opinion of thyself! Raise thy spirits, please!"

speaker: Karl
text: "Far away from the mire of present day society is where I belong. In the wilderness thou canst know what is what."

speaker: Karl
text: "If thou dost want to show Julia the plans, I will give them to thee. They are in my cabin southeast of the BMC office."

speaker: Karl
text: "Make up thy mind! Art thou following me or not?! If thou art following me then close thy mouth, move thy feet and let us get on."

speaker: Karl
text: "I know I can be a bear to get along with sometimes. I reckon it is just my nature to be an ornery bastard. But I do appreciate what few friends I have and I know that thou hast been one to me. Take good care of thyself, Avatar."

speaker: Karl
text: "Cease thy racket then before I lose my temper!"

speaker: Owen
text: Owen will not interrupt his participation in The Fellowship meeting to talk with you.

speaker: Owen
text: "I am late for The Fellowship Meeting! I cannot speak with thee now!"

speaker: Owen
text: You see a young man dressed in an expensive tunic. He is very serious.

speaker: Owen
text: Owen looks at you and sniffs. "It would appear thou dost wish to speak with me again."

speaker: Owen
text: "My name, <HONORIFIC>, is Owen. It is a name I suspect thou shalt be hearing more of in the future."

speaker: Owen
text: He looks you in the eye and speaks without the slightest trace of modesty. "I am," he says, "the greatest shipwright in the history of Minoc. I am the greatest shipwright who has ever lived!"

speaker: Owen
text: "After years of breaking my back trying to make something of this ungrateful little town, I'm giving up. I swear I will never build another ship as long as I live. That will teach them! No matter how they may beg or plead, I will not do it."

speaker: Owen
text: "Well, I shall certainly forgive thy poor manners for I know how privileged thou must feel for meeting me, but thou must know that two people have just been discovered in the sawmill, having been murdered!"

speaker: Owen
text: "And dost thou know how I became that way? I shall tell thee! I started to hear a voice in mine head! Oh, I know that thou shalt think me mad..."

speaker: Owen
text: "These were not the voices of anyone I have ever known. But still these voices had a profound effect on me..."

speaker: Owen
text: "After searching for a meaning to this voice - which proved difficult, for how dost thou tell someone, especially a stranger, that thou art hearing a voice in thine head - I came across The Fellowship. They taught me what the voice was."

speaker: Owen
text: "This was the voice of reason within mine own mind which sought to guide my life in its proper direction. The Fellowship taught me how to trust this voice and heed what it says. And thou canst see the results in mine own life! I have mastered my craft and advanced the techniques of ship-building through the methods I have devised."

speaker: Owen
text: Owen looks at you and suddenly seems flustered. "Uh, I have no ships for sale presently. I have been working on a few improvements. But if thou wouldst, thou couldst commission me to build one for thee. A deed to one of the ships I build costs 1000 gold coins. Dost thou wish to buy one?"

speaker: Owen
text: "'Tis money well spent, thou shalt see! I shall begin work immediately. I will be building based upon some of my more recent designs. I shall give thee thy ship's deed in advance"

speaker: Owen
text: "It will be called the Excellencia."

speaker: Owen
text: "I would give thee thy deed but thou art carrying too much."

speaker: Owen
text: "Take thy gold back! I cannot in good conscious keep it!"

speaker: Owen
text: "I would give thee thy gold back but I seem to have misplaced it."

speaker: Owen
text: "I am dreadfully sorry," he sniffs, "but thou dost not have enough gold."

speaker: Owen
text: "Art thou certain? Thou shalt find no better ships in all of Britannia! Very well, then!"

speaker: Owen
text: "Wouldst thou perhaps be interested in purchasing a fine sextant? I have one which I would be willing to part with for a fine bargain. The price is 150 gold. Art thou interested?"

speaker: Owen
text: "Excellent! I knew that thou wouldst appreciate owning the sextant of Owen the shipwright. Thou art a fine person, able to discern those quality items which are worth a bit of extra coin."

speaker: Owen
text: "Thou knave! To get mine hopes up so, only to cruelly dash them. Thou dost not possess enough gold to buy my treasure. If thou dost return with more coinage, PERHAPS I will allow thee to bid on it again."

speaker: Owen
text: "Thou dost not have enough strength to add my treasure to thy pack. Thou must dispose of some of thy worthless dross to make room for this beauty. I will await thy return to purchase the sextant at this fine, low price."

speaker: Owen
text: "Hmph. Well, let it be known that thou didst pass up the chance to buy the sextant of the famous Owen the shipwright, and thou shalt be known for the knave and simpleton that thou art."

speaker: Owen
text: "Mine establishment is presently closed. I do not wish to discuss business at this time."

speaker: Owen
text: "I have even written a book describing the advances I have made in the methods of ship-building. It is very advanced but I have tried to write it so that it is accessible to the layman. Wouldst thou be interested in purchasing a copy?"

speaker: Owen
text: "Yes, of course thou wouldst."

speaker: Owen
text: "Here it is."

speaker: Owen
text: "Thou art carrying too much to take thy book."

speaker: Owen
text: "I shall return thy money."

speaker: Owen
text: "I wouldst give thee back thy gold but thou cannot take it."

speaker: Owen
text: "Thou dost not have enough money!"

speaker: Owen
text: "Hmph! I suppose that it would be beyond thy comprehension, anyway."

speaker: Owen
text: "I can well understand thine impatience but I have just begun work on it. It shall be ready when I am finished with it. Now, until such time, I would appreciate it if thou wouldst not waste my valuable time."

speaker: Owen
text: "I cannot build thee a ship as I suspect we both know."

speaker: Owen
text: "Nor can I take thy money for one. Here, I shall return it to thee."

speaker: Owen
text: "Oh, my, thou art too encumbered to take back thy 1000 gold coins! Come back when thine hands are less full!"

speaker: Owen
text: "I cannot help thee with that."

speaker: Owen
text: "Despite all this business with murders, I must confess that I love it here. This is the place where I was born. They love me. They are going to be building a monument here in mine honor. I suppose I have been worthy of it, but still I can't help but be flattered."

speaker: Owen
text: "Apparently, building the greatest ships to ever set sail in history and all that that has done for Minoc are no longer enough! No! Thanks to that pompous idiot of a mayor I am denied the rightful tribute of which I have proven myself more than worthy. Design flaws, bah! How many ships has Mayor Burnside built in his miserable little life?!"

speaker: Owen
text: "That is right. The sawmill is located southeast of town. Almost everyone in town is down there. Thou shouldst probably go down there if thou dost want to find out more. I abhor violence."

speaker: Owen
text: He shakes his head slowly. "They are going to be unveiling my monument sometime in the near future. Dost thou think that talk of these events will keep people away from the ceremony? That would be a tragedy!"

speaker: Owen
text: You tell him about the many innocent civilians who lost their lives on the ship he built. Owen shakes his head slowly. "I do not know. I have no idea how it could have happened. It is difficult to conceive of the pain such great loss of life brings into this world. But I did my best when I built those ships. I did not want those men to die. Thou must believe me."

speaker: Owen
text: Owen appears distressed. "The tribute to me is now no more than a tombstone."

speaker: Owen
text: "The changes it has made in my personal life have helped me tremendously."

speaker: Owen
text: "Thou canst ask Elynor all about it unless she is not speaking to thee either. Perhaps the details of thy personal life will amuse her more than do mine."

speaker: Owen
text: "My friend, there was a time when I thought that my life was at its end. I felt as though I had been swallowed into a cold, deep hole of darkness."

speaker: Owen
text: "My very soul felt as though it had sunk into a place into which no light could enter... Soon after I discovered The Fellowship. The difference that it made in my life was miraculous."

speaker: Owen
text: "I have been having a difficult time lately trying to speak to Elynor. It seems that she has no time for me. Back when I was making preparations for the monument she was always stopping by and willing to have words with me."

speaker: Owen
text: "Oh, thou canst ask anyone in town about it. They all know."

speaker: Owen
text: "I know! My work will stand as my monument! My name will endure long after any statue has worn away to dust! People will remember -me-, I promise thee that!"

speaker: Owen
text: And, with a dramatic flourish, Owen produces a dagger. Before you can stop him, he plunges it into his chest. He coughs loudly as blood spurts from his mouth, soaking his fine linen tunic in wine-red guilt. After a moment, it is all over. Owen, the greatest shipwright who ever lived, is dead.

speaker: Owen
text: "The Crown Jewel was in town and left early this morning. It was scheduled to sail for Paws."

speaker: Owen
text: "I have heard nothing more of the Crown Jewel since we last spoke of it, <HONORIFIC>."

speaker: Owen
text: "I saw a man with a hook for a hand wandering around town last night."

speaker: Owen
text: "I have heard nothing more of this man Hook since we last spoke of him, <HONORIFIC>."

speaker: Owen
text: "Tired of benefitting from my presence? Very well. I shall see thee again, I hope!"

speaker: Owen
text: "Be on thy way, then. Time is fleeting, as is fame."

speaker: Burnside
text: The Fellowship meeting is in progress, and Burnside will not speak with you now.

speaker: Burnside
text: "I cannot speak now! I am late for the Fellowship meeting!"

speaker: Burnside
text: You see an elderly man struggling to maintain a regal posture.

speaker: Burnside
text: His eyes widen at the sight of you.

speaker: Burnside
text: "I had heard thou were travelling in Britannia again, but it took mine own eyes to believe it! Welcome, Avatar!"

speaker: Burnside
text: "Ahh, Avatar. Good to see thee again." says Burnside.

speaker: Burnside
text: "Burnside is my name."

speaker: Burnside
text: "I am Mayor of Minoc and have been lo these past twenty years and more."

speaker: Burnside
text: "I beseech thee, <HONORIFIC>, do show some respect for the two poor souls who have been found murdered there in William's sawmill."

speaker: Burnside
text: "Apart from this business of the murders we are a town run by commerce. Gold runs this town. As goes the money, so goes Minoc. Take this monument affair, for instance."

speaker: Burnside
text: "As Frederico and Tania were not actually residents of Minoc there is little I can do as Mayor other than increase the town guard. The investigation falls somewhat beyond my jurisdiction. It would appear the killer or killers were from out of town and are probably long gone by now. Thank goodness."

speaker: Burnside
text: "I am sure thou art aware of the plans for a monument of Owen, the shipwright. He is paying for it himself. I am usually against such public vanity but The Fellowship is very much in favor of it."

speaker: Burnside
text: "This town would have been ruined if I had allowed that monument to be built, so I immediately forbade it, of course."

speaker: Burnside
text: "But in this special case it does immeasurable good for the town. It increases our prestige. People will come from all over Britannia for the unveiling."

speaker: Burnside
text: "Why, even Lord British himself will be in attendance! It is a special opportunity when one gets a private audience."

speaker: Burnside
text: "Ah, I see thou art wearing thy Fellowship medallion. I received mine from Elynor when The Fellowship branch was first opened here a few years ago."

speaker: Burnside
text: "Yes, I wear the Fellowship medallion, given to me by Elynor. Do not worry thyself. I shall not try to make thee join!" He laughs nervously at his own little joke.

speaker: Burnside
text: "Elynor tells me The Fellowship will be doing good works here in the future. I am proud to be a member of thy society although I must confess to being fairly ignorant concerning thy, umm, our philosophy."

speaker: Burnside
text: "Elynor says The Fellowship could bring much money into Minoc. It would be wonderful for trade. I could never let my personal feelings get in the way of the good of this town."

speaker: Burnside
text: "I was given an honorary membership when the Fellowship branch was first opened in Minoc. I do not attend regular meetings. I hope thou'rt not disappointed in me?"

speaker: Burnside
text: "I am sorry, Avatar. I will try to do well and be a more valuable member of the Fellowship. I beg thee, do not speak of this to Elynor."

speaker: Burnside
text: "Thank heaven! I wear this medallion mainly for ceremonial purposes, as I suspect thou dost. We both see that support of The Fellowship is currently the wisest course of action politically, no matter our personal feelings."

speaker: Burnside
text: "Avatar, may I tell thee a secret?"

speaker: Burnside
text: "Avatar, I must confess to thee that I feel The Fellowship promotes a philosophy that is dubious at best, and its membership seems to be comprised chiefly of fools and emotional weaklings."

speaker: Burnside
text: "Hrmph! Well, then, kindly forget mine ill-considered words!"

speaker: Burnside
text: You show the Mayor the plans Owen had drawn, making sure to carefully point out the flaws discovered by Julia. The Mayor is aghast.

speaker: Burnside
text: "This is terrible! No one must see this! It would ruin Owen and cause irreparable damage to our town if it became known that our shipwright caused those deaths!"

speaker: Burnside
text: "But very few suspect the deaths are attributable to Owen's shipbuilding! We can destroy the plans and the truth would never get out! It would save the town from disgrace and possible ruin!"

speaker: Burnside
text: "Then again, the ships Owen builds will continue to sink. It would harm Minoc even more if it were to become known as the place where the "death ships" are made. A town that built a monument to an incompetent."

speaker: Burnside
text: "There are no two ways about it. The statue must be stopped. I am hereby cancelling the erection of the statue."

speaker: Burnside
text: "Oh, and...er, Avatar... couldst thou please go inform Owen of this bad news for me? I am a bit busy at the moment. Besides, I think he will take it much better hearing it from thee."

speaker: Burnside
text: "A pleasure, friend Avatar. A pleasure."

speaker: Rutherford
text: You see a weary-looking man who is missing his right arm. With his one hand he scratches his head and squints in your general direction.

speaker: Rutherford
text: "Oy, how ye been, <HONORIFIC>?" Rutherford calls out to you.

speaker: Rutherford
text: He lets out a sharp cough to clear his throat. "Rutherford's me name. Pleased ta meet 'chur."

speaker: Rutherford
text: He extends his greasy hand for you to shake and does not retract it until it is clasped.

speaker: Rutherford
text: "Why I be the barkeep of The Checquered Cork. No better place in Minoc to discuss the events of the day."

speaker: Rutherford
text: He coughs into the rag he had just been using to polish the bar.

speaker: Rutherford
text: "Hello again, Sir Dupre! Didst thou enjoy mine establishment so much that thou hast returned?"

speaker: Dupre
text: "My dear Rutherford, this is not a reflection on The Checquered Cork, but I simply like a good drink!"

speaker: Rutherford
text: "'Tis no time for idle chatter! There have been two people murdered over at William's sawmill!"

speaker: Rutherford
text: "We have a cornucopian variety of elixirs to quench thy tongue and gourmet dishes to appease thy palate."

speaker: Rutherford
text: "As I have finished my workday, I ask thee to come back another time. Thou dost have my thanks."

speaker: Rutherford
text: "A room for the night is quite reasonable. Only 8 gold per person. Want one?"

speaker: Rutherford
text: "Thou art carrying too much to take the room key, <HONORIFIC>!"

speaker: Rutherford
text: "Here is thy room key. It is good only until thou dost leave."

speaker: Rutherford
text: "Thou dost not have enough gold, eh? That be right bad."

speaker: Rutherford
text: "Mayhaps another night, then."

speaker: Rutherford
text: "If thou wouldst please make thy request at a time that was during my normal business hours, I would be most grateful."

speaker: Rutherford
text: "Yep, this town's usually bloody quiet. That was until recently!" His squinting eye suddenly opens wide and stares straight at you.

speaker: Rutherford
text: "Say, when exackly again didst thou say thou didst arrive in town, stranger?"

speaker: Rutherford
text: After a moment of carefully observing you, he shrugs his shoulders and goes back to wiping off the bar.

speaker: Rutherford
text: "Before all this evil at the sawmill, the buzz were all about the monument."

speaker: Rutherford
text: "Well, I suppose that clears thee from the list o' possible murderers. If'n thou wert the murderer, thou wouldst not have to be askin' questions o'people about wha' 'appened regardin' the murders. Thou wouldst already know, havin' been there."

speaker: Rutherford
text: "Say, thou be not from around here?" He looks at you skeptically. "Thou art not from the Fellowship by any chance, art thou?"

speaker: Rutherford
text: "I thought so!"

speaker: Rutherford
text: "Just askin'! Thou dost not have to take any offense!"

speaker: Rutherford
text: "I know him! He be a pirate who lives in Buccaneer's Den. They say Hook is so mean he'd kill his own mudder for the right price, an' I would wager they's right."

speaker: Rutherford
text: "Why, I got into a fight with this Hook once. I was lucky and I escaped losin' only my right arm and still with one good eye left. It was somewhere around that time that I started having second thoughts about my career as a pirate and now here I be."

speaker: Rutherford
text: "I have not seen him recently, but the description of the murder scene certainly sounds like his handiwork!"

speaker: Rutherford
text: "That ship was, indeed, here of late. In fact, 'twas the night of the murders! Could there be a connection? Hmmm..."

speaker: Rutherford
text: "Thank goodness that with all the town at each others' throats in recent weeks we have the Fellowship tryin' to hold the town together. I be no member or nothin', but I just a'heared of all the good things they done. Feedin' the poor an' such."

speaker: Rutherford
text: "Oh, thou must mean thet statuer they are goin' ta build of our shipwright. His name is Owen, a local boy. I understan' it is to be as tall as a man on horseback and shows Owen gazin' through a telerscope or some such thing like that."

speaker: Rutherford
text: "I shall see thee later... At least I will if thou dost stay in the front o' me good eye."

speaker: William
text: William does not want to avert his attention from the Fellowship meeting.

speaker: William
text: "I must not stop to speak with thee now! I am late for the Fellowship meeting at the hall!"

speaker: William
text: You see a man with a very worried look on his face.

speaker: William
text: "Avatar! What is it? Why dost thou want to talk to me again? What is wrong now?!" says William.

speaker: William
text: "I am called William, <HONORIFIC>."

speaker: William
text: "I work in the sawmill here in Minoc."

speaker: William
text: "What a ludicrous question at a time like this! Why, I have just been given the fright of my life when I entered my sawmill and saw those two who have not only been killed quite dead, but torn apart nearly beyond recognition!"

speaker: William
text: "I take the logs that are made from all the trees that are cut down by the logger in Yew, and cut them into planks in the local sawmill. Then I sell the planks - mostly to Owen the shipwright, and some to the Artist's Guild as well."

speaker: William
text: "It was such a quiet town until these murders happened. I cannot believe it."

speaker: William
text: "I found the bodies first thing this morning when I went to open the sawmill. It took all of the discipline I have gained from the Triad of Inner Strength and the teachings of The Fellowship to keep from going mad at the sight of it. It must have happened sometime last night but I swear to thee I never heard a thing!"

speaker: William
text: "I swear by The Fellowship I have already told thee all I know concerning the murders!"

speaker: William
text: "I have been a member of The Fellowship for only a short time. I have only of late begun attending Elynor's meetings. Only since they announced the monument was to be built."

speaker: William
text: "I am so glad thou art my brother in The Fellowship; I know I may trust thee. It is all of the others in this town that I worry about."

speaker: William
text: "Wouldst thou like to know more of The Fellowship?"

speaker: William
text: "Trust me, thou canst not possibly understand how cruel and terrible life can be! Thou dost need The Fellowship! I am lucky to have found it in time to face mine own moment of truth! I hope thou dost realize that thou dost need The Fellowship before it is too late!"

speaker: William
text: "Thou dost know! The monument of Owen the shipwright standing on the bow of a tall ship. Everyone in town doth know of it!"

speaker: William
text: As soon as he has dismissed you, the overwrought William hides his face in his hands.

speaker: Karenna
text: You see a stealthy-looking woman, dressed all in green. There is a wicked grin on her face.

speaker: Karenna
text: "How good to see thee again," says Karenna.

speaker: Karenna
text: "I answer to Karenna, and to nothing else."

speaker: Karenna
text: "I am a teacher in Minoc, along with Jakher."

speaker: Karenna
text: "An odd question to ask at such a time as this, <HONORIFIC>. Dost thou know that two people lie dead in that sawmill and they are dead from the hand of perpetrator or perpetrators unknown?"

speaker: Karenna
text: "Minoc was usually busy, but quiet. Then our town was bothered by this nonsense over Owen's monument, and now these murders."

speaker: Karenna
text: "Shocking! Such things do not normally happen here. It well proves the value of knowing how to defend oneself."

speaker: Karenna
text: "He is quite an able trainer in his own right. Not as skilled as myself, obviously. But I do think he is cute, though I bid thee, do not tell him that I spoke of this. It will only encourage him."

speaker: Jakher
text: "Art thou speaking about me? Mine ears are burning!"

speaker: Karenna
text: "Nothing thou shouldst be concerned about, Jakher." She winks at you.

speaker: Karenna
text: "I teach that singular skill which enables one to learn all the lessons of life without losing it in the process. Combat!"

speaker: Karenna
text: "I would charge thee 20 gold for each training session. Art thou still interested?"

speaker: Karenna
text: "Very well. If thou art fortunate thou wilt not have cause to regret it."

speaker: Karenna
text: "Our establishment is now closed. Please come by during business hours."

speaker: Karenna
text: "I understand it is to be thirty feet high and will display our local shipwright as he holds aloft a sextant. Thou wouldst not believe a thing as benign as this could create such trouble."

speaker: Karenna
text: "It would seem the increase in hostilities amongst the fair citizenry over our shipwright's monument has filled much of the local populace with a burning desire to acquire combative skills. Business has never been better!"

speaker: Karenna
text: "Everyone in town is all up in arms about this and that. But surely others would know more of these local politics. I care not."

speaker: Karenna
text: "Jakher told thee he doth find me attractive? He denies it, of course, but I have known for years that he doth have feelings for me."

speaker: Jakher
text: "What? What didst thou say?"

speaker: Karenna
text: "Nothing, Jakher. Go away." She giggles conspiratorally at you.

speaker: Karenna
text: "Frederico, the leader of the Gypsies, and his wife, Tania, were good people. Why, the worst thing I ever knew either of them to do was a simple prank."

speaker: Karenna
text: "Once Frederico threw a rock through the window of the local Fellowship branch... Oh, well, I thought it was amusing!"

speaker: Karenna
text: "Farewell. May all thy journeys be interesting ones."

speaker: Jakher
text: You see a stern but friendly-looking man, dressed in a military fashion. As you watch him, you get the feeling he is sizing you up as well.

speaker: Jakher
text: "How may I be of service to thee?" says Jakher.

speaker: Jakher
text: "I am Jakher, named after a great general from the ancient times of Sosaria. Welcome to Minoc."

speaker: Jakher
text: "Along with Karenna, I am a trainer in the fighting arts. My specialty is strength and strategy. On the field of battle, if one does not use his head while using one's muscles, he is in danger of losing it."

speaker: Jakher
text: "Perhaps that is something of which we should speak in a more appropriate time. Right now our concern should be to discover who could have been responsible for the two murders	that have just been discovered in William's sawmill."

speaker: Jakher
text: "My price is 20 gold for each training session. Art thou still interested?"

speaker: Jakher
text: "The true value of what I teach is beyond measure. My time is precious to me and therefore valuable. If thou didst pay me a paltry sum and I trained thee anyway, it would be an insult to us both."

speaker: Jakher
text: "'Tis a pity few truly comprehend the value of strategy and tactics. Thou mayest hack and slash with thy sword all that thou wilt, but it cannot do thy thinking for thee."

speaker: Jakher
text: "I am not in the habit of running training sessions at this particular time."

speaker: Jakher
text: "Ours is a city of commerce, although lately its primary trade seems to be gossip and envy. Before these murders, the latest local scandal had been the statue to be built of Owen, the shipwright."

speaker: Jakher
text: "I suspect the killer -- or killers -- are from out of town, and probably long gone by now. There has not been a local murder for	some time before today. Our fair measure of prosperity has made the people here mostly tolerant of each other. That is why the gypsies settled here. The apparent lack of motive is puzzling."

speaker: Jakher
text: "I doubt that anyone in our community is the killer. If the stranger, or strangers, involved were to remain for long after the crime, they would soon be revealed. Therefore,the killers are no longer in town."

speaker: Jakher
text: "A skillful and fierce battler, but a bit short-sighted when it comes to tactics, I'm afraid. Still, a woman as attractive as	she is diverting enough when encountered. But do not mention to her that I said that. It would just encourage her. It is uncomfortable enough sharing the same roof with her as it is."

speaker: Karenna
text: "What art thou whispering about over there?"

speaker: Jakher
text: "Nothing! Nothing at all!" Jakher winks at you.

speaker: Jakher
text: "She is the sort of person who labors under the belief that all problems can be solved in one of three ways. Hit them harder. Hit them faster. Or, hit them some more."

speaker: Karenna
text: "Art thou talking about me? I feel mine ears burning!"

speaker: Jakher
text: "Thou art dreaming, Karenna. Why would I talk about thee?" He giggles conspiratorially at you.

speaker: Jakher
text: "There used to be two training halls in Minoc but one of them burned down after being struck by lightning. Now we are both forced to share this one."

speaker: Jakher
text: "Ah, so Karenna said I was cute, did she? Yes, I have known she has had her sights set on me for years."

speaker: Jakher
text: "I have known Owen as long as anyone in this town. Several years ago, three ships that he built sank. The brother of Karl, one of our more colorful local residents, was killed. No investigation was ever made into the cause of the sinkings, but Owen once confided to me that he secretly blamed himself. He started drinking heavily, and eventually took up with The Fellowship."

speaker: Jakher
text: "Thou wouldst do better to ask Karenna. She is a good friend of the gypsies and would know more about them than I."

speaker: Jakher
text: "It has been a pleasure speaking with thee."

speaker: Jergi
text: You see a swarthy gypsy with soulful eyes, dressed in colorful clothes. He looks as if he has the weight of the world on his shoulders.

speaker: Jergi
text: "Greetings vonce again," Jergi says as he bows, making a swirling gesture with his hand.

speaker: Jergi
text: "I am Jergi. Pleased to make thine acqvaintance."

speaker: Jergi
text: "I am the King ov the Gypsies."

speaker: Jergi
text: "My people have almost completely died out in this vorld. Now that I am their leader I am making their velfare my sole responsibility. Soon I vill decide if ve vill leave Minoc."

speaker: Jergi
text: "Ve gypsies are a people who live to vander. But there are fewer and fewer places vhere ve are velcome. Ve are victimized by the ancient hatreds that have plagued our kind since the days ov ancient Sosaria."

speaker: Jergi
text: "Our people came here because ve thought ve vould be accepted. It seemed for a very long time that ve vere. But after these savage murders it looks like it is time for us to roam vonce again."

speaker: Jergi
text: "Ve have alvays been subject to the prejudices ov others! Ve are called thieves and vorse! But ve are a people that only vish to play our music, and dance, and live in peace. I thought the people here understood this."

speaker: Jergi
text: "Frederico vas mine only brother, and no vone loved Tania more than I did, save for Frederico himself. Vhat happened to them vas unspeakable. I vish I could tell thee more. If thou vishest thou may speak to Sasha, but only briefly. Now is the time for him to mourn."

speaker: Jergi
text: "Some thought ov my brother Frederico as a harsh man, but those ov us who knew him could see that he vas simply governed by the same prides and passions that rule all gypsies."

speaker: Jergi
text: "She vas the most beautiful voman I had ever seen. Both my brother and I vere in love vith her. Ve both tried to vin her heart. I failed and thought that I vould spend the rest ov my life vith no vone. It vas not until last year that my vife Margareta and I vere married and my secretly broken heart vas mended."

speaker: Jergi
text: "He is the son ov Frederico and Tania. He left us to learn more about The Fellowship. Ov course, he feels responsible for vhat happened..."

speaker: Jergi
text: "Ve do not blame Sasha for vhat happened. Ve vill not punish him."

speaker: Jergi
text: "Sasha vill have to decide if he vants to stay vith his people or return to The Fellowship. I believe he vill make the right choice."

speaker: Jergi
text: "My vife is a vise voman who has some ov the necessary talents to see the future. Thou shouldst speak vith her."

speaker: Jergi
text: "I do not know vhat thou art talking about. I know nothing of a mage named Nicodemus, nor of his hourglass. Be vary -- mages are quite mad these days!"

speaker: Jergi
text: "Mayest thou have much fortune in thine endeavors."

speaker: Mikos
text: Mikos is lost in meditation at the Fellowship meeting and does not hear you.

speaker: Mikos
text: "I must run to the Fellowship meeting! I shall speak with thee another time!"

speaker: Mikos
text: A sneering man watches as you approach. His eyes shift back and forth suspiciously.

speaker: Mikos
text: Mikos heaves his shoulders and sighs. "What dost thou want this time?"

speaker: Mikos
text: "I am Mikos."

speaker: Mikos
text: "I am the foreman of the Minoc mine."

speaker: Mikos
text: He spits on the ground. "A pox on them! Down here I am safe from all of their arguing. Next, they will be killing each other."

speaker: Mikos
text: "This mine is run by the Britannian Mining Company. It is inside what was once the dungeon Covetous. They mine for iron ore, lead and other minerals with highly trained miners and special mining machinery."

speaker: Mikos
text: "Currently most of the miners are away as the machines are being repaired. Right now we have two engineers, Owings and Malloy, down in a branch of the main tunnel. Do not disturb them, for they are involved in a special project. We also have a gargoyle, Fodus, who is helping to maintain a semblance of the mine's usual operations."

speaker: Mikos
text: "This place is full of machinery that is very dangerous if thou dost not know what thou art doing. Thou dost not wish to see what one of those digging contraptions can do to a man if he gets too close!"

speaker: Mikos
text: Mikos shakes his head slowly. "I am not sure where the Britannian Mining Company found them."

speaker: Mikos
text: You repeat the words to Mikos that you heard Fodus say. Mikos gives you a shocked look. "I have no idea what he is talking about, but I would say it is typical for a gargoyle. Just trying to shirk of his duty. Say, thou hadst better leave this place if thou ist spending all thy time disrupting the work of the mine!"

speaker: Mikos
text: "Do not wander around down here, <HONORIFIC>. Thou shouldst leave right away."

speaker: Saralek
text: The creature ignores you.

speaker: Saralek
text: The ape-like female appears nervous.

speaker: Saralek
text: The female Emp appears nervous.

speaker: Saralek
text: Saralek greets you. "Hello is said to you, human."

speaker: Saralek
text: She shies away for a moment, and then cautiously steps forward. "I am called Saralek."

speaker: Saralek
text: "`Job' is not understood. Family is what you mean?"

speaker: Saralek
text: "Yes, I am part of a family. The Silverleaf tree is my home. I am bonded with Trellek."

speaker: Saralek
text: "Trellek is my husband."

speaker: Saralek
text: "Trellek has been met by you?" She smiles proudly, and takes another step forward. "What was said by him?"

speaker: Saralek
text: "There are fewer and fewer Silverleaf trees. Many are cut down often. Soon, no Silverleaf trees will be around for our homes."

speaker: Saralek
text: "The trees are cut by a human with a shiny, sharp item."

speaker: Saralek
text: "To join you is his desire?"

speaker: Saralek
text: She thinks for a moment. "His going away is not desired by me." She turns to look directly at you. "But, joining you may be wise action." She sighs.

speaker: Saralek
text: "Permission from Salamon must be gained first. Then permission from me will be granted. Your return to me is necessary for that."

speaker: Saralek
text: "That is good!" She seems very happy and relieved.

speaker: Saralek
text: "She is a very wise Emp. Many humans have been met by her. Knowledge and experience are her talents."

speaker: Saralek
text: Her eyes begin to mist over.

speaker: Saralek
text: "I am sorry. A lie was told by me. Trellek's leaving is not desired by me. Permission will not be given."

speaker: Saralek
text: Her expression changes.

speaker: Saralek
text: "What is the reason you asked him?"

speaker: Saralek
text: "Adventure is not Trellek's desire."

speaker: Saralek
text: She shrugs.

speaker: Saralek
text: She smiles excitedly.

speaker: Saralek
text: "Your wish is to meet wisps?"

speaker: Saralek
text: "An idea how you can be helped by Trellek is had by me. Wisps are contacted by Trellek's whistling. A whistle for you can be made by him, perhaps. Talking with him again should be your next action."

speaker: Saralek
text: "Oh." She appears depressed again.

speaker: Saralek
text: "Goodbye is said to you, human."

speaker: Fodus
text: You see a wingless gargoyle with a terrible skin disease. It looks as if his face is falling off in patches.

speaker: Fodus
text: "To want something else?" Fodus asks.

speaker: Fodus
text: "To be named Fodus."

speaker: Fodus
text: "To be a digger in the mines. To be looking for iron ore and lead and..."

speaker: Fodus
text: "The secret ore..."

speaker: Fodus
text: A wave of delirium passes over the gargoyle. "To... to be going back to work now, Mikos!... To be working hard!... To have no need to give me any more of the the silver fluid..."

speaker: Fodus
text: "To be called... blackrock."

speaker: Fodus
text: "To be the lode located in a hidden area of the mine..." The gargoyle's eyes roll up into his head. He is obviously sick.

speaker: Fodus
text: "To need the venom... to have more venom..."

speaker: Fodus
text: "To be going back to work now, Mikos..."

speaker: Tavenor
text: The creature ignores you.

speaker: Tavenor
text: The ape-like creature in front of you approaches very cautiously.  After a few minutes of staring you up and down, it cocks its head toward you.

speaker: Tavenor
text: "You are human."

speaker: Tavenor
text: The Emp in front of you approaches very cautiously. After a few minutes of staring you up and down, he cocks his head towards you.

speaker: Tavenor
text: "You are human."

speaker: Tavenor
text: "You are greeted by me, human." Tavenor slowly approaches.

speaker: Tavenor
text: "Tavenor is my name."

speaker: Tavenor
text: "The meaning of `job' is not understood."

speaker: Tavenor
text: "No job is had by me. Food is gathered by me and my family."

speaker: Tavenor
text: "`Job' now understood by me. No job is had by me. Food is gathered by me and my family." He watches you carefully. "Your job is to cut down Silverleaf trees, yes?"

speaker: Tavenor
text: "That is as I expected. You are a menace. You are asked to stop, please." He turns away from you.

speaker: Tavenor
text: "The truth is known to me, but, belief is hard for me."

speaker: Trellek
text: "The truth is spoken by the human," Trellek says to the other Emp. "He is to be trusted. His good will was felt by me."

speaker: Tavenor
text: The Emp nods at Trellek, and then turns to you. "The truth is now clear to me. You are wished good luck."

speaker: Tavenor
text: The Emp eyes you a little longer. "Your good intentions are known to    me. You are asked to be the messenger. Humans will not be destroyers, please."

speaker: Tavenor
text: "Fruit and milk are Emp foods. Especially fruits are liked by me. Meats," he shakes his head,

speaker: Tavenor
text: "are -not- liked by Emps."

speaker: Tavenor
text: "Milk is good. Milk with honey is preferred by me."

speaker: Tavenor
text: "Silverleaf trees are Emp homes."

speaker: Tavenor
text: "Meats are from killed animals. Killing is bad. Destroying is bad."

speaker: Tavenor
text: "Fruits are good and sweet -- like honey!"

speaker: Tavenor
text: "Honey is favorite food of all Emps!"

speaker: Tavenor
text: "You are told `goodbye.'"

speaker: Salamon
text: The creature ignores you.

speaker: Salamon
text: You see a wizened female ape-like creature.

speaker: Salamon
text: You see a wizened female Emp.

speaker: Salamon
text: "You are hailed, human."

speaker: Salamon
text: "I am Salamon," she says.

speaker: Salamon
text: "I am without job. All Emps are without jobs. Food gathering and shelter-building are Emp jobs."

speaker: Salamon
text: She gives you a hard look.

speaker: Salamon
text: "There is a job for Trellek."

speaker: Salamon
text: "Silverleaf trees are where Emp's homes can be found."

speaker: Salamon
text: "Only fruits, vegetables, and milk-stuffs are eaten by Emps. Bread is also eaten."

speaker: Salamon
text: "Milk and cheese and butter are milk-stuffs."

speaker: Salamon
text: "Bread is hard to make for Emps. No stoves or ovens are owned by Emps. But bread is well liked."

speaker: Salamon
text: "Fruits and vegetables are our favorites. Many are sweet."

speaker: Salamon
text: "Sweet things are desired by Emps. Honey is sweetest! More honey is had by you?"

speaker: Salamon
text: Her eyes widen and her lips part around a very large and hopeful smile.

speaker: Salamon
text: "More honey will be given by you?"

speaker: Salamon
text: "You are thanked," she says, taking the honey.

speaker: Salamon
text: "A mean trick was played by you," she says, frowning.

speaker: Salamon
text: She seems surprised, but quickly recovers.

speaker: Salamon
text: "Your feelings are understood by me," she sighs.

speaker: Salamon
text: She sighs, obviously disappointed.

speaker: Salamon
text: "No dead animal flesh -- what is called `meat' by humans -- is eaten by an Emp."

speaker: Salamon
text: "Meat is without a good taste," she shudders. "It is not preferred!"

speaker: Salamon
text: "All violence is abhorred by Emps. No killing is desired, even for what you humans call food."

speaker: Salamon
text: She takes the document from you, smiling when she sees Ben's signature. "Trellek is permitted to join you. You are wished luck and speed."

speaker: Salamon
text: "The signed contract must be seen by me."

speaker: Salamon
text: "Permission will be given to you later. There is a task that must be performed first."

speaker: Salamon
text: "There is a woodcutter who lives in the western part of the forest. Silverleaf trees are being cut down by him. Emp houses are in Silverleaf trees. Contract must be signed by woodcutter to stop."

speaker: Salamon
text: "My condition is understood by you?" Not waiting for your response, she hands you a document.

speaker: Salamon
text: "You are now in possession of the contract."

speaker: Salamon
text: "There is not enough room in your equipment for the contract."

speaker: Salamon
text: "Trellek is another Emp. He should be spoken to by you."

speaker: Salamon
text: "There is much damage to the forest and the Silverleaf trees. The damage is caused by your people, human. The responsibility to reverse the damage is also yours, human."

speaker: Salamon
text: "Trellek should be sought by you," she says emphatically. "He should be asked to join you."

speaker: Salamon
text: "My hope is for your welfare, human."

speaker: Nicodemus
text: Your old friend Nicodemus has a far away look in his eyes.

speaker: Nicodemus
text: "Who art thou?" Nicodemus asks. "Oh, I remember. Remember demember! Ha ha ha!"

speaker: Nicodemus
text: "Hello again, <PLAYER_NAME>," says Nicodemus.

speaker: Nicodemus
text: "That is a very good question. Some days I can actually remember. Let's see... today... Yes! I am Nicodemus! Nicodomus! Nicodimus! Nico-nico-kukodamus! Ha ha ha!"

speaker: Nicodemus
text: "Thou art addressing Nicodemus."

speaker: Nicodemus
text: "To go absolutely mad! For that is indeed what is happening! My magic no longer works! Every time I attempt to change something into a drake, it only becomes a newt! Oh, newty-wewty scooty-booty!" He speaks to an imaginary creature beside him. "Who asked thee? Away with thee!" He turns to you. "Sorry. That bloody newt keeps trying to undermine my conversation. Anyway... I suppose I can sell thee some reagents, potions, or spells. I must make a living somecow. I mean somehow! That was Some Cow! Ha ha ha!"

speaker: Nicodemus
text: "Why, to perform magic! It seems that the disturbance in the ether has been repaired! I can also sell thee some reagents or spells."

speaker: Nicodemus
text: "Magic? What magic!? All the magic in the world has gone completely topsy-turvy! Oh, blurpsy-flurpsy! Ha ha ha! Those are silly words, are they not? 'Tis a pity they are not magical! Ha ha ha!"

speaker: Nicodemus
text: "The ether is repaired. The mages of the world are indebted to thee."

speaker: Nicodemus
text: "Dost thou wish to buy some spells?"

speaker: Nicodemus
text: "Never mind, then!"

speaker: Nicodemus
text: "Dost thou wish to buy some reagents?"

speaker: Nicodemus
text: "Never mind, then!"

speaker: Nicodemus
text: "Potions? What makes thee think I have potions? Art thou sure thou dost not want Lotions? I certainly have lotions! Otions, slotions, motions, votions! Ha ha ha! Wait! Oh, yes! I do have potions! I told thee so, didn't I! Let us see... I have this black potion here. I am not sure what it does exactly, but I am quite sure it turns one invisible."

speaker: Nicodemus
text: "Yes, I have potions. Well, I have this black one. It is an invisibility potion."

speaker: Nicodemus
text: "Dost thou want it for, say, 75 gold?"

speaker: Nicodemus
text: "Here is the potion."

speaker: Nicodemus
text: "Thou dost not have enough room to carry the potion!"

speaker: Nicodemus
text: "Art thou trying to cheat me? Thou dost not have enough gold!"

speaker: Nicodemus
text: "Then why didst thou mention it? Leave me alone!"

speaker: Nicodemus
text: "Timey Limey Lord? Hmmm. I don't know him. Wait! Yes I do. Does he have a big black mustache and three pairs of pants? No! I know who he is. He's the fellow who came to fix my sundial the other day, right?"

speaker: Nicodemus
text: "I thought so! Tell him that bloody thing still doesn't work! It gives me three shadows! Dadows badows whoopeee! Ha ha ha!"

speaker: Nicodemus
text: "He's not? Hmmm. Then he must be the man I am not thinking of!"

speaker: Nicodemus
text: "Wait! I remember! He is my Knight's Bridge opponent! We play on my Knight's Bridge court just north of mine house."

speaker: Nicodemus
text: "I have not spoken to the Time Lord in months! How is the old codger? Give him my regards. Tell him I miss our Knight's Bridge games!"

speaker: Nicodemus
text: "'Tis a life-size board game. I have a book around here somewhere which contains the rules."

speaker: Nicodemus
text: "Yes, I just enchanted it."

speaker: Nicodemus
text: "This Time Lord told thee what? An hourglass! I have no blinking hourglass! Glassy wassy hoursplassy! Ha ha ha! Wait! An enchanted hourglass? That does ring a bell. Clang Clang Clang! Ha ha ha! Wait! I remember. I had an hourglass. I sold it. To a gypsy. Or was it an antique dealer? I think I might have sold it to a gypsy antique dealer in Britain. Or Paws. Somewhere on that side of the land. But if my memory serves me correctly, that hourglass used up its enchantment, which is why I sold it. I suppose if the ether is repaired, I could possibly re-enchant it. Bring it to me and we'll see what we can do. I know! We can play a rousing game of chess! But only if I can deal at all times. I do not trust thee."

speaker: Nicodemus
text: "Mine old hourglass! Of course I remember it! I believe I sold it to an antique dealer in Paws. I might be able to re-enchant it if thou wouldst bring it to me."

speaker: Nicodemus
text: "What's this? An hourglass of some kind? Wait! It looks vaguely familiar! Thief!! This is mine hourglass! I have been looking for it for years! Where didst thou get it, scoundrel? I shall turn thee into a duck!"

speaker: Nicodemus
text: Nicodemus intones some spell and points at you, but nothing happens.

speaker: Nicodemus
text: "Zounds! Thou art no more a quacker than I am. Nothing works anymore. Quacker slacker wacker flacker! Ha ha ha!"

speaker: Nicodemus
text: "Mine old hourglass! I suppose I could revitalize the enchantment upon it."

speaker: Nicodemus
text: "Enchant? Thou dost want me to enchant this wretched thing? Thou must have the brain of a toad! Toady woady bloady coady! Ha ha ha!"

speaker: Nicodemus
text: "Do me a favor, Mister Avatar. Repair the blinking ether, wilt thou? Do that and I can enchant thy glourblass. I mean floursass. I mean hourglass. Tell that to thy 'Time Lord'. Thou canst also tell him he needs a bath."

speaker: Nicodemus
text: "I would be most happy to enchant the hourglass. After freeing the ether, I am most indebted to thee. Let me see it..."

speaker: Nicodemus
text: Nicodemus takes the hourglass and studies it a moment. He sets it on a table and closes his eyes, concentrating. He intones a few words, throws some reagents into the air, and passes his hand over the artifact.

speaker: Nicodemus
text: "That should do it." He hands the hourglass back to you.

speaker: Nicodemus
text: "Where is it? Thou dost not have the hourglass!"

speaker: Nicodemus
text: "Bye bye booby booby bye bye! Ha ha ha!"

speaker: Nicodemus
text: "Goodbye, <PLAYER_NAME>."

speaker: Thad
text: The man scowls at you. "Thou wearest the symbol of that most foul of groups, The Fellowship. Prepare to die!"

speaker: Thad
text: Eyeing you carefully, the man before you takes an aggressive stance.

speaker: Thad
text: "Good day, <HONORIFIC>," Thad says coolly.

speaker: Thad
text: He stares at you for a moment. "Thad is my name, <HONORIFIC>."

speaker: Thad
text: "Job? I have not the time for a job. I am on a quest to rid this land of that which plagues it!"

speaker: Thad
text: "I have devoted mine entire life to this, nothing will get in my way, not even Batlin."

speaker: Thad
text: "He is the leader of the cursed organization, The Fellowship!"

speaker: Thad
text: "Surely thou hast heard of The Fellowship, a most foul and evil organization. It has even infested the lovely forest of Yew!"

speaker: Thad
text: "I know little about their practices, but I do know they live outside the bounds of moral decency. They have kidnapped my beloved sister, Millie, and have cast a spell of enchantment. Now she lives as they do. I have vowed to remove this wicked spell and will slay the entire organization should that prove necessary!"

speaker: Thad
text: "Thou, also, hast taken up a similar cause, I expect. Yes?"

speaker: Thad
text: "Excellent." He shakes your hand. "Thou art indeed a worthy warrior, <HONORIFIC>."

speaker: Thad
text: "No?" He seems genuinely surprised. "Then perhaps thou wilt consider taking up my quest in thine own manner."

speaker: Thad
text: "I expected as much. Thou art truly an honorable warrior."

speaker: Thad
text: "What manner of scoundrel art thou? Remove thyself from my presence before I decide to smite thee from thy wretched life!"

speaker: Thad
text: "I know the land, but not the people. There is nothing useful I have to tell thee." He appears thoughtful for a moment. "Perhaps I can aid thee a bit. I do know that there are two hunters who sometimes frequent this area. One, a woman, carries a spear. The other is an archer. That is all I can tell thee."

speaker: Thad
text: "May thine endeavors reach fruition, <HONORIFIC>."

speaker: Bradman
text: You see a man leaning on a longbow.

speaker: Bradman
text: Bradman greets you. "Hail, <HONORIFIC>."

speaker: Bradman
text: "I am Bradman."

speaker: Bradman
text: "Why, 'tis my job to train the many who visit Yew to become more agile."

speaker: Bradman
text: "The forest attracts a lot of people who want to spend some time away from the larger towns like Minoc and Britain. So they come to Yew."

speaker: Bradman
text: "And, something about the woods makes most people want to explore." He pats his bow.

speaker: Bradman
text: "That is where this comes in. The bow is the tool of survival in the forest. And I," he jerks his thumb to his chest, "teach proficiency with the bow."

speaker: Bradman
text: "There are many exciting things to see in the forest. Not a day goes by when I do not see something interesting: a new type of bird, a beautiful butterfly, or, best of all -- a deer."

speaker: Bradman
text: "'Tis my weapon of choice. It takes a keen eye and a steady arm to shoot accurately. I think it has more finesse than a sword or a spear, for example."

speaker: Bradman
text: "I love the forest. It is very beautiful. Also," he raises his bow, "I moved out here to be near the two great archers, Iolo and Tseramed."

speaker: Iolo
text: Iolo blushes. "I am honored, my friend. I was not aware I had an admirer in this part of the land." He bows to Bradman, who returns the gesture.

speaker: Tseramed
text: "Thank you for thy kind words, good sir. Perhaps we may practice sometime in the future."

speaker: Bradman
text: "I would be greatly honored, milord!"

speaker: Bradman
text: "He is a great archer who resides in the forest. He moved here to get away from the far-too-quickly growing towns."

speaker: Bradman
text: "If thou wantest to train, my charge is 30 gold. Art thou still interested?"

speaker: Bradman
text: "I understand, <HONORIFIC>."

speaker: Bradman
text: "Thou hast met Penni? I hope thou hast not trained with her," he winks. "She is a valuable friend, but she hunts as well as a weed and she is as clumsy as an ox. I am afraid she knows nothing about fighting."

speaker: Bradman
text: "May the trees part around thee, <HONORIFIC>."

speaker: Sir Jeff
text: The man greets you with stern, suspicious eyes.

speaker: Sir Jeff
text: "What is thy business, <HONORIFIC>?"

speaker: Sir Jeff
text: "I am Sir Jeff, <HONORIFIC>."

speaker: Sir Jeff
text: "I am the High Court official at the prison here in the Abbey."

speaker: Sir Jeff
text: "I am the judiciary part of Britannia's government. It is my job to see that criminals are brought to justice."

speaker: Sir Jeff
text: "We have two prisoners already, but there are many scoundrels who still roam free."

speaker: Sir Jeff
text: "Thou, of course, hast never met them," he says, his brow narrowing, "but we have a pirate, and," he pauses, "a troll. If thou dost wish to see them, speak with Goth, the jailer."

speaker: Sir Jeff
text: "See for thyself, the posted bills for known villains are in the log book in the courtroom."

speaker: Sir Jeff
text: "He has only been working here for a few weeks, but I already know he is not trustworthy. There is something obviously unscrupulous about him. He is not a friend of thine, is he?"

speaker: Sir Jeff
text: "I suspected as much." He turns away from you.

speaker: Sir Jeff
text: "No," he says, watching you closely, "of course he is not."

speaker: Sir Jeff
text: "The monks live and study there, but they do little more than winemaking. Well, I know one of them tends the garden."

speaker: Sir Jeff
text: "Keep thine heart and mind on the straight path, <HONORIFIC>."

speaker: Tiery
text: You see an unkempt, yet dapper man talking to himself.

speaker: Tiery
text: "Eh, wot's that? Oh, it's you, <HONORIFIC>."

speaker: Tiery
text: "M'name's Tiery, <HONORIFIC>."

speaker: Tiery
text: "Eh, 'ow's that? Oh, m'job. Why, Oi take good care o' me buddies in the graveyard 'ere in Empath Abbey, Oi do."

speaker: Tiery
text: "What do ye mean did Oi 'umpeth Abby. 'Course Oi didn't. Oi never went anywhere near Abby. 'Oo told ye that?"

speaker: Tiery
text: "Empath Abbey? Why, this 'ere's Empath Abbey, <HONORIFIC>. Oi don't mean to pry, but if ye knowest not where ye be, why 'ave ye come 'ere?" He shakes his head. "It's just as Oi was tellin' Darek the other day, `If ye never want to be lost,' Oi said, `don't ever go nowheres.'"

speaker: Tiery
text: "What wrong with the bodies? Oi don' do nothing more than bury 'em! A fellow could get in lots o' trouble spreading rumors like that."

speaker: Tiery
text: "Barry? Oh, 'im. Oi don't know what ye's talkin' about. Oi never met Barry's woife! 'Twas just a lie they's spreadin' about me."

speaker: Tiery
text: "Oi already told ye that's m'job."

speaker: Tiery
text: "That's right. M'buddies! Oi bury 'em. It's m'job." He squints at you. "Unless, <HONORIFIC>, yer askin' about the people 'ere?"

speaker: Tiery
text: "No! Of course Oi don't use peep holes. What sort o' question is that to ask a fellow, <HONORIFIC>?"

speaker: Tiery
text: "Well, Oi only know a few people 'ere, but Oi'll try an' 'elp as best as Oi am able. 'Oo do ye want to know about? My two best friends are Garth an' Darek, but Oi often talk to Nina an' Bart when Oi get the chance."

speaker: Tiery
text: "Recently, that Perrin fellow from across the way 'as been spendin' some toime with me. 'E's a real nice chap. A l'ttle brainy, perhaps, <HONORIFIC>, but Oi like 'im just the same. Anyone else ye'd like to know about?"

speaker: Tiery
text: "Well, that Perrin fellow'd be a better one to ask than Oi'd be, <HONORIFIC>. 'E knows a lot, that one does."

speaker: Tiery
text: "All right then, glad Oi could introduce ye to a few o' my friends."

speaker: Tiery
text: "G'day, <HONORIFIC>. 'Ave a pleasant journey. Oi'll tell Malc 'allo for ye."

speaker: Iskander
text: You see a large cyclops. It looks at you and blinks its eye in irritation.

speaker: Iskander
text: "What dost thou want?" says Iskander.

speaker: Iskander
text: "I am of the clan Ironheart, the eleventh son of Valador. They call me Iskander."

speaker: Iskander
text: "My cyclopean people say I am a hero. Many of you humans say I am a monster. No doubt, the truth is somewhere in between."

speaker: Iskander
