text: "One hundred and eighty-nine years ago I slew the seven Gazer Princes when they used their magic to steal the eye from the leader of our tribe, but such things are now ancient history and are no longer of any consequence."

speaker: Iskander
text: "On numerous occasions I have caused the unpleasant end of human interlopers who mistakenly believed our race was fit for nothing save to be plundered. But I have no quarrel with thee." He pauses to scrutinize you. "For the moment."

speaker: Iskander
text: "Thou dost know my name, but I still do not know the name of thee. I like to know to whom I am speaking. What is thy name?"

speaker: Iskander
text: "I have heard of thee, Avatar. Thou hast come into conflict against our kind before, I know. But I have also heard the tales of thine heroic and spiritual quests and I believe thee to be a just and noble man. Thou mayest call me friend."

speaker: Iskander
text: "A pleasure to meet thee, <PLAYER_NAME>."

speaker: Iskander
text: "Those of my tribe are a quiet people. They farm the rocky soil, but are also very good tool makers. I was sent to find them a new homeland."

speaker: Iskander
text: "The eye of a cyclops is considered quite a delicacy to some of the less genteel races of Britannia. Twice have foul creatures tried to take mine, and twice have I dined on their hearts."

speaker: Iskander
text: "Then they called me 'Wonder Boy'. For nearly a hundred years that was the nickname by which I was known. I was most grateful when they stopped doing that!"

speaker: Iskander
text: Iskander squints his eye at you. "Do not start that again!"

speaker: Iskander
text: "My village lies a great many days' journey away. The people there desire a place where they can live in peace with their surroundings. I have not found such a place yet, but I will search everywhere until I do."

speaker: Iskander
text: "While I am two hundred and six, not long in years for one of my race, I already have the heart of an old man. A hero's adventures have no more attraction for me. I long to settle down with my people and spend my days tending the fields or in my workshop building things."

speaker: Iskander
text: "My searches have brought me to this dreadful place. I incorrectly surmised that since magic does not work it would be relatively safe. It is here that I have been perplexed by a terrible riddle."

speaker: Iskander
text: "Standing at the doorway of one room in this place, I saw an enormous image of a tetrahedron. As I tried to near it a wave of amnesia passed over me. Once more I was standing in the doorway. I could remember nothing more."

speaker: Iskander
text: "I believe that is word you humans use to describe a polyhedron with four faces."

speaker: Iskander
text: "This same wave of amnesia struck me every time I tried to approach the tetrahedron. I do not know what sort of foul magic this is."

speaker: Iskander
text: "Now that thou hast destroyed the mysterious tetrahedron I will complete mine exploration of this place. I have a feeling that the homeland I seek is very far away but one never knows where the next clue will be that shall lead me to it."

speaker: Iskander
text: "Perhaps thou shalt be able to solve this mystery. I have been unable to as of yet. But I shall remain here until its secret is revealed."

speaker: Iskander
text: "I warn thee that this place is not safe. It holds unknown perils. Perhaps thou wouldst do better to leave this place."

speaker: Iskander
text: "Surely, thou dost know that magic no longer functions as it once did. There are those who say that the age of magic is over. If that is so, then I fear that there may be no place left in this world for my people."

speaker: Iskander
text: "Of course, now that thou hast destroyed the tetrahedron all magic has been restored. I congratulate thee for thine heroic deed!"

speaker: Iskander
text: "Yes, I have heard those names before. Those are the names of two warriors who have been after me for revenge. They say I killed their father and I must admit to thee that it is true. I did kill their father."

speaker: Iskander
text: "I know that Eiko and Amanda have been after me for some time looking for vengeance. I say let them come. I will not stand still for them nor shall I run from them. When they find me they are welcome to try and take their justice from me. If they win then it was meant to be. If they do not I will have no regrets."

speaker: Iskander
text: "Their father's name was Kalideth. He suffered from the mage madness. His attack on me was unprovoked. For some reason he blamed the failure of magic upon my people. His own magics were still quite potent and I barely survived the encounter. I killed Kalideth in self-defense, but I did not want to kill him. I wish there to still be some magic left in this world and I mourned his passing as much as anyone."

speaker: Iskander
text: "Farewell, Avatar."

speaker: Iskander
text: "Farewell, <PLAYER_NAME>."

speaker: Iskander
text: "Farewell."

speaker: Reyna
text: The woman greets you with shining eyes.

speaker: Reyna
text: "Hello, <HONORIFIC>," says Reyna.

speaker: Reyna
text: "I am Reyna," she says, brushing the hair out of her face.

speaker: Reyna
text: "I am a healer. I have chosen to set up shop here near the forest."

speaker: Reyna
text: "I wanted to live and work here because the land is very beautiful. I have found many things to do and see. Unfortunately, the forest is so spread out that I have yet to meet many of the others who live in this area. I do know that the Abbey is just across the way from mine house."

speaker: Reyna
text: "And somewhere nearby is a scholar." She appears thoughtful for a moment. "Also, I believe there is a prison just east of the Abbey."

speaker: Reyna
text: "I've never actually seen it," she laughs, "but rumor has it that the cells are located right next to the court, for quick, easy imprisonment after the trial."

speaker: Reyna
text: "From Aimi I have heard that he is brilliant, and... also a bit overzealous to instruct those interested in increasing their knowledge."

speaker: Reyna
text: "She is the monk who tends the garden at the Abbey."

speaker: Reyna
text: "She is one of the monks who lives at the Abbey. At this time, she is the only other person I have actually met here in the forest."

speaker: Reyna
text: "That is how this area -- Empath Abbey -- got its name, from the monks who live at the abbey of the Brotherhood of the Rose. They are said to make delicious wine. One of the monks cares for a beautiful garden in her spare time. In fact, I often buy flowers from her."

speaker: Reyna
text: " But," she grins, "as for the other monks, all that I	ever see them do is make wine and wander the countryside."

speaker: Reyna
text: "Aimi is the only one I have met, but I know there are one or two others who make wine there."

speaker: Reyna
text: "Yes, I get them for my mother."

speaker: Reyna
text: She looks down at her feet, and then back up at you. It is obvious she is fighting an urge to cry.

speaker: Reyna
text: "Several months ago, my mother passed away in her home town. She was born here in the forests, and had asked to be buried here, near me. Every morning I come out here to visit her and set flowers by her grave."

speaker: Reyna
text: "But," a lone tear escapes and trickles down her cheek, "I am the only member of our family who lives nearby. No one else is able to visit or leave flowers very often."

speaker: Reyna
text: "Her grave looks so bare sometimes." She looks off into the horizon and sighs. "<VAR>It would be nice	if there were some way to have more flowers brought to her."

speaker: Reyna
text: She quickly turns and looks at you.

speaker: Reyna
text: "I am terribly sorry for rambling on like that. Please excuse me, <HONORIFIC>."

speaker: Reyna
text: Her eyes light up as she sees the bouquet of flowers.

speaker: Reyna
text: "They are lovely! Thou art too kind, <HONORIFIC>, to bring flowers for my mother! I cannot wait to set them by her grave."

speaker: Reyna
text: "For thy kindly gift of flowers, I will aid thee for half price." She smiles at you.

speaker: Reyna
text: "I am sorry, <HONORIFIC>, but, unless this is an emergency, I would prefer to wait until my shop is open."

speaker: Reyna
text: She quickly examines you<VAR>.

speaker: Reyna
text: "Thou art correct, <HONORIFIC>. This is a true emergency!"

speaker: Reyna
text: "I am sorry, but thy wounds are not mortal. Perhaps thou canst visit me when my shop is open."

speaker: Reyna
text: She smiles shyly.

speaker: Reyna
text: "I very much love animals. When I was very young, I found an ailing dove that I was unable to nurse back to health. Since that time, I began to study the healing arts, so that I would be able to help other animals who might need healing."

speaker: Reyna
text: "Of course," she laughs, "now that I have the skills, I use them to help people, too."

speaker: Reyna
text: "Goodbye, <HONORIFIC>."

speaker: Reyna
text: "I thank thee for the bouquet!"

speaker: Reyna
text: "May health always follow thee!"

speaker: Wayne
text: You see a monk wandering around apparently without direction.

speaker: Wayne
text: "Greetings, <HONORIFIC>. May I help thee?" asks Wayne.

speaker: Wayne
text: "Thou mayest call me Brother Wayne, <HONORIFIC>."

speaker: Wayne
text: "My job? Well, I, er, do not truly have one at the moment." He looks down at his feet.

speaker: Wayne
text: "Yes, I am... Well, I am lost, <HONORIFIC>. I am from the Abbey to the south of here... or to the north.... Mayhaps the northwest." He cradles his chin and looks up.

speaker: Wayne
text: "Southeast?"

speaker: Wayne
text: "Well... I am sure it is not permanent." He blushes. "I just need to get my bearings, that's all," he says unconvincingly.

speaker: Wayne
text: "I am a monk of the Brotherhood of the Rose. I study geography and nature with a brother named Taylor."

speaker: Wayne
text: "Well," he shrugs, "I suppose I should have studied a little bit better." He smiles sheepishly.

speaker: Wayne
text: "There are so many beautiful things to see in Britannia. Both animals and plants alike offer excitement to the observer."

speaker: Wayne
text: "Well, I haven't actually seen him for some time. I assume he is still continuing his studies."

speaker: Wayne
text: "Ah, yes, <HONORIFIC>, they are quite wondrous to see. I highly recommend to thee to always observe thy surroundings. Otherwise, <HONORIFIC>, thou wilt miss much in life: flowers, trees, birds... landmarks!"

speaker: Wayne
text: "Ah, my least favorite subject. I find the trees much less interesting than the birds."

speaker: Wayne
text: "My favorite type of animal! The birds are so free, able to fly vast distances. How I wish I could roam about the open skies... most especially considering my current situation. Thou canst see so much more from the air, I am certain of it!"

speaker: Wayne
text: "Very, very lovely plants. All the colors of the rainbow, and then some. One of the monks at the Abbey had a lovely flower garden. She may still tend it for all that I know, <HONORIFIC>."

speaker: Wayne
text: "Excellent, <HONORIFIC>. I am glad to hear it. 'Twould be a shame were Aimi to give that up for her other... pastime."

speaker: Wayne
text: "Aimi also paints. Or rather, makes a bold attempt. I must, of course, commend her for her efforts."

speaker: Wayne
text: "My favorite ones are the birds, especially the Golden-Cheeked Warbler. I love to follow and watch them. They do not seem to have a very good sense of direction, however." He sighs. "But there is a great variety of species in this land."

speaker: Wayne
text: "May thy good fortune guide thee down the trail of life."

speaker: Garok
text: You see a mage with a wild look in his eyes.

speaker: Garok
text: You see a mage with a peaceful look in his eyes.

speaker: Garok
text: "Thou art talking to me?" Garok asks, suspiciously.

speaker: Garok
text: The mage stares at you a moment. "Art thou from the Britannian Tax Council?"

speaker: Garok
text: "Then I am nobody!"

speaker: Garok
text: "Good for thee. I would have had to kill thee. I am Garok Al-Mat. At least, the last time I looked in the mirror, that was who I was!"

speaker: Garok
text: "I like thee already! I am Garok Al-Mat."

speaker: Garok
text: Garok looks as if he might suddenly tear out his hair, but he restrains himself.

speaker: Garok
text: "I am... -was-... a mage. Until it all went wrong. I am attempting to correct things."

speaker: Garok
text: "I am, and always have been, a mage. I was down here trying to locate what was amiss with the ethereal waves, but they seem to be all right now."

speaker: Garok
text: Garok suddenly hits himself on the side of the head.

speaker: Garok
text: "Get out! Damn thee! Out of there! No one invited thee into mine head! Away with thee!"

speaker: Garok
text: Garok hits himself again, shakes his head like a wet dog and makes a blubbering sound with his lips.

speaker: Garok
text: Garok looks at you and smiles. "That's better. Now, what was it... oh yes, I remember. Thou dost not believe I am a mage? Well, I am. I live in the mountains. But now I am lost in this wretched dungeon."

speaker: Garok
text: "I usually live in the mountains, but I am lost in this dungeon."

speaker: Garok
text: "My magic is not working!"

speaker: Garok
text: "My magic was not working!"

speaker: Garok
text: "I attributed it to a disturbance in the ethereal waves! I had to find out what was happening. So here I am!"

speaker: Garok
text: "There is a voice in mine head. Some demon of some sort. It is always congratulating me on things. And then other times it scolds me for things. I -know- it is not my conscience. I -know- what -he- sounds like! This is... someone else."

speaker: Garok
text: "I started hearing it around the time my magic began to fail. I do not find it amusing."

speaker: Garok
text: "My crystal ball told me that the source of my problems was in a dungeon, but it did not say which one. This was the first dungeon I had ever explored. I have not found anything that might help me, and I cannot find my way out!"

speaker: Garok
text: "I came down here to find the source of my problems. My crystal ball told me that it was in a dungeon, but did not say which one. This is my first dungeon expedition, and now I am lost."

speaker: Garok
text: You explain to Garok that the Tetrahedron Generator is located in Dungeon Deceit.

speaker: Garok
text: "Hmmmm. Correct idea. Wrong dungeon."

speaker: Garok
text: "Dost thou know the way out?"

speaker: Garok
text: You tell Garok how to get out of the dungeon.

speaker: Garok
text: "Why, it sounds so simple! My marbles must be losing me!"

speaker: Garok
text: "I thank thee! Now I must be on my way. In fact, now that I know the way, I can use what little magic I have going for me to teleport. One must know the direction thou art travelling if one wishes to teleport!"

speaker: Garok
text: "Say, for helping me, wouldst thou like to have some useless reagents? By useless, I mean they are useless to me. They are probably perfectly good reagents. Thou art welcome to have them. Dost thou want them?"

speaker: Garok
text: "Good. One less thing I have to carry."

speaker: Garok
text: "Oh. Thou dost not have the room. Too bad."

speaker: Garok
text: Garok shrugs. "Suit thyself. Thanks anyway."

speaker: Garok
text: You watch as Garok turns, intones a spell, and vanishes.

speaker: Garok
text: "Oh. Thou art as lost as I, eh? Then we shall surely die in here."

speaker: Garok
text: "Grrrr! They are a thorn in my side! They have been seeking me for the past three years! I neglected to report a certain amount of income for reagent distribution, and somehow they found me out. By the way, if thou shouldst ever care to visit me in the mountains, I can sell thee reagents at reduced prices!"

speaker: Garok
text: "Yes, I remember him! He is lost, too! Dost thou know if he found his way out? Give him my best when thou dost speak to him."

speaker: Garok
text: "Goodbye."

speaker: Gharl
text: You see a troll, sulking in his cell. As he breathes, you can see his ribs protrude out from under his hide.

speaker: Gharl
text: "What you want?" growls Gharl.

speaker: Gharl
text: "I Gharl."

speaker: Gharl
text: He shakes his head. "No job. Hunt. Eat. Sleep. Now," he gestures around the cell, "no hunt, no eat, just sleep."

speaker: Gharl
text: "I good hunter. Catch many things."

speaker: Gharl
text: "I still do that," he says, shrugging. "But not as good as when home."

speaker: Gharl
text: He stares at you oddly and says, "With other trolls, fleshface! Under bridges."

speaker: Gharl
text: "No eat." He shakes his head. "Not feed. Hate jailer!" he growls.

speaker: Gharl
text: "You give me food?" His face displays a mixture of surprise and hope. "You give me food, I tell you secret. Yes?"

speaker: Gharl
text: He quickly devours the food.

speaker: Gharl
text: "I thank. You want secret?"

speaker: Gharl
text: "You taunt me. I not like you."

speaker: Gharl
text: "Go away."

speaker: Gharl
text: "Trolls have powerful ally. He warn us in head when trouble around corner."

speaker: Gharl
text: He grunts and turns away.

speaker: D Rel
text: You see a rough-looking man with a bitter expression on his face.

speaker: D Rel
text: D'Rel scowls at you. "What in the blazes do ye want?"

speaker: D Rel
text: "What do ye care about the name of a wretch?"

speaker: D Rel
text: "They've put me in here to rot, they have!"

speaker: D Rel
text: "The Britannian Tax Council done it. They and the two here -- Sir Jeff and Goth."

speaker: D Rel
text: "They told me I'd be here for the rest of my life. I have no reason to doubt them either!"

speaker: D Rel
text: "That stuffed cock believes he's above everyone in Britannia. Just because he presides over the High Court he thinks he can pass judgement over any and everyone."

speaker: D Rel
text: "That thieving scoundrel belongs in here more than I do! Don't trust him if ye've gotta choice."

speaker: D Rel
text: "Thieves, the whole lot of 'em! Tryin' to take a person's hard-earned gold. Mayhaps they wouldn't need to take all of our money if they would go out and earn their own!"

speaker: D Rel
text: "Ye care, do ye? All right, then. I'll tell ye my name if ye tell me thine, deal?"

speaker: D Rel
text: "<VAR>, eh. Very well, a deal's a deal. I'm D'Rel."

speaker: D Rel
text: "I thought as much."

speaker: D Rel
text: "None now. But 'til I made this mine home, I was a sailor, a... privateer, out of Buccaneer's Den."

speaker: D Rel
text: "Well, actually I am in here for not paying my taxes. After all, I... earned the money, why should I give it to the Britannian Tax Council?"

speaker: D Rel
text: "Thou hast heard of Buccaneer's Den, hast thou not? 'Tis the island due east of the mainland. Home of the sort of men who walk with peg-legs, have hooks for hands, and carry parrots on their shoulders! Har! Har!"

speaker: D Rel
text: "Yeah, I know Hook. Lookin' for him, are ye? He be from Buccaneer's Den. He usually travels with some gargoyle named Forskis or something like that. If ye see him, give him my... hello, for me." He gestures to his clenched fist.

speaker: D Rel
text: "Aye, get thy face from my sight!"

speaker: Smith
text: You see a horse. "What else did you expect to see?"

speaker: Smith
text: "What now, <PLAYER_NAME>?" asks Smith.

speaker: Smith
text: "Yes, I have a name."

speaker: Iolo
text: "Scoundrel! When thou art asked thy name, thou shouldst respond politely and accurately! The Avatar has just asked thee for -thy- name."

speaker: Smith
text: "My name? You can call	me what you want, but I will only respond to Smith."

speaker: Smith
text: "My name? You can call	me what you want, but I will only respond to Smith."

speaker: Smith
text: "Job? -Job-? I'm a horse, what kind of job could I have?" He looks off in the distance. "I can see it now: Smith -- Baker extraordinaire."

speaker: Smith
text: "Actually, I have gotten quite good at interior decorating. See how I arranged my abode? You like it, don't you?"

speaker: Smith
text: "Good. I will let you continue talking to me then! Which do you prefer, my living room or my bedroom?"

speaker: Smith
text: "That's funny, I feel the same way about you!"

speaker: Smith
text: "You always did have bad taste!"

speaker: Smith
text: "Yep, that's what I told you to call me. Oh, I get it! You <VAR> something from me, don't you?"

speaker: Smith
text: "I thought as much. You've always been a selfish one. What do you want? Now, let's see... Money? Advice?	Happiness? No, you usually want a clue of some sort, don't you. Of course, you may have become altruistic over the past 200 years...."

speaker: Smith
text: "I know! You want to save Britannia!"

speaker: Smith
text: "Then what are you talking to me for?"

speaker: Smith
text: "From a horse? Right! Like I've got some to give you."

speaker: Smith
text: "Don't talk to horses!"

speaker: Smith
text: "Who doesn't?"

speaker: Smith
text: "You really expect me to believe that? You're just in this for the money."

speaker: Smith
text: "Now we're getting to the nitty-gritty. O.K., I'll give you a clue, but what's in it for me? Let me guess. Money? Love? No, knowing you it's probably nothing. With any luck, you'll go away and leave me alone."

speaker: Smith
text: "I've already got that!"

speaker: Smith
text: "Sure! Like I have a use for that!"

speaker: Smith
text: "Sorry, I don't get into that."

speaker: Smith
text: "Threats, huh? And how do you expect me to respond to that? With courtesy and open hooves?"

speaker: Smith
text: "Tell you what: you go away and leave me alone, and I'll tell you a clue. Fair?"

speaker: Smith
text: "Now we're talking! Done deal. Here we go." He checks around to make sure no else is within earshot. "The gargoyles," he pauses, "are not evil."

speaker: Smith
text: "And Rasputin is a mean Martian. There, that's it! Now get!"

speaker: Smith
text: "Fine. I'm not going to talk to you anyway!"

speaker: Smith
text: "That's just fine. I was getting tired of you anyway."

speaker: Iolo
text: "Why, how dare thou speakest to the Avatar in that manner, Smith!"

speaker: Smith
text: "And who are you? My master?"

speaker: Iolo
text: "Why, as a matter of fact..."

speaker: Smith
text: "Sure, whatever."

speaker: Aimi
text: The monk pulls back her cowl far enough for you to see her face.

speaker: Aimi
text: "Greetings, <HONORIFIC>. I hope thy days are full of beauty."

speaker: Aimi
text: "Thou mayest call me Aimi, <HONORIFIC>."

speaker: Aimi
text: "As a monk, I am not sure how to answer thy question. I often help to make wine. However, <HONORIFIC>, in my spare time I paint or tend my garden here at the Abbey."

speaker: Aimi
text: "I have spent little time with others in the area. Thou mayest wish to speak with Taylor, for he knows much more about the people, animals, and sights in this area than I do."

speaker: Aimi
text: "He is a fellow monk. He spends his time studying the plants, animals, and geography of Britannia."

speaker: Aimi
text: "Yes," she blushes, "I have long admired those who are able to express themselves visually. Sadly," she says, laughing, "I am not very good. However, I also collect art. In fact, I have an original Sterling hanging in my room. Perhaps thou couldst see it sometime."

speaker: Aimi
text: "My garden? I have been tending it for years now. I am a firm believer in the value of aesthetics, so I plant only flowers. Sometimes I sell them in bouquets when people want them, but I do that very rarely."

speaker: Aimi
text: "It refers to the practice or study of all things beautiful."

speaker: Aimi
text: "Thou wishest to buy a bouquet?"

speaker: Aimi
text: "Dost thou have anyone to give these flowers to?"

speaker: Aimi
text: You tell her about the passing away of Reyna's mother.

speaker: Aimi
text: "Ah, yes. I had heard of Reyna's loss. That is a noble reason. Please take these flowers and give them to her."

speaker: Aimi
text: "Good. 'Tis always best to have someone to receive flowers. The flowers will cost 10 gold. Dost thou still want them?"

speaker: Aimi
text: "I think thou wilt find these to be exceptionally beautiful."

speaker: Aimi
text: "It appears thou dost not have room for my flowers. A pity."

speaker: Aimi
text: "I am sorry, <HONORIFIC>. Thou dost not have the gold."

speaker: Aimi
text: "I understand, <HONORIFIC>. Free flowers are indeed the best. And wild flowers are quite free. For now, <HONORIFIC>, do no more than promise me thou wilt take the time to enjoy my garden."

speaker: Aimi
text: "That is indeed unfortunate, <HONORIFIC>. 'Tis always best to have someone to receive flowers."

speaker: Aimi
text: "Perhaps next time, thou mightest be interested. For now, <HONORIFIC>, do no more than promise me thou wilt take the time to enjoy my garden."

speaker: Aimi
text: "I am afraid I do not know of such a person."

speaker: Aimi
text: "Fare thee well, <HONORIFIC>. May the sweet scent of beauty never pass thee by."

speaker: Penni
text: The woman you see in front of you has a concerned expression on her face, as if her thoughts were far away.

speaker: Penni
text: "Hail, <PLAYER_NAME>. Might I assist thee?" asks Penni.

speaker: Penni
text: "My name is Penni, <HONORIFIC>."

speaker: Penni
text: "I have no occupation, <HONORIFIC>. At least not one I would call work. I do, however, teach skills in close quarter combat."

speaker: Penni
text: She thinks for a moment. "I suppose a better way to answer thy question would have been to say `Yes, I do have a job.' I'm a trainer. But," she smiles, "I enjoy it too much to call it work."

speaker: Penni
text: "I have loved close-quarter fighting since I was old enough to grasp my first spear. That's why I moved to Yew."

speaker: Penni
text: "It is my choice in arms. The spear combines the best of both range and power. It is the perfect hunting weapon."

speaker: Penni
text: "I moved here to hunt, of course. The forest is full of game. I would not think of living anywhere else!"

speaker: Penni
text: "Art thou interested in training? My price is 35 gold for each training session."

speaker: Penni
text: "Perhaps next time."

speaker: Penni
text: "I am sorry, <HONORIFIC>, but I am not training at this moment. Perhaps if thou wert to return between 9 in the morning and 6 in the evening, I will be able to help thee."

speaker: Penni
text: "Yes," she nods her head, grinning, "I know Bradman. We go hunting together. Of course, he rarely catches anything with that toothpick shooter of his."

speaker: Iolo
text: "I resent that, my friend. Bows and crossbows can be wielded with deadly effect."

speaker: Penni
text: She smiles, nodding to Iolo. "Perhaps thou art correct, friend archer, but I prefer more physical challenges."

speaker: Penni
text: "Although I consider him a true friend and an honorable companion, I wonder about his physical prowess."

speaker: Penni
text: "Addom is mine husband. But how did...?" She appears confused, but suddenly directs her gaze at you. "Hast thou seen him?"

speaker: Penni
text: "Is he in good health?"

speaker: Penni
text: "Thank goodness!" she sighs in relief.

speaker: Penni
text: "I knew he should not have left this time! I hate it when he leaves!" She chokes back her tears.

speaker: Penni
text: "I do hate it so when he travels so far away for such a long time. I can only hope he returns to mine arms quickly!" She peers off in the distance, as if searching for Addom.

speaker: Penni
text: "Good journeying, <HONORIFIC>."

speaker: Ben
text: Resting an axe on his shoulder, a tall, broad-chested man smiles and nods at you.

speaker: Ben
text: "'ello, <HONORIFIC>. Good day, ay?"

speaker: Ben
text: "Thou kin call me Ben, <HONORIFIC>. I live 'ere in the forest of Yew."

speaker: Ben
text: "I be a logger, <HONORIFIC>. 'Tis what I have done all my life. In fact, <HONORIFIC>, 'tis what my father did. And 'is father before 'im. And so on. We have been doin' this for more than ten generations."

speaker: Ben
text: "It was once a large town, but now, 'tis but a smattering of cottages livin' throughout the woods."

speaker: Ben
text: "I am afraid, <HONORIFIC>, that I know no one in this area. But," he adds proudly, "I do know 'oo runs the sawmill in Minoc. I also know that monks reside in the abbey, next to the high court."

speaker: Ben
text: "The sawyer there is named William."

speaker: Ben
text: "'Tis in the building just northeast of the Brotherhood. I know they keep prisoners there."

speaker: Ben
text: "Why, yes, <HONORIFIC>, I cut down Silverleaf trees. They only grow in one area, so I 'afta travel quite a distance when I needs some of their wood. Why dost thou ask, <HONORIFIC>?"

speaker: Ben
text: "Oh, I see," he grins, "Thou wants some for thyself, ay?"

speaker: Ben
text: "I am sorry, <HONORIFIC>, I do not know 'ow to prepare it. Perhaps thou shouldst try a pub."

speaker: Ben
text: "Thou'st got another reason for askin'?"

speaker: Ben
text: "All right, <HONORIFIC>," he shrugs.

speaker: Ben
text: "They mainly populate the east part o' the Great Forest, way on the other side."

speaker: Ben
text: "What in the bloody 'ell are emps?"

speaker: Ben
text: After you quickly explain the Silverleaf Tree situation to him, he exclaims, "Oh, well, that's 'orrible. I did not realize anyone -- er -- any other creature used the Silverleaf trees. What	kin I do about it?"

speaker: Ben
text: "Why, o' course I'll sign. No more Silverleaf trees for me."

speaker: Ben
text: He takes the contract from you and signs it.

speaker: Ben
text: He turns to Trellek. "Please apologize to thy kindred for me. I never meant to destroy thine 'omes. Friends, ay?"

speaker: Ben
text: Trellek smiles and nods.

speaker: Ben
text: "And please apologize to the Emps for me, <HONORIFIC>. I never meant to destroy their 'omes."

speaker: Ben
text: "Well, I would sign it, but it seems thou hast lost it. If thou dost find it again I will be more than happy to help thee and the Emps."

speaker: Ben
text: "G'bye, <HONORIFIC>. Pleasant journeys, ay."

speaker: Goth
text: The beady-eyed man sneers at you.

speaker: Goth
text: "What dost thou want now?" Goth spits.

speaker: Goth
text: "Goth. Not that it is any of thy business!"

speaker: Goth
text: "What does it look like I do?" he says, holding up a ring of keys. "Gardening?"

speaker: Goth
text: "What? Art thou daft?" He shakes his head. "Well, at least thou art in the right area for gardening."

speaker: Goth
text: "Empath Abbey, dolt!"

speaker: Goth
text: "As a matter of fact,  know quite a bit about the people who live here. And I just might even tell thee. What is it worth to thee in gold?"

speaker: Goth
text: "Fine by me!"

speaker: Goth
text: He glowers at you. "Thou must do better than that, fool!"

speaker: Goth
text: "I will tell thee what I know: Sir Jeff is in charge of the High Court. 'E's a real mean bastard, so I would stay away from 'im. The monks nearby make excellent wine, and Aimi doth warm a man's... heart. And whatever thou dost, do not waste time talking to the undertaker -- 'e's daft in the head."

speaker: Goth
text: "Thou dost not have enough gold, toad."

speaker: Goth
text: "These? They are for the prisoner's cells, witless knave!"

speaker: Goth
text: "I will tell thee for 5 gold. Interested?"

speaker: Goth
text: "One of them is named D'Rel. E's a pirate, from Buccaneer's Den."

speaker: Goth
text: "Thou dost not have enough money, stonehead."

speaker: Goth
text: "Pinchpenny!"

speaker: Goth
text: "Another, eh. Hast thou 5 more gold for me?"

speaker: Goth
text: "The other one is a troll. 'E don't talk much, but	'e's the first troll prisoner I have ever seen."

speaker: Goth
text: "Thou canst not fool me, brainless dolt. Thou dost not have enough gold!"

speaker: Goth
text: "Fine, slug!"

speaker: Goth
text: "Thou dost want these, eh?" he asks, holding up keys. "'Twill cost thee... 20 gold. Still want them?"

speaker: Goth
text: "Done!"

speaker: Goth
text: He smiles cruelly. "I am afraid thou dost not have enough gold."

speaker: Goth
text: "Fine. Rot for all I care!"

speaker: Goth
text: "Indeed, knave. Get thee gone!"

speaker: Carlyn
text: At your approach, the woman raises her eyebrows to indicate she is aware of your presence and interested in what you are about to say.

speaker: Carlyn
text: "And how may I help thee, <HONORIFIC>?" asks Carlyn.

speaker: Carlyn
text: "I am Carlyn." She smiles broadly.

speaker: Carlyn
text: "I am the tailor of Moonglow."

speaker: Carlyn
text: "I also tend the bar for Phearcy in the evenings."

speaker: Carlyn
text: "Wouldst thou prefer food or drink, <HONORIFIC>?"

speaker: Carlyn
text: "He is the owner and bartender. Every night at 9, he goes to the Fellowship meetings, so I serve refreshment for him <VAR>."

speaker: Carlyn
text: "'Tis a very pleasant town, <HONORIFIC>. There are so many different types of people here. I wish I knew more of them."

speaker: Carlyn
text: "If thou hast any questions about them, I highly recommend to thee that thou speakest with Phearcy."

speaker: Carlyn
text: "I know little about the group. Every night at 9 they have a meeting or some such of all the members. And, if I remember correctly, the leader of that branch doth give a speech -- a sermon is what I believe it is called."

speaker: Carlyn
text: "There is another member in town, if thou hast questions about The Fellowship."

speaker: Carlyn
text: "I believe his name is Tolemac. He is a farmer, from what I have heard. Phearcy would know more than I. Or thou couldst ask their clerk."

speaker: Carlyn
text: "'Tis a woman, I know that, but I do not know her name."

speaker: Carlyn
text: "His name is Rankin. I do not believe he has been here terribly long."

speaker: Carlyn
text: "Yes, I love sewing clothing. Wouldst thou be interested in seeing or purchasing some of my creations?"

speaker: Carlyn
text: Shock covers her face.

speaker: Carlyn
text: "Well," she huffs.

speaker: Carlyn
text: "Yes, <HONORIFIC>. 'Tis my job, and my passion. I love sewing clothing. If thou were to come to my shop when it was open, I could show thee many exquisite things."

speaker: Carlyn
text: "Fare thee well, <HONORIFIC>."

speaker: De Snel
text: Though he does not seem hostile, the man greets you in a fighting stance.

speaker: De Snel
text: "What dost thou need?" asks De Snel.

speaker: De Snel
text: "I am called Master De Snel."

speaker: De Snel
text: "I operate the famous fighting school here in Jhelom, the Library of Scars. I also train fighters personally from time to time, if they show potential."

speaker: De Snel
text: "I teach a fighting style of mine own invention. It enables one to gain complete mastery over his opponent. I could arrange a little demonstration for thee..."

speaker: De Snel
text: "This city is devoted to the art of combat. Not mere slavish military discipline, but pure violent confrontation. It is a place after mine own heart."

speaker: De Snel
text: "An elite school of fighters with a long, proud history. Many great fighters have trained within its walls. The group even has its own special weaponry."

speaker: De Snel
text: "I do not feel like discussing business at the moment. Some other time perhaps."

speaker: De Snel
text: "I train my students to be fierce and ruthless fighters!"

speaker: De Snel
text: He unsheathes his own sword and shows it to you. The sword has an elaborate serpentine pattern engraved in it. "Thou mayest recognize a weapon of the Library of Scars by its engraving. It is the sign of the snake. Striking quick, silent, deadly, as are we!"

speaker: De Snel
text: You produce the dagger found at the scene of the murders in Minoc. The serpentine engraving matches the markings of the Library of Scars exactly. De Snel looks at it and then back at you. He cannot conceal his surprise.

speaker: De Snel
text: "From where didst thou get that dagger?"

speaker: De Snel
text: De Snel peers at you, obviously aware you are lying.

speaker: De Snel
text: You look De Snel in the eye and tell him that you found it at the scene of the murders in Minoc. He gives you a curious look.

speaker: De Snel
text: "That dagger was stolen from the Library of Scars weeks ago. I have no further knowledge of it."

speaker: De Snel
text: "By the way, hast thou had a demonstration of my training technique?"

speaker: De Snel
text: "Then perhaps thou shouldst have another."

speaker: De Snel
text: "Then perhaps thou shouldst try one."

speaker: De Snel
text: "Very well. Let us begin!"

speaker: De Snel
text: "I must apologize for the discourtesy, but mine unequaled talents demand that I charge thee 40 gold for a training demonstration. Wilt thou accept?"

speaker: De Snel
text: "Very well, then!" His scowl indicates his displeasure. "If thou dost not like it, perhaps the Library of Scars is not the place for thee."

speaker: De Snel
text: "As thou hast probably seen, a few of our members had a dispute with a local troublemaker over our honor flag. We of the Library of Scars have a fierce dedication to our institution. I do not know what exactly happened to this upstart, but I understand that he is now dead. I am not trying to suggest the Library of Scars had anything to do with it, of course. Only that it would be wise not to cross us."

speaker: De Snel
text: "I have heard that thou didst kill several of our members while champion of a duel defending the thief of our honor flag." His eyes narrow as he stares at you intensely. "Outstanding! I am a man who values nothing higher than the application of skill. I salute thee on thy victory. Perhaps thou wouldst like to join our group?"

speaker: De Snel
text: "Thy companions and thee look fit enough for an informal practice session. Consider it a demonstration of my fighting style."

speaker: De Snel
text: "As my style of fighting is the superior style, I am only interested in training the best. Perhaps thy companions and thee qualify. We might find out, that is, if thou art courageous enough."

speaker: De Snel
text: "Fortunately for Sprellic our honor flag was returned. If it had not been we would have had no choice but to regain our honor with his blood."

speaker: De Snel
text: "Thou canst walk away so easy without a demonstration! Thou shalt have one anyway!"

speaker: De Snel
text: "May thy stay in Jhelom be a memorable one," De Snel laughs as he turns and walks away.

speaker: Joseph
text: You see a man who exudes the outward mannerisms of a shrewd administrator, in contrast to his youthful appearance.

speaker: Joseph
text: Joseph nods his head respectfully to you. "How may I assist thee?"

speaker: Joseph
text: "My name is Joseph."

speaker: Joseph
text: "Presently, I am the mayor of Jhelom."

speaker: Joseph
text: "I may seem a bit young for the job, but in a town such as this I am called upon to help keep order as often as administrate. I use my sword and pen in equal measure."

speaker: Joseph
text: "This town is a rough place. A fine place for fighting men and women to live. Perhaps thou hast seen our local sport?"

speaker: Joseph
text: "Why, 'tis duelling! At twelve noon every day, the town square becomes a battlefield."

speaker: Joseph
text: "Well, the sound is worse than the act. 'Tis actually just a form of training and exercise. The fighters practice with targets and such. That is where I can be found, keeping mine own skills sharp."

speaker: Joseph
text: "I am exaggerating. Many of the fighters in town gather to spar with the training dummies and practice various methods of combat. There are a few harmless matches at times. Some are a bit rough every now and then. Some folks take wagers on it and turn a profit."

speaker: Joseph
text: "Ahem... Of course most duels are simply to the blood, not to the death. It is a practice that helps restrain the passing knaves and rogues."

speaker: Joseph
text: "Speak to Daphne or Ophelia at the Bunk and Stool, our town pub and inn."

speaker: Joseph
text: "That is what many of the duels are fought over! Some say The Fellowship is a load of rot, some say it is the only truth. Others say it is foolishness. Of course, as Mayor I remain neutral on such matters."

speaker: Joseph
text: "Elizabeth and Abraham?" Joseph scratches his head. "Oh, yes! They were the Fellowship members who were just here! They were trying to start a branch in Jhelom. I am undecided on what to tell them. We will probably have a town meeting to decide if there should be a branch here. The couple said they were returning to Britain for a few days."

speaker: Joseph
text: "Elizabeth and Abraham?" Joseph scratches his head. "Oh, yes! They were the Fellowship members who were here -- why, it must have been last week or so. I have not seen them since."

speaker: Joseph
text: "De Snel, the leader of the Library of Scars, requires that his members fight in many duels. One week they will fight for one cause and the next week for the opposite side."

speaker: Joseph
text: Joseph looks a little embarrassed. "I meant no insult to thee as a member of The Fellowship, <HONORIFIC>."

speaker: Joseph
text: "If thou must know mine opinion," he says to you in quiet confidence, "I agree with those that say The Fellowship is a bunch of foolishness."

speaker: Joseph
text: "De Snel says he only wishes the best for his school. If his fighters are ever beaten he throws them out and recruits the winner to join the Library of Scars."

speaker: Joseph
text: "It attracts fighters from all over Britannia who want to learn from De Snel. They are an unruly bunch. Thou wouldst do best to stay clear of them."

speaker: Joseph
text: "Yes, I have heard of the events surrounding this fellow Sprellic and the duels against the Library of Scars, but frankly, mine official policy has been to not get involved in these sort of personal disputes."

speaker: Joseph
text: "De Snel and I have an understanding. He works his side of the street and I work mine. It is hard enough to maintain order in this town without jeopardizing that. If I intervene De Snel will challenge me to a duel and if I am killed then his control of our town would be absolute."

speaker: Joseph
text: "As Mayor and the peacekeeper I have to pick and choose my fights very carefully. There is no love lost between myself and the members of the Library of Scars, but they can legitimately claim that they have been wronged. I am required to remain impartial in this matter. As far as I can see, Sprellic brought this on himself when he took the honor flag. If thou dost wish to stop the duel, thou dost need only convince him to give it back."

speaker: Joseph
text: "Believe me, we are not in each other's company so often because we are friends. We do so to maintain a careful watch on each other. Keep thy friends close, but keep thine enemies closer. Words to live by in Jhelom."

speaker: Joseph
text: "When I say that De Snel would challenge me to a duel I do not mean to insinuate that it would in any way be a fair or honorable contest-- more like a dagger in the back from one of his bullies as I was walking down a dark alley somewhere. That it would be a duel is just the story he would tell to make mine assassination somehow honorable."

speaker: Joseph
text: "Enjoy thy stay in my city. But if thou hast no stomach for fighting thou shouldst not stay long."

speaker: Kliftin
text: You see a battle-scarred old soldier.

speaker: Kliftin
text: "Greetings!" says Kliftin. "Hast thou gotten into any scrapes lately?"

speaker: Kliftin
text: "I am Kliftin."

speaker: Kliftin
text: "In my day I was a pretty damned good soldier. Now I am the master of the Armoury here in Jhelom."

speaker: Kliftin
text: "I sell armour and weapons here. I have something to meet thine every need. Dost thou wish to see armour or weapons?"

speaker: Kliftin
text: "My shop is presently closed for business, but do return again, <HONORIFIC>."

speaker: Kliftin
text: "Surely thou dost not want to listen to old war stories?! I have seen my share of death and destruction. Leave it at that."

speaker: Kliftin
text: "I sell and collect weapons of all types. Business is always excellent, although my best customers keep getting killed in duels!"

speaker: Kliftin
text: "Jhelom is a rough place. If thou dost not like trouble then I can think of many better places for thee to be than here."

speaker: Kliftin
text: "Every day at noon in the Town Square people come to settle their differences. They fight to the blood or to the death. It is a madness! Like that Sprellic fellow for instance."

speaker: Kliftin
text: "Sprellic, our rather mild-mannered innkeeper, stole the honor flag from the wall of the Library of Scars and refused to return it. Now he must fight three of our best local fighters in a duel to the death."

speaker: Kliftin
text: You relate Sprellic's story to the old man who listens intently. "It sounds to me like the work of Sullivan, the Trickster. He is a legendary thief and swindler who has never once been caught! Indeed, few even believe he actually exists. Thou shalt not be able to dissuade the duellists with a tale like that."

speaker: Kliftin
text: "It is good of thee to help that poor Sprellic fellow in his hour of need."

speaker: Kliftin
text: "Thou canst ask about the entire matter at the pub if thou dost wish to know more about it."

speaker: Kliftin
text: "The only thing that can dissuade them from wanting to kill poor Sprellic is to return the honor flag! It must have been taken away by Sullivan, but the duellists do not know that! If we had a duplicate of the honor flag we could give them that instead!"

speaker: Kliftin
text: "In my day I was fairly handy at stitching wounds... Hmmm, perhaps I can make a duplicate of the honor flag. The deception only has to work long enough for them to formally call off the duel."

speaker: Kliftin
text: "I stitched so many of my comrades back together after all the battles I fought in. Now that I am retired, sewing has sort of become mine hobby." He looks at you with a little embarrassment. "There is nothing wrong with that!"

speaker: Kliftin
text: "Even if they notice that it is not their true honor flag they would never admit it. To do so would make them look foolish. They would rather simply challenge anyone who might say it is not their honor flag to yet another	duel! But let us deal with one duel at a time here."

speaker: Kliftin
text: "Dost thou want me to make an honor flag that can be given to the Library of Scars so the duels can be stopped?"

speaker: Kliftin
text: "Then thou must be sure to come pick it up from me before thou dost go to the Duelling Area. It is the area outside my shop next to the Library of Scars. I had best get busy if I am to have it finished in time! Please return to my shop in a few hours."

speaker: Kliftin
text: "Then thou must be sure to come pick it up from me before Sprellic goes to the Duelling Area. I had best get busy if I am to have it finished in time. Please return to my shop in a few hours."

speaker: Kliftin
text: "Thou dost wish to deal with the Library of Scars personally? Very well then, but be warned -- the only type of honor they believe in is victory."

speaker: Kliftin
text: "How canst thou have the key to saving Sprellic's life in thine hand and do nothing as he faces certain death?!"

speaker: Kliftin
text: "Disturb me not! The flag is not finished! Come to my shop later."

speaker: Kliftin
text: "Here is the imitation I have made of the Library of Scars' honor flag."

speaker: Kliftin
text: "The time for the duels must be drawing near. Good luck to Sprellic, and to thee as well!"

speaker: Kliftin
text: "Thou must put something down if thou art to carry the flag!"

speaker: Kliftin
text: "Good day."

speaker: Ophelia
text: A pretty woman gives you a friendly grin and then coyly turns her eyes away from you.

speaker: Ophelia
text: "I bid thee welcome once again, <HONORIFIC>," says Ophelia.

speaker: Ophelia
text: "My name is Ophelia, <HONORIFIC>."

speaker: Ophelia
text: "I am a barmaid. I do most of the work at The Bunk and Stool here in Jhelom."

speaker: Ophelia
text: "Ever since Sprellic, the owner, was challenged to those duels by the three students at the Library of Scars, he has been busy preparing himself. I have been running the place all by myself... although Daphne has been helping me, I suppose."

speaker: Ophelia
text: "Honestly, I cannot imagine why thou wouldst be interested in her." She lets out a throaty laugh.

speaker: Daphne
text: "I heard that, Ophelia. Thou art a spiteful wench!"

speaker: Ophelia
text: "Now, now, Daphne. Temper, Temper! We don't want to scare off the patrons with a poor disposition in addition to a poor face!"

speaker: Daphne
text: "Witch!"

speaker: Ophelia
text: "'Tis said that indeed many strange things happen at this bar. As of late, in addition to being an inn and a pub, where thou mayest buy fine food and drink, it has become a betting parlor."

speaker: Ophelia
text: "It is a pretty rough place to work, but," she whispers to you in confidence, "I must confess I find myself attracted to the type of men that live here."

speaker: Ophelia
text: "Surely thou hast heard of our famous school for fighters by now! What kind of a world traveller art thou? Do not answer. 'Twas a rhetorical question," she sniffs.

speaker: Ophelia
text: "Thou shalt have to see Daphne about that. Thou wouldst not expect me to have to go into the kitchen?" Ophelia laughs.

speaker: Ophelia
text: "For naught more than 5 gold thou canst get a lovely room. Dost thou wish to stay the night?"

speaker: Ophelia
text: "Here is thy key. Be warned, 'twill only work in this establishment, and only for one use."

speaker: Ophelia
text: "Sorry, <HONORIFIC>, thou must lose some weight, er, some bundles, before I can give thee the room key."

speaker: Ophelia
text: "I am truly sorry, <HONORIFIC>, but the rooms cost more gold than thou hast."

speaker: Ophelia
text: "Our rooms are not good enough, I suppose," she says, scowling.

speaker: Ophelia
text: "Right now I am not at work so please do not address me as if I were."

speaker: Ophelia
text: "No one knows old Sprellic better than myself. Although he does not look it, he may well be the deadliest fighting master in all of Britannia."

speaker: Ophelia
text: "After he defeats the fighters of the Library of Scars, he may open his own school teaching his own unique style of fighting."

speaker: Ophelia
text: "It will be a great fighting school. Already, fighting men and women are coming to Jhelom to become Sprellic's students. They all long to know the secret that I can tell thee right now."

speaker: Ophelia
text: Ophelia motions you closer to her. She whispers to you. "Sprellic is really the Avatar returned to us after all these years." She nods solemnly.

speaker: Ophelia
text: Ophelia motions you closer to her. She whispers to you. "Sprellic can call upon the Avatar to come and be his champion." She nods solemnly.

speaker: Ophelia
text: "In case thou hast not noticed, this is a rough town. We see all types of odd characters in this place." She looks you over carefully.

speaker: Ophelia
text: "Sorry, all bets are off, due to the... er, unfortunate passing on of one or more of the parties involved."

speaker: Ophelia
text: "I am taking wagers on Sprellic's duels. Wouldst thou like to place a bet?"

speaker: Ophelia
text: "How much wouldst thou like to bet that Sprellic defeats all three of his challengers?"

speaker: Ophelia
text: "Perhaps thou art not truly serious about thy convictions. Mayhaps Daphne will take thy line of bets."

speaker: Ophelia
text: "Thou wouldst bet <VAR> gold that Sprellic will win?"

speaker: Ophelia
text: "Very well. How much wouldst thou like to bet?"

speaker: Ophelia
text: "Very well. Let me give thee markers for thy gold. Each one is worth 10 gold coins. If Sprellic wins, thou mayest come collect twice that amount of gold from me."

speaker: Ophelia
text: "Should he lose, <HONORIFIC>, thy markers are, of course, worthless."

speaker: Ophelia
text: "I shall soon see thee again, <HONORIFIC>." You notice she is suppressing a tiny giggle. "When thou dost return to collect thy winnings." For a moment it seems she cannot make eye contact with you.

speaker: Ophelia
text: "Thou must return later when thou hast enough room in thy pack for these markers."

speaker: Ophelia
text: "Thou hast not the amount of gold thou dost want to bet! Art thou trying to swindle me?"

speaker: Ophelia
text: "Then if thou wouldst like to bet against Sprellic, thou mayest see Daphne, but I warn thee thou wilt be throwing thy money away!"

speaker: Ophelia
text: "I see thou hast returned to collect thy winnings." She shrugs and pays them to you.

speaker: Ophelia
text: "Thou cannot carry that much gold! Return later when thou canst take all thy winnings at one time!"

speaker: Ophelia
text: "Thou hast already collected thy winnings!"

speaker: Ophelia
text: "Who? Oh, he is a local boy who comes in here and moons over me on occasion. Do not concern thyself with him. I do not."

speaker: Daphne
text: "Why what kind of way is that to speak of he who will soon become thy betrothed! Finally, I can make thee move out of mine house! Every moment of sharing my life with thee has been intolerable!"

speaker: Ophelia
text: "Do not get thine hopes up yet, my dear Daphne! I have put a condition on our marriage and poor Cosmo will never be able to fulfill it!"

speaker: Daphne
text: "Thou dost never know! The thought of thee in thy wedding gown with thy groom Cosmo at thy side is simply delicious! Perhaps he is the man who will finally teach thee to be a lady at last!"

speaker: Ophelia
text: "Hmpf! If thou didst bet against him, then I suppose thou shalt be rich! I wouldst bet that thou wert the one who killed him, too!"

speaker: Ophelia
text: She turns away from you with a sneer.

speaker: Ophelia
text: "Do come and visit us again, <HONORIFIC>."

speaker: Daphne
text: You see a disgruntled, obviously overworked barmaid. She gives you a perfunctory grunt of a hello.

speaker: Daphne
text: "Art thou still here?" she asks Dupre.

speaker: Dupre
text: "I have not finished making mine assessment of thy fine drinking establishment!"

speaker: Daphne
text: "What? Art thou working for Brommer's Britannia travel guides?"

speaker: Dupre
text: "No, my dear. This research is strictly for mine own digestion!"

speaker: Daphne
text: "Good day to thee, <HONORIFIC>. Rest and take a load off."

speaker: Daphne
text: "I am Daphne."

speaker: Daphne
text: "That is an easy one. I am the workhorse in residence of the Bunk and Stool. While our resident princess flirts with the customers I do all the cooking, cleaning and serving."

speaker: Daphne
text: "Sorry, <HONORIFIC>, I do not sell food and drink at this time."

speaker: Daphne
text: "Ever since the owner, Sprellic, got himself into trouble with the Library of Scars, there hath been no one else to run the place. Ohh, mine aching back!"

speaker: Daphne
text: "Hmmph! That would be Ophelia."

speaker: Daphne
text: "Thou shalt have to ask Ophelia about that. My domain is the kitchen!"

speaker: Daphne
text: "Ophelia this! Ophelia that! That is all I ever hear all bloody day! If all thou dost want to talk about is her, talk to someone else!"

speaker: Ophelia
text: "Do not hate me just because I am beautiful, Daphne."

speaker: Daphne
text: "That is not the reason I hate thee, Ophelia!"

speaker: Ophelia
text: "Oh, yes, I remember now. Thou dost hate me because I am beautiful, and thou art not!"

speaker: Daphne
text: "Thank thee so much, <HONORIFIC>, for bringing up my favorite subject."

speaker: Daphne
text: "The Bunk and Stool is where the fighters and ruffians come to drink in Jhelom. 'Tis not an easy job keeping such a lot happy with all their drinking and duelling and gambling."

speaker: Daphne
text: "The fool was caught stealing the honor flag from the wall of the Library of Scars! Now the three students who challenged him will kill him on the duelling field. 'Tis a tragedy."

speaker: Daphne
text: "That is the fighting club in Jhelom which produces perhaps the toughest fighters in all Britannia. Sprellic has never fought before in his entire life."

speaker: Daphne
text: "I am sorry. All bets are off since the matter has been resolved."

speaker: Daphne
text: "In fact, I am taking bets on the upcoming duels. Dost thou wish to bet that Sprellic will lose to any of the three other duellists?"

speaker: Daphne
text: "How much wouldst thou like to bet?"

speaker: Daphne
text: "Perhaps thou art not truly serious about thy convictions. Mayhaps the princess will take thy line of bets."

speaker: Daphne
text: "Thou wouldst bet <VAR> gold that Sprellic will lose?"

speaker: Daphne
text: "Very well. How much wouldst thou like to bet?"

speaker: Daphne
text: "Very well. Let me give thee markers for thy gold. Each one is worth 10 gold coins. If Sprellic loses, thou mayest come collect twice that amount of gold from me."

speaker: Daphne
text: "Should he win, <HONORIFIC>, thy markers are, of course, worthless."

speaker: Daphne
text: "Thou mayest come see me after the duels and exchange this marker for thy winnings if thou hast won."

speaker: Daphne
text: "Oh! Thou must return later when thou hast enough room in thy pack for these markers."

speaker: Daphne
text: "Thou hast not the amount of gold thou dost want to bet! Art thou trying to swindle me?"

speaker: Daphne
text: "Then if thou wouldst like to bet in favor of Sprellic, thou mayest see Ophelia, but I warn thee thou wilt be throwing thy money away!"

speaker: Daphne
text: "Here are thy winnings, <HONORIFIC>. But I have reason to believe that thou wert the one who killed poor Sprellic! If this is the way that thou makest thy money, then thou shouldst be ashamed!"

speaker: Daphne
text: "Thou cannot possibly carry all that gold. Thou must come back when I can give thee the proper amount of gold!"

speaker: Daphne
text: "Enjoy thyself."

speaker: Sprellic
text: You see a scrawny and timid-looking man who eyes you fearfully.

speaker: Sprellic
text: "Oh, my!" he cries. "'Tis really the Avatar this time! Please do not hurt me, Avatar!"

speaker: Sprellic
text: "Greetings again, <HONORIFIC>," says Sprellic.

speaker: Sprellic
text: "My name is Sprellic."

speaker: Sprellic
text: "I am the proprietor of the Bunk and Stool here in Jhelom."

speaker: Sprellic
text: "It is the local inn where all the fighters from the Library of Scars come to drink. They would wreck the place every night if not for Ophelia and Daphne."

speaker: Sprellic
text: "But that does not matter for soon I will be dead."

speaker: Sprellic
text: "This is a town of fighters who pass their time fighting each other in bloody duels. It is no place for me. I should never have left Minoc!"

speaker: Sprellic
text: "It is the club of fighters run by Master De Snel! Second home to the fiercest and most ruthless fighters in all of Britannia."

speaker: Sprellic
text: "Ophelia is one of my barmaids. She is gorgeous. If Daphne cannot handle our patrons when they become unruly, Ophelia will simply charm them."

speaker: Sprellic
text: "Daphne is one of my barmaids. She is, ahem, rather large. If Ophelia cannot charm our patrons when they become unruly, Daphne wrestles them to the ground."

speaker: Sprellic
text: "'Tis a long story. I shall probably be dead before I can finish it."

speaker: Sprellic
text: "My tale is a strange one. It may disturb and puzzle thee. Art thou certain thou wouldst like to hear it?"

speaker: Sprellic
text: "Well, then I hope I was of some assistance to thee. Farewell forever, <HONORIFIC>."

speaker: Sprellic
text: "It all started the previous evening. I had given Ophelia and Daphne the evening off. A stranger had come to mine inn... A very odd stranger."

speaker: Sprellic
text: "He... he claimed he was the -Avatar-!"

speaker: Sprellic
text: "...And I believed him, which shows thee how gullible I am!"

speaker: Sprellic
text: "His eccentricity seemed to be surpassed only by his wealth. He booked both rooms in the inn so that he could try each bed and decide for himself which one was the most comfortable. As for food, he was voracious."

speaker: Sprellic
text: "No offense, but he was also a member of The Fellowship!"

speaker: Sprellic
text: "He was a member of The Fellowship, too!"

speaker: Sprellic
text: "I fear that this stranger was not who he claimed to be at all. I was a victim of a great and terrible deception that was perpetrated upon me."

speaker: Sprellic
text: "This stranger ordered one of every kind of food and drink on the menu. So if he ever wanted anything, it would be right there to eat. I was cooking for hours. But then it got worse. He went to bed."

speaker: Sprellic
text: "Of course most of the food he left was uneaten! I had to give it away once it started to spoil!"

speaker: Sprellic
text: "After he went to bed, he complained that he was too cold. I brought him more and more blankets, but it was not enough. Finally, he had every blanket in the inn. And he was still cold!"

speaker: Sprellic
text: "In desperation I ran down the street. It was the middle of the night. All of the shops were closed. The only thing I could find was some sort of old tapestry hanging on a wall. So I took it down."

speaker: Sprellic
text: "Actually, now as I recall being out in the night air, it was a quite tolerable evening. Alas, I was oblivious to little else but the prospect of earning a goodly sum in the service of the stranger. Woe is me!"

speaker: Sprellic
text: "The next thing I remember there was an angry woman chasing after me. For some reason she wanted to kill me! I managed to get away from her and get back to the inn and cover the stranger with the tapestry. Finally he fell asleep."

speaker: Sprellic
text: "Actually, I had seen this angry woman before. She would enter mine establishment upon occasion. Unfortunately, this was our first formal acquaintance."

speaker: Sprellic
text: "I also fell asleep, only I slept late. When I awoke the guest was gone. He had not paid his bill and had taken all the blankets, even the tapestry. Before I could go look for him I had a visitor."

speaker: Sprellic
text: "As I have said, I was rooked by a professional. A Master Criminal, no doubt -- and one who is still at large!"

speaker: Sprellic
text: "It was the woman who had chased me the night before. Her name was Syria. She said I had stolen the honor flag from the wall of the Library of Scars. She also challenged me to a duel to the death unless I gave it back. And she is much bigger than I! When I tried to explain that I could not give it back, she hit me. It hurt. A lot!"

speaker: Sprellic
text: "I will say this of the Lady Syria. She is quite beautiful when she is angry... At least, the visions of her that swam through mine head after she had hit me were quite beautiful. Tragically, I awoke."

speaker: Sprellic
text: "Later that day I ran into a man named Vokes. He is a fighter at the Library of Scars. He asked me to return the honor flag and when I tried to tell him I could not, he hit me. Then he challenged me to a duel to the death to be fought right after my duel with Syria."

speaker: Sprellic
text: "After Vokes left, I encountered a man named Timmons. He asked me to return the honor flag to the Library of Scars. I told him I could not and he also challenged me to a duel to the death. I told him I was busy, but he scheduled the challenge for right after my duel with Vokes."

speaker: Sprellic
text: "Timmons, Vokes and Syria are the three toughest fighters in Jhelom. I could not hope to survive against one of them, let alone all three. The mysterious guest and the honor flag are nowhere to be found. Even now my barmaids are taking bets on the manner of my demise!"

speaker: Sprellic
text: "Timmons has come to Jhelom only recently. I can tell thee nothing more of him."

speaker: Sprellic
text: "He is a fearless warrior, who cherishes any opportunity for combat. Beware of him."

speaker: Sprellic
text: "She is not as bad as she may appear to be. No doubt that woman has a temper. But I am sure she is quite nice once thou hast gotten the chance to know her. If not for these sad circumstances, we might have gotten the chance to get to know each other better."

speaker: Sprellic
text: "Mine only hope for survival is to find a champion who could stand up to the fiercest fighters in Jhelom."

speaker: Sprellic
text: "Wouldst thou be my champion, Avatar?"

speaker: Sprellic
text: Sprellic falls to his knees before you in gratitude. "Avatar, thou hast saved my life! I cannot thank thee enough!"

speaker: Sprellic
text: "Oh, well. I had no choice but to ask."

speaker: Sprellic
text: You tell Sprellic that the situation has been resolved and how it was done.

speaker: Sprellic
text: Sprellic practically kisses your feet.

speaker: Sprellic
text: "How can I ever thank thee? Thou art the most noble person I have ever met! I shalt be forever in thy debt! I thank thee!"

speaker: Sprellic
text: You tell Sprellic that Kliftin made you a false flag.

speaker: Sprellic
text: "How ingenious! Please! Deliver it to Syria as soon as thou art able! And I thank thee for thy trouble in helping me!"

speaker: Sprellic
text: "Good day to thee, Avatar."

speaker: Vokes
text: You see a fighting man. His voice booms like thunder as he greets you. "Hail to thee, <HONORIFIC>!"

speaker: Vokes
text: "So, once again, I am at thy service," bellows Vokes.

speaker: Vokes
text: "If thou wouldst return the honor flag of the Library of Scars, then it is only proper that is turned back over to Syria, who was guarding it when it was stolen. Please do so."

speaker: Vokes
text: "So, thou wishest to fight for the cowardly Sprellic! Then I have no choice but to finish thee myself!"

speaker: Vokes
text: "So, thou wishes to fight for the cowardly Sprellic! Meet us at the duelling area at next noon!"

speaker: Vokes
text: "My name is Vokes, <HONORIFIC>. As big as a mountain, as strong as an ox, as fierce as... well, more fierce than anything thou hast ever fought!"

speaker: Vokes
text: "Job! I am not in the habit of plowing fields or peddling vegetables, <HONORIFIC>! I earn my gold with this sword arm," he says as he flexes a mighty bicep. "Right now I am in Jhelom continuing my studies in my trade with De Snel, and when I am finished my price is going to go up!"

speaker: Vokes
text: "I was born here! Is it not magnificent?! Why, in any hour of any day thou canst get into a duel with anyone for no reason at all! Now that is what I call the benefits of civilization!"

speaker: Vokes
text: "A responsibility, yes, even a necessity. The cost of being honorable is that one must defend one's honor. There is no telling just where or when the next stain on one's honor may appear. Like this Sprellic fool, for instance. The perfect example!"

speaker: Syria
text: "I'll make a stain on his honor, that's for sure. A blood red one!"

speaker: Vokes
text: "The bloody idiot had no idea that when he took our honor flag he would be seen doing it. Hence, he never considered the fact that he would have to fight a duel over our sullied honor. But now that the whole town is talking of the incident there is no way that we could refrain from standing up for ourselves. Especially since he has refused to return what he has taken from us."

speaker: Timmons
text: "Were he not such a cad, he would see the foolishness of his actions. 'Tis now up to us to show him!"

speaker: Vokes
text: "If he had not returned the honor flag to us we would have had to kill him dead as sure as I am standing here."

speaker: Vokes
text: "There is a widely known and long-standing tradition concerning the honor flag of the Library of Scars. It is said that taking the flag from the wall is a signal meaning that the person who takes the flag can beat anyone who studies at the school in a fight. It is also a grossly insulting way of saying that thou dost think the method of fighting a school teaches is inferior, which the Library of Scars most certainly is not!"

speaker: Vokes
text: "I have heard that rot about it all being a misunderstanding. The only thing misunderstood is how bad Sprellic will look when we finish with him!"

speaker: Vokes
text: "The Library of Scars teaches the supreme fighting style! One that enables thee to get the advantage against thine opponents and soundly defeat them through the brilliantly conceived subterfuge of Master De Snel!"

speaker: Vokes
text: "He is a genius. Perhaps the greatest military mind that ever lived. He told us so!"

speaker: Vokes
text: "If I am not killed and thou art not killed perhaps we may raise a	glass together some day!"

speaker: Syria
text: "I see that coward Sprellic has given thee the flag so that it may be returned to us. Thou hadst better hand it over."

speaker: Syria
text: She takes the banner from you.

speaker: Syria
text: "This matter is now settled. But tell that worm Sprellic from me that he had better keep his hands off of other people's property in the future."

speaker: Syria
text: "It has come to our attention that thou hast been given our honor flag. Apparently Sprellic gave it to thee to return to us. If thou dost wish to keep it then our quarrel is now with thee."

speaker: Syria
text: "Thou mayest fight for Sprellic, but I fight for honor!"

speaker: Syria
text: Standing before you is a statuesque fighting woman with eyes that radiate a familiarity with danger.

speaker: Syria
text: "It seems we meet again," says Syria.

speaker: Syria
text: "I am Syria, a fighter from the south."

speaker: Syria
text: "Currently I am resting from my last voyage as a mercenary. I am	studying in Jhelom with the fighting trainer De Snel	at the Library of Scars."

speaker: Syria
text: "This is a city of fighters and duels. If thou dost not like it the way it is, then leave. Duels are fought here for many reasons. I have mine own reasons for fighting them."

speaker: Syria
text: "There is no question that Sprellic is the one who took the honor flag of our school. If he does not wish to fight the duels then he has only to return it."

speaker: Syria
text: "A pity we could not teach that little fool a lesson. Still, we have regained our honor and that is enough. For now."

speaker: Syria
text: "Since Sprellic has not done this, it proves that he is sincere in the grievous insult that he has made against us."

speaker: Vokes
text: "And I shall grievously insult him-- through his heart!"

speaker: Syria
text: "I was on guard when Sprellic took our club's honor flag. I saw him take it but I lost him in the shadows of the night. My punishment was ten lashes for allowing the thief to escape. I mean to repay him for that."

speaker: Syria
text: "A pity we could not teach that little fool a lesson. Perhaps we have anyway. For his sake, he had better have learned it well."

speaker: Syria
text: "The Library of Scars is the greatest guild of fighters in Britannia."

speaker: Vokes
text: "Here! Here!"

speaker: Syria
text: "Master De Snel teaches a style of pure fighting which takes thee beyond all previous disciplines that thou mayest have learned. He is a great man."

speaker: Syria
text: "I understand that coward Sprellic has given thee the flag so that it may be returned to us. Thou hadst better hand it over."

speaker: Syria
text: She takes the banner from you.

speaker: Syria
text: "This matter is now settled. But tell that worm Sprellic from me that he had better keep his hands off of other people's property in the future."

speaker: Syria
text: "It has come to our attention that thou hast been given our honor flag. Apparently Sprellic gave it to thee to return to us. If thou dost wish to keep it then our quarrel is now with thee."

speaker: Syria
text: "Meet us at the dueling area at next noon!"

speaker: Syria
text: "Prepare to die!"

speaker: Syria
text: "We do not appreciate people who interfere in our private matters. We shall be watching thee."

speaker: Timmons
text: You see a very serious young man. He carries himself like a learned and mannered gentleman.

speaker: Timmons
text: "Dost thou wish to speak with me?" asks Timmons.

speaker: Timmons
text: "I see thou hast the honor flag. As little more than an interested third party in this affair, I ask thee to return the flag to Syria. Please do so."

speaker: Timmons
text: "Well, <HONORIFIC>, I must prove myself to De Snel. If thou art the one who suffers, I will apologize, but I will not back down!"

speaker: Timmons
text: "Prepare to die!"

speaker: Timmons
text: "Well, <HONORIFIC>, I must prove myself to De Snel. If thou art the one who suffers, so be it! Meet us at the dueling area at next noon!"

speaker: Timmons
text: "Timmons is my name, <HONORIFIC>."

speaker: Timmons
text: "At the moment I have no job. I left all that behind in New Magincia. I have come to Jhelom to study under Master De Snel in the Library of Scars."

speaker: Timmons
text: "I am afraid I would not be able to help thee. I know little of this town, except for the duels. I am newly arrived here myself. Perhaps thou shouldst ask someone else."

speaker: Timmons
text: "I had heard of this man Sprellic who claims he is a greater fighter than any in the Library of Scars and how he had stolen the honor flag from their wall. So I sought this man out and challenged him to a duel myself."

speaker: Timmons
text: "Unfortunately, the duels with Sprellic were called off before I had the opportunity to impress Master De Snel."

speaker: Timmons
text: "A sailor on a ship at port in New Magincia first told me of the Library of Scars, of how it was the greatest fighting guild in Britannia and how its trainer, Master De Snel, had created the perfect fighting style. I immediately spent every coin I had to come here. But De Snel now refuses to accept me as a student. I know if I can defeat a fighter who claims to be better than anyone in the guild, and help restore its honor in the process, De Snel will have to finally accept me."

speaker: Timmons
text: "Master De Snel, the trainer at the Library of Scars, has refused me entry until I have proven myself in combat. The only way to prove oneself in combat in the town of Jhelom is by duelling. But my mother raised me to be a perfect gentleman. So far I have not succeeded in offending anyone sufficiently to have them challenge me to a duel. Hmmm. Perhaps I am just not suited to be a member of the Library of Scars."

speaker: Timmons
text: "It was a pleasure speaking to thee, <HONORIFIC>."

speaker: Iriale
text: You see a striking woman in fighter's gear. She looks at you fiercely.

speaker: Iriale
text: "Halt!"

speaker: Iriale
text: "What dost thou want?" Iriale demands.

speaker: Iriale
text: "I am called Iriale Silvermist. Who art thou?"

speaker: Iriale
text: "I do not know thee!"

speaker: Iriale
text: "I do not approve of jokes."

speaker: Iriale
text: Iriale smiles devilishly.

speaker: Iriale
text: "I bar people from entering. Thou hast disobeyed the rule of the Meditation Retreat. Ian will be most displeased. Thou had best leave now."

speaker: Iriale
text: "Thou dost know it. Attendees of the Retreat must stay out of this cave."

speaker: Iolo
text: "Come, <PLAYER_NAME>, we had better leave. I believe this woman is serious."

speaker: Iriale
text: "Is that the name of that smelly barbarian who was here? If thou dost see him on the -way out-, tell him that if he approaches me again, I shall cut off his head!"

speaker: Iriale
text: "Yes, I work for the Meditation Retreat."

speaker: Iriale
text: "And I work for -him-. -He- does not want thee here. I give thee only one chance to turn around and leave."

speaker: Iriale
text: "Wilt thou leave?"

speaker: Iriale
text: "Do so and I shall spare thee!" She watches as you turn away.

speaker: Iriale
text: She sees your jaw set with determination and nods her head. "Then die, foolish one!"

speaker: Iriale
text: "Away with thee!"

speaker: Russell
text: Before you is a shrewd-looking craftsman, obviously filled with the contentment of a peaceful life.

speaker: Russell
text: "What may I do for thee?" says Russell.

speaker: Russell
text: "I am Russell, a shipwright."

speaker: Russell
text: "I build ships in New Magincia. It is a profession I enjoy very much. I also sell deeds for my ships, and sextants by which one can navigate the open seas."

speaker: Russell
text: "But I have already sold thee the deed to 'The Nymphet'! I am afraid that was the only ship I had at this time."

speaker: Russell
text: "Thou wishest to purchase my ship 'The Nymphet'? The deed will cost thee 600 gold."

speaker: Russell
text: "'The Nymphet' is thine, <HONORIFIC>. Enjoy the waters."

speaker: Russell
text: "Thou art carrying too much to take thy deed. Come back after putting some things down."

speaker: Russell
text: "Mine apologies, <HONORIFIC>, thou dost not have enough gold."

speaker: Russell
text: "I understand, <HONORIFIC>, the seas aren't for everyone."

speaker: Russell
text: "When my shop is again open I shall be more than happy to help thee."

speaker: Russell
text: "Thou wishest to purchase one of my fine sextants? 'Twill cost thee 40 gold."

speaker: Russell
text: "'Tis thine, <HONORIFIC>. Enjoy the waters."

speaker: Russell
text: "I would gladly give thee thy sextant but thou shalt have to put something down! Thou art carrying	too much to take it."

speaker: Russell
text: "Mine apologies, <HONORIFIC>, thou dost not have enough gold."

speaker: Russell
text: "I understand, <HONORIFIC>, some of us can navigate with just the naked stars!"

speaker: Russell
text: "At present my shop is closed. If thou wilt come back during business hours I shall be more than happy to help thee."

speaker: Russell
text: "Things have been very peaceful in New Magincia. There has been little trouble from outsiders lately."

speaker: Russell
text: "Before thine arrival there had not been a stranger in New Magincia for years, save for the survivors of the shipwreck."

speaker: Russell
text: "I found the wreckage. Three men were clinging to it for their lives."

speaker: Russell
text: "I had never seen a ship like it before. The markings show it was constructed by a Minoc shipwright named Owen. It was not very well constructed."

speaker: Russell
text: "They were from Buccaneer's Den. Most people that come here come because they are lost on their way to or from Buccaneer's Den."

speaker: Russell
text: "The three men wish to go back. They say there is a house of games in Buccaneer's Den." Russell shrugs. "As if that would be a reason to go there."

speaker: Russell
text: "I offered to sell them a ship, but they had no money. They actually seemed offended when I would not give it to them for free!"

speaker: Russell
text: "The three strangers tried to offer me some kind of trinket to build or sell them a ship. It sounds like the locket thou art describing."

speaker: Russell
text: "I would not have accepted their offer, but I was curious. Later they said nothing when I wanted to see the trinket again. I doubt they have it."

speaker: Russell
text: "I could not help noticing your medallion. It does look somewhat sinister. I cannot recall ever having seen one like it before."

speaker: Russell
text: "The Crown Jewel just left here a short while ago. I do not know where it was headed."

speaker: Russell
text: "I have heard nothing more of the Crown Jewel since we last spoke of it."

speaker: Russell
text: "Just as the Crown Jewel left I saw a man with a hook jump on board. There was a gargoyle accompanying him."

speaker: Russell
text: "I have heard nothing more of this man Hook since we last spoke of him."

speaker: Russell
text: "Fare thee well, <HONORIFIC>."

speaker: Boris
text: "Art thou ready to pay thy bill?"

speaker: Boris
text: "Goodbye, then!"

speaker: Boris
