text: You see a leering, ill-postured man who chortles to himself.

speaker: Boris
text: "Well if it isn't Dupre! -Sir- Dupre now, is it?"

speaker: Dupre
text: "That it is, Boris."

speaker: Boris
text: "Hmmm-- it seems to me thou dost have a tab still going here? Yes?"

speaker: Dupre
text: "Oh? Do I?"

speaker: Boris
text: "Yes indeed! Let me see... I believe the total that thou dost owe is 74 gold pieces. I am afraid that thou must pay up before I can speak with thee or anyone else with thee."

speaker: Dupre
text: Dupre looks embarrassed. He turns to you. "My friend, wilt thou help me out?"

speaker: Dupre
text: "I thank thee, Avatar."

speaker: Dupre
text: You hand the gold over to Boris.

speaker: Boris
text: "'Tis a pleasure to do business with thee, Sir Dupre! And welcome to my pub!"

speaker: Boris
text: "Hmmm, where did our gold go?"

speaker: Boris
text: "I am afraid are pockets are too empty!"

speaker: Boris
text: "Well, I wilt not be serving thee or speaking to thee until thy bill is paid!"

speaker: Boris
text: "Hello again," says Boris.

speaker: Boris
text: "Call me Boris."

speaker: Boris
text: "I run The Modest Damsel, here in New Magincia."

speaker: Boris
text: "It is a little inn and tavern. I am the owner, along with my wife, Magenta. Wouldst thou like something to eat or drink, or perhaps a room?"

speaker: Boris
text: "The Modest Damsel is now closed for business. But do please return during business hours."

speaker: Boris
text: "She became the mayor of New Magincia after the death of the old mayor, her father, several years ago. She has done such a good job that no one has opposed her for the position yet."

speaker: Boris
text: "I am certain thou wilt enjoy our food and drink."

speaker: Boris
text: "Why dost thou not stay the night? For but 3 gold thou canst let one of our rooms. Dost thou wish to stay the night?"

speaker: Boris
text: "Here is thy room key. 'Twill only work in this inn."

speaker: Boris
text: "Sorry, <HONORIFIC>, thou must remove some of thy load before I can give thee the room key."

speaker: Boris
text: "Thou hast not enough gold for my rooms."

speaker: Boris
text: "Some other evening, perhaps."

speaker: Boris
text: "In all of Britannia thou shalt not find a place that changes so little. Even the people always seem the same."

speaker: Boris
text: "There are merchants and laborers, as well as a few new folks."

speaker: Boris
text: "They would be Russell, the shipwright; Henry, the peddler; and Sam, the flower man."

speaker: Boris
text: "They would be Katrina, the shepherd, and Constance, the water carrier."

speaker: Boris
text: "Except for the three strangers, the only relatively new person on the island is Alagner, the sage."

speaker: Boris
text: "Alagner is not from New Magincia, of course, but has settled here after studying the world, for he well knows the value of our peace and solitude."

speaker: Boris
text: "A brilliant artist and craftsman, Russell cares little for wealth or notoriety. He is content simply building his fine ships and watching them sail."

speaker: Boris
text: "Katrina has come to the aid of the people of this town on more than one occasion. She gets an interesting smile on her face whenever thy name is mentioned."

speaker: Katrina
text: "That is because the Avatar is one my dearest friends."

speaker: Boris
text: "Am I not one of thy dearest friends, Katrina?"

speaker: Katrina
text: "Thou art a flirt, Boris! Dost Magenta know how thou dost want to be dearest friends with the other women living on the island?"

speaker: Boris
text: "Thou dost torture me, Katrina!" He laughs.

speaker: Boris
text: "Henry's parents were so poor it is a wonder he did not starve to death. I think Constance kept him going. He has loved her since they were children."

speaker: Boris
text: "Constance is an orphan who was raised mostly by Katrina. Her innocence is surpassed only by her beauty. She is loved by all." Boris stares off into space for a few seconds before coming to his senses.

speaker: Boris
text: Boris laughs. "Thou wouldst have to meet Sam for thyself. He is an incredible person who is perfecting the art of enjoying life."

speaker: Boris
text: "A shipwreck has brought three strangers to our island. Rumor has it one of them is a monied gentleman from Buccaneer's Den, and the other two are his hired swords. They were in here drinking one night. They are not the sort of crowd I would wish to serve at mine establishment."

speaker: Boris
text: "I do not wish to hear of that locket ever again! Do not speak to me of it!"

speaker: Boris
text: "I am quite certain I have never seen such a locket. I shall be happy to keep mine eyes open, though."

speaker: Boris
text: You tell Boris what you had heard from the pirate, Battles. He breaks out into a cold sweat. "Thou hast seen through my deception. I shall hand it over to thee." He opens a secret panel from behind the bar and looks inside. When he looks back to you his face has lost all color. "The locket is gone! I swear to thee, I know not where it is!"

speaker: Boris
text: "I still have not been able to find the locket!" Boris looks as if he is about to tear his hair out, "But I will keep looking until I find it!"

speaker: Boris
text: "Good journey!"

speaker: Magenta
text: You see a humble-looking older woman. She gives you a friendly smile.

speaker: Magenta
text: Magenta smiles. "Good day, <HONORIFIC>. May I help thee?"

speaker: Magenta
text: "I am Magenta, of New Magincia."

speaker: Magenta
text: "I am the Mayor of New Magincia, and the wife of Boris."

speaker: Magenta
text: "It is a job that requires little actual administration. I mostly try to make sure that everyone is getting along with everyone else. Apart from that, the town practically runs itself."

speaker: Magenta
text: "Why even the taxes here are less severe than anywhere else in Britannia. The Britannian Tax Council sometimes forgets to come collecting here for years on end."

speaker: Magenta
text: "Boris is the local innkeeper and a bit of a scoundrel if I say so myself. But he pours a good drink and tells a good story. Although I have to keep an eye on him, I love him."

speaker: Magenta
text: "Oh, nothing is ever new in New Magincia, as the joke around here goes. But that is how we like it. We have few visitors here."

speaker: Magenta
text: "I hear there are three other new arrivals wandering around here somewhere. I always try to give people the benefit of the doubt, but be careful of them."

speaker: Magenta
text: "Certainly some of the other townsfolk must have seen them by now. Perhaps they will have more information."

speaker: Magenta
text: You see the locket Henry described to you hanging around Magenta's neck. "Is it not beautiful? I found it in the secret hiding place behind mine husband's bar."

speaker: Magenta
text: "I would never have suspected anything so romantic from Boris. The locket must be a surprise for me!"

speaker: Magenta
text: "He must be trying to get back on my good side after all of the times I have caught him wenching and carousing."

speaker: Magenta
text: "Well, I -did- think he was going to give it to me to make up for all the times I have caught him wenching and carousing."

speaker: Magenta
text: "Say, dost thou think that Boris could have meant to give this locket to someone else?"

speaker: Magenta
text: Magenta's eyes widen in shock. "Who?"

speaker: Magenta
text: "I cannot possibly wear a piece of jewelry meant for another woman. As mayor, I charge thee, Avatar, with the task of returning it to her, or more properly to the person who had intended to give it to her. As for Boris... well, I shall deal with him later!"

speaker: Magenta
text: "Here is the locket. Take it."

speaker: Magenta
text: "I cannot give thee the locket. Thou art too encumbered. Come back after thou hast put a few things down."

speaker: Magenta
text: Magenta looks puzzled. "I wonder who it could be?"

speaker: Magenta
text: Then Magenta gets a devilish gleam in her eye. "Well then. I shall just beat it out of him!"

speaker: Magenta
text: Magenta sighs with relief. "I am glad thou hast said this. Now I shall feel no guilt about keeping it."

speaker: Magenta
text: "I am flattered Boris would buy me such an obviously expensive gift. But how could he ever have afforded it?"

speaker: Magenta
text: Although Magenta struggles to retain her dignity, she cannot hide her disappointment. "As Mayor, I charge thee with the task of locating the rightful owner of this locket and returning it to them."

speaker: Magenta
text: "Here it is. Take it."

speaker: Magenta
text: "Thou hast not room to carry even such a small thing as this! If thou wilt set something down, I will give thee the locket."

speaker: Magenta
text: Magenta looks puzzled. Then she smiles. "Oh well. It sure is nice, is it not? If he thought this would improve our marital relations, he was not altogether wrong!"

speaker: Magenta
text: "Well, I thought at first that Boris had bought the locket for me as a surprise! Wait until I get mine hands on that no good..." Magenta's face turns as red as her hair.

speaker: Magenta
text: "I look forward to the next time when I will see thee."

speaker: Henry
text: You see a scruffy young man who is obviously suffering from a broken heart.

speaker: Henry
text: Henry greets you. "It is good to speak with thee again, <HONORIFIC>!"

speaker: Henry
text: "My name is Henry, <HONORIFIC>."

speaker: Henry
text: "Job?! Who can work when he has a broken heart?!"

speaker: Henry
text: "Although I am called a peddler, I have the greatest selection of items to be found in New Magincia."

speaker: Henry
text: "I have lived here all of my life and have never known anyplace else. It is a basically a very nice place where people still adhere to the old ways and values. The rest of the world must think it has passed us by, but it is they who have lost what once was."

speaker: Henry
text: "I have been rejected by the woman I love."

speaker: Henry
text: His eyes light up. "Her name is Constance, she is the most beautiful woman in the world, and for a time we were in love." His face falls, and he sighs deeply. "But that was before I made a terrible mistake..."

speaker: Henry
text: "She is the waterbearer of the town. She carries water from the well of Humility to all the homes in town."

speaker: Henry
text: "I promised to give her a very old and valuable locket as a token of mine affection. My childhood friend, Katrina, had given the locket to me."

speaker: Henry
text: "Before I could give her the locket, I lost it. I have searched everywhere but I cannot find it. Now, Constance thinks I am a cad and has forsaken me."

speaker: Henry
text: "Katrina is a shepherd here on New Magincia. She has been a friend of mine since I was a boy."

speaker: Katrina
text: "We have had some good memories, have we not, Henry?"

speaker: Henry
text: "Oh that we have! But thou wouldst not be my sweetheart, so we resigned ourselves to being 'just friends' a long time ago, is that not true?"

speaker: Katrina
text: "Whatever thou dost say, dear Henry."

speaker: Henry
text: "I noticed I had lost the locket right after I spoke with those three strangers yesterday. Wouldst thou help me find it?"

speaker: Henry
text: "Oh, thank thee, <HONORIFIC>! If not for thee, I would be lost."

speaker: Henry
text: "Oh, well... I know thou art busy on thine own quest. I thank thee for listening to my tale, <HONORIFIC>."

speaker: Henry
text: "There are three other strangers in New Magincia. They arrived a few days before thee. Their ship was sunk and they barely made it here with their lives."

speaker: Henry
text: "Thou hast found the locket!"

speaker: Henry
text: You hand the locket to Henry. "Now I may give it to Constance and keep my promise to her! I cannot thank thee enough, Avatar!"

speaker: Katrina
text: "I am glad that this situation has concluded in thy favor, dear Henry."

speaker: Henry
text: "My thanks to thee, Katrina."

speaker: Henry
text: He looks distraught when you make no move to give it to him. "Where is it?! I need it if I am to prove myself to the woman I love!"

speaker: Henry
text: "Travel safely and be well."

speaker: Constance
text: You see an angelic young woman who gives you a smile of complete innocence.

speaker: Constance
text: "<HONORIFIC>!" says a wide-eyed Constance, "What may I do for thee?"

speaker: Constance
text: "My name, <HONORIFIC>, is Constance." She shyly lowers her eyes.

speaker: Constance
text: "I carry water from the well of humility to all of the homes here in New Magincia."

speaker: Constance
text: "The water from the well is pure and cool. If thou wouldst like I will pour thee some."

speaker: Constance
text: With a big smile Constance takes a	dipper and submerges it in the cool water of her bucket. She draws out the dipper and hands it to you. You drink and find the water delicious and very refreshing.

speaker: Iolo
text: "Actually, I feel quite parched myself. Might I have some as well?" Constance nods yes, and hands him a	dipper of water. He drinks with loud gulping sounds.

speaker: Shamino
text: "I, too, am feeling dry. Wouldst thou share thy water with me, milady?" Constance fills the dipper with water for Shamino and he drinks until water runs down his chin.

speaker: Shamino
text: You see Shamino nudge Dupre. "Art thou not going to have a drink?"

speaker: Dupre
text: "I shall wait until we find something a bit stronger than water to quench my thirst."

speaker: Spark
text: Constance hands Spark a dipper full of water. He drinks it down in one long slurp. Upon finishing it, he burps. With an	embarrassed grin he bows	apologetically to Constance	as he hands her back the dipper.

speaker: Constance
text: "If thou wouldst ever change thy mind thou needest only let me know."

speaker: Constance
text: "There are three strangers on the island! They have been shipwrecked here! I have met them. Their leader's name is Robin."

speaker: Constance
text: "I was born in New Magincia and I have lived here mine entire life. But now I wish to leave for mine heart hath been broken."

speaker: Constance
text: "Once I was in love with Henry, the peddler, but then I learned he is a liar and a cad. Perhaps soon mine heart shall belong to another."

speaker: Constance
text: You tell Constance of Robin's plans for her. She gives you a shocked look. "Many thanks. I now know that my rightful place is with Henry."

speaker: Constance
text: You tell Constance of how you have returned the locket that has been stolen from Henry. "Oh, how could I ever have doubted my dear darling Henry?" she frowns. "I thank thee for telling me the truth."

speaker: Henry
text: "Constance, I am sorry that things ran afoul as they did, but if thou wilt, I would like thee to have this locket as a symbol of my love."

speaker: Constance
text: "My sweet Henry, mine heart belongs to only thee."

speaker: Constance
text: "There is a charming and mysterious stranger on the island named Robin. He says one day he may show me the world and buy me many fine things." Constance sighs. "He even gave me some lovely flowers."

speaker: Constance
text: "He is a wealthy man and his two friends are big, strong men. They have been telling me about a very wonderful-sounding place called Buccaneer's Den."

speaker: Constance
text: "Their names were Battles and Leavell. Both of them treated me like proper gentlemen."

speaker: Constance
text: "Buccaneer's Den must be a wonderland. There is a spinning wheel that gives thee money! Canst thou imagine! And opulent, luxurious baths."

speaker: Constance
text: "Battles was quiet at first. I thought he was mean-looking, but he is nice once thou dost get to know him. He told me of the various monsters he fought, and exciting stories of how he raided ships in the south seas."

speaker: Constance
text: "Leavell was charming and witty. He can always make me laugh."

speaker: Constance
text: "Well, they certainly have nothing like that in New Magincia. I had never even heard of such a thing before!"

speaker: Constance
text: "Doth that not sound nice?"

speaker: Constance
text: You gently explain to Constance that Robin, Battles and Leavell were scoundrels with intent to do her great harm. She is quite alarmed. Then you explain that they will not be troubling her anymore. She thanks you.

speaker: Constance
text: "It was a pleasure speaking with thee, <HONORIFIC>."

speaker: Robin
text: You see a roguish man dressed in what appears to be some nobleman's ratty hand-me-downs.

speaker: Robin
text: "Greetings, and how may I be of service to thee?" asks Robin.

speaker: Robin
text: "My name, <HONORIFIC>, is Robin. A pleasure to meet thee. I have come to New Magincia only recently."

speaker: Robin
text: "My father, a well-respected nobleman whose name I will not defame by mentioning, bastardized and disowned me. But he did teach me mine occupation."

speaker: Robin
text: "Why, that most glamorous and respected of occupations, <HONORIFIC>. Winning at games of chance."

speaker: Robin
text: "I am not from here. My colleagues and I had to quickly leave Buccaneer's Den after a dispute with the casino owner. And a rough voyage it was, too."

speaker: Robin
text: "My friends are Battles and Leavell. Their job is to protect me and my winnings. In exchange they share in my profits."

speaker: Robin
text: "I rescued him from his captain who was about to make him walk the plank. I diced with that Captain for the lad's life. Later, Battles led a mutiny that took the ship, and... well, that is another story."

speaker: Robin
text: "I rescued him from a gaggle of angry noblemen's daughters who had just discovered he was courting all of them simultaneously. If not for me he would have certainly perished! But I am ahead of myself."

speaker: Robin
text: "It is where we live most of the year. There are a lot of rough characters there and it is not a place to be seen carrying large amounts of money."

speaker: Robin
text: "I won a vulgar amount of the casino's gold and 'The Mister' of the place, Gordy, accused me of cheating. He sent his legbreaker, Sintag, after us. Pirates do not like to lose!"

speaker: Robin
text: "Do not ask me why he is called that! Everyone there calls him that, though!"

speaker: Robin
text: "We took the first ship out, but before we got back to the mainland it had sunk. The three of us barely managed to make it to New Magincia with our lives. Now we are marooned here."

speaker: Robin
text: "I do not know of any. I only just arrived here myself."

speaker: Robin
text: "One rough character in particular to stay away from is a man called Hook. He would kill thee for a trifle. Thou canst tell him by the hook he has for a hand."

speaker: Robin
text: "I know nothing more. If thou thinkest that I would willingly cross paths with the likes of him thou must have me mistaken for someone else!"

speaker: Robin
text: "We are trying to return to Buccaneer's Den. I was hoping to sell a gold locket which came into my possession to buy our passage back, but I fear it is lost. If thou dost come across it be sure to let me know."

speaker: Robin
text: "Thou art a member of The Fellowship! For years I have been seeing Fellowship members winning heavy stakes at the House of Games. Canst thou tell me their secret?"

speaker: Robin
text: "Of course thou canst. But I do not suspect that thou wilt." Robin shrugs his shoulders.

speaker: Robin
text: "Forgive me if I do not believe thee."

speaker: Robin
text: "That is right. We cannot afford the stinking ship sold by the shipwright."

speaker: Robin
text: "But say, thou must have gotten here in some manner! Dost thou have some manner of ship on which we could leave the island?"

speaker: Robin
text: "I could pay thee well if thou wouldst	take us back to Buccaneer's Den."

speaker: Robin
text: "If thou shouldst come across a way off this island please permit us to leave with thee."

speaker: Robin
text: "Of course, I cannot pay thee right now at this moment.	But when we reach Buccaneer's Den, I promise thee, I shall be able to get mine hands on a lot of money."

speaker: Robin
text: "Yes, money! For I have found something here in New Magincia that will be worth more than gold in Buccaneer's Den."

speaker: Robin
text: "Before I tell thee what it is, wilt thou promise to take me and my mates back to Buccaneer's Den?"

speaker: Robin
text: Robin looks you in the eye. "Thou art truly a kind friend. I suppose then I should tell thee what it is we are planning on bringing back from New Magincia."

speaker: Robin
text: "Then I cannot trust thee enough to tell thee of my plans. Go away."

speaker: Robin
text: "Since thou art truly a friend then I know that I can ask a favor of thee. Why dost thou not bring back that lost locket to me and we shall speak of these things some more." He flashes you a wicked grin.

speaker: Robin
text: "Since thou hast brought my locket back here, I suppose that I can trust thee. I intend to take Constance back with us and sell her to the operator of the baths."

speaker: Robin
text: "Now that I know I can trust thee, I can let thee in on our plan. I intend to take another passenger in thy boat back with us to Buccaneer's Den. Her name is Constance and she should fetch a goodly price from Glenno, operator of the baths. Enough to pay my debts, pay thee for passage and still have plenty left over for another go at the House of Games!"

speaker: Robin
text: "Thou must get thy boat ready to leave this place immediately. My lads and I shall get Constance and then we shall join thee. But wilt thou tell me where thy boat is located?"

speaker: Robin
text: You give Robin the location of your boat. He slowly breaks into an evil laugh. "I thank thee, friend. All that is left for us is to eliminate one remaining loose end. Now that we know where thy boat is we will collect more on our investment by simply killing thee and taking it."

speaker: Robin
text: "Thou hast lost thy stomach for our game, eh? If that is the case then my lads and I have no choice but to kill thee dead to protect our secret!"

speaker: Robin
text: "It has been a pleasure speaking with thee, <HONORIFIC>."

speaker: Battles
text: The man before you examines you with shifty eyes. He has a slightly crouched posture as if constantly poised to strike out at the world around him.

speaker: Battles
text: "What?" asks Battles.

speaker: Battles
text: "Battles. M'self, I be a stranger to New Magincia."

speaker: Battles
text: "I be hired as a bodyguard for Master Robin, as is me partner, Leavell. The pay be good."

speaker: Battles
text: "Robin be a high stakes gamblin' gent who makes his living inna casino at Buccaneer's Den."

speaker: Robin
text: "A living that would not have been anything near as profitable if not for thy good works, Battles."

speaker: Battles
text: "Thank yer, Milord."

speaker: Battles
text: "Gamblin' is how Robin makes his living. I do not think he has had a regular post in all of his life!"

speaker: Robin
text: "Why, I thank thee for the compliment, Battles!"

speaker: Battles
text: "The casino in Buccaneer's Den is called the House of Games and it the most fabulous place I have ever seen in me life. I shall never forget the first time Robin took me there. He walked away with a hundred gold pieces for less than an hour's work!"

speaker: Battles
text: "He's a lady's man, he is. But do not be thinkin' he cannot handle hissel' inna fight. T'would be yer last mistake."

speaker: Leavell
text: "I can near out wrestle thee, Battles, ye old dog!"

speaker: Battles
text: "Har! Har! Har! Har!"

speaker: Battles
text: "Why, I reckon Leavell has broken near as many hearts as I have made stop beating!"

speaker: Leavell
text: "So many!"

speaker: Battles
text: "Just the practice Leavell has had in fending off jealous husbands 'twould make any man a master combatant!"

speaker: Battles
text: "Strangers? "

speaker: Battles
text: "Thou must mean us!" Battles snorts loudly.

speaker: Battles
text: "We be looking to get off this boring rock, New Magincia, and back to Buccaneer's Den. If ye have a way to get us there, and away from these peasant knaves, Master Robin shall pay ye well."

speaker: Battles
text: "Canst thou imagine spending thine entire life here with nothing happening day after day after day? 'Tis enough to drive a man mad!"

speaker: Battles
text: "The people here are so lacking in education that they never even heard of gamblin' before! Never heard of gamblin'? That is what life is all about!"

speaker: Battles
text: "I sar a locket jus' like the one thou be describin' in the possession o' Master Robin. The last time I sar it was... Lessee... It was right before the three of us went drinkin' at the Modest Damsel."

speaker: Battles
text: "Be seein' ye."

speaker: Leavell
text: You see a young man balancing a dagger on the tip of his finger. He tries hard to ignore you.

speaker: Leavell
text: Leavell balances his dagger on his fingertip. In a blur of motion, he snatches it out of the air, pointing at you. He stares you in the eye.

speaker: Leavell
text: "I am Leavell."

speaker: Leavell
text: "Along with Battles, I am a bodyguard for Master Robin. If not for him, I would have landed in prison instead of in New Magincia."

speaker: Leavell
text: "I do not know what thou art talking about."

speaker: Leavell
text: "He has an eye like a hawk, and is quicker than a cat. 'Twould be wise of thee to pay him respect."

speaker: Battles
text: "Har! Har! Thou art too correct, Leavell!"

speaker: Leavell
text: "If Battles had not spotted that approaching storm we would have all been dead men for certain!"

speaker: Leavell
text: "It took a terrible toll on our boat, but if truth be told I have seen far worse."

speaker: Leavell
text: "I have seen Battles has reflexes faster than a snake."

speaker: Leavell
text: "Yes, I have done things to be put in prison for. But I am not ashamed of my life. I do not have to be held accountable to thee about it."

speaker: Leavell
text: "And while thou art about it, thou mayest show respect to me, too." Leavell says with a sneer.

speaker: Leavell
text: "He is a gambler by profession, who earns his winnings at the House of Games's tables on Buccaneer's Den."

speaker: Robin
text: "Soon we shall return and the money will pour like sweet wine once again, eh, Leavell?"

speaker: Leavell
text: "Gambling is what Robin does for money. But he spends so much time talking about Lord British that thou wouldst think he was royalty or something!"

speaker: Leavell
text: Suddenly Leavell gets an embarrassed look on his face and stops talking.

speaker: Robin
text: "Enough about that, Leavell!"

speaker: Leavell
text: "We ran into some misfortune the last time we were there. The Mister at the House of Games learned	of Master Robin's system and caused him to lose much of his gold."

speaker: Leavell
text: "He had devised a clever method of cheating at all the various games at the House of Chance. It had earned him several times his weight in gold coins, I am certain."

speaker: Leavell
text: "When Master Robin could not pay his debts, The Mister sent his legbreaker, Sintag, and his knaves after us. We had to leave on the first ship out of Buccaneer's Den. I do not know why he is called 'The Mister'."

speaker: Leavell
text: "Battles and myself are more than capable of taking care of Sintag..."

speaker: Battles
text: "Yeh, thou art bloody right we coulda handled him! We'd a slit him like a sheep! Har!"

speaker: Leavell
text: "But Gordy had hired a troupe of ruffians to chase after us. 'Tis a pity. I would have liked to teach him a lesson or two. In fact, one day I think I shall."

speaker: Leavell
text: "The ship we sailed on sank, leaving us stranded here. We were lucky to make it to New Magincia with our lives!"

speaker: Leavell
text: "The crew could not believe it! The vessel was almost new. It had sailed all the way from Minoc without a problem. In fact, that was the first storm that ship had ever encountered. None of the crew survived, poor buggers."

speaker: Leavell
text: "If thou wouldst have some way of getting us back to Buccaneer's Den, Master Robin would reward thee handsomely."

speaker: Leavell
text: "Peasant fools and sheep. The only thing worth a second look in this whole town is Constance."

speaker: Leavell
text: "Here, what is not one is the other. This place is so isolated that it is backward. What is worse, they prefer it this way!"

speaker: Leavell
text: "She doth put a spring in a man's step! We have our eye on her, we do!" Leavell quickly clears his throat and he looks away from you momentarily.

speaker: Leavell
text: "While I myself have seen no such locket, perhaps thou shouldst ask Master Robin about it."

speaker: Leavell
text: With that Leavell goes back to playing with his dagger.

speaker: Sam
text: You see a content-looking bearded man, with deep-set laugh lines in his face and gentle eyes.

speaker: Sam
text: "Hey there, how are things with thee?" says Sam.

speaker: Sam
text: "My name is Sam. I am the Flower Man. And what is thy name?"

speaker: Sam
text: "It is nice to meet thee."

speaker: Sam
text: "Fine. If thou dost wish to be the Avatar, I will not argue. Thou canst be the Avatar if thou dost want to be."

speaker: Sam
text: "The way I perceive it I do not really have a job. I sell flowers to the people of New Magincia. Although I am paid for it, it is something I enjoy doing very much. I wonder, does that still qualify as a job?" He scratches his chin thoughtfully.

speaker: Sam
text: "I grow all of the flowers that I sell in a greenhouse which is also mine home. I sell a lot of red roses but I have many varieties. If thou art interested in buying some, please say so!"

speaker: Sam
text: "I built my greenhouse by hand. When I am not selling flowers I am engaged in various studies of plants and nature there. I find it fascinating. As thou mayest have noticed, I prefer to grow them big!"

speaker: Sam
text: "Presently I am studying possible uses and applications of wheatgrass. One day soon I shall begin compiling my notes but it will require a long effort for there is much that I have learned. It is mostly to support my work that I operate my flower wagon."

speaker: Sam
text: "It is because of what I learn in my studies that I may grow my flowers to be so large and healthy."

speaker: Sam
text: "Actually my business does quite well and I do like the way my flowers brighten the whole place. But who really cares about business anyway, so why shouldst thou ask? Suffice it to say that life is sweet!"

speaker: Sam
text: "Thou hast enough money as long as thou dost have a place to live and can afford food, so I consider myself a wealthy man. I enjoy a good drink and round of song at the Modest Damsel nightly. I have a thriving business and stimulating work. I consider every resident of this island a good friend. I feel anger towards no one and do not desire anything more. I have never had reason to feel lonely, worried or bored. What else is there? Life is good!"

speaker: Sam
text: "There are many pretty ladies on this island and they are in the habit of receiving flowers from the gentlemen they meet. It would cause a dreadful embarrassment if thou didst not have any!"

speaker: Sam
text: "The gentlemen of this island have a peculiarity in their taste in women. They cannot refuse anything of a woman who wears flowers. If thou dost not wear any they will simply ignore thee!"

speaker: Sam
text: "Surely thou dost wish to purchase some?"

speaker: Sam
text: "A bouquet costs 12 gold. Art thou still interested?"

speaker: Sam
text: "The bouquet is thine!"

speaker: Sam
text: "Thine hands are too full to take the bouquet!"

speaker: Sam
text: "Thou dost not have the money to buy flowers. But take heart, whenever thou canst afford them, I shall still be selling them."

speaker: Sam
text: "Perhaps next time, <HONORIFIC>," he responds, smiling.

speaker: Sam
text: "Perhaps another time then."

speaker: Sam
text: "I am afraid that my shop is now closed, but if thou wilt return during business hours, I shall provide the solution to thine apparent floral emergency."

speaker: Sam
text: "There are three strangers on this island that have washed ashore in a shipwreck. Perhaps thou shalt meet them."

speaker: Sam
text: "Yes, I saw Henry walking past my shop with that locket looking for Constance. It must have been shortly after he received it from Katrina. I remember it because I gave him a flower to give to Constance. Poor fellow, by the time he found her it was all he had to give her."

speaker: Sam
text: "Why, he sounds like one of those three strangers! I have met him. He talked as if he wanted to buy some flowers but he just walked away. Later I noticed a bouquet of flowers was missing from my wagon. The scoundrel must have pilfered them!"

speaker: Sam
text: "He must be one of those shipwrecked visitors we have on our island. Yes, when the three of them came up to my wagon he gave me a stare that sent a chill through my blood. I did my best to ignore him. I absolutely abhor violence."

speaker: Sam
text: "So that is the name of one of our uninvited guests! When the three of them came to my wagon earlier, he was very friendly while talking to me, but I saw through him. He mentioned noticing Constance, but the others gestured for him to be quiet."

speaker: Sam
text: "I was not born here. I came here as a young man. My father was a nobleman who was more interested in my counting gold than devoting myself to my studies. For a time I travelled the world until I landed here. It is a special place unlike any other in all of Britannia. So while thou art here please help us take good care of it."

speaker: Sam
text: "Enjoy thy life, friend."

speaker: Gorn
text: You see a familiar face, a stern-looking bearded warrior whom you have met on one of your previous journeys to Britannia.

speaker: Gorn
text: "Ho, Avatar!" says Gorn. "Thou dost vish to speak mit me?"

speaker: Gorn
text: "De voice ov Brom has told me not to trust thee, Avatar," says Gorn. "I tought dat ve vere friends and I do not vish to cause thee harm. But I varn thee, do not speak mit me anymore!"

speaker: Gorn
text: The warrior's eyes narrow. "I am Gorn, as if thou didst not remember! It is good to see thee again." He laughs and slaps you on the shoulder.

speaker: Gorn
text: "My job is a never-ending qvest of high adventure. Ever since I vas a child und vas taken from mine homeland of Balema, I haf spent my life in search of heroic deeds to perform."

speaker: Gorn
text: "Yah, Balema is vere I vas born. I vas a child dere. It is a vonderland ov snow-covered mountains und dark forests. It vas not an easy life, but it vas a place dat made young boys into strong heroic men. Dat vas long before I came to Britannia."

speaker: Gorn
text: "Yah! I came to Britannia t'rough vone ov de Moongates, de same as thee. Dat vas many, many years ago."

speaker: Gorn
text: "I perform heroic deeds in honor ov Brom. Everyting I do is in service to him."

speaker: Gorn
text: "He is my master, und de master ov all ov de people ov Balema. Brom is all powerful und if I am strong he vill aid me. Sometimes I hear de voice ov Brom inside ov mine head."

speaker: Gorn
text: "Ya! Brom he is my master. If he vishes me to do someting, I must do it! If he does not vant me to do someting, I must not do it!"

speaker: Gorn
text: "Ya! Only recently I haf begun to hear his voice in mine head. His voice tells me vat to do! As I came tovard dis cave de voice ov Brom became clearer."

speaker: Gorn
text: "Vhen I first heard de voice ov Brom, he told me dat I should follow him. But how does one follow de voice ov someone dat thou cannot see vhen de voice is coming from inside ov thine head?"

speaker: Gorn
text: "Dis vas very, very difficult for me but after a vhile I vas able to figure out how to do it. Vhen I came nearer to da camp surrounding dis cave da voice vould get louder. Vhen I vould move avay de voice vould be qvieter."

speaker: Gorn
text: "It vas very simple for a trained varrior like myself to slip into de camp ov dose who are holding Brom prisoner. Dey posed no threat vatsoever. So dat means dat de danger must be vaiting down here. But I cannot find it!"

speaker: Gorn
text: "I can see by dat medallion thou dost vear dat thou hast snuck into dis place by disguising thyself as vone of dem. Very clever, Avatar!"

speaker: Iolo
text: Iolo whispers to you, "This fellow is quite sharp, is he not?"

speaker: Gorn
text: "Zo far de only danger I haf found down here has been a female fighter. She vas beautiful. Vhen I vent to talk to her she hit me over de head mit her svord. Vhen I voke up she vas gone. I bet she tought she had killed me but mine head is harder dan dat. I vas not even vounded."

speaker: Shamino
text: Shamino whispers to you. "Luckily, Gorn was hit in the one spot where he has no feeling whatsoever -- his head!"

speaker: Gorn
text: "Hey, vhat are you vhispering about over dere?"

speaker: Shamino
text: "Oh, nothing. Nothing at all."

speaker: Gorn
text: "I know dat Brom is somevhere down in dis cave, und I vill not leave dis place until I find him!"

speaker: Gorn
text: "The nearer I haf come to dis cave, the more times I haf been hearing de voice ov Brom. But lately he has been saying tings to me dat are very, very strange!"

speaker: Gorn
text: "De first strange ting dat he says to me is "Strive For Unity". I say, yah, dat is vhy I am performing mine heroic deeds. Den Brom says someting else dat is strange."

speaker: Gorn
text: "Next de voice ov Brom says to me "Trust My Brothers". Dis is strange because all ov my brothers are back in Balema, und I vould never trust dem anyvays. Dey vere all bigger den me and vere alvays beating me. But even dat vas not as strange as da next strange ting."

speaker: Gorn
text: "De voice ov Brom tells me dat "Worldliness Receives Avard". I haf been tinking about dat von for a long time und I still haf not figured it out. But I vill not give up until I find Brom."

speaker: Dupre
text: "A mysterious voice speaking inside someone's head, suggesting the philosophy of The Fellowship. Does this sound familiar, <PLAYER_NAME>?"

speaker: Gorn
text: "Wouldst thou help me find Brom?"

speaker: Gorn
text: Gorn seems distracted for a moment. He places his hand to his ear as if he is listening to something. He looks back at you and there is a shocked look on his face. "I haf just heard de voice ov Brom and he has told me not to trust thee! Go avay from me, Avatar! I tought dat thou vert my friend! I do not vish to speak vith thee anymore!"

speaker: Gorn
text: Gorn has a confused look on his face. "Vhy vill thou not help me find Brom? Dost thou tink dat dis is all some kind ov trick, or should I go on looking for Brom by myself?"

speaker: Gorn
text: "If dat is how thou vants it. Den I shall go on searching for Brom mit no vone else but myself. Good luck in vhatever qvest thou art on, Avatar. Farewell to thee!"

speaker: Gorn
text: Gorn seems distracted for a moment. He puts his hand to his ear as if he is listening to something. He looks back at you with a shocked expression on his face. "I haf just heard de voice ov Brom and he says dat I should not trust thee! I tought dat thou vert my friend, Avatar! Go avay! I do not vish to speak vith thee again!"

speaker: Gorn
text: "Dat is de name ov de female fighter who has been guarding dis place. I haf fought her vonce already. She is a strong fighter! I haf to find her so I can make her to tell me vhere is Brom!"

speaker: Gorn
text: "Until ve meet again, Avatar."

speaker: Markham
text: This undead fellow looks through you. Though he is obviously aware of his surroundings, you are quite sure that he doesn't even see you.

speaker: Markham
text: You attempt to start a conversation with the portly ghost, but he seems distanced from you and everything else.

speaker: Markham
text: The heavy-set ghost looks a bit shaken and his speech is a little slurred as he says, "Excuse me, yer honor. But I got me a splittin' headache. Do ya mind if we continue this little chat later?"

speaker: Markham
text: He begins to rub his temples with both hands.

speaker: Markham
text: "Oh, hello there, lady Rowena. 'Tis good to see ye again. It brings a ray o' sunshine into this old man's heart ta see yer beauteous face," he says, smiling.

speaker: Rowena
text: She curtsies delicately and smiles back.

speaker: Rowena
text: "Hello, Markham. It is good, indeed, to see that none of this horrible business can keep thee from giving a lady a compliment."

speaker: Markham
text: "Oh, uh, hello there Mayor. I thought ye were sequestered in the Town Hall. Well, uh, it's good ta see ya again."

speaker: Forsythe
text: "Yes, well, it is good to see thee again, too."

speaker: Markham
text: The corpulent, undead barkeep greets you with a wide, gruesome smile. "Come, stranger. Have a seat near old Markham and tell me o' yer travels. I don't often get visitors in here anymore."

speaker: Markham
text: Markham hails you and drinks down a tankard of the house spirits. "Welcome, my friend. Sit with me a while and enliven my eternity with yer wondrous wit." He smiles in that charming way that only the half-rotted can.

speaker: Markham
text: The heavy-set zombie wipes his mouth off on the back of his hand. "I be Markham. Markham o' the Keg." He pats the large keg of wine he carries.

speaker: Paulette
text: The lovely <VAR> strolls over and pats Markham's rather large belly. "Yes, he's Markham of the Keg, all right." She smiles sweetly down at the older man.

speaker: Markham
text: "That's enough of that!" Markham smacks the pretty young woman on her ghostly posterior.

speaker: Markham
text: "Make yerself useful and fetch me a haunch o' venison." She turns away, giggling. He looks at you with a mirthful expression, "I just don't know what I'm goin' ta do with that girl."

speaker: Markham
text: "Why, I run this fine establishment, the Keg O' Spirits." For a moment he becomes serious. "This place once drew folk from all across Britannia, gargoyle and human alike. Until the fire, that is."

speaker: Markham
text: He looks uncomfortable, "Caine blew the town to the four winds, and now we're all trapped here, slaves of that bastard Horance." Tiny blue flames appear in the pupils of his glazed eyes, then go out as he regains his composure.

speaker: Quenton
text: "Please, Markham. Have a little pity for Caine. He was trying to create something to save the town when he made his fatal mistake." The pale ghost looks deeply troubled.

speaker: Markham
text: "Oh, I suppose <VAR> he was tryin' ta help us when he called the proverbial fires o' Hell down on us. It just rankles me to have died in my prime." His roguish smile once again lightens his ghostly visage.

speaker: Markham
text: A look of disgust comes to his disfigured features. "That tortured soul haunts the crater made by his foolish mistake. I wouldn't go near him though, he's a bit daft, ya know." He refills his mug from the cask at his side and swigs down most of the wine in one swallow.

speaker: Markham
text: "That's just the name the rest of us in Skara Brae call him -- the Tortured One," he grins, embarrassed.

speaker: Markham
text: "That's the name o' the island yer on." He shakes his head.

speaker: Markham
text: "For all the years I've been in Skara Brae, he's been a raving lunatic. What with all o' them silly rhymes and his crazy laughter."

speaker: Markham
text: "Then one night, we all hears thunder when there isn't a cloud in the starry sky, and I seem to recall a full moon..." He gets a thoughtful look on his face. "But as I was sayin', there was this thunder, then this deep, dark laughter coming from the tower on the northern point -- Horance's Dark Tower." After this he falls silent for a moment.

speaker: Quenton
text: The pale ghost moves forward and whispers, "I was already living in the half world of the dead when these events took place, and ever since, I've felt a strange pull coming from the tower."

speaker: Markham
text: After a brief swig, he continues, "Then, even worse... I'm out checkin' on the cows when I hears a sound like moanin'. It's off to the east, so I look that way, into the graveyard y'know, and what do I see?"

speaker: Markham
text: "I'll tell ya what I seen. The graves, rippin' open like the people in 'em got a place to go." Eyes wide, he tips back another sip.

speaker: Markham
text: He truly looks sad as he says, "This place was once my pride and joy. The Keg was known all 'round Britannia, and a few other places, too. Well, now it don't look like too much, but in it's heyday, it saw the likes of nobles, knights, minstrels, and merchants. And o' course, a bit o' riff raff to be sure." He winks at you. His spirit seems indomitable.

speaker: Markham
text: You relate the need for a sacrifice to enter the Well of Souls. Afterwards, Markham seems to think long and hard.

speaker: Markham
text: "So, yer wantin' me to go mad as a March hare, an' jump right into this... Well O' Souls?" He looks at you incredulously.

speaker: Markham
text: "Listen now. I haven't had courage like that since I were a young lad. Since then I got some sense, too. You'll have to look elsewhere fer yer sacrifice."

speaker: Markham
text: "All right, now. I already told ya. I ain't interested." He looks a little put out by your persistence.

speaker: Markham
text: "Oh, are ya leavin' then? Well, ya take care now. And watch out for those walkin' dead. Some o' them aren't too happy about their state, and none too picky about who they complain to, neither."

speaker: Horance
text: You attempt to speak to the undead creature, but it does not, or cannot, respond.

speaker: Horance
text: The Liche practically glows, power coursing visibly through its undead veins.

speaker: Horance
text: You step forward to confront this vile-looking creature and he slowly turns to face you. As his intense gaze locks onto your form, you almost wish you hadn't been so bold.

speaker: Horance
text: "<PLAYER_NAME>." A sardonic expression comes to his undead features. "How may I help thee?" You get the distinct impression that help is the last thing you'll get from the Liche.

speaker: Shamino
text: Shamino steps near you and speaks in a whispered tone.

speaker: Shamino
text: "Do not trust this one, <HONORIFIC>. Methinks he'll cause naught but evil."

speaker: Iolo
text: Iolo steps near you and speaks in a whispered tone.

speaker: Iolo
text: "Do not trust this one, <HONORIFIC>. Methinks he'll cause naught but evil."

speaker: Spark
text: "Uh, <HONORIFIC>? I am ready to go now," he says to you, cowering from the undead creature.

speaker: Horance
text: The Liche performs something akin to a smile and speaks with a sarcastic flair.

speaker: Horance
text: "Ah, the wondrous Avatar has returned. What have I done to deserve such an honor?" The word "honor" sours on this creature's tongue.

speaker: Horance
text: The Liche's dry features take on a haughty appearance. "Thou mayest call me Lord Horance. It would only be prudent, as I shall one day rule all of Britannia."

speaker: Horance
text: "Surprised, Avatar? Come now. Surely thou dost not think that Lord British will stand in my way. I know how to deal with his ilk."

speaker: Horance
text: "Ah, it is good to hear such an obeisance from the Avatar. Perhaps thou wilt have a place in my New Order." The Liche looks at you with an expression somewhere between malice and humor.

speaker: Horance
text: "Why, what else wouldst thou call it? Surely thou art truly humbled by my `majestic' presence."

speaker: Horance
text: An expression of zeal lights the dead face of the Liche.

speaker: Horance
text: "Yes, <PLAYER_NAME>. The dead will rule! I will be their leader and thou canst become an Avatar... to ME!"

speaker: Horance
text: "Why, <PLAYER_NAME>. I thought that was understood. It will be my pleasure to help thee enter the realm of the dead."

speaker: Horance
text: "Yes, I thought thou wouldst see the wisdom of my vision." He looks at you like a cat toying with a mouse.

speaker: Horance
text: `Evil' is a mild word for the sneer that appears on the Liche's cracked lips. "It has recently come to my attention that a certain ore found in the Britannian surface can, if fashioned properly, become the bane of the vaunted Lord British."

speaker: Horance
text: "I know this ore and have used it	before for other purposes. I will use it once again to destroy that so-called Lord."

speaker: Horance
text: He gestures at the walls of the tower. "How else didst thou expect my tower to withstand the ravaging effect the ether is having	on my magic?"

speaker: Horance
text: He gestures at the walls of the tower. "It served as an effective barrier against the ravaging effects of the disrupted ether."

speaker: Horance
text: A harsh cackle escapes his dry throat. "I am the illustrious Lord of the Dead, soon to be Lord of all Britannia. Dost thou have any idea of the number of dead people and creatures there are? I thought not."

speaker: Horance
text: "The dead of the ages are mine to summon and control. The graves of beloved ancestors will spew forth their contents into an army. A special treat for the living, mine undead monsters will be. Imagine a skeletal dragon that cannot be killed. Consider a cabal of everliving mages eternally enthralled to me."

speaker: Horance
text: "And the most beautiful part of my plot is that, as the living die in these battles, and they will die, they will swell the ranks of the undead host. I will rule supreme -- a world of the dead!" A terrifying glimpse of his sick and twisted future causes you to shiver	ever so slightly.

speaker: Horance
text: "And I will have a queen, the lovely Rowena."

speaker: Rowena
text: "Yes, my Lord. I must be the happiest Lady in all the land." Her gaze never wanders from the horrid face of the Liche.

speaker: Horance
text: "Is she not the most beautiful lady thou hast seen? "

speaker: Horance
text: "She shall have eternal beauty at my side, and we shall rule together."

speaker: Horance
text: "She is the most beautiful lady I have been witness to. She shall have eternal beauty at my side, and we shall rule together." After hearing him speak of his plans for the future, you find this a very unlikely statement.

speaker: Horance
text: "Now, now, Avatar, that would be revealing. Then I would have no secret from thee, would I?"

speaker: Horance
text: "It is truly sad to see thee go." He says with a sardonic smile.

speaker: Dupre
text: "Yeah, right."

speaker: Iolo
text: "Yeah, right."

speaker: Horance
text: "Feel free to explore mine humble abode. Though, have a care. My guardians are none too intelligent and will most likely assault anything living." He smiles with his death's head grin.

speaker: Trent
text: Trent glares, giving his eyes an intensity that leaves no doubt in your mind about his attitude. "If I thought that thou wert going to run off at a moment's notice I'd not have asked thee to help me free my love."

speaker: Trent
text: "Now please, take the cage and go to	Mordra. She will instruct thee in its use." His manner smoothes, "I have placed mine only chance at reunion with Rowena in thy capable hands."

speaker: Trent
text: "Please, do not disturb me whilst I build this cage, for my thoughts are on nothing but the destruction of that foul Horance!" He continues the construction of the Soul Cage.

speaker: Trent
text: The large, angry-looking ghost ignores your presence and continues to hammer on a strange iron cage.

speaker: Trent
text: The large, angry-looking ghost ignores your presence, while obviously searching for some item.

speaker: Trent
text: You see in the fire of the ghostly forge a large, heavily-muscled ghost with a full beard and mustache. He does not notice your approach.

speaker: Trent
text: Trent continues his work on the strangely-shaped iron cage.

speaker: Trent
text: Trent seems to be searching for something.

speaker: Trent
text: A deep furrow, accentuated by thick eyebrows, creases the ghost's weary brow. He doesn't look away from his work. "I am Trent. Now, please, leave me to my work."

speaker: Trent
text: He continues hammering on a strangely-shaped iron cage.

speaker: Trent
text: "I cannot find the iron cage!" he shouts. "Some fool must have taken it! When I find out who did it and where it is, that fool will sorely regret having removed it from my shop!"

speaker: Trent
text: "Art thou blind! Canst thou not see that I am a smith?" He doesn't seem the sort for idle conversation.

speaker: Trent
text: Anger radiates from the large ghost in almost tangible waves. He looks up from the cage and you see that the light of fire isn't coming from the forge, it's coming from his eyes. "I build this cage to destroy that bastard, Horance, who took my wife from me."

speaker: Trent
text: For a moment, you think he is going to strike out at you, then he unclenches his fists with a heavy sigh and returns to his work.

speaker: Trent
text: His whole body tenses as you speak.

speaker: Trent
text: "Horance..." The word comes out like a curse. "I will see his foul spirit burn before mine eyes. Then I will laugh as he cries out pitifully for mercy." For some reason you think that you'd rather avoid hearing that laugh.

speaker: Trent
text: One hot tear slips from the ghost's eye and falls on a heated piece of the iron cage. It sizzles, and then is gone.

speaker: Trent
text: "Rowena was my life, mine only joy in this world." His voice is almost tender, but then he returns to his guttural tones. "He killed her and took that joy from me. Now I am only a hollow shell of a man, burning with hatred."

speaker: Trent
text: "In an attempt to steal her away from my side, the evil fiend sent his undead minions to bring her to the dark tower. The mindless creatures slew her as she struggled." The ghost turns to you in anguish, "I could do nought to save her... the sheer numbers of skeletal warriors bore me to the ground as she was bereft of life."

speaker: Trent
text: Insane determination flickers in the big ghost's eyes, "For this I will never forgive and never forget."

speaker: Trent
text: He holds up one hand as you say the name of his late wife. "Please, do not say that name. It takes from me	a little of mine Hatred, which is all I have now. Wouldst thou rob me of the one thing that keeps me alive?" It would seem that he is unaware of the fact that he is, indeed, no longer alive. An odd expression crosses his face.

speaker: Trent
text: "I gave her a music box for our wedding, and now it is all I have left to remember her by." His tone changes.

speaker: Trent
text: "Do thou see what thou hast done?! I cannot work when I think of her!" He returns to his work with renewed passion.

speaker: Trent
text: You notice the music box he spoke of sitting nearby.

speaker: Trent
text: You hold out the ring to Trent. At first he ignores you. Then, recognizing the ring, he takes it from you and holds it before him. Something in him snaps and his huge frame slumps forward.

speaker: Trent
text: You let the ghost cry for a while, and when he finishes, you see a remarkable change in his appearance.

speaker: Trent
text: The flames that once burned in his eyes are now gone, replaced by a deep shade of blue. He looks like a new man, or rather, ghost as it were.

speaker: Trent
text: "Forgive my behavior, <HONORIFIC>. I know not what came over me. I remember flames, but they burned no hotter than mine own Hatred." He looks pained at the memory.

speaker: Trent
text: "Thou hast seen her? Thou hast seen Rowena? And she still cares for me. Well, all the more reason to finish this Soul Cage. We must free her from Horance's vile sorcery."

speaker: Trent
text: If he heard you, he ignores the fact as you take your leave. You truly feel pity for this deeply wounded spirit.

speaker: Mordra
text: The old, ghostly woman hums the tune to an ancient ballad and smiles up at you. This old woman brings to mind every grandmother you've ever seen.

speaker: Mordra
text: Apparently she is not entirely oblivious to your presence. However, when you speak to her, it seems as if your words fall on deaf ears. She looks puzzled for a moment, then moves her arms in magical passes. You recognize the words to be a variant of the Seance spell.

speaker: Mordra
text: The old, ghostly woman looks very strange. Her eyes are open, but she doesn't seem to be awake, or at least not aware of her surroundings.

speaker: Mordra
text: "I am sorry, <HONORIFIC>. Do not take offense, but I must rest before we speak further. I thank thee for thy patience, young one." She looks very weary as she turns away.

speaker: Mordra
text: "Hello, <HONORIFIC>. Thou mayest call me Mistress Mordra." She peers at you closely.

speaker: Mordra
text: "And thou must be <PLAYER_NAME>, the Avatar." She looks you over thoroughly.

speaker: Mordra
text: "Greetings once again, <PLAYER_NAME>."

speaker: Mordra
text: She lifts up her arms and in one of them you see an ankh. Words which you vaguely recognize flow from her lips and the ankh glows brightly. She stops chanting and the ankh dims. After her analysis of your condition is complete, "Ah, it is good to see that the world has been treating thee well. How may I serve thee, 'O Virtuous One?"

speaker: Mordra
text: She smiles at you. "Thou art quite forgetful, <PLAYER_NAME>. As I have told thee, I am known as Mordra."

speaker: Mordra
text: "I was the healer of this town before the fire erupted that shattered the lives of those here. I also dabbled in secret magical arts for a while." She winks at you slyly.

speaker: Mordra
text: "If I tell thee, thou must be sure to get them right. Otherwise, what happened when I told that blasted mayor will happen again. And, while we here in Skara Brae have no more lives to lose, thou hast quite a valuable one! "

speaker: Mordra
text: "The ingredients necessary for the concoction to dissolve the liche are a potion of invisibility, a dose of a potion of curing, and one	vial of the essence of mandrake -- I have one set aside somewhere in mine house. Remember, only -one- vial of the mandrake!"

speaker: Mordra
text: "The Soul Cage must be empowered with the might of the dead. The way to accomplish this is to go to the back of the Dark Tower, to the Well of Souls. Thou must lower the cage into the well, where the souls trapped there will lose a little of themselves to imbue it with the required power."

speaker: Mordra
text: "I know this sounds harsh, but it is a necessary evil if thou wouldst see them freed." She looks at you sharply.

speaker: Mordra
text: "The next step is to wait until midnight, then clap the cage upon the recumbent form of the Liche. This is the period of time in which he drains the spirits of the townsfolk in his Black Service."

speaker: Mordra
text: After a brief moment, she continues. "Finally, thou must pour a magical formula upon the Liche within the cage. This formula is the same substance that destroyed the town."

speaker: Mordra
text: "Do be careful when procuring it from the alchemist, Caine."

speaker: Mordra
text: "Thou must have Caine's assistance in creating the formula, but I can give thee the ingredients."

speaker: Mordra
text: "The Dark Tower lies on the northwestern point of Skara Brae. There is something odd about its construction, for I find it very hard to penetrate with my magical senses."

speaker: Mordra
text: "Within it," she says, "thou wilt find the Well of Souls."

speaker: Mordra
text: "The Well of Souls is a powerful artifact, located beneath the Dark Tower, from which the Liche draws his power. The souls of the dead are incarcerated there, doomed to the torment of Horance's all-consuming appetite." An expression of pain shows in her features.

speaker: Mordra
text: Angrily, Mordra says, "Each night, at the stroke of midnight, the spirits of Skara Brae travel to the Dark Tower and are used to infuse Horance with power to continue his dark existence. None of the others are aware when this happens, but I feel it without being able to stop myself."

speaker: Mordra
text: "Even though the Liche is gone, we are still drawn to the place of his Black Service. He must have bound us with a geas and tied it to the power of the Well of Souls. Oh, what a crafty villain he was." Grudging respect for a skilled mage is mixed with disgust in Mordra's expression.

speaker: Mordra
text: "Wouldst thou like to know about the townsfolk of Skara Brae?"

speaker: Mordra
text: "I might have some new information on my fellow townsfolk that could be of use to thee," she says, adding a smile.

speaker: Mordra
text: "Very well, <HONORIFIC>. What wouldst thou care to know about?"

speaker: Mordra
text: "'Twas the doom of this town, although I place no blame upon the alchemist, Caine. For I was the one who told him the recipe that I am sure will rid us of Horance the Liche."

speaker: Mordra
text: "'Twas but a simple mixture of a few ingredients. It should have worked." Her eyes narrow.

speaker: Mordra
text: "I expect that mayor of ours, Forsythe, fouled things up!"

speaker: Mordra
text: "That man is a bumbling idiot. It is his fault that the island was destroyed. I gave him the exact portions of the reagents to be used in the magical formula, and he paraphrased it to the alchemist, Caine. By the size of the fire, I am sure he misquoted the amount of mandrake root by	tenfold. Damn that foolish man!"

speaker: Mordra
text: Her brow creases and you	can see that this is a subject that she likes to avoid.

speaker: Mordra
text: "Now those who reside here call him `the Tortured One.' That is because he is in eternal pain, caused by searing flames licking at his flesh."

speaker: Mordra
text: "The pain is imagined, but to him, 'tis as real as thou or I... or, at least, as real as	thou art!"

speaker: Mordra
text: Her eyes twinkle mischievously. "If I were to reveal them to thee, they wouldn't be secret any longer, now would they?"

speaker: Mordra
text: She smiles at first, then turns serious. "I have tied my spirit to powers beyond the realm of this mortal world. Were I to enter the Well of Souls, this entire island and a good bit of the mainland would be destroyed in a magical discharge. Wouldst thou lose the town of Skara Brae for all eternity?"

speaker: Mordra
text: "Thou knowest full well that I cannot. If thou wouldst	see mass destruction, thou shalt have to cause it thyself." She turns away quickly for a woman of her age.

speaker: Mordra
text: "Goodbye, young <PLAYER_NAME>. Take care of thyself, but should ill befall thee, I hope that thou wilt come back here and let me minister to thine ailments." She smiles kindly as you leave.

speaker: Rowena
text: The beautiful ghost looks through you with a slack look. Nothing	you do seems to attract her attention.

speaker: Rowena
text: You see a ghostly lady wearing a long, black gown. Something is a bit strange about the way she looks, but you can't quite place it. After a pause, she says, "Greetings, <HONORIFIC>. I am Rowena, lady of this wondrous tower." She gestures around the room, indicating the moldering walls and cobwebbed rafters.

speaker: Rowena
text: Rowena smiles in an abstract manner as you approach. "Ah, thou hast returned, <HONORIFIC>. How may the lady of the tower be of assistance to thee?"

speaker: Rowena
text: "I am called... Rowena"

speaker: Rowena
text: She stares blankly for a second, then, as if on cue, "I am the Mistress of the Tower. I tend to my Lord Horance's needs and keep our place looking respectable." It would appear that she's been falling behind in the latter duty.

speaker: Rowena
text: After a moment, "This is a lovely tower, dost thou not agree?" Before you can answer, she continues.

speaker: Rowena
text: "Dost thou see the lovely rays of light playing across the flagstones of the floor? Water sparkles in the fountain. This is truly a beautiful place in which to live." Her eyes fix upon the floor.

speaker: Rowena
text: She blinks once, then, "Horance... What a wonderful name. He found me lost and lonely and brought me here to be a lady. Is he not truly the most magnificent of Lords?"

speaker: Rowena
text: She pauses. "Goodbye, <HONORIFIC>. I hope thou hast enjoyed thy visit to our glorious tower. Please, return whenever thou wishest." You feel as if you've been speaking to a statue.

speaker: Paulette
text: The lovely apparition goes about her tasks without offering any response.

speaker: Paulette
text: The lovely barmaid stares off into oblivion, completely unaware of her location and position.

speaker: Paulette
text: The pretty barmaid looks as if she's about to fall over for a moment, then quickly rights herself. "Oh, I feel a bit... faint." She turns away, distracted.

speaker: Paulette
text: "Go away! Thou art cruel and mean-hearted." She turns away, but not before you see the tears in her eyes.

speaker: Paulette
text: Paulette perks up as she sees Rowena.

speaker: Paulette
text: "Hello, milady. 'Tis good to see thee again. How art thou?"

speaker: Rowena
text: "I am fine, Paulette. I thank thee for thy concern."

speaker: Paulette
text: "'Tis good news indeed, milady."

speaker: Paulette
text: "Hello, Mayor. It has been quite a while since we've seen thee in our tavern. There was a time, I remember, when we couldn't keep thee away."

speaker: Forsythe
text: The mayor becomes quickly embarrassed as he tries to quiet the rather friendly Paulette.

speaker: Forsythe
text: "I, er, used to be a wine connoisseur of sorts," he says to you.

speaker: Paulette
text: "'Tis not all thou wert a connoisseur of," adds Paulette, eyes twinkling. "I seem to remember thou had quite a taste for redheads."

speaker: Paulette
text: You see a pretty, ghostly girl with long black hair. "Hello, <HONORIFIC>. I am called Paulette. How may I help thee?"

speaker: Paulette
text: Standing before you, with a hand on her hip, is a lovely, young woman with long black hair. "Ooooh... Thou art a big one, <HONORIFIC>." She traces the line of your bicep.

speaker: Paulette
text: "I'd wager thou couldst lift me over thine head." She smiles enticingly. However, you doubt that you could even touch her in her ghostly state.

speaker: Paulette
text: "Thou mayest call me Paulette, gorgeous. What can I do for thee?" She winks at you.

speaker: Paulette
text: "Yes, <HONORIFIC>?", she asks sweetly.

speaker: Paulette
text: Paulette turns to face you and smiles coquettishly, "I had thought that thou might return." Her eyes sparkle up at you mischievously.

speaker: Paulette
text: "Why, <HONORIFIC>, hast thou forgotten already? I am Paulette."

speaker: Paulette
text: "Well, <HONORIFIC>, before the fire," she shudders, "I used to be the barmaid here."

speaker: Paulette
text: "Well, <HONORIFIC>. I used to clean tables here..." As she says this, she bends over and pretends to wipe a table clean. You notice how low the cut of her bodice really is.

speaker: Paulette
text: "...and serve people, like thyself. Of course, none so handsome." Her ghostly features blush prettily.

speaker: Paulette
text: "But that was before," she shudders, "the fire."

speaker: Paulette
text: "Thou dost wish to purchase something?"

speaker: Paulette
text: "I am sorry, <HONORIFIC>," she giggles, "but all we serve here are... spirits!"

speaker: Markham
text: "That's a good one, wench," laughs the portly ghost.

speaker: Paulette
text: "Very well, <HONORIFIC>."

speaker: Paulette
text: She appears puzzled for an instant, but then she nods her head.

speaker: Paulette
text: "Oh, thou must be referring to Caine. He was the alchemist who was responsible for the fire."

speaker: Paulette
text: "Oh, yes. It was horrible! The tavern caught on fire. I ran to my room, hoping to escape the flames. But then I started coughing. I couldn't breathe." Her chest rises and falls quickly as if she's reliving the experience.

speaker: Paulette
text: "Finally, I could take it no longer." She brings the back of her hand to her forehead, dramatically. "I fainted. Then I was here again, just like thou dost see me now." Her smile is like that of a child.

speaker: Paulette
text: "Yes, 'twas quite odd. When I awoke, it was as if I had never left when the fire began. In fact, were it not for the scorch marks everywhere, I would doubt the fire ever happened."

speaker: Paulette
text: "Why, 'tis called the Keg O' Spirits. That's a fine name for a tavern, dost thou not agree?" She smiles <VAR>.

speaker: Paulette
text: "Thou wantest me to... to jump in a well?" Her eyes widen with astonishment.

speaker: Paulette
text: "Well, thou canst go jump in a lake!" She crosses her arms on her buxom chest and turns away from you angrily.

speaker: Paulette
text: She recovers her composure, "Oh. For a moment there, I thought that thou wouldst have me be thy... sacrifice."

speaker: Paulette
text: "Please, just leave me alone!" she looks as if she's about to cry.

speaker: Paulette
text: "Goodbye, <HONORIFIC>." The pretty ghost turns away.

speaker: Paulette
text: Paulette rushes up to you as you say goodbye and gives you a little kiss on the cheek. She backs away slowly, "Farewell, handsome."

speaker: Quenton
text: The pale ghost seems to see you but cannot speak to you for some reason. In frustration the ghost turns away.

speaker: Quenton
text: As you start to speak to the pale ghost, you notice that he seems to be looking through you, as if you don't exist at all. You wave your hand in front of his face, but there is no response.

speaker: Quenton
text: "Please, please. I... cannot speak with thee right now. I am not sure what has come over me. Please forgive me, <HONORIFIC>." The wan ghost looks more pale than usual.

speaker: Rowena
text: "Hello, Quenton. I hope thou art doing well." Rowena gives the pale ghost a winning smile.

speaker: Quenton
text: "Yes, milady. I am doing as well as can be expected. It gladdens mine heart to see that thou art once again free. Hast thou been to see Trent yet?"

speaker: Rowena
text: "Alas, no. This kind person is taking me to him." She indicates you.

speaker: Quenton
text: "These are glad tidings, for he misses thee so."

speaker: Forsythe
text: "Well met, Quenton." The Mayor's mustache spreads as he smiles.

speaker: Quenton
text: "Hello, Mayor. How dost thou fare, milord?"

speaker: Forsythe
text: Forsythe seems taken aback by Quenton's sincere sounding query. "Why, I fare well, Quenton. I thank thee for thy concern."

speaker: Quenton
text: He smiles in acknowledgement of the Mayor's thanks.

speaker: Quenton
text: The pale-looking ghost turns in your direction and gives you a wan smile. "Hello, could it be that we have met somewhere before, <HONORIFIC>?" You see recognition in his eyes, then it fades.

speaker: Quenton
text: "Forgive me." He shakes his head, then smiles. "I am the shade of Quenton."

speaker: Quenton
text: Quenton turns in your direction. "Greetings, <HONORIFIC>. Come, take rest from thy travels and sit a while with me. I am but a simple shade, but I may have information useful to thee."

speaker: Quenton
text: "I am called Quenton, <HONORIFIC>."

speaker: Quenton
text: He smiles at your question, "I once roamed the sea, for days at a time, gathering mine harvest of fish."

speaker: Quenton
text: "I have been around for many, many years. And," he smiles, "I have seen many, many things in that time."

speaker: Quenton
text: "Caine? He was an alchemist here on Skara Brae. Now he spends his days in eternal pain caused by his guilt from causing the fire that destroyed this town."

speaker: Quenton
text: "My story is a long and a sad one. I hope thou hast some time." He appears thoughtful for a moment, and then begins.

speaker: Quenton
text: ["When I was a young man, I met a lovely woman by the name of Gwen. I made her my wife, and we lived for a time, happy and carefree. She brought a light into the world and we called her Marney, which means the cool breeze after a storm." He smiles to himself at some memory, then continues with a furrowed brow.

speaker: Quenton
text: "Then, one day, my wife was taken from me. I know not where, or by whom, save that they were evil men. Soon after, my sweet Marney became sick at heart and I feared for her health. I could not take time from my fishing to care for her, but I needed gold. So I made a deal with a man who was not to be trifled with. This was mine undoing, for when I failed to repay his loan, he came to me one night and slew me. I had not a chance to fight back or call for help." He falls silent.

speaker: Quenton
text: "But that was long before the fire that turned this whole island into the land of the dead."

speaker: Quenton
text: "After I was murdered, my good friend, Yorl, cared for her as his own. He tried his best, but her sickness only worsened. After several months she weakened, and died." He stops here, tears filling his ghostly eyes, then, angrily, he says, "And now her spirit is held by Horance the Liche. Thou must rescue her from that foul beast!" He attempts to grab you, but his hands pass through without resistance.

speaker: Markham
text: "Now, now, Quen. Settle down." <VAR> moves closer to you and whispers, "Fergive him, <HONORIFIC>."

speaker: Markham
text: "He sometimes loses control like that when he talks about his daughter. Sure'n ya can understand, tho'."

speaker: Quenton
text: Quenton regains control of himself. "Forgive me, <HONORIFIC>. I've no right to inflict my woes upon thee. It hurts to think of my sweet Marney in the power of that... creature."

speaker: Quenton
text: "It seems that Mistress Mordra, the town healer, thought she had a plan to stop the Liche, Horance, which she told to the Mayor. I am not sure exactly what she planned, but it involved Trent, the town smith, and Caine, the alchemist. Not long after Caine began his work, a maelstrom of fire tore over the island, destroying everything. Skara Brae burned for days."

speaker: Quenton
text: "Once, over two centuries ago, I knew a gifted mage named Horance. His two loves in life were the study of magic, and writing lovely poetry. The people of Skara Brae felt safe in the knowledge that this sort of mage protected the town. Then he began to change."

speaker: Quenton
text: "First his beautiful sonnets became a rhyming doggerel. It became the only way in which he would speak. His spells, which he displayed before the townsfolk, became destructive and violent. People began to fear him. My death occurred at about this time. Not long after that, he became reclusive. He had a tower built on the northern point and never removed himself from it."

speaker: Quenton
text: "Then, one night, the graves in the graveyard opened and the dead began to walk."

speaker: Markham
text: <VAR> nods his head emphatically, "'At's right, I seen it, I did."

speaker: Quenton
text: "They marched to his tower, and now they roam all over the island, performing his bidding."

speaker: Markham
text: "It be gettin' so's a ghost cannot make an honest livin' no more. Hmph." <VAR> looks a bit disgruntled.

speaker: Quenton
text: Quenton looks hopeful, "If thou wouldst like to assist us, she is the best one to speak to. She seems to know the way to rid us of the Liche, at the least."

speaker: Quenton
text: "The mayor...," Quenton selects his words carefully. "...well, he believes that discretion is the better part of Valor. So, he may be able to offer thee some aid, but thou art likely first to need convince him that thou'rt not here to hurt him."

speaker: Quenton
text: "Ah, the poor man knows the spirit-wrenching feeling of loss almost as well as I. His wife, Rowena, was killed by the walking dead. And Mistress Mordra claims that she saw her sitting on a throne next to the Liche's own. I believe this has driven Trent somewhat mad. He works night and day upon some oddly formed cage. Strange, though, he never seems to finish it. He doth not seem to recall that he died in the fire, either, but a great hatred for Horance still burns in his heart."

speaker: Quenton
text: He looks as if he expected your question. "Alas, Caine, in his attempt to free us of the Liche, instead damned us to become slaves of the selfsame Liche."

speaker: Quenton
text: "Yes, we are his slaves. Every night at midnight, we must go to the Dark Tower and become servants of his Black Mass. I only know this because Mordra tells us it is so. I have no recollection of ever having been to the Dark Tower at all." His expression betrays his fear.

speaker: Quenton
text: You explain that you need a spirit to volunteer to freely enter the Well of Souls in order to bring about its destruction. Quenton considers for a while, and then responds, "Please understand, <HONORIFIC>. I truly wish that I had that kind of Courage. But I cannot risk doing anything that might destroy Marney. Remember, her spirit is kept in that well, along with all of the dead of the graveyard."

speaker: Quenton
text: "No, I am sorry. I cannot risk it." He looks very weary.

speaker: Quenton
text: "Goodbye, <HONORIFIC>."

speaker: Quenton
text: He turns back to his conversation with <VAR>.

speaker: Forsythe
text: You see a ghostly man cowering in the corner. Holding up an ankh in a protective fashion, he looks around the room frantically, but takes no notice of you.

speaker: Forsythe
text: He looks into the well, at the swirling pool of trapped souls and his newfound resolve seems to diminish. "Perhaps this was not such a good idea. Art thou sure that I must go through with this?"

speaker: Forsythe
text: You nod. His resolve firms once again.

speaker: Forsythe
text: "Yes, thou art quite right. No time for speeches. No time for a wavering will. No time for..." He sees that you're not buying his attempt to stall.

speaker: Forsythe
text: "Well then, this is it." He moves toward the well. "I suppose I didn't make a very good Mayor in life." Forsythe's jowls droop.

speaker: Forsythe
text: "Well, at least in death, I'll make a name for myself and do the job right." With that, he's gone.

speaker: Forsythe
text: The souls of the well rush out of their confinement, leaving the blackened remains of the powerful artifact.

speaker: Forsythe
text: "Thou must merely lead me to the well, and I shall do my duty." He seems quite resigned to his fate.

speaker: Forsythe
text: The man looks strangely relaxed, almost too relaxed. He also ignores your attempt to converse with him. It would seem that he is not in control of his actions.

speaker: Forsythe
text: "No! Back! Please, leave me alone!" The Mayor looks terrified. It seems that you must give up trying to get anything useful out of him for the time being.

speaker: Forsythe
text: You see a middle-aged ghost cowering in the corner of this burned-out room. He's shaking from head to toe, and, as you approach, he jumps out, waving an ankh in your face.

speaker: Forsythe
text: "Thou'lt not have me, foul beast! Back, back I say! In the name of the Virtues, back!" He slowly notices that this is having no effect other than to surprise you and looks more closely in your direction. He looks from you to a picture of you on the wall. Back and forth he looks, squinting his eyes until they go wide with relief.

speaker: Forsythe
text: "Oh, thank thee for coming. Lord British finally called thee to help us." He's obviously suffering from some delusion. "I am Mayor Forsythe. Dost thou think it will take long for thee to defeat the Liche?"

speaker: Forsythe
text: "Ah, hello, <HONORIFIC>. May I be off assistance to thee?"

speaker: Forsythe
text: "Greetings, <HONORIFIC>." The mayor smiles at you half-heartedly.

speaker: Forsythe
text: "Ah yes, good Avatar. 'Tis good to see thee again. <VAR>Of what service can I be to one so great as thee?" He bows.

speaker: Forsythe
text: "As I told thee, my name is Forsythe."
