text: "I have lived here in Paws all my life. I will not leave it now. I shall never leave."

speaker: Merrick
text: "It is good to see that thou art one of us. Having the Avatar as a Fellowship member gives The Fellowship much prestige. Already I am certain that more people have been wanting to join because of it."

speaker: Merrick
text: "I have heard that some of Morfin's venom hath been stolen. I cannot imagine who would do it, unless it was that brat that lives with the farmer widow."

speaker: Merrick
text: "I believe his name is Tobias."

speaker: Merrick
text: "I believe her name is Camille."

speaker: Merrick
text: "He once owned one of the largest farms in all of Britannia. He was born to wealthy parents. After he lost his farm he took to sleeping along the road. One night a gang of bullies wanted to steal his gold. He had none so they beat him until he was lame. He is a very bitter man. Tragic."

speaker: Merrick
text: "Fenn was a farm laborer, and one of Komor's most trusted friends. With the farm gone Fenn just did not have any place to go or any way to live."

speaker: Merrick
text: "For years Komor, Fenn and I lived off of the rubbish of others, sleeping by the side of the road. Then I found The Fellowship and my life was changed for the better. I have tried to share my newfound fortune with my friends but I fear they hate me for being more resourceful than they."

speaker: Merrick
text: "Good day, <PLAYER_NAME>."

speaker: Garritt
text: You see a jovial young man who gives you a friendly greeting.

speaker: Garritt
text: "A pleasant day to thee, <HONORIFIC>," says Garritt.

speaker: Garritt
text: "I am Garritt, the son of Feridwyn and Brita."

speaker: Garritt
text: "I am too young to learn a trade of mine own yet, but I do assist my parents in running the shelter. I hope to be a counselor in The Fellowship one day. Or a professional whistle panpipes player."

speaker: Garritt
text: "My father works for The Fellowship helping the poor people in Paws. He tries to recruit them, but most refuse."

speaker: Garritt
text: "Actually, I do not like this town very much. The people here are all poor and the only one mine own age is Tobias."

speaker: Garritt
text: "And," he adds, "there is a thief here."

speaker: Garritt
text: "I have been playing panpipes since I was little. I'm pretty good now, if I say so myself! I keep the whistle by my bed and practice every night before going to sleep!"

speaker: Garritt
text: "I may not have told the truth about Tobias stealing the venom, but I know that he is up to no good. He shall come to a bad end, just thou wait and see!"

speaker: Garritt
text: "He and his mother reject The Fellowship. They are witless and stupid and I do not like them."

speaker: Garritt
text: "I have said it a thousand times. Tobias is weak of character! He and his mother are poor because they are lazy. Now I am proven right because Tobias is a thief. A thief who has been caught!"

speaker: Garritt
text: "My father was once the head recruiter in Britain until they moved him here. I once heard him talking to mother about how The Fellowship was wasting its time here."

speaker: Garritt
text: "My father says that the poor people reject The Fellowship because the Triad of Inner Strength requires strength of character."

speaker: Garritt
text: "My father says the poor are weak of character and that is why they are poor. They do not have to be. They are just too lazy to work. Dost thou agree?"

speaker: Garritt
text: "I was not so sure, but since that is what my father says, it must be true."

speaker: Garritt
text: "Hmpf. For a Fellowship member, thou dost lack recognition. Thou dost not understand the teachings of The Fellowship."

speaker: Garritt
text: "Then thou must be a person of weak character, also."

speaker: Garritt
text: "Oh, she is just my mother. She does whatever my father doth tell her to do."

speaker: Garritt
text: "Plenty of beds are available if thou wouldst like to stay in the shelter," he says with a condescending tone.

speaker: Garritt
text: "I am a member and I am proud to say I recruit for them as well."

speaker: Garritt
text: "Oh, I can tell thee all thou dost need to know about us!"

speaker: Garritt
text: "I am also quite knowledgeable when it comes to our philosophy. We follow the Triad of Inner Strength and do let personal failures get in our way or slow us down."

speaker: Garritt
text: "Dost thou want to join?"

speaker: Garritt
text: "I got another one!" he says gleefully. "Thou must speak with my father right away!"

speaker: Garritt
text: "Contemplate it for the nonce, then."

speaker: Garritt
text: "Thou hast found me out! Yes, it was I who planted the venom on Tobias. He did deserve it! I beg thee, please do not tell my parents!"

speaker: Garritt
text: "I stole the venom from Morfin so I could put the blame on Tobias."

speaker: Garritt
text: "I do not know why Morfin has it or what he does with it. I only knew that it was valuable and that it would cause everyone worry if it were stolen."

speaker: Garritt
text: Garritt does not meet your eyes. You instinctively know he is not telling the truth and may very well be using the venom.

speaker: Garritt
text: Garritt shuffles his feet and frowns. "Well... I tried it just once. I am sorry. I will never use it again."

speaker: Garritt
text: "I thought that if Tobias were accused of stealing something that everyone would notice, his mother would join The Fellowship and force him to join, too. It would improve their lives and force them to see the truth about themselves."

speaker: Garritt
text: "Wilt thou tell my parents?"

speaker: Garritt
text: "But I, like thee, am a member of The Fellowship. Thou must stand in unity with me for what I tried to do!"

speaker: Garritt
text: "Thou art weak of character! Or otherwise thou wouldst understand what I tried to do!"

speaker: Garritt
text: "I thank thee most enthusiastically! It will be our little secret then."

speaker: Garritt
text: "There is a thief in this town! Our merchant Morfin had some valuable silver serpent venom stolen from him. The culprit is still free. So be wary!"

speaker: Garritt
text: "Goodbye, then."

speaker: Morfin
text: You see a man whose eyes slowly shift back and forth as a crooked smile curls his lips. He walks up to you, looks you up and down. "Oh, there must be a travelling show in town!" he says sniggering. "That is a very nice clown costume! Who art thou?"

speaker: Morfin
text: "Very well, <PLAYER_NAME>. What dost thou want?"

speaker: Morfin
text: "Rude dog!"

speaker: Morfin
text: "Thou art a vile fool, desperate for others to like thee. I would pity thee, were it not that I loathe thee even more!"

speaker: Morfin
text: "Greetings, <PLAYER_NAME>," says Morfin.

speaker: Morfin
text: "My name is Morfin."

speaker: Morfin
text: "I am a merchant who operates one of the most thriving businesses in Paws, which includes the slaughterhouse."

speaker: Morfin
text: "Oh, I sell a little of this and that, here and there. Wherever there is a demand, I try to supply it."

speaker: Morfin
text: "There is quite a demand for the venom of the silver serpent in certain areas, for instance."

speaker: Morfin
text: "I keep a small stock of silver serpent venom from time to time which I sell to the apothecary in Britannia for a modest profit. The government is trying to control sales of it until they can determine how dangerous the effects are."

speaker: Morfin
text: "His name is Kessler."

speaker: Morfin
text: "I do suppose my ventures are profitable enough for me to afford to move to Britain, but things are so much less expensive here. Of course, the theft has me a bit wary."

speaker: Morfin
text: "If thou dost wish to know more about the people here, speak to the couple who run the Fellowship shelter, Feridwyn and Brita."

speaker: Morfin
text: "I take it thou hast noticed the smell. If so I do apologize." He shrugs his shoulders, grinning, and holds his palms upward.

speaker: Morfin
text: "I think of it as the smell of success. Thou mayest purchase some meat if thou so wishest."

speaker: Morfin
text: "I sell mutton, beef, and ham. Which wouldst thou like?"

speaker: Morfin
text: "The slaughterhouse is closed. Come around when it is open for business and I shall sell thee meats then."

speaker: Morfin
text: "Some other time, perhaps."

speaker: Morfin
text: "'Twill cost thee 3 gold each. Still interested?"

speaker: Morfin
text: "How many dost thou want?"

speaker: Morfin
text: "Here it is."

speaker: Morfin
text: "Thou hast not the room for this meat."

speaker: Morfin
text: "Thou hast not the gold for this, <PLAYER_NAME>. Perhaps something else."

speaker: Morfin
text: "Perhaps next time, <PLAYER_NAME>."

speaker: Morfin
text: "'Twill cost thee 2 gold each. Still interested?"

speaker: Morfin
text: "How many dost thou want?"

speaker: Morfin
text: "Here it is."

speaker: Morfin
text: "Thou hast not the room for this meat."

speaker: Morfin
text: "Thou hast not the gold for this, <PLAYER_NAME>. Perhaps something else."

speaker: Morfin
text: "Perhaps next time, <PLAYER_NAME>."

speaker: Morfin
text: "'Twill cost thee 4 gold each. Still interested?"

speaker: Morfin
text: "How many dost thou want?"

speaker: Morfin
text: "Here it is."

speaker: Morfin
text: "Thou hast not the room for this meat."

speaker: Morfin
text: "Thou hast not the gold for this, <PLAYER_NAME>. Perhaps something else."

speaker: Morfin
text: "Perhaps next time, <PLAYER_NAME>."

speaker: Morfin
text: "A terrible crime, causing me no small amount of monetary distress. It has caused the surrounding community to worry about their possessions as well."

speaker: Morfin
text: "I would be thine humble servant shouldst thou help investigate the matter. Wilt thou?"

speaker: Morfin
text: "Then I shall cooperate fully, <HONORIFIC>." He bows.

speaker: Morfin
text: "I do hope the culprit will be revealed through other methods then."

speaker: Morfin
text: "I thank thee for solving the mystery of who was behind it."

speaker: Morfin
text: "Thou art a stranger in Paws. Beware the thief who roams this town! The culprit has stolen a quantity of my valuable silver serpent venom!"

speaker: Morfin
text: "I do apologize for my rudeness earlier, <PLAYER_NAME>. I have since realized that thou art an honest person. Please forgive mine insults." He bows, dripping insincerity.

speaker: Morfin
text: You tell Morfin that you have seen his ledger. "Wait, <PLAYER_NAME>! I admit I do sell Silver Serpent Venom to other places besides the Apothecary. But what I am doing is not -precisely- against the law!"

speaker: Morfin
text: "My supply comes from some old friends in Buccaneer's Den. Where they get it, who can say?"

speaker: Morfin
text: "I have a notarized contract with the Britannian Mining Company. They use it to keep their gargoyles working longer hours. It seems gargoyles have a greater resistance to the effects of Silver Serpent Venom. Poor devils." He grins maliciously at his own joke.

speaker: Morfin
text: "They are widely known. Silver serpent venom is a reagent that, when ingested in small doses, temporarily enhances one's physical strength, stamina and quickness along with bringing a feeling of euphoria."

speaker: Morfin
text: "After the effects	wear off, the subject feels quite drained. This tends to make them want to take it again."

speaker: Morfin
text: "Prolonged use in such a fashion will bring about a condition that deteriorates the skin, eventually causing it to rot away."

speaker: Morfin
text: "Finally, too great a dose, or too great an accumulation of doses, is fatal, as the venom is a deadly poison."

speaker: Morfin
text: "It may very well have some healing properties when used in other ways we have yet to discover, but any user of the venom should not do so without caution."

speaker: Morfin
text: "I am not so sure Tobias was the one who stole the venom. I have not seen any of the signs of venom use in Tobias and I am quite familiar with its symptoms. But, now that I think about it, I have noticed that Garritt has appeared very tired lately. He seems hyperactive one moment and unhealthy the next."

speaker: Morfin
text: "I do not believe I have noticed anyone in town who is showing the symptoms of venom use. From now on I shall keep watch, so thou shouldst ask again later."

speaker: Morfin
text: "Perhaps thou shouldst make a search of Garritt's belongings! Which reminds me-- I saw him earlier playing near the slaughterhouse. He dropped this key. Perhaps it opens something... significant."

speaker: Morfin
text: "Here it is."

speaker: Morfin
text: "I shall give it to thee when thine hands are not so full."

speaker: Morfin
text: "I thank thee for ferreting out the thief and returning my snake venom."

speaker: Morfin
text: "So Garritt was the culprit, eh? I am not surprised now that I think about it. I must keep closer tabs on my venom from now on."

speaker: Morfin
text: "Of course, I do wish for thee to return my venom to me if thou hast recovered it."

speaker: Morfin
text: "Good day to thee."

speaker: Beverlea
text: You see an old woman who gives you a smile of grandmotherly sweetness. You can see immediately that her vision is poor.

speaker: Beverlea
text: "Why, hello again, <HONORIFIC>. It is so good to see thee!" says Beverlea.

speaker: Beverlea
text: "My name is Beverlea."

speaker: Beverlea
text: "Why, I run the House of Items here in Paws."

speaker: Beverlea
text: "It is a shop that sells antiques and previously used items. Running this shop allows me to remain youthful and active. It is heartening to sell things to the poor people of this town that they might not otherwise be able to	afford."

speaker: Beverlea
text: "Here in Paws the people have very little money, but it matters not, because they care for each other."

speaker: Beverlea
text: "There are many rare and fine things to be bought here in my shop. Bargains to be had nowhere else in all of Britannia."

speaker: Beverlea
text: "My store is now closed. I am usually open in the afternoons."

speaker: Beverlea
text: "Let me see... There is a cradle for sale. A rocking horse. A bell. An hourglass. A spittoon. A lute. A sextant... Since I am moving a bit more slowly these days, I let my customers help themselves and take what they have bought. Providing they pay me first, of course. I do trust folks to pay me the correct amount. I am nearly blind, I am afraid."

speaker: Beverlea
text: "That old cradle was the cradle used to rock Gorn the Barbarian to sleep at night when he was just a baby. Thou canst see that there is a crack in its side proving that even as a child Gorn was a strong little tyke. I can let thee take it for ten gold coins. Dost thou wish to buy the cradle?"

speaker: Beverlea
text: "Thou mayest take it then. I hope that thou dost enjoy it."

speaker: Beverlea
text: "Thou dost not have enough gold!"

speaker: Beverlea
text: A sour look flashes across Beverlea's face. "Very well. Perhaps I may interest thee in something else."

speaker: Beverlea
text: "This is the rocking horse that once belonged to a little girl from Britain named Diane. She grew to be one of the finest equestriennes to ever sit upon a horse. I could let thee have this rare and unusual piece for twelve gold. Dost thou wish to buy it?"

speaker: Beverlea
text: "Then thou art free to take the rocking horse. It is thine!"

speaker: Beverlea
text: "Thou dost not have enough money to pay for it!"

speaker: Beverlea
text: Beverlea rolls her eyes. "In a browsing mood, are we? Take thy time."

speaker: Beverlea
text: "That bell came from the High Court of Justice in Yew. It was rung to announce that court was in session. I can sell thee that interesting conversation piece for six gold coins.	Dost thou wish to buy it?"

speaker: Beverlea
text: "Thou mayest take thy bell. Use it in good health!"

speaker: Beverlea
text: "Thou dost not have enough money to buy it!"

speaker: Beverlea
text: "Not in the mood for a bell today?" She wrinkles her lips in the best attempt at a smile. "Perhaps something else will strike thy fancy."

speaker: Beverlea
text: "I also have an antique hourglass. It was sold to me by this old man who was so daft that he could not recall how to use it! I will sell it to thee for five gold pieces. Dost thou wish to buy it?"

speaker: Beverlea
text: "I thank thee. Thou mayest take thy glass."

speaker: Beverlea
text: "Thou dost not have enough money."

speaker: Beverlea
text: "Thou art not interested in the hourglass?" She sighs, "Very well. Look around. I have all the time in the world." You catch just a hint of sarcasm in her voice.

speaker: Beverlea
text: "Curse mine old head and failing memory! Has the hourglass already been sold?! No! It must have been stolen! One of the few dishonest people in this town must have taken it!"

speaker: Beverlea
text: "I also have an old spittoon. It was once used by... a great many people. Thou mayest have it for a gold piece. Take it! Please!"

speaker: Beverlea
text: "I thank thee! Now thou canst go and please do not forget to take it with thee when thou dost leave!"

speaker: Beverlea
text: "Thou dost not even have a single gold piece! Nor the decency to inform me that I was wasting my time in talking with thee."

speaker: Beverlea
text: "I have many more things in my shop. Many things of high quality and great value as well. Please keep looking."

speaker: Beverlea
text: "I have a lute for sale that once belonged to a travelling bard who lost it in a game of dice. I am asking twenty gold coins for it. A song! Wouldst thou like to buy it?"

speaker: Beverlea
text: "I thank thee, kind customer. Thou mayest take thy lute. I can see that thou art a true artisan with an appreciation for quality."

speaker: Beverlea
text: "Thou canst not afford the lute!"

speaker: Beverlea
text: "Very well, then. Do keep looking. After all, that is why my shop is here." You thought you could also hear Beverlea mutter to herself for a few moments after saying this, but you are not entirely certain.

speaker: Beverlea
text: "I have a sextant that was sold by the world-famous shipwright Owen of Minoc. They are going to be building a monument to him, I understand. Anyway, the sailor who sold it to me had just suffered some harrowing experience out on the waters. He said when he sold it to me that he was going to retire. He obviously did not realize the value of this item. But I can let thee have it for twenty gold pieces. Dost thou wish to buy it?"

speaker: Beverlea
text: "Thou mayest take thy sextant! And may thou always have smooth sailing!"

speaker: Beverlea
text: "Thou dost not have enough money!"

speaker: Beverlea
text: "I am certain I have something that will interest thee. Browse to thine heart's content."

speaker: Beverlea
text: "A good day to thee, <HONORIFIC>."

speaker: Komor
text: You see a beggar leaning on a crutch. His eyes shine like diamonds with sheer bitterness.

speaker: Komor
text: "Happy days, <HONORIFIC>?" Komor asks.

speaker: Komor
text: "My name is Komor."

speaker: Komor
text: "I am a dancer, <HONORIFIC>." He cannot keep a straight face and almost falls off his crutches.

speaker: Fenn
text: "Ha! Ha! Ha! Ha! Ha! Ha! 'Tis a ripe one, Komor!"

speaker: Komor
text: "I was not always a beggar. Like Fenn and Merrick, I used to be a farmer, too. But times got worse, and times are always bad in Paws."

speaker: Komor
text: "Fenn and me are chums and will be to the day we die. We share in each other's vast expanses of wealth."

speaker: Fenn
text: "Ha! Ha! Ha! Ha! With thy wit thou shouldst be on stage!"

speaker: Komor
text: "Fenn and me have been friends since we were little tiny babes."

speaker: Komor
text: "I would bet thee that thou didst not think we would end up like this. Eh, Fenn?"

speaker: Fenn
text: "Not in me wildest dreams, Komor.*"

speaker: Komor
text: "Yea verily, Fenn and I share all that we own. Which, in its totality, is the clothes on our backs and the snot in our	throats!"

speaker: Komor
text: "A royal rotten egg, he is. Merrick turned his back on us and now spends each night in a warm, cozy bed. Which is more than either one of us have had for some time."

speaker: Komor
text: "A veritable wonderland, is it not?"

speaker: Komor
text: "The only thing worse than this miserable existence is having Merrick sniff around and try to recruit us! The bloody parasite!"

speaker: Komor
text: "Merrick sleeps in the shelter run by The Fellowship. They feed him, too. He had to join before they would help him."

speaker: Komor
text: "The shelter? 'Tis the large building filled with fawning hypocrites. Thou shouldst have little trouble finding it!"

speaker: Komor
text: "We could have joined, but they are a foul lot. Anybody acting so bloody nice must be up to no good. There are some compromises we will not make, even to survive."

speaker: Komor
text: "Wilt thou give me a bit of money?"

speaker: Komor
text: How much?

speaker: Komor
text: "Thank thee, <HONORIFIC>."

speaker: Komor
text: "I am unable to take thy money, for some strange reason."

speaker: Komor
text: "Hmpf! Thou dost not have that much gold! Thou art almost as poor as I!"

speaker: Komor
text: "Fine. Go on and live thy life in peace and happiness."

speaker: Komor
text: "Hold thine head high, <HONORIFIC>."

speaker: Fenn
text: You see a beggar. You cannot tell from the look on his face whether he is about to laugh or cry.

speaker: Fenn
text: "Beg thy pardon, <HONORIFIC>," Fenn says.

speaker: Fenn
text: "My name is Fenn, <HONORIFIC>."

speaker: Fenn
text: After you tell him about finding the venom vial, he says, "Thou didst our town a service when thou didst uncover that no good brat Garritt as the thief! Perhaps now some people will start to realize the hypocrisy of the Fellowship!"

speaker: Fenn
text: "I know that boy Tobias is innocent of any wrong doing, no matter what Feridwyn and his Fellowship says."

speaker: Fenn
text: "Be wary for there is a thief in this town! Some silver serpent venom was stolen from the merchant Morfin, who runs the slaughterhouse."

speaker: Fenn
text: He looks away from you shamefully. "I have none, <HONORIFIC>."

speaker: Fenn
text: "I used to be a farmer in more prosperous times. I used to work with Komor and Merrick."

speaker: Fenn
text: "He is my best friend and the bravest man I know."

speaker: Komor
text: "Oh, please! Thou art making mine eyes leak!"

speaker: Fenn
text: "Merrick joined The Fellowship so he could live in their shelter, the poor sod."

speaker: Fenn
text: "If The Fellowship truly wants to help people, why would they let us starve just because we do not want to join? They cannot answer that one!"

speaker: Fenn
text: "Hmf! If thou art so unfortunate as to want to live there, thou wouldst do better on the corner with Komor and I."

speaker: Fenn
text: "Even when pockets are light, there is still some mercy left in this world. Begging for money is not a proud profession, but there are worse ones."

speaker: Fenn
text: "At least we do not have to do what Merrick does. He recruits for The Fellowship."

speaker: Fenn
text: "Do not worry. We shall not starve. Camille sends her son Tobias with food and clothing for us every so often."

speaker: Fenn
text: "Camille is a good woman. She lives at the farm bordering the dairy."

speaker: Fenn
text: "He is a fine lad, always willing to give us a hand. Unlike that rude urchin, Garritt."

speaker: Fenn
text: "Tobias would not become involved with that sort of affair. I know for certain he is no thief."

speaker: Fenn
text: "If thou art seeking out this venom thief, thou wouldst do well to ask Andrew about it."

speaker: Fenn
text: "Andrew owns the dairy and lives across from Camille's farm and the slaughterhouse. He might have seen something."

speaker: Fenn
text: "He is the son of Feridwyn and Brita, who run the shelter. Garritt crosses the road to avoid us."

speaker: Komor
text: "We would not want the likes of him walking down our side of the road anyway!"

speaker: Fenn
text: "Wilt thou give me a bit of money?"

speaker: Fenn
text: How much?

speaker: Fenn
text: "Thank thee, <HONORIFIC>."

speaker: Fenn
text: "It appears thou dost not have any money either!"

speaker: Fenn
text: "I am truly sorry if I have bothered thee, <HONORIFIC>."

speaker: Fenn
text: Fenn hangs his head low.

speaker: Fenn
text: "Good fortune to ye, <HONORIFIC>."

speaker: Andrew
text: You see a cheerful, handsome young man who gives you a friendly wave as you approach.

speaker: Andrew
text: "Greetings, <HONORIFIC>," says Andrew.

speaker: Andrew
text: "My name is Andrew. How art thou, <HONORIFIC>?"

speaker: Andrew
text: "I am the owner and proprietor of the dairy here in Paws."

speaker: Andrew
text: "Yes, I sell milk and cheese. Thou mayest find the dairy between Camille's farm and the slaughterhouse."

speaker: Andrew
text: "A gallon will cost thee 3 gold. Art thou interested in buying some?"

speaker: Andrew
text: "Here it is," he says, handing you the jug. "Wouldst thou like another?"

speaker: Andrew
text: "Thou hast not the room for the jug."

speaker: Andrew
text: "Thou hast not the gold for this, <HONORIFIC>. Perhaps some other time."

speaker: Andrew
text: "Perhaps next time, <HONORIFIC>."

speaker: Andrew
text: "I would be more than happy to sell thee a jug of milk, but for now the dairy is closed."

speaker: Andrew
text: "I sell wedges for 2 gold each. Still interested?"

speaker: Andrew
text: "How many dost thou want?"

speaker: Andrew
text: "Here it is."

speaker: Andrew
text: "Thou hast not the room for this cheese."

speaker: Andrew
text: "Thou hast not the gold for this, <HONORIFIC>. Perhaps something else."

speaker: Andrew
text: "I understand, <HONORIFIC>. Perhaps when thou dost become more hungry."

speaker: Andrew
text: "I would be more than happy to sell thee some cheese, but for now the dairy is closed."

speaker: Andrew
text: "Camille is a good woman. She is still an advocate of the old virtues. She runs the farm by herself. Well, with the help of her son, Tobias."

speaker: Andrew
text: "A rather defensive young lad, I cannot say that I know that much about him."

speaker: Andrew
text: "Of course everyone is up in arms about this business concerning the missing venom."

speaker: Andrew
text: "It could be hidden anywhere. With all the trade that occurs in this town, it would be easy to hide. I do not know much else about the substance. Perhaps Morfin himself would know what kinds of effects it might produce."

speaker: Andrew
text: "Be wary, for there is a thief in this town! Some silver serpent venom was stolen from Morfin."

speaker: Andrew
text: "Thou hast put the people in our town at ease by finding the culprit!"

speaker: Andrew
text: "The slaughterhouse is run by Morfin, the merchant. He is always busy, coming and going at all hours, sometimes carrying things."

speaker: Andrew
text: "He bought the slaughterhouse a few years ago, soon after he joined The Fellowship. I knew the previous owner."

speaker: Andrew
text: "I was just a lad when I first saw the old slaughterhouse. The old man who owned it even showed me the storeroom in there once. The door to it is locked. I think Morfin has the key somewhere in his house."

speaker: Andrew
text: "I hope I was of some assistance to thee, <HONORIFIC>."

speaker: Camille
text: "Avatar! My son Tobias has been wrongly accused! He is no thief! And I cannot believe a vial of venom was found in his possession. I truly believe it was planted there! Please -- I beg thee! Please clear my son's name. He has done no wrong!"

speaker: Camille
text: "I know my son Tobias has suffered for not having a father. I have tried my best on mine own to raise him well, but this farm requires so much work that I fear I do not have enough time to devote to him. But I know in mine heart that my son is not a thief."

speaker: Camille
text: "Might I suggest that thou speak with Morfin again. He may have recognized signs of usage of this foul substance in other members of the village."

speaker: Camille
text: You see a farm woman. She rubs her hands, which are covered with dirt and lines drawn by toil.

speaker: Camille
text: "My dreams have become reality. Thou art the Avatar, art thou not? I recognized thee immediately!"

speaker: Camille
text: "How art thou, <HONORIFIC>?" Camille asks.

speaker: Camille
text: "My name is Camille, Avatar. It is an honor to meet thee."

speaker: Camille
text: "I run a small farm here in Paws with my son, Tobias. I am a widow."

speaker: Camille
text: "I grow a few crops. Especially carrots and wheat."

speaker: Camille
text: "I believe my carrots are especially tasty. Wouldst thou like to purchase some? They would only cost thee one gold for three."

speaker: Camille
text: "How many dost thou desire?"

speaker: Camille
text: "I am sure thou wilt love them."

speaker: Camille
text: "Thou must first lighten thy load. Then I can give thee some delicious carrots."

speaker: Camille
text: "I am sorry, Avatar." She shakes her head sadly. "Thou dost not have the gold to be able to taste them."

speaker: Camille
text: She stares at you for a moment, obviously thoughtful. Lowering her voice, she says,

speaker: Camille
text: "Go ahead, Avatar, take one."

speaker: Camille
text: Smiling gently, she hands you a carrot.

speaker: Camille
text: "Thou art carrying too much..." She seems truly disappointed.

speaker: Camille
text: "If that is thy wish, Avatar, but they are quite good!"

speaker: Camille
text: "That reminds me. This package needs to be taken to the mill today. If thou canst deliver it for me, Thurston will pay thee for it. Wilt thou?"

speaker: Camille
text: "Be sure and take this to Thurston, the mill owner. He shall pay thee for thy trouble."

speaker: Camille
text: "Thou art carrying too much! Go put something down and I will give it to thee then."

speaker: Camille
text: "I understand that thou art busy on thy quest, Avatar."

speaker: Camille
text: "Life is hard here in Paws. It is a town of poor people with all the ills that poverty brings. At least The Fellowship brings us some relief."

speaker: Camille
text: "I know my son. I know that he is growing up unhappy. But I cannot believe that he would steal things."

speaker: Camille
text: "He is basically a good boy. He works hard and misses his father."

speaker: Camille
text: "I am not sure whether I trust The Fellowship. It has undoubtedly done some good things in this world so it cannot be all bad. Or, at least, the people in it cannot be all bad."

speaker: Camille
text: "Recently, our town has been plagued by a thief."

speaker: Camille
text: "Some silver serpent venom was stolen from the merchant Morfin who operates the slaughterhouse."

speaker: Camille
text: "I do not care what Feridwyn says! My son is no thief!"

speaker: Camille
text: "That man Feridwyn knows that I do not trust The Fellowship, and for	that he considers me his personal enemy. I do not know why he would seek to attack me through my son but he must not be allowed to succeed."

speaker: Camille
text: You tell Camille how you discovered that Garritt was really the thief and that her son Tobias has been cleared. "I want to thank thee for finding the thief in our town and clearing my son's name. It does mine heart good to see that the Avatar has returned to us once again and that thou dost care enough about the people of Britannia to help solve our local troubles here in Paws. Again Avatar, I thank thee."

speaker: Camille
text: "Pleasant journey, Avatar."

speaker: Tobias
text: You see a sulking lad, who doesn't seem to want to look you in the eye.

speaker: Tobias
text: "Just what I need. Another Avatar," he mumbles under his breath.

speaker: Tobias
text: "Yes, Avatar?" Tobias asks.

speaker: Tobias
text: "What dost thou want?" Tobias asks.

speaker: Tobias
text: "I am still Tobias!"

speaker: Tobias
text: "I am Tobias. I suppose I am to believe thou art someone important."

speaker: Tobias
text: "I am too young to have a job. I just help my mother on the farm."

speaker: Tobias
text: "Her name is Camille. She speaks of thee. Or rather she speaks of the Avatar, is what I meant to say. Some people in town think she is mad because she still believes in the Eight Virtues."

speaker: Tobias
text: "Thou hast already met her."

speaker: Tobias
text: "But thanks to thee I have more respect for her beliefs."

speaker: Tobias
text: "Art thou truly the Avatar?"

speaker: Tobias
text: "Yes, I do believe thou art the true Avatar." Tobias smiles briefly.

speaker: Tobias
text: "Thou art no Avatar!" Tobias frowns.

speaker: Tobias
text: "I think that thou mayest have a little bit of the way of the Avatar about thee. There is a little bit of the Avatar in everyone, or so my mother says."

speaker: Tobias
text: "I knew that thou wert nothing but an imposter."

speaker: Tobias
text: "My mother once took me to the Shrine of Sacrifice when I was younger. That was soon after my father died so I do not remember it very well."

speaker: Tobias
text: I do not think it is there anymore, for she never talks about going back.

speaker: Tobias
text: "I think that perhaps she does not want to mention it because there are so many in town who belong to The Fellowship. And because it makes her sad."

speaker: Tobias
text: "My mother grows grain."

speaker: Tobias
text: "Dost thou not know a farm when thou dost see one?"

speaker: Tobias
text: "Surely thou canst find the farm. It is just north of the shelter."

speaker: Tobias
text: Tobias looks at you as if he thinks you are a bit dim.

speaker: Tobias
text: "She sells grain to Thurston the miller from time to time so that we may go to the pub or buy milk at the dairy every once in a while, but we usually just grow crops to keep ourselves fed."

speaker: Tobias
text: "It's that place just south of here. It's run by The Fellowship."

speaker: Tobias
text: "He is one of the few people in town that I like. He is nice to us."

speaker: Tobias
text: "The dairy is south of the shelter. Andrew -- the man who runs the dairy -- his father was friends with my father."

speaker: Tobias
text: For the first time he looks you in the eye. "I hate The Fellowship! The only other person in town mine own age is that cretin Garritt and it is all he ever talks about! He is always trying to convince my mother to join." He clenches his fist angrily. "Please do not mention them again."

speaker: Tobias
text: "Those bloody Fellowship people know that everyone is never more than a meal away from being penniless. They say that they want us to join immediately because the shelter is intended to help only Fellowship members. If we ever need to live there they may have to turn us away in favor of other Fellowship members."

speaker: Tobias
text: "There is a thief running free in Paws! He stole silver serpent venom from Morfin, owner of the slaughterhouse. No one knows who he is."

speaker: Tobias
text: "I do not know anything about the stolen venom. I am falsely accused!"

speaker: Tobias
text: "That is right! Garritt did it. I just know it. He was in my room the other day when I came in from the fields. He said he was looking for a ball, but I do not believe him. Thou canst believe me or not, I do not care. But if thou art truly the Avatar, thou wilt know I am telling the truth."

speaker: Tobias
text: You tell Tobias how you discovered that Garritt was the thief. "Thank thee, <HONORIFIC>, for not believing I was the guilty one. I am not sure if thou art truly the real Avatar but thou dost certainly have the way of the Avatar about thee."

speaker: Tobias
text: "He is the only other boy in town anywhere near mine age. His parents do not want him playing with me because they think that 'associating with those kind of people' will 'hamper his education' or some such rubbish. I cannot stand the little bastard. And I hate the way he plays those stinking whistle panpipes!"

speaker: Tobias
text: "That spoiled brat Garritt must have planted the venom in my room! He is usually lounging about, even if his parents disapprove of him playing with me. I know he is up to something no good! Thou shouldst look in HIS room!"

speaker: Tobias
text: "Goodbye, Avatar. Good luck to thee."

speaker: Tobias
text: "Be on thy way then, o great and wise Avatar."

speaker: Polly
text: You see the town bartender. She looks very busy, but she obviously takes pride in her work.

speaker: Polly
text: Polly smiles. "What can I do for thee, <HONORIFIC>?"

speaker: Polly
text: "I am Polly. It is a pleasure to meet thee."

speaker: Polly
text: "The owner and proprietor of the Salty Dog, the finest eating and drinking establishment in all of Paws, at thy service."

speaker: Polly
text: "However, the Salty Dog is now closed. Please return during business hours."

speaker: Polly
text: "For but 5 gold thou canst let one of our lovely rooms. Dost thou wish to stay here for the night?"

speaker: Polly
text: "Here is thy key for this inn. 'Twill only work once."

speaker: Polly
text: "Sorry, <HONORIFIC>, thou must lose some of thy bundles before I can give thee thy key."

speaker: Polly
text: "I am truly sorry, <HONORIFIC>, but the rooms cost more gold than thou hast."

speaker: Polly
text: "Perhaps another evening then."

speaker: Polly
text: "Actually, there are no other inns or pubs in Paws. It is a small place, but our food and drink here is quite good, honestly."

speaker: Polly
text: "There is a thief in this town! Silver serpent venom was stolen from Morfin, the merchant who operates the slaughterhouse."

speaker: Polly
text: "He used to be a farmer. He is not a bad sort. He has just had a bad run of luck. Now he is a devout Fellowship member."

speaker: Polly
text: "Morfin is a very shrewd and successful merchant, and also a Fellowship member, but I cannot help but feel that he would sell his own mother if he could get the right price for her. 'Tis little wonder why the thief chose to steal from him."

speaker: Polly
text: You relate to Polly what you heard Thurston say about her. She is taken completely by surprise. "Thurston really said that about me! I have always liked him, but in truth I have always thought I was not good enough for him!"

speaker: Polly
text: "Good day to thee, <HONORIFIC>."

speaker: Draxinusom
text: You see an aged gargoyle, bent and withered, with a regal bearing. He smiles gently.

speaker: Draxinusom
text: "To be good to see you again, old friend. To be needing Draxinusom again so soon?"

speaker: Draxinusom
text: "To have been many years. To be your old acquaintance, <PLAYER_NAME>, Draxinusom."

speaker: Draxinusom
text: "To ask about Job? To be unable to say that I truly have one at this time. To notice how the young ones no longer look to me for guidance any more. To look more to Teregus, or, more often, to those in The Fellowship."

speaker: Draxinusom
text: "To be quite comfortable for our needs. To be, however, unfortunate that it was thought necessary to isolate us from the humans. To have engendered resentment and tension in our younger generations. To remember not the old days, my friend -- the days when we had to work together to survive." He smiles, reliving old memories, then shakes his head.

speaker: Draxinusom
text: "To have had to give up many much when we moved."

speaker: Draxinusom
text: "To have been many favorite possessions. To be too much trouble to move so much." He sighs.

speaker: Draxinusom
text: "To especially regret selling my Ethereal Ring."

speaker: Draxinusom
text: "Ah. To be, indeed, a lovely treasure. To have been quite useful. A shame to have been, really, to have had to sell it. To have been one of my favorites."

speaker: Draxinusom
text: "To have sold most of my treasures when we were... uh... asked, shall to say, to move to the island. To have all happened rather quickly, you see. To have sold most to the Sultan of Spektran."

speaker: Draxinusom
text: "To have seemed nice enough, for a human. To be a bit mad, he is, even for a human. To tell you he lives on an island just to the west of us. To know, at least, that my prized possessions would be safe in his hands."

speaker: Draxinusom
text: He nods his head. "To be rumored to have one of the best-guarded vaults in all of Britannia. To be supposedly enchanted. To know not details."

speaker: Draxinusom
text: "To be a fine young gargoyle. To have been raised by Teregus, keeper of the altars. To have left town because of the tension between the altar worshippers and The Fellowship. To have been angry and distrustful of The Fellowship. To have news of him?"

speaker: Draxinusom
text: "To be excellent! To have seen him? To know how he is faring? To be well?"

speaker: Draxinusom
text: "Ah. To be too bad. To tell you Teregus wanted to know how he was doing."

speaker: Draxinusom
text: "To be very good. To know Teregus will be pleased to learn that, as well!"

speaker: Draxinusom
text: "To be terrible news! To have been such a fine gargoyle. To know Teregus will be heartbroken. To be wishing not for him to grieve, but to take to him the news immediately. To be better to hear it from you."

speaker: Draxinusom
text: "Mine own Orb of the Moons exploded recently! To no longer be able to travel via Moongates. To be strange!"

speaker: Draxinusom
text: "To be a shame. To be taking the news to Teregus of his youngling. To be wondering why we had not heard from Inamo recently."

speaker: Draxinusom
text: "To be truly a fine young gargoyle. To be one of the most sensible, too. To have seen fit to adhere to the old ways, the ways of the altars. To see that some of the youngest still look up to him, but the majority seem to have been wooed away by the glamor of The Fellowship."

speaker: Draxinusom
text: "To tell you that his weanling, Inamo, is in Trinsic at this time."

speaker: Draxinusom
text: "To know not what to think of them and their tenets. To seem not dangerous, but not to be following the old ways, the ways of Passion, Diligence, and Control. To feign worship to the shrines here in Terfin, of course, especially to Control, but not yet to trust them. To wait and see. To have forceful leaders who espouse doctrines of submission." He shrugs.

speaker: Draxinusom
text: "To be genuinely inspired, perhaps, and perhaps not."

speaker: Draxinusom
text: "To inform you that The Fellowship is directed by two winged brethren. To be called Runeb and Quan."

speaker: Draxinusom
text: "To mean, in your language, `Red Mist'. To have been given that name because that is all he leaves behind of an adversary in battle. Before his conversion by The Fellowship, to have been known as a particularly cruel and dangerous gargoyle."

speaker: Draxinusom
text: "To be gone -- dead -- now."

speaker: Draxinusom
text: "Ah, to be an interesting one. To be a strong, powerful personality, to be from one of the families most able to claim noble lineage in our society. To have been always most self-serving, striving only to gain status and wealth for himself. To have certainly changed his tune since joining The Fellowship. To have my doubts, however, that his goals have changed as well."

speaker: Draxinusom
text: "To bid farewell, old friend. To not be hesitating to return if there is aught else I can do for you. To be lonely here now for an old gargoyle dedicated to the ancient ways..."

speaker: Inforlem
text: The gargoyle has a pleasant expression on his face.

speaker: Inforlem
text: "To be pleased at your return, human," says Inforlem.

speaker: Inforlem
text: "To be known as Inforlem."

speaker: Inforlem
text: "To mean `make strong one.'"

speaker: Inforlem
text: "To train others in Terfin to be strong and powerful. To sell some weapons, also."

speaker: Inforlem
text: "To sell during shop hours. To ask you to come back to me at that time, please."

speaker: Inforlem
text: "To be a better warrior or mage?"

speaker: Inforlem
text: "To train during training hours. To ask you to come back to me at that time, please."

speaker: Inforlem
text: "To charge 50 gold for each training session. To be all right?"

speaker: Inforlem
text: "To apologize, but I must charge that amount!"

speaker: Inforlem
text: "To charge 50 gold for each training session. To be acceptable?"

speaker: Inforlem
text: "To apologize, but I must charge that amount!"

speaker: Inforlem
text: "To know of the conflicts between the altars and the Fellowship, but to have no information. To suggest you see Quan, The Fellowship leader here and ask him."

speaker: Inforlem
text: "To see there are troubles here, but to be unaware of the causes and solutions."

speaker: Inforlem
text: "To tell you Forbrak knows much about Terfin and its residents, and," he says, "about its conflicts."

speaker: Inforlem
text: "To be the tavernkeeper."

speaker: Inforlem
text: "To expect to see you again, human."

speaker: Inmanilem
text: You are greeted by a friendly gargoyle.

speaker: Inmanilem
text: "To see you are doing well, human," says Inmanilem.

speaker: Inmanilem
text: "To be called Inmanilem, human. To wish information about Terfin?"

speaker: Inmanilem
text: "To be Gargoyle for `make healed one.'"

speaker: Inmanilem
text: "To be the healer."

speaker: Inmanilem
text: "To feel sorry, but to be busy with other things now. To ask you to come back when I have the time to heal you."

speaker: Inmanilem
text: "To tell you to seek out Draxinusom, human, or Forbrak. To have much information about Terfin."

speaker: Inmanilem
text: "To be the tavernkeeper. To be very strong of body, and of mind."

speaker: Inmanilem
text: "To be the city of gargoyles. To be the one of two towns where many gargoyles live. To like it here," he adds, smiling.

speaker: Inmanilem
text: "To tell you the other is called Vesper. To be in the desert in northeastern Britannia. To have also humans living there, unlike here."

speaker: Inmanilem
text: "To be our leader. To live near the Hall of Knowledge."

speaker: Inmanilem
text: "To be where the three altars of singularity are kept."

speaker: Inmanilem
text: "To be Passion, Control, and Diligence. To be the values that most gargoyles hold as the key of our existence."

speaker: Inmanilem
text: He nods his head emphatically. "To be quite similar to the human concept of virtues."

speaker: Inmanilem
text: "There is a rival now -- The Fellowship. To know not if it is good or bad, but to know I do not follow it!"

speaker: Inmanilem
text: "To know only of one dissatisfied gargoyle. To have always been problem, but now acting hostile and aggressive. To be named Silamo, the gardener."

speaker: Inmanilem
text: "To recommend you talk to Silamo."

speaker: Inmanilem
text: "To wish you good health, human."

speaker: Teregus
text: You see a winged gargoyle in his physical prime.

speaker: Teregus
text: "Hail, human! To be welcome to the house of the altars. To be helpful to you in any way?"

speaker: Teregus
text: "To have returned! To be glad to see you again, human," says Teregus. "To be welcome to the house of the altars. To be helpful to you?"

speaker: Teregus
text: "To be called Teregus."

speaker: Teregus
text: "To be caring for the altars of Control, Passion, and Diligence. To be a position of great responsibility. To be especially important in these times of trouble."

speaker: Teregus
text: "To have been many disagreements in town lately. To be much tension between the followers of the principles of the altars and the followers of The Fellowship. To have heard rumors of threats to the altars."

speaker: Teregus
text: "To be glad that Quan is now running our branch. To believe that he is misguided, but to be a much more reasonable gargoyle to deal with now that Runeb is gone."

speaker: Teregus
text: "To be wary of Fellowship ideals. To be ignoring the altars in their search for unity, and to be losing respect for the old ways. To be not bad. To tell you our branch is run by Quan and Runeb."

speaker: Teregus
text: "To be sorry that we have lost Runeb. Perhaps to be for the best. To be certainly overjoyed to have avoided damage to the altars."

speaker: Teregus
text: "To have heard that someone in town is planning to destroy the physical representations of the altars. To be not the same, of course, as actually destroying the basic principles of Control, Passion, and Diligence, but to be bad for us nonetheless. To be finding out for us who is planning this, if there is time, perhaps. To return to me with evidence when you determine course of action. To be very grateful for your assistance."

speaker: Teregus
text: "To have brought me something, some evidence about the rumors?"

speaker: Teregus
text: "To be wonderful! To see it, please."

speaker: Teregus
text: You hand him the note from Runeb that you found in Sarpling's shop.

speaker: Teregus
text: "Ah. Runeb. To have suspected as much. To be always reaching for more by the most violent means."

speaker: Teregus
text: He sighs.

speaker: Teregus
text: "To ask that you confront him with this evidence. To suggest that anything less will not reveal truth. To be prepared for anything, please, human, for to know not how he will react."

speaker: Teregus
text: He shakes his head.

speaker: Teregus
text: "To be not hopeful for a peaceful solution. To thank you for your assistance."

speaker: Teregus
text: "To have found nothing yet? Ah, well. To return, please, when anything unusual is found. To suggest that you confront the suspect as soon as you have a clue. To wish to stop him before any damage is done to the altars."

speaker: Teregus
text: "To be sad to have lost Quan to The Fellowship, human. To have been a good gargoyle when young, but to have fallen into bad company later. To have concentrated mostly on self-aggrandizement and hedonism in the last few years. To be a shame."

speaker: Teregus
text: "To have been a sad case. To have wished to have been able to save him. To always have been uncontrollable, but to have gotten worse in the last few years. To have seemed to want to start as many fights as possible. To have found a reason for using his strength against all those weaker when to have joined The Fellowship."

speaker: Teregus
text: He smiles sadly, but with obvious pride.

speaker: Teregus
text: "To have been a fine young gargoyle. The pride of us all. To wish to know who was responsible for his dishonorable end."

speaker: Teregus
text: "To miss him greatly. To have raised him from an egg. To have been rather vocal in his disagreements with The Fellowship. To have felt it safer for him to leave."

speaker: Teregus
text: He sighs, then looks up hopefully.

speaker: Teregus
text: "To have news of him?"

speaker: Teregus
text: "To be well?"

speaker: Teregus
text: "To be good. To be hoping to hear from him soon."

speaker: Teregus
text: "To be not well? To be terrible! To think there is anything to do to help?"

speaker: Teregus
text: "Ah. Too bad. To be waiting long for news from him."

speaker: Teregus
text: "To be too late? To mean what by too late? To tell me what has happened!"

speaker: Teregus
text: He seems very distraught.

speaker: Teregus
text: "To be murdered?"

speaker: Teregus
text: He takes a step back, stunned by the news.

speaker: Teregus
text: "To be murdered? To be unbelievable. To have no real enemies!"

speaker: Teregus
text: He sighs heavily.

speaker: Teregus
text: "To tell me, please, exactly what happened."

speaker: Teregus
text: You relate to him the particulars of Inamo's death. He sighs again.

speaker: Teregus
text: "To be such a waste of gargoyle life. To be grateful if you would send news if you discover who was responsible for wanting him dead."

speaker: Teregus
text: He is quiet for a few moments, getting accustomed to the situation.

speaker: Teregus
text: "To apologize. To need some time to grieve. Please to come back later."

speaker: Teregus
text: He turns away.

speaker: Teregus
text: "To be caretaker and group leader for the altars of the three principles. To wish to make a donation?"

speaker: Teregus
text: "Excellent. To which altar do you wish to donate?"

speaker: Teregus
text: "Ah. To donate next time, perhaps."

speaker: Teregus
text: "To be an excellent choice. To meditate at the shrine for you for a donation of 5 gold. To be willing to donate 5 gold?"

speaker: Teregus
text: "To meditate for you this evening, human. To wish you well in your journeys."

speaker: Teregus
text: "To not have 5 gold? To return	later when you have the gold. To meditate for your success on your journeys."

speaker: Teregus
text: He smiles kindly.

speaker: Teregus
text: "Ah. To have misunderstood. To apologize. To let me know if you change your mind."

speaker: Teregus
text: He looks disappointed.

speaker: Teregus
text: "To tell you goodbye for now, human. To return and be welcome."

speaker: Runeb
text: The gargoyle turns to you, frowning. He moves his massive hand to his mouth and use one finger to cross his lips. The Fellowship meeting is in progress.

speaker: Runeb
text: The gargoyle, obviously in a hurry, ignores you.

speaker: Runeb
text: The gargoyle gives you a menacing glare. Judging by his size, he would make a formidable foe.

speaker: Runeb
text: "To ask what you need?" says Runeb.

speaker: Runeb
text: "To be Runeb."

speaker: Runeb
text: "To be Fellowship clerk."

speaker: Runeb
text: "To mean `busy one,'" he says sarcastically.

speaker: Runeb
text: "To have a branch here. To meet at usual time each night."

speaker: Runeb
text: "To have more important things to do now. To ask me later, human."

speaker: Runeb
text: "To be sorry you know that. To need now to kill Sarpling." He grins at you.

speaker: Runeb
text: "To need now to kill you!"

speaker: Runeb
text: He waits for you to leave before he returns to what he was doing.

speaker: Quan
text: The gargoyle seems to be too busy conducting the Fellowship meeting to speak with you now.

speaker: Quan
text: You see a winged gargoyle. Noticing you, he turns and says, "To be welcome, human. To need assistance?"

speaker: Quan
text: "To ask how I may assist, human."

speaker: Quan
text: "To be the one named Quan."

speaker: Quan
text: "To have no meaning in Gargish. To be a special name, specific to me," he smiles.

speaker: Quan
text: "To head The Fellowship in Terfin."

speaker: Quan
text: "To be the inner voice of guidance that lives in all creatures. To become more distinct and frequent with stronger Fellowship ties."

speaker: Quan
text: "To be the only gargoyle city in Britannia. To have fewer gargoyles in the land than during your last visit to Britannia, human." He shakes his head.

speaker: Quan
text: "To have succumbed to the effects of disease and famine that have recently struck Britannia. To tell you that gargoyles breed less frequently, and we have not had the time to make up for losses in our population."

speaker: Quan
text: "To have new hope, however," he grins, "with The Fellowship."

speaker: Quan
text: "To suggest talking to Runeb, the Fellowship clerk, or Quaeven. To have jobs needing knowledge of others in Terfin." He grins apologetically.

speaker: Quan
text: "To be too busy to know all in Terfin."

speaker: Quan
text: "To hold meetings at 9 p.m., in unity with other branches, human. To be welcome at our meetings."

speaker: Quan
text: "To be a boon to gargoyles and humans alike. To have a philosophy to help all creatures of all races reach their highest level of potential."

speaker: Quan
text: "To be a boon to gargoyles and humans alike. To have a philosophy to help all creatures of all races reach their highest level of potential."

speaker: Quan
text: "To have just missed the human Fellowship officials who were here collecting funds. To have left for the Meditation Retreat near Serpent's Hold. To be sorry."

speaker: Quan
text: "To have not seen human Fellowship officials in many days."

speaker: Quan
text: An almost gleeful expression fills his visage.

speaker: Quan
text: "To be very similar to the altar of singularity. To have three principles called the Triad of Inner Strength. To apply three principles in unison to be more creative and happy."

speaker: Quan
text: "To see the similarity? To have control, passion, and diligence mesh into one -- singularity. To have Triad -- Strive for Unity, Trust your Brother, and Worthiness Precedes Reward -- applied in unison!"

speaker: Quan
text: "To understand not," he says, puzzled.

speaker: Quan
text: "To know nothing of this! To believe it not! To be not possible."

speaker: Quan
text: "To know that all members are content with their lives, and incapable of such acts, even if the altars be outdated."

speaker: Quan
text: "To tell you to speak with members themselves to see and believe."

speaker: Quan
text: "To need the Triad for proper application to the individual gargoyle -- or person!"

speaker: Quan
text: "To talk to Runeb, Sarpling, and Quaeven."

speaker: Quan
text: "To have been the clerk of The Fellowship here."

speaker: Quan
text: "To be the clerk of The Fellowship here."

speaker: Quan
text: "To sell magics and such at his shop."

speaker: Quan
text: "To be in charge of the learning center."

speaker: Quan
text: "To be impossible for Runeb to be responsible." He smiles kindly. "To be a practical joke."

speaker: Quan
text: "To be too heinous a plot for Runeb." He frowns. "To be some kind of bad joke."

speaker: Quan
text: "To hope you find unity."

speaker: Quan
text: The Cube did not vibrate once while speaking with Quan. You realize he is totally innocent of the dangerous powers above him.

speaker: Quaeven
text: "To have not the time to speak now. To talk after meeting."

speaker: Quaeven
text: "To have not the time to speak now. To hurry to Fellowship meeting."

speaker: Quaeven
text: The gargoyle, a contented grin on his face, greets you with a handshake.

speaker: Quaeven
text: "To express happiness at your return," says Quaeven.

speaker: Quaeven
text: "To be known as Quaeven, human."

speaker: Quaeven
text: "To mean `problem finder.' To be an observant one."

speaker: Quaeven
text: "To be master of the Recreation Facility and Learning Center. To be in charge of much information valuable to the gargoyle race."

speaker: Quaeven
text: "To be a good place for gargoyles to go to exercise their muscles. To have many resources available, including stuffed bags to punch and practice fighting skills."

speaker: Quaeven
text: "To be located in the same building as the Recreation Center. To provide an excellent atmosphere for strengthening gargoyle minds. To have a large supply of books and educational material."

speaker: Quaeven
text: ""To be a member, too." He holds up his medallion. To have needed The Fellowship to become happy."

speaker: Quaeven
text: "To want to know about the organization or the tenets?"

speaker: Quaeven
text: "To be a group of spiritual seekers striving to reach the highest levels of gargoyle potential. To share with all gargoyles and humans."

speaker: Quaeven
text: "To share tenets and material well-being."

speaker: Quaeven
text: "To support financially and personally a poorhouse in Paws. To organize feasts and festivals in Britannia to help morale. To be a much needed group by all gargoyles and men. To have needed The Fellowship myself!"

speaker: Quaeven
text: "To apply an optimistic order of thought through the Triad of Inner Strength."

speaker: Quaeven
text: "To be the three concepts of Strive for Unity, Trust your Brother, and Worthiness Precedes Reward."

speaker: Quaeven
text: "To have had poor life before The Fellowship. To have been pained, ignored, and mistreated by many."

speaker: Quaeven
text: "To be happy now in my new life and, to hope to hear the voice soon." His eyes widen in excitement. "To be bringing happiness to another's life soon."

speaker: Quaeven
text: "To be a good voice that will help me make choices, and to help win on Buccaneer's Den."

speaker: Quaeven
text: He continues on, excitedly.

speaker: Quaeven
text: "To be working on my first convert. To know the joy and well-being I will bring. To feel content and happy."

speaker: Quaeven
text: "To need a little more persuasion," he looks down, "but to be almost ready to join!"

speaker: Quaeven
text: "To be Betra, the provisioner. To feel confident he will join soon."

speaker: Quaeven
text: "To hope for your well-being and happiness."

speaker: Silamo
text: You see a frowning gargoyle.

speaker: Silamo
text: "To ask what you need, human," says Silamo.

speaker: Silamo
text: "To be named `Silamo.'"

speaker: Silamo
text: "To know my name if I were winged." He scowls at you.

speaker: Silamo
text: "To be the gardener," he shrugs, "nothing more."

speaker: Silamo
text: He does not seem to be interested in speaking with you.

speaker: Silamo
text: He stares at you for a moment.

speaker: Silamo
text: "To be right, human."

speaker: Silamo
text: "To feel I am treated less for an absence of wings. To see Quaeven treated better since joining The Fellowship. To be devoted to the altar of singularity. But, perhaps to change if The Fellowship cares not about wings."

speaker: Silamo
text: "To be also without wings, but to be respected as if he were winged."

speaker: Silamo
text: "To see many others include him in many events from which I am excluded. To know others include him in many more decision-making councils, too."

speaker: Silamo
text: "Gargoyles in The Fellowship."

speaker: Silamo
text: "To get back to work."

speaker: Sarpling
text: The gargoyle is too involved with the Fellowship meeting to talk to you at this moment.

speaker: Sarpling
text: "To be unable to talk now. To see me after the Fellowship meeting." He continues on his way.

speaker: Sarpling
text: You see a very distraught gargoyle.

speaker: Sarpling
text: "To give you greetings, human."

speaker: Sarpling
text: "To be able to call me Sarpling."

speaker: Sarpling
text: "To provide various magics and items in Terfin."

speaker: Sarpling
text: "To be the city in which you are located. To be the city of gargoyles."

speaker: Sarpling
text: "To know Quan is the Fellowship leader. To believe he gives good guidance." He appears thoughtful.

speaker: Sarpling
text: "To have spoken to Draxinusom?"

speaker: Sarpling
text: "To see Forbrak or Quaeven, then. To know they see all the citizens regularly."

speaker: Sarpling
text: "To see first, Draxinusom. To be leader of the city. To know many of the residents."

speaker: Sarpling
text: "To be an important part of my life. To support The Fellowship fully."

speaker: Sarpling
text: "To know nothing about the altars. To wonder what you mean?"

speaker: Sarpling
text: A surprised expression, mixed with fear, covers his face.

speaker: Sarpling
text: "To be all Runeb's decisions! To be all Runeb's doing! To want nothing to do with the destruction of the altars, or with the assassination plot!"

speaker: Sarpling
text: "To not already know about the plot?" he wails.

speaker: Sarpling
text: "To have caused problems this time, Sarpling," he says to himself. "To have brought much trouble!"

speaker: Sarpling
text: "To tell you Runeb wanted to frame Quan for the altars. To kill Quan if plan failed, and to be in control of The Fellowship in Terfin. To be Runeb's goal."

speaker: Sarpling
text: "To be in much danger you and me!"

speaker: Sarpling
text: "To want reagents or jewelry and potions?"

speaker: Sarpling
text: "To sell you things when my shop is open."

speaker: Sarpling
text: "To give you farewell, human."

speaker: Forbrak
text: "To greet you, human," the gargoyle says to Dupre. "To ask how well the study is progressing?"

speaker: Dupre
text: "Why 'tis progressing nicely, friend Forbrak."

speaker: Shamino
text: "-What- study?"

speaker: Dupre
text: "Why, er, surely thou hast heard of the famous guides compiled for Brommer!"

speaker: Shamino
text: "Aye, I have. But I'll be tarred if there is one detailing various drinking establishments!"

speaker: Dupre
text: "Well, yes, er, 'tis, ah, something new. Now, how about a drink!"

speaker: Shamino
text: "New? 'Tis about as new as my backside...," mutters Shamino.

speaker: Forbrak
text: The gargoyle tending bar lifts a tankard to you.

speaker: Forbrak
text: "To ask what brings you to this fine establishment?" asks Forbrak.

speaker: Forbrak
text: "To be Forbrak."

speaker: Forbrak
text: "To mean `strong arm' in the language of the gargoyles."

speaker: Forbrak
text: He gestures around the room with an open hand.

speaker: Forbrak
text: "To serve food and drink at the Hall of Refreshment."

speaker: Forbrak
text: "To ask you to please come back when my shop is open."

speaker: Forbrak
text: "To know many of the residents in town, and some of the troubles."

speaker: Forbrak
text: "To know of only two. To see the conflict between the shrines and The Fellowship, and to know of the struggles of the wingless ones."

speaker: Forbrak
text: "To believe there are disagreements between the old philosophy and the new. To expect no violence, but to ask you to seek the trainer and healer. To know they are observant and may have seen something. To also suggest you speak with members of The Fellowship."

speaker: Forbrak
text: "To recommend you talk to their leader and their clerk."

speaker: Forbrak
text: "To watch wingless friends be discontented with their lot. To wonder why, but to never ask. To talk to the healer and the trainer. To expect they will have seen evidence if there is evidence to be seen."

speaker: Forbrak
text: "To know many gargoyles. To want to know about some of them?"

speaker: Forbrak
text: "To be sure you already know our leader. To wonder if you have met Teregus, or the learning center head."

speaker: Forbrak
text: "To be more practical, you may need the provisioner," he nods his head.

speaker: Forbrak
text: "To tell you about them later if you wish."

speaker: Forbrak
text: "To be named Inforlem. To be very strong."

speaker: Forbrak
text: "To be named Inmanilem."

speaker: Forbrak
text: "To be very friendly. To be called Quan."

speaker: Forbrak
text: "To be extremely violent." He shakes his head. "To be named Runeb, which means `red mist.' To be all that he leaves of a foe after combat."

speaker: Forbrak
text: "To be dead now, though."

speaker: Forbrak
text: "To be a wonderful place to gain knowledge and exercise. To be managed by a gargoyle name Quaeven. To be very educated, this Quaeven. Also, to be wingless, like Silamo."

speaker: Forbrak
text: "To be called Betra. To be one of two shopkeepers. To say the other is Sarpling."

speaker: Forbrak
text: "To be a sage. To be very well-educated, like Quaeven. To live here a long time."

speaker: Forbrak
text: "To be the gardener who lives to the east of the mountains."

speaker: Forbrak
text: "To know him little, and to have never been in his shop, and, therefore, to be unable to tell you what he sells. To know his name means `snake tongue.'"

speaker: Forbrak
text: "To wish you well, human."

speaker: Betra
text: The gargoyle welcomes you by making a sweeping motion with his open hand.

speaker: Betra
text: "To welcome you again, human," says Betra.

speaker: Betra
text: "To be named Betra. To be new to Terfin?"

speaker: Betra
text: "To tell you to talk to Teregus, the sage or Forbrak, the tavernkeeper, for information about town. To help with building locations and residents."

speaker: Betra
text: "To welcome you back to Terfin."

speaker: Betra
text: "To be the word for `small valor.'"

speaker: Betra
text: "To be the seller of provisions."

speaker: Betra
text: "To be the town set aside for us gargoyles who wish to reside in our own culture."

speaker: Betra
text: "To have many things unique to our race -- other than our appearance -- that distinguish us from humans. To be different, but also equal."

speaker: Betra
text: "To have been put here by the humans. To be permitted to leave, and also to reside elsewhere, but to know that many humans do not like us."

speaker: Betra
text: "To be very ironic. To say that the only town with an equal number of humans and gargoyles is the one where most racial conflicts occur."

speaker: Betra
text: He shrugs. "To have been unwise, perhaps, to put so many differences together. To be sad times."

speaker: Betra
text: "To sell to you during the hours of 9 in the morning and 6 in the evening. To be sorry, but to sell nothing before or after those hours."

speaker: Betra
text: He smiles at the mention of the name.

speaker: Betra
text: "To be a likable young gargoyle."

speaker: Betra
text: "To join The Fellowship?" He shakes his head. "To be an organization not for me. To be quite happy as I am, devoted to the altars. To believe Quaeven to have been misled by the others in The Fellowship. To not trust them, especially Sarpling."

speaker: Betra
text: "To believe that there is deceit from The Fellowship, and to expect that is not what it appears. To believe promises of happiness made when Quaeven first joined came true from Quaeven, himself, not The Fellowship."

speaker: Betra
text: "To trust him as far as I could throw him, and to certainly throw him as far as I could."

speaker: Betra
text: "To have heard the rumors about destroying the altars. To be upset, but to have no evidence."

speaker: Betra
text: "To know that only two gargoyles have easy access to such weapons. To be one of those gargoyles, and to know Sarpling is the other."

speaker: Betra
text: "To wish you safe travels, human."

speaker: Martingo
text: You see a nobleman, all alone, with a demented gleam in his eye.

speaker: Martingo
text: "Who in blazes art thou?" the man asks. His attitude is that of someone who was just interrupted from something terribly important.

speaker: Martingo
text: Martingo shakes your hand but acts thoroughly disinterested. "I'm thrilled."

speaker: Martingo
text: He turns to his right and speaks to no one.

speaker: Martingo
text: "What? Oh, really! I do not think <PLAYER_NAME> looks particularly brainless. We shall have to see, shall we not?"

speaker: Martingo
text: He turns back to you and grins.

speaker: Martingo
text: "Of course thou art! And I am the evil spirit of Mondain, come back to wreak havoc over all Britannia. Funny, thou dost not look like an Avatar -- thou dost look like a fool."

speaker: Martingo
text: "What can I do for thee, Miss Fool?"

speaker: Martingo
text: "What can I do for thee, Mr. Fool?"

speaker: Martingo
text: He turns to his right and speaks to no one.

speaker: Martingo
text: "What? Oh, really! Thou dost think this Avatar looks like the real thing? I doubt it, Lucinda. I doubt it very much."

speaker: Martingo
text: He turns back to you and grins.

speaker: Martingo
text: "What'chu want?" Martingo asks, belligerently.

speaker: Martingo
text: The nobleman looks at you with impatience. "I am Martingo, the Sultan of Spektran. Is that all right with thee?" He rolls his eyes. He turns to his right side and whispers again to an imaginary person, "I believe we have an ignoramus on our hands."

speaker: Martingo
text: "I am the Sultan of Spektran! What, is thy brain the size of a pea? Do not answer, 'twas a rhetorical question."

speaker: Martingo
text: He turns to his left side and whispers to no one, "Dost thou not think her brain is the size of a pea? I do!" He giggles conspiratorially with his invisible friend.

speaker: Martingo
text: He turns to his left side and whispers again to an imaginary person, "Dost thou not think his brain is the	size of a pea? I do!" He giggles conspiratorially with his invisible friend.

speaker: Martingo
text: Martingo then pulls out a banana and begins to peel it.

speaker: Martingo
text: "Come on, do not insult mine intelligence. Surely thou dost know what a Sultan is! Canst not thou see mine harem?"

speaker: Martingo
text: "Lovely, are they not?"

speaker: Martingo
text: Martingo looks bewildered. "Then thou must have thine eyes examined! I am surrounded by ten..." He looks around quickly. "No, -eleven- beautiful women!"

speaker: Martingo
text: "Each day I enjoy a different one. Thou canst not imagine how much fun being a Sultan really is!" He leans over and kisses an invisible cheek. "Today, I am enjoying Lucinda." He grins broadly.

speaker: Martingo
text: Martingo looks you up and down lecherously. "Hmmm. Wouldst thou like to join mine harem?"

speaker: Martingo
text: Your answer takes Martingo by surprise. "Thou wouldst?" He looks around nervously. "Oh, uhm, I had better consult mine astrologer about this matter. I shall get back to thee, all right?"

speaker: Martingo
text: "Pity."

speaker: Martingo
text: "'Tis the island thou dost stand upon!" He turns to the invisible person on his left and whispers, "Thou art correct -- this person really is a fool!"

speaker: Martingo
text: Martingo turns back to you. "As I said, I am the Sultan here. I am the master of all of these subjects." He gestures	around the room.

speaker: Iolo
text: Iolo whispers to you. "This fellow is quite daft. Be careful."

speaker: Martingo
text: "She is beautiful, is she not?" Martingo leans over and sticks his tongue in an ear that isn't there.

speaker: Martingo
text: "Oh, forgive my manners! Wouldst thou like a banana?"

speaker: Martingo
text: "Well, it shall cost thee 3 gold coins. Still want one?"

speaker: Martingo
text: "Here thou art." Martingo hands you a banana and takes your gold. He turns to 'Lucinda' and whispers, "That rotter took my last banana!"

speaker: Martingo
text: "Thou dost have wheat for brains! Thou hast not room for a single banana!"

speaker: Martingo
text: "Broke, art thou? Too bad." Martingo sniffs. "Well, I am very rich, I must say."

speaker: Martingo
text: "That's a relief. I only had one left."

speaker: Martingo
text: "That's a relief. I only had one left."

speaker: Martingo
text: "I already sold thee my last banana!"

speaker: Martingo
text: Martingo looks suspicious. "Art thou wanting to steal mine Ethereal Ring?" He turns to his imaginary friend and whispers, "Thou wert right. Our guest looks like a thief." He turns back to you and smiles. "Yes, I do have an Ethereal Ring. I purchased it from the King of the Gargoyles. What was his name?" He leans toward the invisible companion on his right. "What? Oh yes, Draxinusom. I knew it all the time." He turns back to you. "It is in my vault."

speaker: Martingo
text: Martingo's eyes light up. "My vault is the most protected vault in all Britannia. No one, and I repeat, -no one- can steal anything from my vault. I have many fine treasures there." He turns to 'Lucinda' and bites an nonexistent ear lobe.

speaker: Martingo
text: "I collect magical items. The vault is full of them. Including this ring thou dost mention."

speaker: Martingo
text: "The vault's security is my secret. Feel free to try and enter it. In fact, I dare thee! If thou canst succeed in getting inside, thou art welcome to take anything!" Martingo laughs. "All thou dost need is the key!" He laughs with his imaginary harem, as if they were all laughing with him. "I'm sure thou wilt find it!" He breaks up, laughing so hard that tears begin to fall down his cheeks.

speaker: Martingo
text: "Fine. Go away. It shall do thee good!"

speaker: Menion
text: The large, muscle-bound man smiles pleasantly at you.

speaker: Menion
text: "Greetings, <HONORIFIC>," says Menion.

speaker: Menion
text: "I am Menion, <HONORIFIC>." He shakes your hand.

speaker: Menion
text: "I am a trainer. I help warriors become bigger and stronger and better fighters. I also forge swords to match the strength in my students' arms."

speaker: Menion
text: "I have taught many a warrior how to use his -- or her -- force against an opponent."

speaker: Menion
text: "Yes, <HONORIFIC>. The key to effective fighting is striking hard and accurately at one's foe."

speaker: Menion
text: "Physical strength permits the attacker a better chance of penetrating the other fighter's armour. Obviously, in a lethal combat, that is an important objective."

speaker: Menion
text: "Needless to say, some targets on an individual are better than others. 'Tis always best to hit something that will either seriously incapacitate one's foe, or create enough pain to distract him."

speaker: Menion
text: "I will train thee for 45 gold. Wilt thou pay?"

speaker: Menion
text: "Fine."

speaker: Menion
text: "Perhaps this would be a more appropriate topic when I am at work."

speaker: Menion
text: "Dost thou wish to make a sword?"

speaker: Menion
text: "Perhaps sometime when thou hast more time."

speaker: Menion
text: He smiles. "I would be very happy to show thee the steps necessary to create a very fine blade." He quickly jots down a few things on a scroll and turns to give it to you.

speaker: Menion
text: "May thy blade be sturdy and sharp!"

speaker: Menion
text: "Perhaps when thou hast fewer things to occupy thy pack, I can give this to thee."

speaker: Menion
text: "I can help thee with that when I am at work."

speaker: Menion
text: "May the strength in thine arms always match the strength of thy will."

speaker: Pendaran
text: You are greeted with a stern look on this man's face.

speaker: Pendaran
text: "^<HONORIFIC>." He nods at you.

speaker: Pendaran
text: "Thou mayest call me Sir Pendaran."

speaker: Pendaran
text: "I am a knight here in Serpent's Hold. 'Tis my job to help protect the citizens of Britannia."

speaker: Pendaran
text: "Aye, <HONORIFIC>. Britannia can be a dangerous place outside town boundaries. Especially now that the ruling faction have gone soft!"

speaker: Pendaran
text: "Well, I mean Lord British and his advisors."

speaker: Pendaran
text: "Though I'd follow the land's ideals to the ends of the land, I find it difficult to accept how poor the conditions are in Britannia. Brigands populate the land, disease overruns the towns, and corruption fills the councils. Were it not for The Fellowship, I would be hard pressed to avoid falling on mine own blade, despite how dishonorable an act that may seem."

speaker: Pendaran
text: "A noble group of people who strive to instill a greater sense of spiritual knowledge throughout all of Britannia. 'Twill be but a matter of time, <HONORIFIC>, before all people will see the wisdom."

speaker: Pendaran
text: "I live here in the hold with my lady."

speaker: Pendaran
text: "Her name is Jehanne, <HONORIFIC>," he says suspiciously. "She is the provisioner."

speaker: Pendaran
text: "Terrible shame, <HONORIFIC>." He eyes you coldly.

speaker: Pendaran
text: "What! Thou art accusing me! Preposterous. I had nothing to do with it!"

speaker: Pendaran
text: He shakes his head.

speaker: Pendaran
text: "Thou wouldst take the word of a woman over that of a knight of the Hold? Thou art lower than a worm!" He glares at you for a moment, and then his expression changes.

speaker: Pendaran
text: "All right," he says, "I am the one	who defaced the statue, but only because the government has become so worthless and soft!" He quickly turns away from	you, ashamed.

speaker: Pendaran
text: "If thou dost think it best," he sighs, "tomorrow I shall beg forgiveness from my fellow knights."

speaker: Pendaran
text: Nodding his agreement, he sighs again, and turns away.

speaker: Pendaran
text: "No, no, <HONORIFIC>. Thou hast shown me the way. I must repent." He turns away from you to reflect on his decision.

speaker: Pendaran
text: "Good day to thee, <HONORIFIC>."

speaker: Jehanne
text: The woman greets you with a curtsey.

speaker: Jehanne
text: "Good day, <HONORIFIC>," says Lady Jehanne.

speaker: Jehanne
text: "I am the Lady Jehanne, <HONORIFIC>."

speaker: Jehanne
text: "I am the provisioner of Serpent's Hold."

speaker: Jehanne
text: "And," she adds, "I also have a ship for sale shouldst thou be interested in that."

speaker: Jehanne
text: "Well, it was once the magnificent `Constellation.' However, 'twas destroyed by the ship's captain, himself, to prevent it from falling into the hands of attacking pirates.
