What little remained was rebuilt into an even finer ship, `The Dragon's Breath?' Art thou interested in purchasing it for 600 gold?"

speaker: Jehanne
text: "Here is thy deed."

speaker: Jehanne

text: "I am the director of this Meditation Retreat for Fellowship members."

speaker: Ian
text: "I manage the various activities and lead the initiates in their exercises in meditation."

speaker: Ian
text: "The activities of the retreat consist of philosophical training and studies."

speaker: Ian
text: "The members must all grow to hear and understand the voice which guides them down the path of Inner Strength. The exercises in meditation accelerate this process."

speaker: Ian
text: "It is that voice which one hears inside. We all have the capability of hearing it. Some are able to hear it quite easily and do not have to attend sessions here at the Meditation Retreat. Others, however, find it more difficult to hear the voice. Then they require study at the Retreat."

speaker: Ian
text: "It was set up by The Fellowship so that new members can attend and learn more about our group, get in touch with themselves, and help them to become better brothers in The Fellowship. Most of the work is done inside the barrier."

speaker: Ian
text: "Most of the people who come to The Fellowship are wrestling with the failures in their lives. They are essentially	afraid of themselves. Here at the Meditation Retreat people learn to believe in themselves. And they build up that belief by learning how to best apply the philosophy of The	Fellowship to their lives."

speaker: Ian
text: "It was set up to keep out those who are not members. Inside the barrier, Fellowship members find it much easier to hear their inner voice. Each member is given a key which they may use at any time."

speaker: Ian
text: "Ah, but thou art not a true Fellowship member! Thou art wearing a medallion falsely. I cannot let thee inside. Goodbye."

speaker: Ian
text: "Oh, wouldst thou like to meditate with us, fellow brother?"

speaker: Ian
text: "Then here is thy key. Be happy! Oh, one more thing. There is a rule which must be followed."

speaker: Ian
text: "Oh. Then I cannot give thee a key."

speaker: Ian
text: "Art thou a Fellowship member?"

speaker: Ian
text: "<VAR>must go to Britain and speak with Batlin at our headquarters there. Only he can properly initiate thee into The Fellowship."

speaker: Ian
text: "Do not venture into the cave which thou wilt find inside the barrier. The cave is off-limits to attendees."

speaker: Ian
text: "Alas, thou hast just missed them. My good friends Elizabeth and Abraham were here delivering funds. I believe they have gone from here to Buccaneer's Den."

speaker: Ian
text: "I have not seen them in quite some time."

speaker: Ian
text: "Goodbye."

speaker: Cador
text: You see a broad-shouldered man with a solemn look about him.

speaker: Cador
text: "Yes, <HONORIFIC>?" says Cador.

speaker: Cador
text: The man shakes your hand. "I am Cador."

speaker: Cador
text: "And thy name is?"

speaker: Cador
text: "What? Dost thou mean to tell me that thou art the one who brought those gargoyles to our precious land?" He turns quite angry.

speaker: Cador
text: "Daemon lover!"

speaker: Cador
text: "I am happy to make thine acquaintance, <HONORIFIC>."

speaker: Cador
text: "I oversee the local branch of the Britannian Mining Company in Vesper. We mine many different minerals."

speaker: Cador
text: "Gold and lead."

speaker: Cador
text: "That is the name of our town. Liana at town hall can give thee any more information that thou mightest need, but I have lived here with my family since the branch opened."

speaker: Cador
text: "It is a wonderful organization. They perform many works of charity and special events -- parades and such."  He points to his medallion. "As thou canst see, I am a member. I fully believe in the triad of inner strength."

speaker: Cador
text: "As a matter of fact, two Fellowship officials were just here. They said it was important to see how a town's economy worked before starting a branch in that town. Dost thou realize what that means?" He smiles proudly. "They are going to build a Fellowship branch here in Vesper."

speaker: Cador
text: "Those are The Fellowship's three basic principles: Strive for Unity, Trust thy Brother, and Worthiness Precedes Reward."

speaker: Cador
text: "They were the two Fellowship officials that were here! They only stayed for a minute or two. I have no idea where they are now."

speaker: Cador
text: "I work with Mara and a gargoyle named Lap-Lem."

speaker: Cador
text: "She is a fantastic worker. Better than most men I have mined with."

speaker: Cador
text: "Well, for a gargoyle, he is not too lazy. He works much harder than that other one who left, Anmanivas. But I would fain let him go if we did not need the extra hand."

speaker: Cador
text: "She keeps the records at town hall."

speaker: Cador
text: "Yes, my wife, Yvella, and my daughter, Catherine."

speaker: Cador
text: "It has been a pleasure, <HONORIFIC>."

speaker: Mara
text: You see a well-muscled woman who lifts her head in acknowledgement of your presence.

speaker: Mara
text: "Yes, <HONORIFIC>?"

speaker: Mara
text: The woman grabs your hand and shakes vigorously. "Hello. M'name's Mara."

speaker: Mara
text: "What is thine?"

speaker: Mara
text: "The Avatar!" she shouts angrily. "Why thou art the one responsible for bringing those wretched gargoyles into our fine land!"

speaker: Mara
text: "'Tis good to meet thee!"

speaker: Mara
text: She flexes proudly, "I am a miner in Vesper."

speaker: Mara
text: "This used to be a pleasant town," she looks around, apparently checking if anyone is near, "'til the gargoyles became so unruly. Now most of us have to spend far too much time wondering when the gargoyles will decide they want to kill us."

speaker: Mara
text: She shrugs. "There is naught to say, except that they are a menace. This town would be a much better place without them."

speaker: Mara
text: "Well, I know Cador feels as I do, as does his wife. I have heard the mayor express his concern about them. I don't really know his clerk, Liana."

speaker: Mara
text: "Yvella is a lovely woman. She spends her days caring for their daughter, Catherine."

speaker: Mara
text: "I have only seen her a few times. I do not know her well enough to say this, but I think she is angry about something, for she is always in a bad mood."

speaker: Mara
text: "He is in charge of managing the mines. Does a fair job, too. He usually joins me at the Gilded Lizard."

speaker: Mara
text: "His name is Auston. I like him, but I suspect that Liana is the one who truly keeps Vesper in order."

speaker: Mara
text: "That is the tavern here in Vesper. Yongi's the barkeeper. He serves a passing fair tankard of ale."

speaker: Mara
text: Mara shakes your hand and slaps you on the back, saying, "Fare thee well, friend!"

speaker: Zaksam
text: A strong, powerful man looks at you and nods acknowledgment.

speaker: Zaksam
text: "What can I do for thee?" asks Zaksam.

speaker: Zaksam
text: "I am Zaksam," he states proudly.

speaker: Zaksam
text: "I teach others to be strong fighters. I am a trainer here in Vesper."

speaker: Zaksam
text: "I have taught here for many years. I like the town, but I am not too fond of some of the residents."

speaker: Zaksam
text: "The land to the northeast is a bit dry, but the oasis and nearby shores give us plenty of water for drinking and bathing."

speaker: Zaksam
text: "Most of us are respectable, but there are a few that I wonder about. Blorn and the mayor, for example."

speaker: Zaksam
text: "'Tis not that I do not trust him. I just wonder about his ability to run the town. His name is Auston. Talk to him and see for thyself what thou thinkest. Better yet, talk to his clerk, Liana."

speaker: Zaksam
text: "That one I do not like a bit. I do not trust him. He reminds me of those gargoyles."

speaker: Zaksam
text: "What is there to say, but do not let them get too close or they will rob thee. Any day now they may try to use violence to take over the town. The mayor himself has asked that I fight if necessary. Though I have no fear of death, that is a battle I do not look forward to."

speaker: Zaksam
text: "I have already heard that some of my fellow residents have had things stolen by those wretched creatures."

speaker: Zaksam
text: "As thou must surely know, all gargoyles are prone to senseless fits of violence. 'Twould be quite natural to expect them to use it for their own selfish gain."

speaker: Zaksam
text: "I can train thee for 40 gold. Is this all right?"

speaker: Zaksam
text: "Perhaps next time, <HONORIFIC>."

speaker: Zaksam
text: "I can train thee when I am at my training hall, <HONORIFIC>. Please feel free to see me when it is open."

speaker: Zaksam
text: "May thy strength be thy guide."

speaker: Eldroth
text: A very neat, well-groomed, kindly man stands before you.

speaker: Eldroth
text: "Greetings, <HONORIFIC>. How may I help thee?"

speaker: Eldroth
text: He smiles at you. "Ah, excellent. Thou art not afraid to ask question. Remember, there are no stupid questions, only dumb ones. My name is Eldroth, <HONORIFIC>."

speaker: Eldroth
text: "I, my friend, am the provisioner. And, if I may be immodest, also a counselor for Vesper. Perhaps I can someday give thee advice, <HONORIFIC>. For remember, that which does not kill us, makes us wounded."

speaker: Eldroth
text: "Yes, <HONORIFIC>, this town is full of wonderful people to whom I have given advice."

speaker: Eldroth
text: "Early to bed, early to rise, makes Jack a dull boy."

speaker: Eldroth
text: "Thou wishest to make a purchase. Excellent. But remember, a gold piece saved is a gold piece not spent."

speaker: Eldroth
text: "Perhaps thou couldst wait until my shop is open, <HONORIFIC>."

speaker: Eldroth
text: "About whom doth thou wish to know? Auston? The gargoyles? Liana? Cador? Perhaps Yongi?"

speaker: Eldroth
text: "Liana is a very fine young woman who clerks at the townhall."

speaker: Eldroth
text: "He is the bartender at the Glided Gizzard." He stops, shakes his head, and then corrects himself. "I mean the Lilded Lizard," he frowns. "No, that's the Gilded Lizard. Yes that's it!"

speaker: Eldroth
text: "Cador oversees the mines. He and his wife, Yvella, have a lovely daughter named Catherine."

speaker: Eldroth
text: "The mayor? I would have thought thou wouldst have met him by now, <HONORIFIC>. He is performing an excellent job. Thou mayest not realize this," he blushes, "but 'tis I who suggested he run for the office."

speaker: Eldroth
text: "I fear they will stage an uprising. I know Auston holds the same thoughts, for very recently he approached me and asked for my guidance to prepare for just such an incident. I will warn thee just as I warned him. Always remember, <HONORIFIC>, the best defense is a good defense!"

speaker: Eldroth
text: "Farewell, <HONORIFIC>. Never forget, the grass is always greener when it rains."

speaker: Yongi
text: "Ah, me good friend, Dupre. What kinna do fer ye this fine day?"

speaker: Dupre
text: "Ah, master Yongi, always ready to offer a tankard of thy finest."

speaker: Yongi
text: Tending the bar is a jovial-looking man. "Welcome ta the Gilded Lizard."

speaker: Yongi
text: "Welcome back ta the Gilded Lizard. What may I do fer ye?" asks Yongi.

speaker: Yongi
text: "Me name is Yongi, <HONORIFIC>."

speaker: Yongi
text: "And ye are?"

speaker: Yongi
text: "Aye, <HONORIFIC>. Right ye are. If ye dinna care ta tell me, I don't mind a bit." He winks.

speaker: Yongi
text: "Welcome ta me tavern, <PLAYER_NAME>."

speaker: Yongi
text: "Right ye are, <HONORIFIC>. There's no need ta tell anyone yer name."

speaker: Yongi
text: "Why, I tend me bar. And lend me ear ta the customers," he adds, touching his right ear for emphasis.

speaker: Yongi
text: "Why, I wouldna wanna live anyplace else. 'Course, this town would be a better place if we could rid ourselves of those jackals, the gargoyles."

speaker: Yongi
text: "Gargoyles! What about them? They be the vilest, evilest, cruelest, most despicable things ever ta crawl upon this great land. I kinna tell ye too well ta stay away from them. I kin only imagine whata fine town this'd be if there weren't na more gargoyles. 'Course, I know those dogs are probably sayin' the same about us. Everybody knows they're gonna come an' kill allus in our sleep one evenin'."

speaker: Yongi
text: "Why, only the other day one attacked Blorn. G'won, ask him about it."

speaker: Yongi
text: "Well, all I really know in Vesper are me regulars: Cador, Mara, and Blorn. Ye might be wantin' ta talk to Auston, the mayor, or his clerk, Liana. Ah, now there's a fine, young lass." He winks at you.

speaker: Yongi
text: "He used ta come here every night, 'til he was killed in a brawl." The bartender's eyes narrow as he talks.

speaker: Yongi
text: "He be in here every night after work. Good man, hard worker."

speaker: Yongi
text: "She worked with Cador at the mines. She was more man than most men, that one was. An' she died like it, too -- in a brawl here at the tavern!" He says, eyeing you suspiciously.

speaker: Yongi
text: "She works with Cador at the mines. Hard as stone, that one. She be more man than most of the men in town."

speaker: Yongi
text: "There be one who knows what's what. He knows what be wrong with this town! Gargoyles! That is what be wrong. He hates 'em, 'e does."

speaker: Yongi
text: "He was even accosted by one of those jackals not too long ago. Ask 'im about it, why don't ye."

speaker: Yongi
text: "Be ye wantin' food or drink?"

speaker: Yongi
text: "May the road rise up ta meet ye!"

speaker: Blorn
text: The man before you narrows his eyes to slits as he sees you.

speaker: Blorn
text: Blorn sighs heavily. "Why dost thou bother me now?"

speaker: Blorn
text: "Blorn, if thou must know."

speaker: Blorn
text: "I don't believe I wish to tell thee."

speaker: Blorn
text: A growl escapes his throat.

speaker: Blorn
text: "What about the bloody gargoyles? Don't tell me thou art a gargoyle lover."

speaker: Blorn
text: "Thou art disgusting, swine!" He spits on your boot.

speaker: Blorn
text: "That is good, my friend."

speaker: Blorn
text: A sudden inspiration seems to flash across his face.

speaker: Blorn
text: "Perhaps thou canst help me. As thou undoubtedly knowest, I was set upon by a cruel gargoyle not too long ago. He nearly took my life!"

speaker: Blorn
text: "'Twould be a great honor, <HONORIFIC>, if thou wouldst agree to avenge me! Art thou willing?"

speaker: Blorn
text: "I thank thee, <HONORIFIC>, thank thee. But I must warn thee, he is a very violent gargoyle. His name is Lap-Lem, which means `man slayer.' And, do not mention my name, for he hates me more than any other human and would surely attack thee without provocation if my name were to be mentioned."

speaker: Blorn
text: "Fine, <HONORIFIC>. Thou art nothing more than a coward." He shakes his head.

speaker: Blorn
text: He glares at you for a moment, then shrugs, muttering, "It's not like he earned it honestly or anything..."

speaker: Blorn
text: "Here! I hope it strangles him!" He thrusts the amulet into your palm. "And I hope he bloody strangles thee, too!"

speaker: Blorn
text: "Thou dost not even have room for it! Get thee away, thou son of a jackal!"

speaker: Blorn
text: "Thou hast killed the jackal?"

speaker: Blorn
text: "Wonderful! Thou art truly a trusted friend. I thank thee for thine assistance!" He grins at you.

speaker: Blorn
text: "Well, I am sure thou wilt have time soon enough, for he will surely head this way to attack me again."

speaker: Blorn
text: He gives a slight nod and a quiet grunt, and returns to his business.

speaker: Auston
text: You see a middle-aged man with a furrowed brow, as if he is constantly worried.

speaker: Auston
text: "How may I help thee, <HONORIFIC>?"

speaker: Auston
text: "Please call me Auston."

speaker: Auston
text: He sighs before responding. "I am the Mayor of Vesper."

speaker: Auston
text: "It was a pleasant place in days past. But now, <HONORIFIC>, the turmoil between our people and those gargoyles has caused many problems."

speaker: Auston
text: "I am worried that the gargoyles may get restless and attack us. Blorn has not helped things." He points to his chest. "I am the one charged with maintaining order here. If there is not any, it will be my responsibility. I have asked Eldroth what to do in case of an uprising and I am trying to plan accordingly."

speaker: Auston
text: "I don't trust them any more than thou dost, <PLAYER_NAME>, but, officially, they are citizens, too. I am afraid they may try to forcefully gain control of the town someday."

speaker: Auston
text: "She is my clerk. She is very efficient. I couldn't govern Vesper without her."

speaker: Auston
text: "I try to stay in touch with as many of the citizens as I can, but I do not know all of them that well. I know Cador<VAR>has been in charge of the local branch of the Britannian Mining Company ever since it opened. He is married to Yvella. I believe they are members of that Fellowship organization."

speaker: Auston
text: "Of course, there's Eldroth, and a trainer, and also, Yongi. And," he scowls as he adds the last one, "Blorn. Also, thou shouldst speak with Liana. She knows a few of the people that I do not. I am afraid that I do not know everyone as well as I should."

speaker: Auston
text: "I would have thought thou wouldst know." He strokes his beard.

speaker: Auston
text: "Cador was slain in a fight at the Gilded Lizard. 'Twas the first act of this kind ever in Vesper. Quite odd."

speaker: Auston
text: "Eldroth acts as our counselor. He has been giving advice to the people of our town for... well, longer than I can remember. He owns the provisions shop."

speaker: Auston
text: "Zaksam is our trainer. He can teach thee how to better defend thyself. Should the gargoyles cause trouble, I am comforted that he would defend our side."

speaker: Auston
text: "He serves drinks at the tavern. Many have claimed him to be the best bartender on this side of the desert. People come from all around Britannia to speak with him," he says proudly.

speaker: Auston
text: "I am not sure what to think about him. I do not know what he does for a living, but I know the gargoyles hate him more than they do the rest of us. I am frightened of what will happen, since it is obvious that he holds mutual feelings towards them."

speaker: Auston
text: "They are Fellowship members. They were just here to see about starting a branch in Vesper. I imagine we will allow it. I believe the couple have gone to Moonglow. They said they were on their way there to conduct a training session for the branch leader there. But I do know that they were going to stop at the Britannian Mining Company branch on the way out of town. I do not know why."

speaker: Auston
text: "I have not seen that Fellowship couple for many, many days. I have no idea where they could be now."

speaker: Auston
text: "Goodbye, <HONORIFIC>."

speaker: Liana
text: You see a short woman with a distracted look on her face.

speaker: Liana
text: "What is thy concern?"

speaker: Liana
text: Breaking from her work, the woman turns to look at you long enough to respond, "My name is Liana."

speaker: Liana
text: "I am the Mayor's clerk. I am responsible for keeping track of official records and documents in Vesper."

speaker: Liana
text: "I like the town, but 'tis so far from Britain that it attracts some truly... unusual people."

speaker: Liana
text: "I respect Auston in an unofficial capacity. But," she adds, raising her eyebrows, "as a mayor, he is far too spineless. He is afraid of taking sides on any issue. I do not think he should have volunteered for the election."

speaker: Liana
text: "Well, there are a couple of strange ones: Mara and Yongi. And there is Blorn -- he is a mean one, and... well... of course, there is Eldroth. And," she says with a shudder, "the gargoyles."

speaker: Liana
text: "I feel bad about the things I said now that she is gone. Too bad she was killed in that bar fight."

speaker: Liana
text: "Mara? She needs to learn how to act like a woman. Her manly attitude doth not fool anyone."

speaker: Liana
text: "Yongi is nothing more than a drunk. The only reason he opened a tavern was to have an excuse to purchase large amounts of alcohol at wholesale prices. And do not	ask him about the gargoyles unless thou dost want him to talk thine ear off. He hates them almost as much as Blorn does!"

speaker: Liana
text: "He is nice, I suppose, but he is also a doddering old fool. I do not think he hath had a brain for more than a decade."

speaker: Liana
text: "There is a troublemaker and thief if I have ever seen one. He needs to think about leaving town -- quickly, if he knows what is best for him. There is one thing I like about him, though -- he hates the gargoyles more than anyone!"

speaker: Liana
text: "Now there is a disgusting creature for thee. I think they were better named back when we called them daemons!"

speaker: Liana
text: "In fact..." She hands you a piece of paper.

speaker: Liana
text: "Well, there are Cador, Yvella, and Zaksam -- those are the	normal ones."

speaker: Liana
text: "He is the trainer. Quite a good fighter from what I hear."

speaker: Liana
text: "'Tis too bad he is dead. I have heard many compliment his abilities as a leader at the mines."

speaker: Liana
text: "Cador is the head of the Britannian Mining Company branch here in Vesper."

speaker: Liana
text: "He was killed in a brutal slaughter in Yongi's tavern. No one really knows what happened, but I suppose that is how many people meet their death when drinking." She shrugs.

speaker: Liana
text: "She is Cador's wife."

speaker: Liana
text: She nods at you as she returns to her business.

speaker: Lap Lem
text: You are greeted with a smile from this gargoyle.

speaker: Lap Lem
text: "To be pleased to again see you, human." Lap-Lem smiles.

speaker: Lap Lem
text: "To be known to you as Lap-Lem."

speaker: Lap Lem
text: "To mean `rock one.'"

speaker: Lap Lem
text: "To be a miner. To be now the only miner of my race in this town."

speaker: Lap Lem
text: "To know of many gargoyles who work in the other mines, but to see the Vesper mine has only humans now."

speaker: Lap Lem
text: "To be called Vesper. To be the only place, other than parts of Britain, where gargoyles live with humans. To tell you that here are more conflicts." He sighs.

speaker: Lap Lem
text: "To wonder if Terfin would be a better choice to maintain a home."

speaker: Lap Lem
text: "To see the humans grow in hostility to us. Sadly, to also see many gargoyles begin to show mutual feelings. To hope the situation never becomes violent."

speaker: Lap Lem
text: "To be the gargoyle home city. To have been constructed two hundred years ago when the codex was placed in the void and the gargoyles were without places to live. Though not prohibited, no humans reside there."

speaker: Lap Lem
text: "To tell you that there was another -- Anmanivas. To have left because of racial hatred. To sit now in tavern all day with brother, Foranamo. To feel bad for Anmanivas and brother, but to need job." He shrugs.

speaker: Lap Lem
text: "To put up with hatred."

speaker: Lap Lem
text: "To know of incident?"

speaker: Lap Lem
text: "To be very sorry for attack, but was in defense of possession." He lowers his head as if ashamed.

speaker: Lap Lem
text: "To be ashamed. To want nothing more than return of my possession from human."

speaker: Lap Lem
text: "To have had an amulet with sentimental value. To have been stolen by the human." He looks down at his feet. "To want it back."

speaker: Lap Lem
text: "To have returned with amulet?"

speaker: Lap Lem
text: He grins widely as you return the jewelry to him.

speaker: Lap Lem
text: "To thank you, human! To be an example for your race!"

speaker: Lap Lem
text: "Oh. To not have amulet with you." He perks up and smiles. "To return later with amulet!"

speaker: Lap Lem
text: "To hope to see you again soon."

speaker: Yvella
text: The matronly woman you see has a look of concern on her face.

speaker: Yvella
text: "Good day, <HONORIFIC>. I am Yvella." She curtseys. "Might I know thy name?"

speaker: Yvella
text: "Pleased to meet thee, <PLAYER_NAME>."

speaker: Yvella
text: "Now, now, <HONORIFIC>, thou shouldst not lie like that."

speaker: Yvella
text: "Good day, <PLAYER_NAME>."

speaker: Yvella
text: "I am Yvella, <HONORIFIC>."

speaker: Yvella
text: "I take care of my daughter, Catherine, while Cador is at work."

speaker: Yvella
text: "Thou hast not heard of The Fellowship? It is a wonderful organization. They hold parades and festivals and have even built shelters for homeless folk throughout Britannia. Mine husband learned of them some time ago, and we have been happy members ever since."

speaker: Yvella
text: "Cador was mine husband. He was the overseer at the Britannian Mining Company here in Vesper. I cannot believe he is gone," she sobs.

speaker: Yvella
text: "I told him again and again that tavern was a bad place to spend the evening. And now, he is dead, leaving me and Catherine without a husband and a father!"

speaker: Yvella
text: "Cador is mine husband. He is the overseer at the Britannian Mining Company here in Vesper."

speaker: Yvella
text: "He is often at the tavern at this time. I do wish he would not go there every night with that... that...	woman!"

speaker: Yvella
text: "Her name is Mara. She is a fellow miner. She is very nice, but also very beautiful. I do not like mine husband spending all that time with her."

speaker: Yvella
text: "Well, it would be a lovely town if it were not for those... those... gargoyles.  They are disgusting beings. I think Auston should have them run out of town."

speaker: Yvella
text: "He is our mayor. Eldroth recommended that we elect him, so, of course, we did. However, between the two of us, I think we ought to have someone new if Auston does not do something quickly. As a matter of fact, thou shouldst run for mayor, <HONORIFIC>. What dost thou think? Wouldst thou like to run for mayor?"

speaker: Yvella
text: "I agree, thou ought to consider it."

speaker: Yvella
text: "That is too bad. I believe thou wouldst be perfect for the office."

speaker: Yvella
text: "He is our town advisor. Very wise man that Eldroth. He also sells provisions."

speaker: Yvella
text: "Perfectly wretched beasts. Thank goodness most of them stay on their side of the oasis. I do not know how Cador stands working with them. Well, for him, that is. There is only one who still works there."

speaker: Yvella
text: "Here," she says fumbling through her robes. Finally, she finds a piece of parchment and hands it to you.

speaker: Yvella
text: "I worry about her. Every day at noon, she seems to disappear for a few hours. She has these foolish notions that gargoyles are friendly and honorable. I am afraid she may be visiting the other side of the oasis. Oh, I do hope not."

speaker: Yvella
text: "Thou knowest where my daughter doth go at noon?"

speaker: Yvella
text: "Wilt thou tell me?"

speaker: Yvella
text: After you tell her, she responds, "I knew it! That girl must be taught some sense. Associating with those vile creatures. Imagine!" She shakes her head.

speaker: Yvella
text: "If only her father were here today, he would show that loathsome creature his place!"

speaker: Yvella
text: "Just wait until I tell her father about this! He and Mara will certainly take care of the situation.!"

speaker: Yvella
text: "I thank thee, <PLAYER_NAME>. I will put a stop to this right away!"

speaker: Yvella
text: After you tell her, she responds, "I doubt that is true, <HONORIFIC>, but I will look into the matter. I thank thee for thy concern."

speaker: Yvella
text: "Get thee away and cease taunting me! Thou art cruel, <PLAYER_NAME>!"

speaker: Yvella
text: "Oh, well. I thank thee for thy concern."

speaker: Yvella
text: "Pleasant journey, <HONORIFIC>."

speaker: Catherine
text: You see before you a young girl with a carefree expression. As she notices you, her eyes grow wide as she exclaims, "Thou art the person in one of For... one of -my- story books! Thou art the Avatar!"

speaker: Catherine
text: "How dost thou do, <HONORIFIC> Avatar?" She curtseys.

speaker: Catherine
text: "My name is Catherine, <HONORIFIC> Avatar."

speaker: Catherine
text: "I have no job, <HONORIFIC> Avatar. I live with my father and mother here in Vesper."

speaker: Catherine
text: "He is the overseer at the mines, <HONORIFIC> Avatar."

speaker: Catherine
text: "Of course, he's gone now..." She looks down at her feet.

speaker: Catherine
text: "Yes, <HONORIFIC> Avatar. She is there right now." She points, apparently indicating her house.

speaker: Catherine
text: "That is the name of our city, <HONORIFIC> Avatar. If thou art lost, thou mayest wish to speak with the town clerk."

speaker: Catherine
text: "I'm sorry, <HONORIFIC> Avatar, my mother told me never to speak with strangers." She quickly turns away.

speaker: Catherine
text: A tear glistens as it rolls gently down her cheek. "He is no more. My -- my father killed him for talking to me, and -- and 'tis all thy fault!" She turns away, sobbing.

speaker: Catherine
text: "Goodbye, <HONORIFIC> Avatar."

speaker: For Lem
text: You see a very large, strong wingless gargoyle.

speaker: For Lem
text: "To wish you good day, human," says For-Lem.

speaker: For Lem
text: "To answer to For-Lem."

speaker: For Lem
text: "To mean `strong one.'"

speaker: For Lem
text: "To do odd jobs for others. Also, to record gargoyle legends in written form."

speaker: For Lem
text: "To be friends with Lap-Lem, and know he is a good miner. Also to know Ansikart, who reminds us of Singularity in these troubled times."

speaker: For Lem
text: "To be angry with the humans. To be treated poorly and with contempt. To know not why," he shrugs.

speaker: For Lem
text: "To have many interesting stories about our race. To be writing them down for future generations."

speaker: For Lem
text: "To have had many exciting myths from before the Avatar's encounters with our race. To share the concept of a hero with the humans, but to have had different heroes from our own history."

speaker: For Lem
text: "To be afraid for the future of gargoyle youths. To tell you they know little about their heritage. To feel it important to educate them and the offspring who follow them in our ways and history."

speaker: For Lem
text: A look of concern quickly appears on his face.

speaker: For Lem
text: "To talk about the human girl, Catherine? To mean no harm to her." He holds out his hands.

speaker: For Lem
text: "To read gargoyle mythology to her during the day only. To have been asked by her!" His eyes widen.

speaker: For Lem
text: "To ask you not to tell her parents, for they will punish her." He looks hopeful. "To tell not, agreed?"

speaker: For Lem
text: "To be making the right decision." He appears relieved. "To thank you, human." He smiles.

speaker: For Lem
text: "To be making a mistake." He appears disappointed. "To have the girl punished now because of me." He shakes his head.

speaker: For Lem
text: "To feel responsible. To be very sad."

speaker: For Lem
text: "To tell you goodbye, human."

speaker: Ansikart
text: The winged gargoyle has a very calm air about him. As he first sees you, a smile of recognition appears on his face. "To present greetings, Avatar."

speaker: Ansikart
text: "To ask how to help you?"

speaker: Ansikart
text: "To be called Ansikart."

speaker: Ansikart
text: "To mean `anti-dry-master.'"

speaker: Ansikart
text: "To serve food and drink to others."

speaker: Ansikart
text: "To apologize, but to ask you to return when I am open."

speaker: Ansikart
text: "To know all the gargoyles in Vesper. To want to know about specific ones?"

speaker: Ansikart
text: "To want information, perhaps, about the provisioner or the sage?"

speaker: Ansikart
text: "To warn you that many hold resentment for their poor treatment. To be careful, please."

speaker: Ansikart
text: "To be a town full of hate -- to have the humans hate us and to know many hate them, especially Anmanivas and Foranamo. To be not a good thing." He appears saddened.

speaker: Ansikart
text: "To be named Wis-Sur."

speaker: Ansikart
text: "To be a great mind, knowledgeable in many things."

speaker: Ansikart
text: "To have once been a great mind. To be now paranoid and reclusive. To feel pity for Wis-Sur."

speaker: Ansikart
text: "To be Aurvidlem. To have become sullen lately, but to know not why."

speaker: Ansikart
text: "To be a laborer for the town."

speaker: Ansikart
text: "To mine for the Mining company here. To be the only gargoyle still mining here." He nods his head.

speaker: Ansikart
text: "To be very tolerant, like For-Lem."

speaker: Ansikart
text: "To work now with only humans, who hate and degrade him. To continue working, however, despite this. To be quite tolerant of human intolerance." He nods, as if to emphasize his point.

speaker: Ansikart
text: "To have been killed by you in this very tavern. To remember not?"

speaker: Ansikart
text: "To have been his fault, but still, to tell you I feel remorse for him and his brother."

speaker: Ansikart
text: "To have worked the mines with Lap-Lem, but to have left just recently." He shakes his head.

speaker: Ansikart
text: "To hate the humans who work there, and who live on the other side of the oasis. To be too violent. To <VAR> no longer permitted on the other side."

speaker: Ansikart
text: "To be brother to Anmanivas and to have been raised by the same parent. To hate humans as much as Anmanivas, and," he sighs, "to <VAR> allowed no longer to visit the human side."

speaker: Ansikart
text: "To hope you will bring peace again to our people, Avatar."

speaker: Wis Sur
text: You see a winged gargoyle with an authoritative disposition.

speaker: Wis Sur
text: "To offer welcome for you, human," says Wis-Sur.

speaker: Wis Sur
text: The winged gargoyle in front of you has a wild look about him.

speaker: Wis Sur
text: "To go away, human! To have nothing you want!" screams Wis-Sur.

speaker: Wis Sur
text: "To be named Wis-Sur, which means `wise sun.'"

speaker: Wis Sur
text: "To sell magic to others."

speaker: Wis Sur
text: "To be interested in spells, reagents, or potions?"

speaker: Wis Sur
text: "To be familiar with only the other gargoyles in Vesper. To tell you to ask Ansikart, who knows all other gargoyles here. To tell you about one of the following?"

speaker: Wis Sur
text: "To be a provisioner in Vesper."

speaker: Wis Sur
text: "To perform assorted duties for town. To be a good, strong worker."

speaker: Wis Sur
text: "To be a miner for the Britannian Mining Company."

speaker: Wis Sur
text: "To be a miner for the Britannian Mining Company."

speaker: Wis Sur
text: "To say farewell, human."

speaker: Wis Sur
text: "To wonder why you want to know."

speaker: Wis Sur
text: "To sell the few items I possess."

speaker: Wis Sur
text: "To want to buy something?" He looks at you carefully, as if he is unsure whether to sell to you.

speaker: Wis Sur
text: "To be possible," he says, nodding. "To ask what you need?"

speaker: Wis Sur
text: "To suspect you are wasting my time!"

speaker: Wis Sur
text: "To be good that you leave."

speaker: Anmanivas
text: "To have no desire to tell you. To demand to know who you are!"

speaker: Anmanivas

speaker: Anmanivas

speaker: Aurvidlem
text: The gargoyle standing before you has a sour expression on his face.

speaker: Aurvidlem
text: "To offer you greetings, human," says Aurvidlem.

speaker: Aurvidlem
text: "To be called Aurvidlem. To recognize you to be the Avatar."

speaker: Aurvidlem
text: "To provide provisions for others in Vesper."

speaker: Aurvidlem
text: "To be a town filled with prejudice and hatred. To know the humans expect us to begin a violent confrontation."

speaker: Aurvidlem
text: "To believe the humans deserve it," he shrugs, "but to hope my brethren display more control than that."

speaker: Aurvidlem
text: "To be not selling at this time. To come back tomorrow to buy provisions."

speaker: Aurvidlem
text: "To have only a few gargoyles living in town. To know mainly Wis-Sur, and," he gives a slight grunt, "Ansikart. Also to know of some wingless ones."

speaker: Aurvidlem
text: "To have only a few gargoyles living in town. To know mainly Wis-Sur and Ansikart, and to know of some wingless ones."

speaker: Aurvidlem
text: His eyes shift quickly from left to right before finally settling on you.

speaker: Aurvidlem
text: "To know since change in Wis-Sur, Ansikart gained too much respect. To be sure that I have studied more and would be a wiser and better leader here. To be dissatisfied with Ansikart as choice."

speaker: Aurvidlem
text: "To be unsure when change happened, but has affected Wis-Sur greatly. To now see him avoid others and shut himself away. To be concerned for Wis-Sur."

speaker: Aurvidlem
text: "To bid you goodbye."

speaker: Sullivan
text: "'Twas very kind of thee to release me from my cell. I shall now return to my former life. Good day!"

speaker: Sullivan
text: The man in the prison greets you with a rather large smile.

speaker: Sullivan
text: "Why, hello, <HONORIFIC>. In what way could I help thee this fine day?"

speaker: Sullivan
text: "I am Sullivan, <HONORIFIC>," he says pleasantly. "Who wouldst thou be?"

speaker: Sullivan
text: "Pleased to meet thee, <PLAYER_NAME>." He moves his hand to shake yours but is prevented by the bars.

speaker: Sullivan
text: "Ah, well, sorry, <HONORIFIC>. Consider thyself well shaken."

speaker: Sullivan
text: "Of course, <HONORIFIC>. I understand." He smiles.

speaker: Sullivan
text: "Oh, I see. Oops..." He shrugs.

speaker: Sullivan
text: "Well, in all honesty, <HONORIFIC>, I have no job. Although, for a time, I was a thieving scoundrel."

speaker: Sullivan
text: "'Tis truly a fantastic group of people, <HONORIFIC>. We spread guidance and prosperity to the people who reside in our fair land. Of course, at the moment, my fellow members are a bit... displeased with me."

speaker: Anton
text: "That's a bit of an understatement!"

speaker: Sullivan
text: "The Fellowship teaches people to follow their leaders like sheep. Canst thou think of better guidance?"

speaker: Sullivan
text: "When a member behaves properly and follows directions and so forth, he -- or she -- can hear the `inner voice' that teaches one how to win at the games. 'Tis the very reason I joined!" he grins broadly.

speaker: Sullivan
text: "However, I have yet to hear the voice."

speaker: Sullivan
text: "Well, apparently I hadn't striven hard enough to be deserving of the loan I... acquired from the money box upstairs."

speaker: Sullivan
text: As best he can, he leans toward you. For perhaps the first time in his entire life, he turns somber. "Actually, deserve is a relative term. I have finally realized -- being on the racks for many hours during the day leaves time for quite a number of realizations -- the true nature of The Fellowship. Batlin and Abraham and Danag, they all are in error."

speaker: Sullivan
text: "When the Guardian makes his appearance here in Britannia, I have no doubt he will simply eliminate everyone, including The Fellowship leaders." His smile returns.

speaker: Sullivan
text: "That is why I decided to get everything out of The Fellowship and Britannia now, before we are all killed."

speaker: Sullivan
text: "Well... I was going to return the money eventually. I just needed it to win more in the games."

speaker: Anton
text: "What the fool means is that he used to don a costume and pretend to be thee in an attempt to woo goods from the proprietors."

speaker: Sullivan
text: "Quite true, Avatar. The ruse worked far too well. 'Twas a true shame, to be honest. I should not have gotten away with it, and, indeed, am being properly castigated for it now."

speaker: Sullivan
text: "Oh, just that I have been impersonating thee for some time now to take items from shopkeepers without paying for them. Well, -had- been actually. Now I am being properly castigated for it."

speaker: Grod
text: "I thank thee."

speaker: Sullivan
text: "Thou art welcome." He nods.

speaker: Sullivan
text: "Well, until I was caught, I would go from shop to shop all across Britannia, posing as `the Avatar.' The owners were all too happy to supply me with numerous gifts. Thou truly hast a good life, <HONORIFIC>."

speaker: Anton
text: "Ask him about his taxes, <HONORIFIC>."

speaker: Sullivan
text: "Oh, just anything I asked for -- weapons, armour, provisions, spells. Of course, I had no real use for the spells, but it was nice to acquire them for free, regardless."

speaker: Sullivan
text: He smiles.

speaker: Sullivan
text: "The Britannian Tax Council created a tax to raise money for the government. I did not feel like paying them," he shrugs, "so I didn't. And, of course," he says, grinning, "now they often put me on that fine rack."

speaker: Sullivan
text: He stretches his neck and peers at the wooden slab.

speaker: Sullivan
text: "Very fine workmanship." He nods. "Indeed, that is by far the best rack I have ever seen!"

speaker: Sullivan
text: "Is not that the finest rack thou hast ever seen? Exquisite workmanship, beautiful detail."

speaker: Sullivan
text: "Pleasant days, <HONORIFIC>. See thee soon on the surface world!"

speaker: Wench
text: The woman looks up in surprise and says, "I am not working at the moment and I ask thee to respect my privacy. If thou dost wish to speak with me, come to The Baths in the late evening hours."

speaker: Wench
text: This attractive woman looks at you with surprise and says, "A moment! Thou didst just enjoy thyself, didst thou not? Please come back when thou art rested."

speaker: Wench
text: You see a gorgeous young woman with seductive eyes.

speaker: Wench
text: "Hello, handsome!"

speaker: Wench
text: "Hello. Art thou sure thou dost not really want to speak with Roberto?"

speaker: Wench
text: "Fine, sweetheart. Whatever makes thy blood boil... "

speaker: Wench
text: "Then thou hadst best speak with Roberto! He is probably more thy type."

speaker: Wench
text: "Who art thou?"

speaker: Wench
text: "Well, I am very pleased to meet thee, <PLAYER_NAME>."

speaker: Wench
text: "Hello, <PLAYER_NAME>."

speaker: Wench
text: "Oh ho! A real live Avatar?"

speaker: Wench
text: "Say, we should get to know one another better!"

speaker: Wench
text: "And female, as well! And I thought I had seen it all..."

speaker: Wench
text: "Hello again, <PLAYER_NAME>," Wench says.

speaker: Wench
text: "Thou canst just call me... Wench."

speaker: Wench
text: She blows you a kiss.

speaker: Wench
text: She laughs aloud. "Thou must be kidding!" She composes herself and says, "It is my duty to see that thou art comfortable whilst at The Baths."

speaker: Wench
text: "I have been working here since it opened. I love it. I am not exploited in the least. I make piles of gold and live a great life."

speaker: Wench
text: She winks at you. "I meet many nice men, too!"

speaker: Wench
text: "Well, we could have a swim in the spring pools, or thou couldst have a massage. Or we could just talk."

speaker: Wench
text: "Or... thou couldst come with me into the Community Room and I'll 'show' thee my 'job'!"

speaker: Wench
text: "Thou dost want to join me in the Community Room?"

speaker: Wench
text: Wench leads you into a private room.

speaker: Wench
text: "It really isn't a Community Room at all. We shall be all alone," she giggles.

speaker: Wench
text: "By the way, it is a good thing thou didst choose me. Roberto and Martine enjoy stealing gold from their customers. I may have questionable morals, but I am not a thief! Now, let us get down to business, shall we?"

speaker: Wench
text: A while later, after the woman has shown you more tricks than a mage on stage, you emerge from the Community Room a much happier Avatar.

speaker: Wench
text: "'Tis not a problem, <PLAYER_NAME>."

speaker: Wench
text: Wench helps you with your clothing and leads you into the warm spring water. It feels terrific, and you would prefer to go to sleep, but you know you have a quest to fulfill. After a while, Wench helps you out of the water and you dress.

speaker: Wench
text: Wench helps you with your clothing and leads you to a comfortable table. You lie on your stomach and the woman expertly kneads and rubs your aching muscles, slowly sending you into a state of total relaxation. After a while, Wench helps you up and you dress.

speaker: Wench
text: Wench shrugs. "Fine with me! What shall we talk about? I know! Want to know a secret?"

speaker: Wench
text: "Didst thou know that there are secret passages in the mountains connecting the buildings on Buccaneer's Den? 'Tis true! I am fairly sure the entrance is through the House of Games,	and I do know that there is a way into The Baths from the passages!"

speaker: Wench
text: Wench pouts. "Well never mind, then!"

speaker: Wench
text: You and Wench speak of a number of other subjects when you realize that you are spending too much time in the spa. There is a quest to fulfill!

speaker: Wench
text: "Oh, please come again soon, <PLAYER_NAME>!"

speaker: Wench
text: Wench blows you a kiss.

speaker: Wench
text: Wench waves goodbye.

speaker: Glenno
text: You see a handsome, muscular man with an air of mischief about him.

speaker: Glenno
text: "Yes, may I help thee?" Glenno asks.

speaker: Glenno
text: "Glenno at thy service!"

speaker: Glenno
text: "I am the manager of The Baths."

speaker: Glenno
text: "The entrance fee is 300 gold. Everything is included in this fixed price. No tips are necessary. Dost thou want to enter?"

speaker: Glenno
text: "Excellent! Here is thy key!"

speaker: Glenno
text: "Thine hands are too full to carry the key!"

speaker: Glenno
text: "What art thou trying to pull? Thou hast not 300 gold!"

speaker: Glenno
text: "Well, some other time, then! Thou wilt not be sorry if thou dost! It is well worth the price."

speaker: Glenno
text: "Enter! Please relax! Enjoy thyself! Allow one of our hosts or hostesses to make thy stay more comfortable. "

speaker: Glenno
text: He notices your medallion. "Fellowship members are especially welcome!"

speaker: Glenno
text: "Please! Make thyself at home. If thou dost want a drink, let me know."

speaker: Glenno
text: "Uhm, wait a minute. How old art thou, boy?"

speaker: Spark
text: "Uhm, eighteen."

speaker: Glenno
text: "Thou dost not look eighteen."

speaker: Spark
text: "All right, I am sixteen."

speaker: Glenno
text: "Thou dost not look sixteen either. Well, never mind. Thou canst enter. But make sure the management doth not see thee." Glenno scratches his head. "Yes, but... no! I am the management! All right, come on. Just don't cause any trouble."

speaker: Spark
text: "All right! Wenches!"

speaker: Iolo
text: Iolo whispers to you, "Methinks young Spark hath learned a lot whilst adventuring with thee!"

speaker: Glenno
text: "Please come visit in the late evening hours when our hosts and hostesses are here!"

speaker: Glenno
text: "The Baths exist for the pleasure of visitors to Buccaneer's Den. Thou canst bathe in our spring pools. Thou canst lounge in our Community Room and socialize with our attractive hosts or hostesses. Thou canst drink fine wine and ale. Thou canst view our collection of fine artwork. Thou canst... escape into a dream-world!"

speaker: Glenno
text: "They have come from all over Britannia to serve thine every wish! I, Glenno, have assured them that The Baths is the most prestigious establishment of its kind anywhere in the known world. It is probably the only establishment of its kind in the known world!"

speaker: Glenno
text: "The water is guaranteed to be pure, warm and cleansing."

speaker: Glenno
text: "Thou canst lie in comfort among the many soft cushions and pillows. Get to know thy neighbor. Get to know thy neighbor 'very well'!"

speaker: Glenno
text: "Ah, yes, those are erotic masterpieces from the brush of Britannian artist Glen Johnson. Notice how the curves on that one are extremely naturalistic, dost thou not agree?"

speaker: Glenno
text: "Yes, I am a member. If it were not for The Fellowship, I would not be manager of The Baths! I served the group well, trusted my many brothers, strived for unity, and... well, my worthiness preceded my reward! And all of this... was my reward!" speaker: Glenno
text: "Yes, The Fellowship gave me this place. They own it, thou knowest." Suddenly Glenno holds his hand to his mouth, as if he has said something he shouldn't have. I must tend to business!" With that, Glenno turns away from you.

text: "'Tis a fabulous place to work. I absolutely love it. I would not work anywhere else. I have more gold than I could possibly spend."

text: "Thou dost have many choices. We could take a swim in our spring pools. Or I could perform a massage on thee. Or we could simply talk."

speaker: Martine
text: Martine smiles. "That is just fine with me, honey. I would wager thou hast many stories to tell about adventuring, yes? Say! Hast thou been in the secret passages in the mountains? Didst thou know they are all connected? I know that there is a secret door that leads right into the back of this building!" She whispers, "I believe the entrance is through the House of Games."

speaker: Martine
text: You and Martine speak of a number of other subjects until you realize you have spent too much time in the spa. There is a quest to finish!

speaker: Martine
text: "I hope to see thee again soon, honey!"

speaker: Martine
text: Martine blows you a kiss.

speaker: Martine
text: Martine waves goodbye.

speaker: Roberto
text: The man looks up in surprise and says, "I am not working at the moment and I ask thee to respect my privacy. If thou dost wish to speak with me, come to The Baths in the late evening hours."

speaker: Roberto
text: The man looks at you with surprise and says, "Hold, <GENDER_FLAG>! Thou didst just enjoy thyself, didst thou not? Please come back when thou art rested!"

speaker: Roberto
text: You see a strikingly handsome man with eyes that pierce your soul.

speaker: Roberto
text: "Hello, gorgeous!"

speaker: Roberto
text: "Hello. Uhm, art thou sure thou dost not really want to speak with Wench or Martine?"

speaker: Roberto
text: "Fine, sailor, whatever makes thy blood boil..."

speaker: Roberto
text: "Then thou hadst best speak with one of them. They are probably more to thy liking!"

speaker: Roberto
text: "What is thy name?"

speaker: Roberto
text: "Well, I am very pleased to meet thee, <PLAYER_NAME>."

speaker: Roberto
text: "Hello, <PLAYER_NAME>."

speaker: Roberto
text: Roberto does a double-take. "The Avatar, eh? And I thought I had heard it all..."

speaker: Roberto
text: "Hello again, <PLAYER_NAME>," Roberto says.

speaker: Roberto
text: "I am known in these parts as Roberto."

speaker: Roberto
text: Roberto takes your hand and says, "And thou art the most beautiful woman I have ever laid eyes upon!"

speaker: Roberto
text: Roberto smiles broadly. "Thou dost not really want to know that, dost thou?" He shakes his head, suppressing a laugh. "Very well -- it is my task to see that thou art truly comfortable whilst at The Baths."

speaker: Roberto
text: "Nice place, is it not? I certainly enjoy working here! It brings me much wealth, and I have many opportunities to meet <VAR>such as thyself!"

speaker: Roberto
text: "What would suit thee? We could swim in the spring pools, or I could give thee a massage. If thou dost prefer to converse, we could simply talk. Or if thou wouldst like, we could wander into the Community Room and... communicate!"

speaker: Roberto
text: "Thou dost want to join me in the Community Room?"

speaker: Roberto
text: Roberto leads you into a private room.

speaker: Roberto
text: "It really isn't a Community Room at all. We shall be all alone!"

speaker: Roberto
text: A while later, after you have received the man's full attention, you emerge from the Community Room a much happier Avatar.

speaker: Roberto
text: "Do not worry about it, <PLAYER_NAME>. We can do something else."

speaker: Roberto
text: Roberto helps you with your clothing and leads you into the warm spring water. It feels terrific, and you feel like going to sleep, but you know you have a quest to complete. After a while, Roberto helps you out of the water and you dress.

speaker: Roberto
text: Roberto helps you with your clothing and leads you to a comfortable table. You lie face down and the man expertly kneads and rubs your aching muscles, slowly sending you over the edge into a state of total relaxation. After a while, Roberto helps you up and you dress.

speaker: Roberto
text: Roberto smiles. "That is all right. What shall we talk about? Adventuring? Secret passages and dungeons?"

speaker: Roberto
text: Roberto leans closer and whispers, "Didst thou know that there are secret passages connecting the buildings on Buccaneer's Den? 'Tis true! I am fairly sure the entrance is through the House of Games, and I am quite sure there is a way into The Baths."

speaker: Roberto
text: You and Roberto speak of a number of other subjects until you realize that you are spending far too much time in the spa. There is a quest to fulfill!

speaker: Roberto
text: "I hope to see thee again, <PLAYER_NAME>."

speaker: Sintag
text: You see the meanest, toughest-looking guard you have ever seen in Britannia.

speaker: Sintag
text: "What?" Sintag grunts.

speaker: Sintag
text: "Sintag," the man grunts.

speaker: Sintag
text: "I am the guard at the House of Games. I rid the place of trouble-makers."

speaker: Sintag
text: "I have worked for the House of Games since The Mister agreed to pay me and asked me to stay. I know all who go in or out. I see everything."

speaker: Sintag
text: "That would be Mister Gordy, the overseer of the House of Games. Thou might find him in his office during business hours."

speaker: Sintag
text: "We see all sorts of trouble-makers in this place. I especially do not like people who claim that they are the Avatar. I find it blasphemous. The last fellow who claimed to be an Avatar was caught cheating. He'll not be doin' that again!"

speaker: Sintag
text: "There is a man named Robin who used to come in here and cheat at the games. He had his two varlets named Battles and Leavell intimidate anyone who tried to stop him. One day my brothers came to visit and we ran Robin, Battles and Leavell all the way off the island! We have not seen them since!"

speaker: Sintag
text: The Cube vibrates a little. "He is in the caverns, in the torture chamber. What's left of him."

speaker: Sintag
text: "Thou dost not need to know any more."

speaker: Sintag
text: Sintag glares at you.

speaker: Sintag
text: The Cube vibrates. "It is where The Fellowship interrogates their prisoners."

speaker: Sintag
text: "What torture chamber? Did I say torture chamber?"

speaker: Sintag
text: "He has been in our care for a while now." Sintag smiles enigmatically.

speaker: Sintag
text: The Cube vibrates as Sintag speaks. "Hook lives in the cavern behind the House of Games. There is a locked door from the gaming room which leads there. I have the key. There is also a secret door in Gordy's office which Hook uses to get home."

speaker: Sintag
text: "I do not know any man by that description."

speaker: Sintag
text: "Do I look like I am working now? Leave me alone. Come to the House of Games during normal business hours."

speaker: Sintag
text: "Dost thou want the key?"

speaker: Sintag
text: "Here it is."

speaker: Sintag
text: "Thou art carrying too much!"

speaker: Sintag
text: "Suit thyself."

speaker: Sintag
text: Sintag grunts.

speaker: Blacktooth
text: This tall, middle-aged pirate looks at you with suspicion.

speaker: Blacktooth
text: "Before I will look twice at thee, I must know who thou art." His voice is menacing.

speaker: Blacktooth
text: The pirate chews on something in his mouth before replying. "Hi," he finally says.

speaker: Blacktooth
text: The pirate looks as if you have just insulted his mother.

speaker: Blacktooth
text: "I... do... not... like... Avatars!!"

speaker: Blacktooth
text: The pirate spits on the ground. "But thou dost not look as much like fishbait as the last Avatar I spoke with. All right. I will speak with thee."

speaker: Blacktooth
text: "What dost thou want?" Blacktooth asks in a threatening voice. "Oh, 'tis thee, <PLAYER_NAME>."

speaker: Blacktooth
text: "I thought thou didst not want to be my friend!" Blacktooth grumbles.

speaker: Blacktooth
text: "I am Blacktooth. See?" The pirate smiles, revealing his teeth.

speaker: Blacktooth
text: "Making fishbait out of Avatars!" He laughs aloud. "I have had all I can stand of puny weaklings running around claiming they are an Avatar! I am seeking a particular Avatar that was here last week. A particular Avatar that is a Fellowship member!"

speaker: Blacktooth
text: "He was through here a week ago. Tried to filch some gold off of me! Imagine! The nerve of that bastard! He was gone before I had realized what he had done."

speaker: Blacktooth
text: "We were playing cards in the pub. Damn me if he did not deal from the bottom. I can usually spot tricks like that, but he was good!"

speaker: Blacktooth
text: The pirate notices your Fellowship medallion. "I see that thou art one of them, too!"

speaker: Blacktooth
text: "<VAR>I do not trust 'em. I think they are all hiding something. I think they are all tricksters. Take mine old friend Mole, for example. Well, mine old ex-friend Mole. He has changed a great deal since joining them."

speaker: Blacktooth
text: "He is another aging pirate that has retired and lives on the island. We were mates for years, but then he joined that damned Fellowship. Now he thinks his droppings do not smell foul, if thou knowest what I mean."

speaker: Blacktooth
text: "He has abandoned all of his pirate ways! He is a bloody saint now, and whenever he sees me he tries to convince me to join The Fellowship. I avoid him at all costs now. I cannot stand to see him this way. It burns my blood!"

speaker: Blacktooth
text: Then, in a moment of weakness, the tough pirate says in a small voice, "I miss him, too. We were best mates." You could swear there are tears in his eyes.

speaker: Spark
text: Spark whispers, "Oh, come on, be a man!"

speaker: Dupre
text: Dupre turns away to suppress a smirk.

speaker: Blacktooth
text: You can see that the pirate is upset, so you decide to leave him alone.

speaker: Blacktooth
text: "Yeah, go away. That's right! I never can keep any friends!"

speaker: Blacktooth
text: "That would be just like an Avatar to leave me like this!"

speaker: Blacktooth
text: "Typical Fellowship member! That's right! Leave me alone! Go away!"

speaker: Blacktooth
text: "I shall just remain here alone and destitute! Where is my dagger? I shall slit my throat!!"

speaker: Blacktooth
text: "He said that? Really?" Blacktooth looks as if he may cry again.

speaker: Blacktooth
text: "I must go take a look for him. I thank thee, <PLAYER_NAME>, for considering my feelings in this matter." Blacktooth gives you a big hug, then turns away to look for Mole.

speaker: Blacktooth
text: "Another time, then."

speaker: Blacktooth
text: "Yeah, goodbye! Leave! They all leave me alone eventually!"

speaker: Mole
text: You see an aging pirate who might have looked extremely dangerous at one time.

speaker: Mole
text: "What is it?" Mole asks.

speaker: Mole
text: "My name be Mole, it be! Do not ask me how I came by it. 'Tis a long story."

speaker: Mole
text: "For years and years I roamed the seas, pillaging and raping and terrorizing. Now that I am past the age of fifty, I want to live the rest of my life in relative peace and quiet here on Buccaneer's Den."

speaker: Mole
text: "Thou dost really want to hear it? 'Tis very long."

speaker: Mole
text: "All right. I was born in a cave. So my mother named me Mole."

speaker: Iolo
text: "I thought thou said it was a long story."

speaker: Mole
text: "Very well. How 'bout if I just say that I was born in a cave, so my mother named me Mole."

speaker: Mole
text: Mole shrugs. "I thought I would make a long story short."

speaker: Mole
text: "It is a good life. I grew weary of pirating. I grew weary of the salt water and the raw meat and the sewage on deck and the parrot droppings and the fact that every other word one heard was 'Har!'"

speaker: Mole
text: "I spend my time at the House of Games or the Fallen Virgin. I love the sound of the die as it bounces against the felt. I love the taste of warm ale as it splashes down my throat! And... I have The Fellowship."

speaker: Mole
text: "The group has given me a new lease on life. I thought I had mates when I was an active pirate, but they were nothing compared to my brothers in The Fellowship."

speaker: Mole
text: "Say, I see that thou art a member! Thou must be of sound character!"

speaker: Mole
text: "Mine old mates, like my friend Blacktooth, have fallen by the wayside."

speaker: Mole
text: "Blacktooth lives here on the island. We used to be the same link on a chain, knowest what I mean? But since I joined The Fellowship, he does not give me the shadow of a sundial! He acts as though I had the plague or something. I do not understand it. Makes me want to cut something up into mincemeat!"

speaker: Mole
text: "Blacktooth was like my brother. Not like my brothers in The Fellowship, but a 'real' brother, knowest what I mean? We did 'everything' together. We would share booty! We would share wenches! We did it all!"

speaker: Mole
text: "Well, he is not a brother now! He hates me! If he wants nothing to do with me, so be it!" But Mole quickly adds, "He does not realize what I did for him. I made his life livable! Who was it that nursed him when he had scurvy? Me! Who was it that patched him up when he was sliced to bits by that butcher Silverbeard? Me!"

speaker: Mole
text: "Oh, he was some old pirate with a temper. He's probably dead now, if he knows what's good for him!"

speaker: Mole
text: "Yes, it was a different life in those days..." Mole reflects on some past memory as his eyes glaze over temporarily. Finally he says, "I may have dwelt too strongly on my Fellowship business. Perhaps I pushed him too hard. I am sorry. If he would give me another chance I would probably leave The Fellowship. They are not as wonderful as I made them sound. They are more crooked than the pirates I used to sail with!" Mole frowns. "Thou hast put me in a foul mood."

speaker: Mole
text: You tell Mole what Blacktooth said. A change comes over the salty pirate, as if you had just given him a bouquet of flowers.

speaker: Mole
text: "Thou must be kidding me! Blackie misses me? I thought he hated mine innards! I shall have to go for a little walk and maybe I will run across that old dog! I thank thee, stranger, for imparting this information to me."

speaker: Mole
text: With that, Mole turns away from you, doing a little jaunt.

speaker: Mole
text: "Goodbye, stranger."

speaker: Lucky
text: You see a man whose sinewy body is like steel. The glint in his eye tells you that he is no fool.

speaker: Lucky
text: "What dost thou want with Lucky?" the pirate asks.

speaker: Lucky
text: "I am Lucky... in all things."

speaker: Lucky
text: "I make my living off the world! It gives... and I take!" The pirate laughs boisterously. "I am a worldly gentleman, friends -- that is my 'job'! Oh, and I train initiates for a bit of pocket change."

speaker: Lucky
text: "The ways of the world, is what I mean. I am a man of the road; I am a seasoned traveller. I travel through the world as a hundred different men."

speaker: Lucky
text: "In truth there are few places where I have not been and little that I have not done."

speaker: Lucky
text: "Thou canst be a different person just by assumption. 'Tis an attitude. I am an expert in the art of charismatic communication for the purposes of deception. It gives one many skills. For example, I can walk into any shop and make a purchase. But I will walk away with much more than I bought, for I know how to fool the shopkeeper. Little things like that."

speaker: Lucky
text: "I charge 35 gold for a training session. Doth this meet with thine approval?"

speaker: Lucky
text: Lucky shrugs. "Thou wilt not find another trainer on the island!"

speaker: Lucky
text: "I shall be happy to show thee my ways of the world during normal business hours at my residence -- afternoons and evenings."

speaker: Lucky
text: "Be careful, my friend."

speaker: Budo
text: You see a fat, cheerful-looking merchant.

speaker: Budo
text: "Hello, hello my friend! Thou dost look like thou needest to spend money!"

speaker: Shamino
text: "This place looks quite well-off."

speaker: Iolo
text: "The entire island is very opulent. It is not the same island we once knew."

speaker: Budo
text: "Hello! How art thou, my friend?"

speaker: Budo
text: "How may I help thee?" Budo asks.

speaker: Budo
text: "Budo the Fourth at thy service! 'Tis a fine day today, is it not?"

speaker: Budo
text: "I am a provisioner, like my father before me, and like his father before him, and like his father before him. Budo's is an island tradition! Just as The Fellowship will be someday!"

speaker: Budo
text: "If thou art interested in weapons, armour, provisions, or a ship deed, <VAR><VAR><VAR>"

speaker: Budo
text: "Budo's carries nothing but the finest quality armour in all Britannia. I have all the best types of equipment available."

speaker: Budo
text: "Budo's offers thee excellent weaponry with superb craftsmanship. Thou wilt not find a better buy for thy money anywhere else!"

speaker: Budo
text: "Budo's also carries a variety of useful things for thy convenience."

speaker: Budo
text: "But I have already sold thee the deed to 'The Lusty Wench'! She was the only ship I had at this particular time! I am sorry!"

speaker: Budo
text: "I can sell thee the deed to my ship 'The Lusty Wench.' She is beautiful, my friend. She is guaranteed to last and is the sleekest vessel on the seas! She goes for 800 gold. Want her?"

speaker: Budo
text: "A wise move. A magnificent ship for thee!" He takes your gold.

speaker: Budo
text: "Thou art carrying too much, my friend! Unload thyself of some of thy belongings and I will sell thee the deed to this beautiful ship."

speaker: Budo
text: "But thou dost not have enough gold! Perhaps thou shouldst visit the House of Games and increase the bulges in thy pockets!"

speaker: Budo
text: "But thou wilt never see a ship like this one anywhere in the world! Too bad!"

speaker: Budo
text: "The Fellowship has helped me to become a very rich man! Although the business is an inherited enterprise, I owe everything to The Fellowship!"

speaker: Budo
text: "My great-grandfather started this business many, many years ago. He was moderately successful, thanks to the Thieves' Guild. But that era has passed."

speaker: Budo
text: "My great-grandfather passed the shoppe on to his son, and so forth, down to me. We are born merchants! That is why I know why thou hast come to Budo's! Thou wantest to become a part of the great Budo Legacy! Thou dost need to buy something!"

speaker: Budo
text: "There was a period shortly after my father died, just as I had inherited the shoppe, when business was poor. There was a danger that I would not be able to keep the shoppe open. But The Fellowship convinced me that I should join them. I proved my worthiness and The Fellowship helped me financially."

speaker: Budo
text: "I do not mind telling thee. The Fellowship shares in one half of my profit."

speaker: Budo
text: "It is no more. They dwindled away during my grandfather's time. By the time The Fellowship arrived, when I was a boy, there was no trace of them except in family mementos. Even the pirates are different."

speaker: Budo
text: The cube vibrates a moment.

speaker: Budo
text: "That ship sails here frequently. I know it makes regular runs to the mainland, stops here, then moves on to the Isle of the Avatar the next morning. Then it repeats the trip, going the other direction."

speaker: Budo
text: "It stops here regularly. Don't know much more about it. The crew is very secretive." Budo looks away, obviously not wanting to talk about the ship.

speaker: Budo
text: "I hope I can help thee again some time, my friend!"

speaker: Gordy
text: You see a pirate who is elegantly dressed and obviously rich. He reeks of pomade.

speaker: Gordy
text: "Yes?" Gordy asks.

speaker: Gordy
text: "I am Gordy." He grins widely offering you his hand. You notice that it is none too clean.

speaker: Gordy
text: "I am 'The Mister' of the House of Games. Inside mine House thou mayest challenge thy skill at games of chance." He eyes you carefully, measuring your worth and gullibility.

speaker: Gordy
text: "Enter and enjoy! But first thou must register. Please sign the book so that we may verify thy proclaimed worth." Which name do you sign?

speaker: Gordy
text: You sign your name. "Very good, <PLAYER_NAME>. Welcome to the House of Games!" Gordy spreads his arms in an expansive gesture, obviously pleased to welcome your money to his gambling parlour.

speaker: Gordy
text: Gordy frowns when he sees what you wrote. "Avatar, eh? We just had one of them a week ago. He was caught cheating at the tables!" He takes a step back and glowers. "Art thou going to give us trouble?"

speaker: Gordy
text: "Then thou canst not enter!"

speaker: Gordy
text: "We shall see about that!"

speaker: Gordy
text: You sign in a false name. "Fine, <HONORIFIC>. I be glad to welcome thee!" Gordy spreads his arms in an expansive gesture, obviously pleased to welcome your money to his gambling parlour.

speaker: Gordy
text: "I hope to see thee there during business hours."

speaker: Gordy
text: "Ah, thou art a Fellowship member. Thou wilt surely find thy reward at these tables!" Gordy winks and nudges you, then guffaws loudly.

speaker: Gordy
text: "The House of Games was established six years ago with the funds of... an interested party. It attracts people from all over Britannia who wish to live dangerously with their money. The business is very profitable." He pats his pouch, and coins clink. "Very profitable." He grins.

speaker: Gordy
text: "It refers to my being the overseer, but everyone here has always called me 'The Mister'. I am not sure why. But it appeals to me." He puffs up like a bantam rooster, trying to look important. He almost succeeds.

speaker: Gordy
text: "And that is 'Mister' Gordy, to thee!"

speaker: Gordy
text: "Yes, what can I do for thee?"

speaker: Gordy
text: He grins, very pleased with himself.

speaker: Gordy
text: "Each game requires a definite skill in determining the most profitable way to place a bet. Many visitors to the House of Games find that they have a skill. Others, sadly, do not."

speaker: Gordy
text: He gestures toward your Fellowship medallion. "Thou shouldst not have any problem." He winks and wiggles his eyebrows.

speaker: Gordy
text: "Well, Buccaneer's Den is not in the jurisdiction of the Britannian Tax Council. We are not subject to Britannia's taxes." Gordy smiles wickedly. "And that... is very profitable!"

speaker: Gordy
text: The Cube vibrates a moment. "Yes, I know Hook very well. He lives beneath the House of Games. Talk to Sintag. He can direct thee."

speaker: Gordy
text: "I do not know anyone of that description." Gordy looks around nervously and loosens his collar as though it has suddenly gotten too tight.

speaker: Gordy
text: The Cube vibrates a moment. "That would be The Fellowship, of course."

speaker: Gordy
text: "Well, now,... that would be revealin' the secret of my business and profit, now wouldn't it?" His demeanor becomes threatening as he leans closer to you and snarls, "Find thine own backers, whelp!"

speaker: Gordy
text: "Farewell, friend. I look forward to thy return."

speaker: Mandy
text: You see a woman in her fifties who might have been a pirate wench in her earlier years. Though she is coarse, she has a certain motherly quality.

speaker: Mandy
text: "Hello, again," Mandy says.

speaker: Mandy
text: "I am Mandy."

speaker: Mandy
text: "I run the Fallen Virgin Inn and Tavern. We are open for breakfast, dinner, and late night hours."

speaker: Mandy
text: "If thou dost want food or drink, or perhaps a room, please say so."

speaker: Mandy
text: Mandy looks at Dupre and says, "Don't I know thee?"

speaker: Dupre
text: "Yes, milady. I was here a few months ago."

speaker: Mandy
text: "I remember! Thou art working for Brommer's Britannian travel guides! Thou art a pub critic!"

speaker: Dupre
text: "That is right, milady."

speaker: Mandy
text: "Welcome back! Please try anything on the menu. It is all still very good."

speaker: Dupre
text: "I thank thee, milady."

speaker: Iolo
text: "Thou art a swine, Dupre."

speaker: Mandy
text: "Please come to the Tavern then and I will be happy to serve thee."

speaker: Mandy
text: "We serve a good plate of slop, if I do say so myself! That Silverleaf is something. Thou shouldst try that."

speaker: Mandy
text: "I can offer thee wine and ale."

speaker: Mandy
text: "Our rooms are 10 gold per person. The only one available now is the southwest room. The other two already have occupants. Dost thou want one?"

speaker: Mandy
text: "Look there now. Thou hast too many bundles to take the room key!"

speaker: Mandy
text: "Here is the room key. It is good only until thou dost leave the inn."

speaker: Mandy
text: "It doth seem that thou art a trifle short, <HONORIFIC>."

speaker: Mandy
text: "All right. Some other time."

speaker: Mandy
text: "Best bloody swill thou wilt eat on the face of the earth!"

speaker: Mandy
text: "Yes, I have run this tavern and inn since my wenching days." Mandy laughs. "I was quite a beauty back then, but thou canst not tell it now. I know everyone in town and they all know me. If thou dost need to know something about anyone, let me know."

speaker: Mandy
text: "He helps out at that Fellowship place. He is always interim branch leader for some reason. The real leader, a fellow named Abraham, is never here. Danag is all right. Kind of gullible."

speaker: Mandy
text: "He is a former pirate and rogue, and he can be fairly mean. If he does not warm up to thee immediately, he may not at all. But once he does, thou wilt learn he is quite a sensitive man."

speaker: Mandy
text: "I was a wench with Mole's gang of pirates back in... well, it seems a century ago. Mole was rough and tough and a trouble-maker. Until he joined The Fellowship. That changed him into...," Mandy shrugs. "I know not, a middle-aged former pirate or some such."

speaker: Mandy
text: "His family has been on Buccaneer's Den for generations. Comes on a trifle too strong with the barking of wares, if thou dost ask me."

speaker: Mandy
text: "He makes me laugh. He is a dear. Thou wouldst not find a more pleasant, and eager-to-please, man on the island. He is a surprisingly good person." Mandy pauses then adds, "For a pimp."

speaker: Mandy
text: "She is a very private person. Works at The Baths. I hear she won some kind of competition -- that is why she is fortunate to be there. I understand Glenno pays them well over there."

speaker: Mandy
text: "She is a very private person. Works at The Baths. I have not spoken three words to her in my life."

speaker: Mandy
text: "He is a very private person, but, oh, is he an attractive man, I must say! He works at The Baths. I will admit I am one of his clients. He doth truly clean my dishes, if thou dost know what I mean."

speaker: Mandy
text: "He is a former rogue, I can tell thee that! And to think he makes a living now by teaching others to be the same!" Mandy shrugs. "To each their own."

speaker: Mandy
text: "I do not know him that well, although he seems to be a sincere man. He runs the House of Games like a ship. He is a former pirate as well. Must have been a captain."

speaker: Mandy
text: "He was another pirate. I know he works at the House of Games. I suppose he is the man in charge of the actual games. I do not know him well."

speaker: Mandy
text: "Brrrr! He is a scary man. Thou canst tell that he has killed. He is the guard at the House of Games. Thou dost not want to be caught cheating by him!"

speaker: Mandy
text: You feel your Cube vibrate, but somehow you know that Mandy would have told you the truth without it.

speaker: Mandy
text: Mandy whispers to you. "I know who thou dost mean. He lives somewhere on the island, but I am not sure where. He rarely comes in to the tavern, but I have seen him on occasion."

speaker: Mandy
text: "He scares me to death."

speaker: Mandy
text: "Well, he is a killer. Some think he is the one responsible for the murder that happened last year."

speaker: Mandy
text: "This man they call Hook has the way of the killer about him. Thou canst see it in his eyes. I would be extremely careful if I were to run afoul of him."

speaker: Mandy
text: "There was a thief named Duncan who had stolen funds from the House of Games and The Baths. I believe he may have broken into the Fellowship Hall as well. Anyway, he was arrested. But one morning, when the guard brought the man his breakfast, he was gone! Everyone thought he had escaped until his body was found in the house where old Blacktooth lives. This was before Blacktooth lived there."

speaker: Mandy
text: "It was mutilated -- his arms and legs had been cut off, and he had literally lost his head! To this day, no one knows who did it. But when Hook is around, people talk behind his back. He is certainly capable of doing it!"

speaker: Mandy
text: "Nice talking with thee. I shall see thee later, I hope."

speaker: Smithy
text: You see a well-dressed pirate with oil in his hair.

speaker: Smithy
text: "May I help thee?" Smithy asks.

speaker: Smithy
text: "I am Smithy."

speaker: Smithy
text: "I run the games at the House of Games."

speaker: Smithy
text: "I can explain the rules and how to play for thee. I also make sure that one does not cheat."

speaker: Smithy
text: "Please do come and try thy skill when the facility is open for business."

speaker: Smithy
text: "If thou art caught cheating, thou wilt be arrested. And we do prosecute!"

speaker: Smithy
text: "There are three games that thou canst play. The first is Virtue Roulette. The second is The Rat Race. The third is Triples. Wouldst thou like to hear any rules?"

speaker: Smithy
text: "For which game dost thou want to hear the rules?"

speaker: Smithy
text: "That is all right."

speaker: Smithy
text: "Simply place the amount of gold coins thou dost wish to bet on one or more colors. Use the wheel and thy money will be increased if thou hast bet correctly."

speaker: Smithy
text: "Place thy bet on the green spot at the end of the lane which corresponds to the trough in which thy rat is running."

speaker: Smithy
text: "Thou canst bet on a triple, that is, three ones, three twos, or three threes. This has the highest payback. A '1, 2, 3' pays slightly less. A sum total of '4', '5', '7', or '8' pays the least. Do not place thy money in between numbers, especially the '4' and '5'. A '6' made up of anything other than three twos loses. After placing thy bet, spin the wheel."

speaker: Smithy
text: "Fine then. Thou art on thine own."

speaker: Smithy
text: "See thee again, <HONORIFIC>."

speaker: Paul
text: You see a young entertainer who beckons to you.

speaker: Paul
text: "Yes?" Paul asks.

speaker: Paul
text: "I am Paul. My colleagues' names are Meryl and Dustin."

speaker: Paul
text: "We perform a Passion Play about The Fellowship. It costs only 2 gold per person to see. If thou dost want us to perform it, please say so."

speaker: Paul
text: "A Passion Play is a morality tale performed on stage."

speaker: Paul
