text: "It would be much simpler to view the play."

speaker: Paul
text: "I am sorry to say we are on our break. Please return to the stage area during normal hours."

speaker: Paul
text: "Wouldst thou like to see our Passion Play?"

speaker: Paul
text: Paul takes your gold. "We thank thee. If thou wouldst make thyself comfortable, we shall begin."

speaker: Paul
text: "Oh dear. I am afraid thou dost not have enough gold to pay for the performance. Some other time, I hope."

speaker: Paul
text: "I am sorry. It seems my fellow thespians are not available. The Passion Play has temporarily	closed."

speaker: Paul
text: "Some other time, then, I hope."

speaker: Paul
text: The actor bows to you.

speaker: Meryl
text: You see a middle-aged actress with a very serious expression. She is unable to speak with you because she is concentrating on her part in the Passion Play. Perhaps you should speak to Paul.

speaker: Dustin
text: You see a short, stocky actor in his mid- to late forties. He cannot speak to you now because he is concentrating on his lines for the Passion Play. Perhaps you should speak to Paul.

speaker: Ellen
text: Ellen puts her finger to her lips. There is a Fellowship meeting going on.

speaker: Ellen
text: "Hello. I am sorry to be rude, but I am late to the Fellowship meeting. May we speak another time?"

speaker: Ellen
text: This is a woman who seems pleasant and welcoming. "I am proud to meet the Avatar," she says, beaming.

speaker: Ellen
text: "Yes, Avatar?" Ellen asks.

speaker: Ellen
text: "My name is Ellen."

speaker: Ellen
text: "I do the bookkeeping at the Fellowship Branch. I work with mine husband, Klog."

speaker: Ellen
text: "'Tis awful, is it not? Of course, I was home with Klog all night."

speaker: Ellen
text: "Perhaps thou couldst call it a 'confident philosophy'. We meet here at the branch office every night."

speaker: Ellen
text: "The Fellowship has branches all over Britannia. It is a most popular philosophical society."

speaker: Ellen
text: "Mine husband Klog is a wonderful branch leader. He is an inspiration to all of the Trinsic members."

speaker: Ellen
text: "Goodbye. I hope to see thee again, soon."

speaker: Kessler
text: You see a very authoritative-looking older man who looks at you with thoughtful concern.

speaker: Kessler
text: "I am very glad thou hast come to see me again," says Kessler.

speaker: Kessler
text: "My name is Kessler."

speaker: Kessler
text: "I run the apothecary shop here in Britain."

speaker: Kessler
text: "While the normal function of an apothecary is to administer potions and magical reagents, I am nowadays working almost exclusively for Lord British trying to study a specific problem."

speaker: Kessler
text: "They are certainly not a recent invention here in Britannia! Potions are liquids that possess certain magical qualities which are used for all sorts of purposes, such as the treatment of injury and disease. I have a quantity of them for sale if thou art interested."

speaker: Kessler
text: "Since the mages have become so ineffective, we have been forced to develop other ways to accomplish all the things we used to be able to depend on mages to do. Unfortunately, many of these new methods are as yet untested."

speaker: Kessler
text: "We still know very little about the effects of most of the substances we use. Many cause more problems than they solve, or react differently if taken in unison with other elements. Some might cause thee to become dependent on them for thine health and some may simply be poisonous."

speaker: Kessler
text: "I am studying the effects of a particular substance known as silver snake venom. But I am encountering a number of difficulties."

speaker: Kessler
text: "As one may surmise from the name it is the venom taken from the dangerous silver snake. The fascination that many people possess for these creatures has created a great deal of curiosity about the venom itself."

speaker: Kessler
text: "There are those who claim that gargoyles take the venom which results in their becoming enhanced in combat and such. Now this may be just a myth, but the curiosity people feel is real enough."

speaker: Kessler
text: "My greatest difficulty is in finding any significant quantity of silver snake venom. But it is by no means mine only difficulty."

speaker: Kessler
text: "If by any chance thou wouldst come across any silver snake venom bring it back to me here. I shall pay thee fifty gold coins for every vial of it thou canst supply."

speaker: Kessler
text: "People need to be alerted to how dangerous silver snake venom is. To this end I wish to announce my findings before Lord British and a consortium of lords and mayors, but to do that I must first finish my study."

speaker: Kessler
text: "Recently there has been a dramatic rise in the use of a very strange substance. People have begun to purposefully ingest the venom of the silver snake."

speaker: Kessler
text: "The silver snake produces a venom that is extremely poisonous, but when taken in less than lethal amounts, it causes a variety of strange effects."

speaker: Kessler
text: "For a time the venom will heighten one's physical and mental performance, such as allowing one to work harder, for example. But after the effects have worn off, it will impair the user permanently."

speaker: Kessler
text: "It first makes the user feel extremely tired and eventually causes a sloughing of the skin. The venom is a dangerous substance and thou shouldst not partake of it under any circumstances."

speaker: Kessler
text: "Thou dost not have any vials of venom!"

speaker: Kessler
text: Kessler examines the vial carefully.

speaker: Kessler
text: Kessler examines the vials carefully.

speaker: Kessler
text: He looks up at you and nods. "This is indeed silver snake venom. I shall pay thee 50 gold coins per vial. All right?"

speaker: Kessler
text: Kessler opens his coinpurse and pays you <VAR> gold coins.

speaker: Kessler
text: "Thou art too burdened to carry any more money."

speaker: Kessler
text: "I see thou dost have a quantity of silver snake venom in thy possession. Perhaps we should talk further."

speaker: Kessler
text: "Very well."

speaker: Kessler
text: "The Apothecary is closed. It is open from noon until midnight. Thou mayest return then."

speaker: Kessler
text: "I always keep a fresh stock of ingredients and an inventory of prepared potions in case anyone should be in need of them. Wouldst thou like to buy one?"

speaker: Kessler
text: "Be sure to come back if thou dost ever need any potions."

speaker: Kessler
text: "It was good speaking with thee, <HONORIFIC>."

speaker: Perrin
text: The man before you stretches and inhales deeply.

speaker: Perrin
text: "Glorious day, <PLAYER_NAME>." Perrin grins.

speaker: Perrin
text: "Please, <HONORIFIC>, call me Perrin. I reside here in Empath Abbey."

speaker: Perrin
text: "I am a scholar, <HONORIFIC>. Dost thou want training in the realm of books?"

speaker: Perrin
text: "My price is 45 gold for each training session, but I will also teach thee what little I know about magic. Is this acceptable?"

speaker: Perrin
text: "Very well, <HONORIFIC>."

speaker: Perrin
text: "Forgive me, I am a bit overzealous in my search for students. I hope thou wilt return in the future."

speaker: Perrin
text: "This is a pleasant location. I like the privacy, which gives me a chance to study when I need to. The Brotherhood is across the road, and I am near a healer. Also, I have begun a study on the effects of dealing with death for undertakers. I am using Tiery as a case study."

speaker: Perrin
text: "That is the abbey. The monks who reside there are famous for their ability to produce exquisite wine. Nearby is the Highcourt and a prison."

speaker: Perrin
text: "Thou shouldst try some. The monks have been making it for more than three hundred years!"

speaker: Perrin
text: "The official there is named Sir Jeff. From what I hear, he runs his ship very tight. I do not envy the jailer that works with him. It must be extremely difficult to be near such a strict disciplinarian all day long."

speaker: Perrin
text: "It is located just behind the court. And," he grins, "I am proud to say that is at least one thing about which I know nothing."

speaker: Perrin
text: "He is the undertaker who lives just north of the Brotherhood."

speaker: Perrin
text: "I have yet to meet her, but I know she loves animals. I have seen her playing with the deer and squirrels that inhabit this region."

speaker: Perrin
text: "Goodbye, <PLAYER_NAME>. Best of luck in thy journeys."

speaker: Owings
text: Before you is a skinny man with a silly smile on his face. He is holding a lantern in one hand and a dirty spoon in the other.

speaker: Owings
text: "Hello, again," says Owings. He smiles and tips his mining hat to you.

speaker: Owings
text: "My name is Owings," he says giving you a rapid up and down handshake. "Pleased to meet thee."

speaker: Owings
text: "My partner's name is Malloy."

speaker: Owings
text: "Thou dost already know my partner, Malloy."

speaker: Owings
text: "I do what he does." Owings jerks his thumb towards Malloy digging away next to him. The fat man is trying to chisel through the rock wall using only a spoon. Owings's thumb hits him in the back.

speaker: Malloy
text: Malloy looks over at you and gives you a friendly wave as he goes to stand up. As he does this, he bumps his head. There is a loud knocking noise. He says, "Oooooooohh!" very loudly. His cry echoes through the length of the mineshaft. You can feel dust from the cracks in the ceiling settling on your shoulder.

speaker: Owings
text: Owings suddenly looks very nervous and throws both of his arms over his head. There is a terrible rumble and you feel the ground beneath you start to shake. After a moment the tremor subsides. Both of them look very relieved.

speaker: Malloy
text: Malloy puts one hand up to his bruised head and feels around on the ground with the other. He eventually finds and picks up a metal mining helmet. He gingerly places it over his head which appears to still be causing him pain. You can see that the top of Malloy's head barely fits into it.

speaker: Owings
text: "Allow me to rephrase that. I do what he does, except I always wears me helmet." With that Owings gives a big nod, throwing his head up and down. This causes his helmet to fall down over his eyes.

speaker: Malloy
text: Malloy looks over at you and at Owings, giving both of you an incredulous pouting grimace.

speaker: Owings
text: "Normally I am digging, but as of late I cannot seem to find my partner Malloy. So I suppose my job is to look for him. I wonder where he has gone to?"

speaker: Owings
text: Owings puts his hand on your shoulder and puts a finger up to his lips. "Shhhhh! Be very quiet! This is an old tunnel. Mikos, the foreman, says that any sudden loud noise could trigger a cave-in!"

speaker: Malloy
text: Malloy goes back to digging. The exertion from his work causes his helmet to fall off. He sighs, picks it up, puts it back on and goes back to work. Almost immediately it falls off again. He puts it back on. It falls off. He puts it back on. Malloy grunts and sighs. It falls off. Dejected, he puts it back on. This happens again and again so many times that it is almost painful to watch. Finally, Malloy just lets the helmet lie there and throws a tantrum. He trembles and bites into his hand to keep from crying out in frustration.

speaker: Owings
text: Owings steps up to Malloy and puts his finger to his lips. "Shhhhhh!" Looking down, Owings sees Malloy's helmet on the ground. "Dost thou not remember Mikos telling thee to always wear thine helmet?" he says. Owings picks it up and dusts it off. He pushes it down on top of Malloy's sore head, causing Malloy to wrinkle his face in pain. "No need to thank me!" Owings says. With that, he nods his head up and down, causing the front of his helmet to fall down over his eyes. He reaches out with his arms blindly.

speaker: Malloy
text: Malloy looks over at Owings and at you, giving you both a pouting grimace.

speaker: Owings
text: You reach up and tip Owings's helmet back so that it is no longer covering his eyes. He smiles at you thankfully. He takes off his helmet to scratch at the top of his head. He puts it back on and it immediately tilts back down over his eyes.

speaker: Malloy
text: Malloy watches this, smirks and slowly shakes his head.

speaker: Owings
text: "Mikos, the foreman of this mine told us to always wear a helmet. It is very important. The two of us even sent a mining helmet to Lord British. A funny man dressed just like the Avatar told us of how Lord British had been hit in the head with falling objects - twice! So we sent a helmet to him."

speaker: Malloy
text: It appears Malloy can no longer stand being left out of the conversation. "It was -mine- idea to send Lord British the helmet," he says proudly. "While we have not yet heard back from him about it I am sure he will find some way to thank us." Malloy's helmet falls off and he stands there a long time before regaining the composure to pick it up again.

speaker: Owings
text: "Thou art a kind person to fix mine helmet for me," Owings says, giving you a big grin.

speaker: Malloy
text: You see Malloy look very suspiciously at Owings's helmet. "Thou art wearing mine hat!" He lets out a growling "Hmmmf!" and snatches Owings's helmet off of his head. Malloy removes his helmet, casually tossing it to the ground. He then puts Owings's helmet on. It fits him perfectly. Malloy flashes you both a big condescending smile. With a curt nod he turns to go back to work.

speaker: Owings
text: Owings looks at Malloy and then back to you. He is very confused. "That was not very nice, Malloy! Thou didst take mine hat!" Owings's face is covered with a large frown. His lower lip starts to tremble.

speaker: Owings
text: Owings reaches over and takes the mining helmet off Malloy's head so carefully that he does not notice. Owings puts the helmet back on with a little sneaky laugh of triumph. Pointing to the hat he taps Malloy on the back to let him know what he's done.

speaker: Malloy
text: Malloy stops digging and goes to stand up. As he does this he hits his head on the ceiling. Once again it makes a loud knocking noise. Malloy says "Oooooh!" After shaking his head clear, he slowly steps toward Owings. He is quite angry - so angry that he does not notice that he has stepped into the other helmet and it is stuck onto his foot. Taking his spoon he whaps Owings in the nose with it.

speaker: Owings
text: Upon getting hit in the nose, Owings jerks his head back, causing his helmet to fall off. "Ooh! Mine helmet!" he cries.

speaker: Malloy
text: Malloy is so angry that he can no longer contain himself. "That is not thine helmet! It is mine helmet!" he shouts. This sends a thunderous echo down the mineshaft. You can feel a shower of falling dust and rocks. There is a low rumble and an ominous vibration of the earth. Owings and Malloy are so scared that in their panic they run right into each other. Malloy's foot - the one with the helmet stuck on it - slides out from under him and he lands on his posterior. Both cover their heads in anticipation of a massive cave-in.

speaker: Owings
text: After a few moments of fearful anticipation, the tremor subsides. The tunnel is still standing, none the worse for wear. "I thought I was done for!" says Owings. With that, a large piece of rock falls from the ceiling and lands squarely on Owings's head. It makes a loud knocking noise. Owings starts to pout and cry very childishly.

speaker: Malloy
text: Malloy points at Owings and laughs until tears run down his face. Glancing up at the ceiling, Malloy starts feeling around for his helmet. Finally, feeling underneath himself, he pulls out his helmet, on top of which he had fallen! Looking at the hat, Malloy discovers that his bulk has crumpled it. It is ruined. He puts it on anyway, looking most ridiculous, and his tears of laughter turn to tears of sorrow. Now, both of them break down into fits of childish bawling. Malloy looks at Owings and says "This is another fine mess thou hast gotten us into!"

speaker: Owings
text: Owings and Malloy, both unable to stop their crying, wave goodbye.

speaker: Owings
text: "Good day to thee, <HONORIFIC>."

speaker: Anton
text: "I thank thee,<HONORIFIC>. Truly thou possesseth great honor! I hope one day to be able to repay thee for thy kindness!"

speaker: Anton
text: You are greeted by a man with a sour expression.

speaker: Anton
text: "Harrumph," says Anton.

speaker: Anton
text: "I," he says scratching his nose, "am Anton, not that thou wouldst be concerned with me. Unless, of course, thou art about to put me in the stocks."

speaker: Sullivan
text: "Be polite, Anton. I am sure <HONORIFIC> is truly interested in thy name."

speaker: Anton
text: "What kind of bloody stupid question is that? I am in the prison! What kind of job could I possibly have?"

speaker: Grod
text: "Yeah, stupid question."

speaker: Sullivan
text: "Relax, Anton. I am sure that thou wilt have a job again soon enough." He turns to you.

speaker: Sullivan
text: "He was apprenticed to the sage Alagner who bade him find out information about The Fellowship..."

speaker: Anton
text: "Silence, fool! They will slay me for sure, now!" He looks at you with despair.

speaker: Sullivan
text: "Hast thou already forgotten, dear Anton? Thou didst divulge that information to them some time ago."

speaker: Anton
text: "I did?"

speaker: Sullivan
text: He nods.

speaker: Anton
text: Anton turns to the troll.

speaker: Anton
text: "I did?"

speaker: Grod
text: The troll nods.

speaker: Anton
text: "Oh, well, then. Carry on!"

speaker: Sullivan
text: "As I was saying, his instructor sent him to observe the Fellowship. Of course, he was discovered and brought here for torturing." He turns back to Anton.

speaker: Sullivan
text: "Never fear, however, Anton. 'Twill be no time before thou art free again, able to return to thy tutor, Alagner, and resume thy studies," he says, smiling.

speaker: Anton
text: "Yes, they are likely to keep me in them the next time until I rot. Or, at the very least, until I die from the troll's lashings."

speaker: Anton
text: "I am being held here for spying, <HONORIFIC>. 'Tis a false accusation, but they will likely kill me anyway...."

speaker: Anton
text: "Well, so few people are, really."

speaker: Anton
text: "Well, I am certainly not guilty of such an act!"

speaker: Anton
text: "To think I would seek information for any reason other than to enhance myself with knowledge is more than preposterous! It is... it is... ludicrous is what it is!"

speaker: Anton
text: "Why, The Fellowship, <HONORIFIC>."

speaker: Anton
text: "The troll beats me many times during the day. I will not be able to survive for much longer."

speaker: Sullivan
text: "Come, come, Anton, surely it cannot be that terrible. After all, The Fellowship is providing us with a place to stay and more food than we could... more food... Well, they are also giving us food!"

speaker: Anton
text: "He is a sage who resides in New Magincia. Perhaps the most learned man in all Britannia! And now," he sighs, "I will no longer have the opportunity to glean knowledge from his voluminous body of wisdom."

speaker: Anton
text: "Why, they are a wonderful group of people who are constantly seeking to bring health, happiness, and spirituality to the people of Britannia."

speaker: Anton
text: With his index finger, he motions you closer to him and lowers his voice.

speaker: Anton
text: "In a pig's eye, that is! I am departing this den of evil as soon as I get the chance. And I advise thee to do the same!"

speaker: Anton
text: "Do not hurry too much, <HONORIFIC>, for the world as we know it will soon be no more."

speaker: Papa
text: "Go away, bee killers!"

speaker: Papa
text: You see a naked man who looks a bit wild. He is not in the least concerned that he has on no clothes.

speaker: Papa
text: "Huh?" asks Papa.

speaker: Papa
text: "I am Murray."

speaker: Papa
text: "Me Papa!" The man grins, revealing several missing teeth. He nonchalantly scratches his behind.

speaker: Papa
text: "Hey, what job? I am having a great time here. Leave me alone!"

speaker: Papa
text: The man looks confused. "Job? Me no job. Me live. Me live here with Mama. No need job. Cave provides all."

speaker: Papa
text: "They make me itch so I do not wear any."

speaker: Papa
text: "Clothes?!" The man laughs heartily and slaps his belly. "No clothes, no clothes," he assures you, still chuckling.

speaker: Papa
text: "Quite a lady, is she not?" He nudges you and winks.

speaker: Papa
text: "Mmm. Mama! Me Papa. She Mama. We make zug-zug. Maybe someday make Boy or Girl!"

speaker: Papa
text: "We love the cave. The bees do not bother us. When they sleep we get our honey. We cook mice on the campfire. They are really not bad. Thou shouldst try them!"

speaker: Papa
text: "Cave good to us. We stay away from bees. They no hurt us. We no hurt them. We take honey when they sleep. We eat the mice in cave. Cook them up on campfire. Very good!"

speaker: Iolo
text: "I may puke."

speaker: Papa
text: "They won't bother thee if thou dost not bother them."

speaker: Papa
text: "They friendly if we no hurt them."

speaker: Papa
text: The man sees Tseramed and frowns. He points at you accusingly. "Hunt bees?"

speaker: Papa
text: "Go away!" The man spits at you and turns away.

speaker: Papa
text: He points at Tseramed. "Him bee hunter! Go away!" The man spits at you and turns away.

speaker: Tseramed
text: "This is an act, I tell thee! These people are not savages! They are Britannians!"

speaker: Iolo
text: "He seems quite savage to me!"

speaker: Papa
text: The man rubs his belly and smiles, licking his lips.

speaker: Papa
text: "Yummmmmmmmmmmmm!"

speaker: Papa
text: The man rubs his belly and makes smacking noises with his mouth.

speaker: Papa
text: "Mmmmmmmmmmmmmmm!"

speaker: Papa
text: "Sure. They know Mama and me. We are their friends."

speaker: Papa
text: The man nods. "They know Mama and me. We are bees' friends. Bees let us have honey when bees sleep. Bees no like giving honey if bees awake."

speaker: Papa
text: "I told thee. We have been here a long time."

speaker: Papa
text: "Mama and me live in cave since babies."

speaker: Iolo
text: "Avatar! They must have been abandoned in here! Why, they must be brother and sister!"

speaker: Papa
text: The man nods. "We babies then."

speaker: Papa
text: The man's eyes widen, realizes you are serious, then rolls his eyes to the floor.

speaker: Papa
text: "Damn! All right. Thou didst catch me. Thou art right. Mama and I are from Yew," the man speaks in a perfect voice booming with intelligence. He then laughs heartily. "We had thee going, though, did we not!"

speaker: Papa
text: "That's right. My real name is Murray. Mama is really Myrtle. I was a fully licensed apothecary in the town until the Britannian Tax Council came after me. They wanted the shirt off my back, so I gave it to them!"

speaker: Papa
text: "Since then, Myrtle and I prefer to live down here with the bees. Life is so... carefree down here. We have chosen to live with nature. Now, if thou dost not mind, I shall isolate myself from thee and bid thee farewell."

speaker: Papa
text: Papa smiles and waves.

speaker: Taylor
text: You see an attractive, studious-looking man.

speaker: Taylor
text: "Yes, <HONORIFIC>," Taylor asks. "May I assist thee?"

speaker: Taylor
text: "My name is Taylor, <HONORIFIC>."

speaker: Taylor
text: "I study the local flora, fauna, and geography here at the monastery."

speaker: Taylor
text: "There are many beautiful plants in this area. I am working on learning about all of them."

speaker: Taylor
text: "Many different species of animals reside in the forest. I have encountered some fascinating ones in my studies."

speaker: Taylor
text: "Our order is called the Brotherhood of the Rose."

speaker: Taylor
text: "Yes, <HONORIFIC>. One other monk, Aimi, lives here in the Abbey. She is a painter and a gardener."

speaker: Taylor
text: He smiles. "Between us, she is a far better gardener."

speaker: Taylor
text: "She raises the most lovely flowers that I have ever seen! Thou must see them to believe of their existence."

speaker: Taylor
text: "I use my knowledge of the local landscape to aid in my studies. The better I know the locale, the farther away I can travel from the Brotherhood Abbey and still be sure I will able to return -- unlike a fellow monk of mine."

speaker: Taylor
text: "He became lost some time ago while surveying the area for birds -- the Golden-Cheeked Warbler, I believe it was. Sadly, he travelled too far, and we have not heard from him since."

speaker: Taylor
text: "I do not wish to suffer the same fate."

speaker: Taylor
text: "That name does not sound familiar, <HONORIFIC>. Perhaps he is not from this area."

speaker: Taylor
text: "Julius? I cannot be certain, but 'tis possible he may be someone who now resides in the... cemetery. I have heard that name mentioned as someone who was brought to the Abbey to be buried, though I know not who brought him	and I do not remember from whom I heard it. I do hope he was not a friend of thine," he says, apologetically.

speaker: Taylor
text: "The wisps?" he laughs. "I doubt they exist. I realize many people seem to believe in them, but I have never seen any."

speaker: Taylor
text: "If thou must know, popular legend maintains that they inhabit the forest area, near the Emps. Supposedly, the Emps are able to speak with them." He shrugs. "Thou mayest look for them if that is thy wish, but I would not waste precious time, myself."

speaker: Taylor
text: "There are so many exciting things to investigate... tree flowers, for example, <HONORIFIC>."

speaker: Taylor
text: "Ah, the Emps. I have not been able to glean much information about them."

speaker: Taylor
text: "They live on the eastern edge of the deep forest, not too terribly far from here."

speaker: Taylor
text: "They resemble apes, but only slightly. They are exceedingly shy, and will rarely feel comfortable enough to approach a human."

speaker: Taylor
text: "The only way I was able to view an Emp closely occurred when I happened to have honey in my pack which I had just picked up from Bee Cave. The creature appeared, stared at me for a few minutes, and then asked -- asked, I say -- for mine honey. I believe they are empathic, hence their name."

speaker: Taylor
text: "Quite an interesting species, dost thou not agree?"

speaker: Taylor
text: "The honey from the caves is quite tasty, but rarely can one get it without a fight. The Bee Caves can be a rather dangerous place."

speaker: Taylor
text: "Bee Cave is located to the southwest of the Abbey. But if thou art planning a trip there, beware the giant bees that live in the caves. Their venom is very poisonous."

speaker: Taylor
text: "If thou wishest, I can give thee a smoke bomb that will repel the bees for a short time. Dost thou want it?"

speaker: Taylor
text: "Here it is."

speaker: Taylor
text: "Perhaps thou shouldst lighten thy load before taking the bomb."

speaker: Taylor
text: "Very well. But be careful if thou dost happen by the caves!"

speaker: Taylor
text: "May thy knowledge increase with thine encounters with nature, <HONORIFIC>."

speaker: Malloy
text: You see before you a short, roly-poly man with a pompous smirk on his face. He is holding a lantern in one hand and a dirty spoon in the other.

speaker: Malloy
text: "Hello, good friend," says Malloy. "A pleasure to see thee again."

speaker: Malloy
text: "My name is Malloy. Pleased to make thine acquaintance." Malloy bows politely.

speaker: Malloy
text: Malloy's face carries an exasperated smirk. "My partner over there is Owings," he says, pointing to Owings, the skinny man digging away next to him. "Where are thy manners?! Say hello to our visitor!"

speaker: Malloy
text: "Thou dost already know my partner over there," he says, pointing to Owings.

speaker: Owings
text: "Hello there!" says Owings, giving you a big smile. The front of his mining helmet falls down over his eyes. Blinded, he gropes the air around him.

speaker: Malloy
text: Malloy shakes his head sadly.

speaker: Malloy
text: Malloy regains his composure. "Hello there, I am Malloy. I do apologize for my partner's childish antics."

speaker: Malloy
text: "Normally my job is to dig, but as my partner Owings seems to be missing I suppose my job is to look for him. I hope nothing has happened to the little fellow."

speaker: Malloy
text: "Owings and myself are working as mining engineers, a position we were fortunate enough to have acquired quite recently. We are working on a special project for the Britannian Mining Company."

speaker: Owings
text: Owings gives a big nod, throwing his head back and snapping it straight down. "That is absolutely right, Malloy."

speaker: Owings
text: "That is absolutely right, Malloy," says Owings. He gives a big nod which causes his helmet to fall down over his eyes.

speaker: Malloy
text: "My partner and I are not exactly mining engineers, although we did travel to Minoc to become miners. We came here with a map..."

speaker: Owings
text: "It was the map that the funny man dressed like the Avatar sold us!"

speaker: Malloy
text: "That is correct. But when we got here we discovered that the Britannian Mining Company owned the rights to this area of land already!"

speaker: Owings
text: "That funny man dressed like the Avatar lied to us." Owings scratches his head thoughtfully. "The Britannian Mining Company wanted to throw us in the prisons of Yew for claim jumping!"

speaker: Malloy
text: "I was able to convince them that we would be more valuable to the Britannian Mining Company if we could come to work for them." Malloy beams proudly.

speaker: Malloy
text: "We paid nearly a hundred gold pieces for that map. It was supposed to lead to a spot of valuable minerals found over a hundred years ago. It was a terrific investment. The map was an antique, but it looked like it could not have been more than a few years old! Thou dost not see preservation like that every day!"

speaker: Malloy
text: "Someone told us his name. Let me see if I can remember it... Sullivan, I think it was. Funny name for an Avatar, but there thou art!"

speaker: Malloy
text: "Owings and myself are now involved in a very important special project, but it is a secret. Can we trust thee?"

speaker: Malloy
text: "In that case I thank thee for thine honesty. I do not really mind if a person is untrustworthy. But someone who is untrustworthy and dishonest about it, that is something that I cannot abide."

speaker: Owings
text: You see Owings nod his head most enthusiastically. A second later he has a very confused expression on his face.

speaker: Malloy
text: "The Britannian Mining Company has asked us to dig a tunnel to New Magincia! It will revolutionize the mining industry."

speaker: Owings
text: "They do not want anybody to find out about it. They said that bringing more mining equipment over here would just make people suspicious, so they told us to start by using these spoons!" Owings proudly holds up his spoon to show it to you. He smiles.

speaker: Malloy
text: "Yes, it was such a special project they told us we were the only ones they could think of who would even attempt to do such a thing!" Malloy beams proudly. "Well come on, Owings, we had best get back to work. We have a schedule to meet."

speaker: Malloy
text: Malloy looks at you and puts a finger to his lips. "Shhhhhhhh!!! I asked thee not to speak of this to anyone!"

speaker: Malloy
text: "Owings, have a look at that schedule and find out how we are doing."

speaker: Owings
text: Owings bends over and goes to pick up a very large scroll. As he touches the tip of it he sends it rolling away down the mineshaft. As it rolls away it is unravelling leaving a lengthy trail of paper behind it. Owings chases after it but succeeds in doing little else but tangling up his legs in the long roll of the paper. When at last he has the other end, it is an unreadable mess.

speaker: Malloy
text: "Give me that!" says Malloy as he snatches a piece of the scroll away. He examines it for a moment. "According to this we shall be finished in... one hundred and seventy three years! Owings, we have got to start working faster!" The two of them go back to digging with their spoons. As they dig Malloy turns to Owings and says, "This is another fine mess thou hast gotten me into!"

speaker: Malloy
text: Malloy kicks out with his foot, trying to dislodge the helmet which is stuck there. He looks at Owings and pouts, "Why dost thou not do something to help me?!"

speaker: Owings
text: Owings grabs the helmet on Malloy's foot and attempts to dislodge it. After several fierce tugs it comes off with a loud popping noise. Owings pulls the helmet right into his own face and this makes a loud knocking noise.

speaker: Malloy
text: Malloy goes hurling backwards, crying out in panic. He smacks the back of his head on the rock wall behind him. He takes off his crumpled helmet and points to it. "A good thing I was wearing this or I might have been hurt!" With that a loose rock tumbles down from the ceiling landing squarely on his head. Malloy says "Ooooooh!" Owings breaks into a giggling fit. Malloy flashes you an incredulous pouting grimace.

speaker: Malloy
text: Both Malloy and Owings stop what they are doing and give you a friendly goodbye wave.

speaker: Malloy
text: "Good day to thee, <HONORIFIC>."

speaker: Cairbre
text: The warrior carries himself with confidence.

speaker: Cairbre
text: "Hail, <HONORIFIC>," says Cairbre.

speaker: Cairbre
text: "Thou mayest call me Cairbre, <HONORIFIC>."

speaker: Cairbre
text: "I am a sell-sword. But at the moment, I am trying to help my friend regain his senses."

speaker: Cairbre
text: "I was not about to let Cosmo venture down here by himself. So, I offered to accompany him, as did Kallibrus."

speaker: Cairbre
text: He points to the gargoyle.

speaker: Cairbre
text: "He is a comrade in arms of mine, and also a friend of Cosmo's. I have yet to meet a more trustworthy companion, for he more than disproves all the rumors about gargoyles."

speaker: Cairbre
text: "'Tis a long story. Cosmo is looking for the unicorn that supposedly inhabits this cavern." He looks you in the eye and shrugs.

speaker: Cairbre
text: "He is a fool."

speaker: Cosmo
text: "I heard that, Cairbre!"

speaker: Cairbre
text: "The unicorn is traditionally a way to prove the purity of a young maiden. However, less commonly known is that it will also reveal a young man's, uh, lack of, um, wild oats."

speaker: Cairbre
text: "Ophelia does not love him! She simply sent him on this quest to be rid of him. I doubt she expects him to find the unicorn, let alone return to her."

speaker: Cairbre
text: "He met her in Jhelom. She was serving in the Bunk and Stool. Apparently it was `love at first sight,' as he calls it."

speaker: Cairbre
text: "The nature of her request is quite ironic, for I would expect that the unicorn would have shunned her quite some time ago. He is not to her tastes, I would imagine, and, were he to truly know her, she would not be to his. But, alas, love is blind, as they say."

speaker: Cairbre
text: "I do not know who `they' are, but that is what they say, is it not?"

speaker: Cairbre
text: "'Til next time, <HONORIFIC>."

speaker: Kreg
text: The friendly-looking monk signals you over to him.

speaker: Kreg
text: "Hello, <HONORIFIC>."

speaker: Kreg
text: He smiles. "My name is Kreg, <HONORIFIC>."

speaker: Kreg
text: "I am a monk here at the Abbey. I am working on an alchemical mixture."

speaker: Kreg
text: "Ah! Found me out, didst thou? 'Tis too bad... for thee!"

speaker: Kreg
text: "Sadly, I am so involved with my studies that I have no time to visit the surrounding area or learn any new faces."

speaker: Kreg
text: "Well, <HONORIFIC>, we here at the Abbey will soon be taking a vow of silence. However, it will take some time for all of us to become accustomed to the sound of silence. Therefore, I am creating a potion that enables the imbiber to become temporarily silent. The concept is very similar to a potion of invisibility."

speaker: Kreg
text: "Well," he looks embarrassed, "after reading a book on how we compare to our predecessors, we learned that most people expect us to take a vow of silence."

speaker: Kreg
text: "So," he shrugs, "we have chosen to do so, once I can make that potion. I realize that it sounds foolish, but I truly believe it will help us produce more wine."

speaker: Kreg
text: "Surely thou knowest of what I speak? Meditation, silence, aesthetics, ascetics, and so forth."

speaker: Kreg
text: "The monks' wine is renowned throughout all of Britannia, or so I thought." A puzzled look fills his face.

speaker: Kreg
text: "Ah, well, that is no matter. Regardless, I sincerely recommend to thee to try some of our exquisite drink."

speaker: Kreg
text: "As a matter of fact, my research has reached an impasse, for I cannot determine the nature of some critical reagents. What I need is a potion of invisibility to analyze. Then I could progress from there." He looks at you, hopefully. "Wouldst thou be willing to obtain a potion for my studies? It is likely that thou couldst find one easily at the mage, Nicodemus'."

speaker: Kreg
text: He sighs, obviously relieved. "Thank thee, <HONORIFIC>."

speaker: Kreg
text: "Art thou sure? I will give thee information in return."

speaker: Kreg
text: "I will tell thee about Lord British, The Fellowship, or Buccaneer's Den if thou bringest me the potion of invisibility."

speaker: Kreg
text: He takes the potion from you and quickly drinks it. "Thank thee, <HONORIFIC>, for helping in mine escape!" As he fades from view, his laughter fills your ears.

speaker: Kreg
text: "Thou dost not have a potion to give," he says sadly. "My research will again have to wait."

speaker: Kreg
text: He nods farewell to you.

speaker: Alagner
text: You see a large man with an almost cunning, erudite aura about him.

speaker: Alagner
text: "Hello, again," Alagner says.

speaker: Alagner
text: The sage smiles and nods his head. "My name is Alagner. And who art thou?"

speaker: Alagner
text: "I see. Nice to meet thee. Go away. I am busy."

speaker: Alagner
text: Alagner's eyes widen.

speaker: Alagner
text: "By the skies above! I do recognize thee! This is quite an honor! What may I do for thee?"

speaker: Alagner
text: "My profession -- rather, my destiny -- is to learn and know all things. I came to New Magincia to build my workshop and do so."

speaker: Alagner
text: The sage sighs. "I left the Britannian mainland to come to the relative peace and quiet of New Magincia. I am content here because it is isolated and free from... the filth and corruption going on in Britannia. Not many see it."

speaker: Alagner
text: "This is my workshop. I peruse my books and papers here. Occasionally, I invent things, such as this crystal ball."

speaker: Alagner
text: "It is a device for recording. If I forget a procedure or a step in an experiment, I may look into the crystal ball and see yesterday's events. Please, feel free to use it. Thou wilt see what I was doing yesterday."

speaker: Alagner
text: "They are unusually aloof creatures of another dimension. Thou wilt think they are thy friends, but they could very well be spying on -thee- for someone else! They have no loyalties to good or evil -- all they care about is the acquisition of information -- how they acquire it is sometimes honorable, sometimes not."

speaker: Alagner
text: "The Britannian people are becoming careless and lazy. They do not seek true knowledge. They do not respect their land. They do not respect each other. The resources of our land are being wasted. Miners are experimenting with dangerous reagents. There is an evil in the land, and I am not so sure that it is in the people themselves."

speaker: Alagner
text: "True knowledge is the only way to complete fulfillment."

speaker: Alagner
text: "Thou art a member of The Fellowship, I see. Thou must not know everything about them. If thou didst, thou wouldst not be a member!"

speaker: Alagner
text: "Thou hast heard of The Fellowship by now, I am sure."

speaker: Alagner
text: "They are cunning and two-faced. I am working on obtaining proof of this."

speaker: Alagner
text: "I am documenting this information in my notebook."

speaker: Alagner
text: "It is all contained within the notebook."

speaker: Alagner
text: "Thou didst join The Fellowship to study their ways? Thou dost suspect them as well? Perhaps thou hast more substance to thee than I thought. We are working towards the same goal."

speaker: Alagner
text: "Thou dost suspect The Fellowship of foul deeds? Well then! Thou art perceptive indeed! Perhaps we are working toward the same goal!"

speaker: Alagner
text: "It is hidden in a safe place, along with mine other treasured sources of knowledge."

speaker: Alagner
text: Alagner listens as you tell him you would like to borrow the notebook.

speaker: Alagner
text: "Since thou art on an honorable quest, I suppose I might allow thee to borrow it if thou dost give me thy word that thou wilt return it, and if thou dost offer proof of thine eagerness to learn the true knowledge of the world."

speaker: Alagner
text: "Very well. Dost thou know the answers to the questions of Life and Death?"

speaker: Alagner
text: "I do not believe thou dost."

speaker: Alagner
text: "No, of course thou dost not."

speaker: Alagner
text: "Only those souls who have passed on from this life know these things. Seek out the spirit of The Tortured One. Ask him what the answers are to the questions of life and death. When thou dost return with the correct answer, I will believe that thou art sincere in thy quest for knowledge. Only then will I allow thee to borrow the notebook."

speaker: Alagner
text: "Alas, he is a poor soul who is doomed to haunt his abode throughout eternity."

speaker: Alagner
text: "Seek him out in Skara Brae. But be careful. It is a dangerous place. I should also advise thee that thou must use Seance Spells to speak with anyone on that island. They are all undead."

speaker: Alagner
text: "Thou hast spoken to the Tortured One and learned the answers to the questions of Life and Death?"

speaker: Alagner
text: "Then what are the answers?"

speaker: Alagner
text: "Do not return until thou hast done so."

speaker: Alagner
text: "Farewell. May thy journeys be profitable."

speaker: Caine
text: The non-corporeal man stares past you, seemingly past the confines of the building, and, perhaps, of the world. Then, he suddenly shudders, as if he is filled with pain.

speaker: Caine
text: The ghostly man displays a face filled with pain.

speaker: Caine
text: "Greetings, <HONORIFIC>." Caine breathes deeply, apparently forcing back his torment.

speaker: Caine
text: "I," he gasps, "am called Caine. But I have also been given an alias by my... fellow townspeople. To them, I am known as `the Tortured One.'" He moves his hands in a sweeping gesture, but seems to indicate nothing. "And thou canst see why."

speaker: Caine
text: "The flames, fool! The flames!" Again he gasps.

speaker: Caine
text: He smirks at your comment.

speaker: Caine
text: "Thou wishest to know my job? I will tell thee my job!" he shouts.

speaker: Caine
text: "To burn here in eternal flames for my crime against the fair city of Skara Brae! That," he pauses for emphasis, "is my job!"

speaker: Caine
text: After a moment, he calms down.

speaker: Caine
text: "I apologize, <HONORIFIC>. I realize thy question was not intended to further torment me," he sighs, and turns his face away from you. "At one time, I was the alchemist here."

speaker: Caine
text: He looks down at the ground, a remorseful expression on his face.

speaker: Caine
text: "The flames are my punishment. Years ago, when the evil Liche first exerted his reign of death over Skara Brae, the healer, Mordra, conceived of a plan to remove the creature most foul."

speaker: Caine
text: "She designed a concoction that would destroy the magical bonds that form the Liche. The formula was presented to our mayor, who passed it on to me."

speaker: Caine
text: "But," he scowls, "something went wrong when I was preparing the potion. The proportions were mixed improperly, or... I don't know!" he shouts, fists clenched.

speaker: Caine
text: "All I remember is the shop exploding, and the fire! The fire! All those people dead... because of me... because of my mistake...."

speaker: Caine
text: "'Twas a thriving town -- before I destroyed it!" His jaw tightens and his face clenches. "Why? Why, why, why!" He again gasps in agony, but quickly regains control.

speaker: Caine
text: "There were so many innocent people," he says, staring directly at you. "I cannot believe I am responsible for all their deaths."

speaker: Caine
text: "I am sorry, <HONORIFIC>, but I must spend my eternity here in constant memory of those whom I have destroyed."

speaker: Caine
text: "Forsythe is the mayor. Perhaps thou canst find him in the Town Hall, shouldst thou wish to speak with him."

speaker: Caine
text: "Thou trusts me to tell thee the formula! After what I have done to this town? Art thou mad? I hope at least, that thou hast checked with Mordra for the correct proportions, yes?"

speaker: Caine
text: He shakes his head in disbelief.

speaker: Caine
text: "Thou art truly insane. But," he shrugs, "thou hast nothing to lose but thine own life...."

speaker: Caine
text: "That is better. Thou hadst me wondering." His tone is a mixture of both relief and disappointment.

speaker: Caine
text: "First thou wilt need the three potions. Then, thou must place each one just below a connecting tube -- the order matters not. Take an empty vial -- I should have one here in my lab -- and set it below the nozzle. Then, turn on the burner. After but a few minutes, the mixture will form, and the filled vial will be ready for thee."

speaker: Caine
text: "Thou wishest to know whom I killed? I can only assume that all perished in the blaze: Markham and his Barmaid, Paulette; Trent and Forsythe; and, of course, Mordra the healer."

speaker: Caine
text: "He is -- was -- the blacksmith. Mine one consolation lay with him, for I thought there would be at least one advantage to his death. Sadly," he inhales quickly, "even that did not occur."

speaker: Caine
text: "He was once a master of all things metal. Now all he does, so I am told, is work endlessly on that blasted cage!"

speaker: Caine
text: "I know nothing about it other than that it was necessary to put the liche in it before my... potion could work on him."

speaker: Caine
text: "The liche took from Trent the one most valuable thing in the blacksmith's life -- his wife, Rowena. I had hoped his death would at least extinguish his pain." He smiles sardonically.

speaker: Caine
text: "Well, it did end his pain, in a manner of speaking."

speaker: Caine
text: "The pain is gone, but only to be replaced by his obsessive anger. The poor fool does not even realize he is dead! He thrives on his anger."

speaker: Caine
text: "She was all he lived for. When the liche tried to take her from him, he was consumed by the emptiness of her death. But, after his own demise," he stares directly at you, "his bitter feelings soured even further."

speaker: Caine
text: "I suspect there is no reasoning with him now."

speaker: Caine
text: "I doubt he would believe even his own death, let alone care."

speaker: Caine
text: The ghost looks at you with a hint of amusement. "Thou art looking for the answers to the questions of life and death?"

speaker: Caine
text: The Tortured One looks hard at you. After a pause, he speaks. "I will tell thee what I know if thou dost agree to help me. Free me. Free all of us. Free us from the evil Liche."

speaker: Caine
text: "Then I have no answers for thee."

speaker: Caine
text: "Thou hast freed us from the Liche. Thou art entitled to mine half of the bargain."

speaker: Caine
text: "So thou dost want to know the answers to the questions of life and death?"

speaker: Caine
text: The Tortured One looks hard at you. Then, smiling, he shakes his head. "I have no secrets, my foolish friend. Thou art a fool. There are -no- answers. Only questions."

speaker: Caine
text: He looks as if he might cry out in pain. And then Caine turns away from you. "Go away now. Leave me to mine eternity."

speaker: Caine
text: "Then why hast thou wasted thy time? Go away, fool!"

speaker: Caine
text: "Thou hast not rid us of the evil Liche yet. Fulfill this quest as thou hast agreed and I shall give thee the answers thou dost seek."

speaker: Caine
text: "He is an evil spirit who inhabits poor dead Horance's body. He has a hold on every being in this town -- even me. He sucks the life forces -- the little that remain -- from our souls. Please, thou must free us from his power. Wilt thou try?"

speaker: Caine
text: The Tortured One's eyes brighten somewhat, as he sees the light at the end of a long, dark tunnel. "Then thou hast given me hope. To begin, speak with Mistress Mordra. She can tell thee how to accomplish this feat."

speaker: Caine
text: "Then thou shalt never know the answers to the questions of life and death. An eye for an eye, my friend."

speaker: Caine
text: "Goodbye, <HONORIFIC>." He suppresses a pained scream as you depart.

speaker: Brion
text: You see a scholarly-looking man with a friendly expression.

speaker: Brion
text: "Salutations, <HONORIFIC>." Brion smiles.

speaker: Brion
text: "Why, thou mayest call me Brion."

speaker: Brion
text: "I am the head of the observatory here in Moonglow," he says proudly. "This is where the telescope is kept."

speaker: Brion
text: "Why, I love living here in Moonglow. I very much like the people here."

speaker: Brion
text: "Hast thou spoken with my twin, Nelson? He heads the Lycaeum. Or Elad? And surely thou knowest about the mage, Penumbra."

speaker: Brion
text: "Oh, I see," he shrugs. "I never really thought about my brother's assistant in such a manner. That is too bad, for my time permits nothing but mine observations. Ah, well, what else can I help thee with?"

speaker: Brion
text: "I do not see him as often as I would like, for we are so heavily involved with our work. He will be easy to recognize shouldst thou see him, for people tell us we look identical. I do not see it, of course, for, not only was he born with the brains, but also the handsome face."

speaker: Brion
text: "Poor Elad. He sometimes joins me at night to view the heavens. He has been trying to leave Moonglow for many years. He likes the island, but is filled with wanderlust." He smiles.

speaker: Brion
text: "Thou hast not heard? Why, two hundred years ago she put herself to sleep."

speaker: Brion
text: "I have it upstairs, of course. Thou art welcome to use it as often as thou wishest. In fact, I also have an orrery, shouldst thou desire to see that as well."

speaker: Brion
text: He looks at you strangely, shrugs, and says, "Why, Caddellite is a mineral that is not native to Britannia. In fact, it only comes from meteorites."

speaker: Brion
text: "And the last known meteor to strike the planet landed somewhere in the North East sea. Why dost thou want to know?"

speaker: Brion
text: "Thou dost want a helmet made of Caddellite?" He thinks carefully. "Perhaps Zorn in Minoc would have the skills to build a helmet such as thou desirest. If thou findest the Caddellite, take it to him."

speaker: Brion
text: "I have heard rumors of an island that once existed in the North East sea. Perhaps my brother at the Lycaeum could help with that."

speaker: Brion
text: The orrery? Why, 'tis a model of all the planets in our solar system, including the two moons of Britannia. The orrery moves to match the actual, current orbits of our real system.

speaker: Brion
text: "I am very excited, for shortly a very rare event will occur!"

speaker: Brion
text: "Thou art referring to what we in the business call the Astronomical Alignment. The planets and the moons will all line up perfectly, something that happens only once every 800 years!"

speaker: Brion
text: "Good day, <HONORIFIC>. Thou mayest use mine observatory as often as thou wishest."

speaker: Brion
text: "Before thou dost depart, let me show thee a few of my trinkets. Here is my..."

speaker: Brion
text: "This represents one of the moons that orbit Britannia." He hands the model to you. Taking it, you quickly realize that it is made up entirely of green cheese.

speaker: Brion
text: "I carved it myself," he says as you return it to him.

speaker: Brion
text: "Now where did that go?" he says, scratching his head. "Well, it is around here somewhere. I can show thee at a later time." He seems more distraught than he is willing to convey.

speaker: Brion
text: He hands you a solid gold sextant. "This has been passed on to each and every individual who has ever held a position at the observatory here in Moonglow. 'Tis more than 200 years old." He beams as you return it to him.

speaker: Brion
text: "Damn! 'Tis gone! That has been here for more than 200 years." He does not seem pleased.

speaker: Brion
text: He shows you a kite. "I made this myself by reading one of the books in my brother's library."

speaker: Brion
text: "Where did that disappear to?" He scratches his chin, obviously puzzled. "I do hope it has not disappeared. I constructed it from a book in my brother's library."

speaker: Brion
text: "This," he says, presenting a collection of crystals that seem to be attached in some indeterminable fashion, "is an orrery viewer. It permits one to see mine orrery here from anywhere in Britannia."

speaker: Brion
text: He seems thoughtful.

speaker: Brion
text: "I know thou cannot stay around here to see the alignment."

speaker: Brion
text: "Wouldst thou like to have this to view mine orrery and better predict the planet's position?"

speaker: Brion
text: He smiles proudly. "I thought thou wouldst. However, there is one problem. I still need one more crystal to completely finish the viewer. If thou wouldst visit the tavern, thou mightest find one of the merchants or travellers there who sometimes provide me with crystals. If thou canst find another crystal, I will be able to give thee the completed viewer."

speaker: Brion
text: "Very well, <HONORIFIC>. I hope thou dost not regret this later."

speaker: Brion
text: "Thou hast the crystal? Excellent." He takes the crystal that you got from the adventurer and begins attaching it to his orrery viewer. Shortly he is finished.

speaker: Brion
text: "I am sorry, <HONORIFIC>, but I must have the crystal to complete the viewer."

speaker: Brion
text: "Use it well, <HONORIFIC>." He gives the contraption to you.

speaker: Brion
text: He shakes his head. "Thou dost not have enough room for it. Perhaps when thou dost return at a later time."

speaker: Nelson
text: You see a scholarly-looking man with a friendly expression.

speaker: Nelson
text: "Salutations, <PLAYER_NAME>."

speaker: Nelson
text: "Thou mayest call me Nelson."

speaker: Nelson
text: "I am the Lycaeum head here in Moonglow, but," he leans close to you, "mine assistant, Zelda, does most of the work."

speaker: Nelson
text: "She is an excellent assistant. The Lycaeum has never performed better. However, she is a little too stern, I believe, and," he leans in again, "I think she is quite beautiful."

speaker: Nelson
text: "I have heard the rumors of an island, but I know nothing else about it, I am afraid. Thou mightest wish to speak with Jillian -- she should know a little about the area."

speaker: Nelson
text: "She has put an extraordinary amount of time and effort into ensuring the activities in this edifice happen smoothly. And," he adds, "she takes it personally when they do not!"

speaker: Nelson
text: "Dost thou not agree? I am flushed whenever her fair presence passes by. But!" he holds up his index finger, "I fear she does not share a mutual attraction. And she is far too serious for me to feel comfortable with a proposal."

speaker: Nelson
text: "I love the island and the people. Mostly the people."

speaker: Nelson
text: "Hast thou met my twin brother? He heads the Observatory here. And somewhere in the Lycaeum thou canst find Mariah. Sadly, she is not well up here." He touches his head.

speaker: Nelson
text: "Jillian, the sage, also studies here in the Lycaeum. A good person to see about other residents of Moonglow would be the bartender at the Friendly Knave. Phearcy knows almost all of us here on the island."

speaker: Nelson
text: "Oh, and thou must not forget the legend of Penumbra. 'Twas two hundred years ago she cast herself into a deep slumber. Now that I think about it, <PLAYER_NAME>, thou art the one she predicted would awaken her."

speaker: Nelson
text: "Better hasten, <HONORIFIC>," he chuckles.

speaker: Nelson
text: "His name is Brion. People often mistake us for each other, but I think we are nothing alike -- he got all the looks -and- the brains!"

speaker: Nelson
text: "She was once an adept mage, but ever since the wizards began losing their, er, faculties, she followed suit."

speaker: Nelson
text: "She rarely has time for visitors, but I know she takes on students every now and then."

speaker: Nelson
text: "That one keeps up on his politics, or rather, his gossip," he says, grinning. "If thou dost want to learn about a resident of Moonglow, visit him."

speaker: Nelson
text: "Interestingly enough, no one has ever discovered how to enter her house. I believe those mysterious signs on the door require one to have specific items to place next to the plaques."

speaker: Nelson
text: He smiles broadly. "Truly that was her response? I am pleased to no end! I thank thee, <PLAYER_NAME>, for bringing this joyful message."

speaker: Nelson
text: "Oh. Oh well," he shrugs in an attempt at indifference. "She was not truly important anyway."

speaker: Nelson
text: "Good day, <HONORIFIC>. Thou of course dost have free reign of the Lycaeum."

speaker: Nelson
text: "Of course thou mayest have free reign of the building. But first," he grins, "let me show thee my..."

speaker: Nelson
text: "This solid brass bookstand has matching, overhanging candleholder for late-night exploration in literature. I invented it myself."

speaker: Nelson
text: "'Twas just here..." he scratches his chin. "Oh well, never mind."

speaker: Nelson
text: "This," he says, holding a solid-gold sheet shaped like a maple leaf, "I purchased at an auction for only half of its value."

speaker: Nelson
text: He appears upset. "I knew someday that would be stolen," he says angrily.

speaker: Nelson
text: "I should have known better than to show it to every person who comes to visit."

speaker: Nelson
text: He shows you a serpent-shaped, oaken quill holder and its matching scroll opener. "This I picked up	while travelling through -- thou canst guess it -- Serpent's Hold."

speaker: Nelson
text: He shows you a serpent-shaped, oaken quill holder.	"This I picked up while travelling through -- thou	canst guess it -- Serpent's Hold. But," he appears puzzled, "I could have sworn the matching letter opener was here as well. How odd."

speaker: Nelson
text: "The quill holder is gone?" he exclaims. "And what about the..." he seems to be searching for something.

speaker: Nelson
text: "The matching scroll opener is also missing!"

speaker: Nelson
text: He gingerly pulls out a leatherbound tome. From his robe, he removes a handkerchief and meticulously wipes away the dust.

speaker: Nelson
text: "This was given to me by Lord British himself. See, 'tis the first edition."

speaker: Nelson
text: The book he carefully places in your palms is very old, and the gold leaf plating of the title has been almost entirely rubbed off. Turning the book right side up, you can read the title: "Stranger in a Strange Land."

speaker: Nelson
text: "'Tis not here... Oh well, Zelda must have put it back on the shelf." He sighs.

speaker: Rankin
text: Rankin is unable to speak with you now, for he is conducting the Fellowship meeting.

speaker: Rankin
text: The man is too busy to speak with you now, for he is conducting the Fellowship meeting.

speaker: Rankin
text: The man greets you with a pleasant smile.

speaker: Rankin
text: Rankin smiles. "Please tell me how I may be of assistance, <PLAYER_NAME>."

speaker: Rankin
text: "Thou mayest call me Rankin, <PLAYER_NAME>."

speaker: Rankin
text: "I am the new branch leader of The Fellowship here in Moonglow."

speaker: Rankin
text: "What dost thou want to know about her, <PLAYER_NAME>?"

speaker: Rankin
text: "She has left for Britain on important business," he smiles. "I do not expect her return any time soon."

speaker: Rankin
text: "Oh? Thou hast not seen her lately, either? I wonder what she has been up to." He gives a slight smile.

speaker: Rankin
text: The Cube vibrates. "Actually, I know exactly where she is."

speaker: Rankin
text: "She is right there," he says, pointing to Balayna.

speaker: Rankin
text: "I have not seen her in some time, <PLAYER_NAME>. Perhaps thou mayest find her in her house."

speaker: Rankin
text: "She has conveniently stopped breathing!" Rankin laughs.

speaker: Rankin
text: "Yes, I told thee the merchant brought it from Britain. Didst thou give it to her?"

speaker: Rankin
text: "What then," he asks, "is the problem?"

speaker: Rankin
text: "Ah, well. Then I hope thou wilt have the chance later." He stares at you oddly for a moment, and then smiles again.

speaker: Rankin
text: "Excellent, then."

speaker: Rankin
text: "What!" he appears stunned. "Died? How is that possible?"

speaker: Rankin
text: "Well this is truly a tragedy! Please, <PLAYER_NAME>, I would prefer to be alone now. If thou wouldst be so kind..."

speaker: Rankin
text: "The liqueur? Why, art thou implying that the merchant had cause to kill her? That is absurd!" He appears thoughtful.

speaker: Rankin
text: "Or perhaps not. Mayhaps we will look into that, what sayest thou?"

speaker: Rankin
text: "Excellent. Let me know if thou dost find any information. Meanwhile, I will make arrangements for her funeral." He shakes his head sadly.

speaker: Rankin
text: "Very well, then I must conduct the search on mine own, -after- I have arranged for the funeral."

speaker: Rankin
text: "Dost thou have any news of the travelling merchant who killed Balayna?"

speaker: Rankin
text: "Very good, <PLAYER_NAME>. What is thy news?"

speaker: Rankin
text: "Ah, well. Keep searching. I am positive thou wilt come across some information soon!"

speaker: Rankin
text: "Very well, <PLAYER_NAME>, I can wait until thou hast learned more."

speaker: Rankin
text: ""Really!" he seems genuinely surprised. "How, ah, wonderful." Then I guess the murder has been avenged."

speaker: Rankin
text: ""He grins, obviously embarrassed. "I am sorry. Though the branch opened here several years ago, it is the newest branch on Britannia. I still consider myself a new branch head here."

speaker: Rankin
text: "Ah, yes, Moonglow. It is a pleasant town. It is possible to find all sorts of people here."

speaker: Rankin
text: "I am sorry, but I prefer not to gossip."

speaker: Rankin
text: "As is customary, our meetings are at 9 p.m. Please feel free to join us."

speaker: Rankin
text: "Thou shouldst really return thy medallion to the person from whom it came. Only Fellowship members are permitted to wear them."

speaker: Rankin
text: "If thou hast a free moment, I would be quite happy to discuss our philosophy with thee."

speaker: Rankin
text: "Relax, friend, thou wilt hear when the time is right."

speaker: Rankin
text: "There is an inner voice that exists within each and every one of us. This voice is our companion and guide."

speaker: Rankin
text: "The deeper one's involvement with The Fellowship, the more often one is able to hear one's inner voice."

speaker: Rankin
text: "What dear people! They were just here in order to give me my training session. I was just appointed branch leader. This is a new branch, thou knowest. Anyway, Elizabeth and Abraham left to travel all the way to the gargoyle island, Terfin."

speaker: Rankin
text: "I have not seen them since they gave me my training session, many days ago."

speaker: Rankin
text: "Shhh! Talk to me about it later," he whispers, gesturing subtly towards Balayna, "when she is not around."

speaker: Rankin
text: He begins to look amused.

speaker: Rankin
text: "I would not let it worry thee too much, <PLAYER_NAME>. I am afraid Balayna is a bit too ambitious. I would expect she overheard one of my conversion speeches and misunderstood my words. I will have to discuss this with her when I have more time so I may allay her fears." His eyes widen, as if he is remembering something.

speaker: Rankin
text: "I had forgotten, she requested a small vial of liqueur from an itinerant merchant who would be passing through Britain. He brought it here a few days ago and I have not had a chance to give it to her. Wouldst thou be willing to deliver it to her for me, <PLAYER_NAME>?"

speaker: Rankin
text: "Excellent, my friend."

speaker: Rankin
text: "I thank thee." He gives you the vial of liquor.

speaker: Rankin
text: "Ah, well, thou art carrying too much. I will simply have to save it for when I have time to talk with her. Thank thee anyway."

speaker: Rankin
text: "Very well. I will have to save it for when I have time to talk with her. Thank thee anyway."

speaker: Rankin
text: "May the triad guide thy life."

speaker: Rankin
text: "Shouldst thou find an interest in The Fellowship, <PLAYER_NAME>, seek Batlin in Britain. Farewell, <PLAYER_NAME>."

speaker: Danag
text: Danag nods his head at you. "I do not mean to be impolite, but I am concentrating on the games. I wish to win a bundle tonight!"

speaker: Danag
text: He rubs his hand with glee.

speaker: Danag
text: You see a jovial man with a wide smile. It is obvious he is enjoying his life.

speaker: Danag
text: He notices your medallion.

speaker: Danag
text: "Fellow member! How art thee! I hope thy journey to Buccaneer's Den was not too troublesome! Welcome to our island!"

speaker: Danag
text: The Cube vibrates.

speaker: Danag
text: "And I recognize thee as the Avatar! I know that thou art condemned to die!"

speaker: Danag
text: Danag smiles as if he had just said that you had been invited to dine with the king.

speaker: Danag
text: "Hello, there!" Danag says.

speaker: Danag
text: "I am Danag, my friend." The man overdoes a majestic bow.

speaker: Danag
text: "I am interim Fellowship Branch leader here on Buccaneer's Den. Our regular leader, Abraham, is away on Fellowship business at the moment."

speaker: Danag
text: "The Fellowship has been present on Buccaneer's Den for a long time. This is one of the oldest branches in Britannia, second only to the headquarters in Britain. Thou mayest wonder why an island of such ill-repute would attract The Fellowship."

speaker: Danag
text: "The founders of The Fellowship felt that the people who inhabit this island would benefit the most from our organization."

speaker: Danag
text: "Especially since we would help them build an empire of sin and gluttony out of Buccaneer's Den."

speaker: Danag
text: You notice the Cube has been vibrating while Danag was speaking.

speaker: Danag
text: "Amidst all of the sin, the debauchery, the piracy, the gambling, the drunkenness -- The Fellowship has made its stand and recruited members to follow our principles. Buccaneer's Den has changed as a result."

speaker: Danag
text: "Long ago it was merely a hideout for pirates, scavengers, and rogues. Look around."

speaker: Danag
text: "Now it is the center of corruption in all of Britannia. The pirates are all controlled by The Fellowship."

speaker: Danag
text: The Cube continues to vibrate.

speaker: Danag
text: "Now Buccaneer's Den is an island paradise. It has its own commerce. It pays taxes to Lord British. The pirates here are now businessmen. They have made something of their lives."

speaker: Danag
text: "As a result, The Baths and The House of Games are two of the most profitable establishments in the country."

speaker: Danag
text: "It is, of course, a place where one may experience the pleasures of the flesh. All of the profits go to The Fellowship."

speaker: Danag
text: "It is a purely innocent business which caters to the weary who are in need of relaxation. One may receive physical and mental cleansing there."

speaker: Danag
text: "It is truly a jewel in the crown that is Britannia."

speaker: Danag
text: "Why, it is a gambling parlor! The Fellowship certainly takes in a bundle from that place!"

speaker: Danag
text: "It is an outfit which challenges the mind and its ability for assessing strategy in life. Exercising this aspect of one's brain is important for one's self-esteem and well-being."

speaker: Danag
text: "Abraham is one of the members of the inner circle of The Fellowship. He and his colleague Elizabeth travel the country periodically, usually distributing or collecting the organization's funds and doing business at the other branches."

speaker: Danag
text: The Cube vibrates.

speaker: Danag
text: "Uhm... er... he is also a coordinator for executions and he cheats at cards."

speaker: Danag
text: "Elizabeth is an extremely intelligent woman who acts as Director of Special Projects. She usually works with Batlin in Britain, but she spends most of her time travelling from branch to branch."

speaker: Danag
text: As the Cube vibrates, Danag adds, "She is, uhm... also a royal she-bitch and will murder thee at a moment's notice."

speaker: Danag
text: "They might be anything from building a shelter for poor peasants to creating a new branch in a town without the benefit of a Fellowship Hall."

speaker: Danag
text: As the Cube vibrates, Danag proudly adds, "Our current Special Project is building the Black Gate for The Guardian. It is located at the Isle of the Avatar in our secret underground complex!"

speaker: Danag
text: Danag's eyes widen with excitement. "It is the gateway for our coming Lord and Master! He will be coming through in virtually a few hours!"

speaker: Danag
text: "It is inside a dungeon within the Shrine of the Codex. A barrier keeps out unwanted visitors. A special key opens the barrier, and only a few select people have one."

speaker: Danag
text: "I do not own one. The only people that do are Elizabeth and Abraham, Batlin, and Hook himself. Hook probably keeps his key in his abode."

speaker: Danag
text: The Cube vibrates.

speaker: Danag
text: "Man with a Hook? That's his name! 'Hook'! He lives here on the island! In fact, his quarters are in the secret catacombs behind the House of Games! Thou canst reach it by asking Sintag the guard about Hook. Of course, thou dost know that Hook is The Fellowship's chief executioner... along with his assistant, the gargoyle Forskis."

speaker: Danag
text: "A pirate with a hook for a hand? No... I do not believe I know him. There are many pirates on this island. Many of them are missing appendages, too!"

speaker: Danag
text: "They usually travel together. They just arrived from our Meditation Retreat near Serpent's Hold and I believe they are somewhere on the island. Abraham told me I must keep working as interim branch leader until his return."

speaker: Danag
text: The Cube vibrates.

speaker: Danag
text: "Actually, I believe they are on their way to the Isle of the Avatar to take care of our new Special Project."

speaker: Danag
text: "That's right. Hook does all the dirty work for The Fellowship. He was trained by Master De Snel in Jhelom. De Snel trained all the previous executioners as well. In fact, De Snel himself was The Fellowship's first executioner!"

speaker: Danag
text: "I understand the gargoyle's name means 'henchman' in Gargish. He's a tough wingless gargoyle who helps Hook out. I believe he resides in the catacombs with Hook."

speaker: Danag
text: "Farewell!"

speaker: Kallibrus
text: You see a rather reserved-looking gargoyle.

speaker: Kallibrus
text: Kallibrus smiles and greets you with a nod.

speaker: Kallibrus
text: "To be known as Kallibrus."

speaker: Kallibrus
text: "To be not my true name. To have been given this name by Cairbre, who could not pronounce my Gargish name."

speaker: Kallibrus
text: "To work as a warrior for hire most of the time. To be between jobs now. To help friend Cosmo find unicorn."

speaker: Kallibrus
text: "To have been partners for many, many years. To have been bonded for even longer!"

speaker: Cairbre
text: "He, uh, means by bonded, that we are very good friends." He turns to the gargoyle.

speaker: Cairbre
text: "I told thee to be careful how thou dost phrase things. Thou couldst start many false rumors if thou wert not more specific."

speaker: Cairbre
text: The gargoyle nods sheepishly.

speaker: Kallibrus
text: "To have known him for many years, but not as long as Cairbre. To be good friend."

speaker: Kallibrus
text: "To be unsure but to think it has something to do with a woman and, to say how... sex?"

speaker: Kallibrus
text: "To know nothing about this word. To mean something similar to reproduce?"

speaker: Kallibrus
text: "To tell you gargoyles reproduce differently than humans seem to, but to explain too poorly to be useful."

speaker: Kallibrus
text: "To be quite confused." He shrugs.

speaker: Kallibrus
text: "To be related to difference in genders, I know, but to see no such thing in gargoyles. To believe there is a certain human... woman... who sent him here."

speaker: Kallibrus
text: "To have heard Cosmo say, `love,' but Cairbre claims there is no such thing. To comprehend not, but to help friends anyway."

speaker: Cairbre
text: "That is what I like about him, <HONORIFIC>, loyal to the end!" he says, patting the gargoyle on the shoulder.

speaker: Kallibrus
text: "To say `til next time, <HONORIFIC>," he says.

speaker: Cosmo
text: The wide-eyed expression of this youth seems indicative of his naivete.

speaker: Cosmo
text: "Why, hello there, <HONORIFIC>," says Cosmo.

speaker: Cosmo
text: "I am Cosmo, <HONORIFIC>, betrothed of Ophelia."

speaker: Cosmo
text: "I am, uh, searching for something, <HONORIFIC>."

speaker: Cosmo
text: "Aye, <HONORIFIC>, we are to be wed as soon I return to her silky arms."

speaker: Cairbre
text: "Oh, please!" He rolls his eyes.

speaker: Cosmo
text: "Well, <HONORIFIC>, 'tis a bit of a personal matter."

speaker: Cairbre
text: "What he is searching for, <HONORIFIC>, is his virginity!"

speaker: Cosmo
text: "That is not true!" He blushes.

speaker: Cosmo
text: "I am looking for a way to -prove-... my virginity!"

speaker: Cosmo
text: "I would... rather... not discuss it, <HONORIFIC>," he stammers.

speaker: Cosmo
text: "She is the most beautiful woman in all Britannia. I still find it hard to believe she has agreed to marry me, a lowly warrior. I will travel to the ends of the world for her, if that be necessary, to keep her heart!"

speaker: Cosmo
text: He looks down at his feet. "Milady Ophelia is concerned that I might not be... pure. I have waited mine entire life for someone like her. Can she not see that I held myself for marriage?"

speaker: Cosmo
text: "Surely thou dost see the value in that, <HONORIFIC>. No woman would want me if I had not refrained from... well... thou dost understand."

speaker: Cosmo
text: "I must prove to the lovely Ophelia that I am still a virgin. To do this I need to demonstrate that a unicorn will allow me to touch it. My friends and I are here to find such a creature, for recent legend purports that one lives in this dungeon."

speaker: Cosmo
text: "Thou hast seen the unicorn?" He frowns for a moment, but that quickly melts away.

speaker: Cosmo
text: "Nevertheless, I shall endeavor to seek it out. Nothing shall keep me from my beloved Ophelia."

speaker: Cosmo
text: "Good day,<HONORIFIC>. If thou dost see the unicorn, tell it to wait for me."

speaker: Lasher
text: You see a creature the size and shape of a horse. From its head protrudes a single straight horn. It looks at you with eyes that shine with intelligence.

speaker: Lasher
text: "I greet thee once again, Avatar," says Lasher, the unicorn.

speaker: Lasher
text: The creature speaks. "My name is Lasher."

speaker: Lasher
text: Lasher looks at you and blinks. "Come now, Avatar! I do not live by the rules that govern the society of Mankind. There is what I am, which is a unicorn. Then there is my purpose, which is another thing altogether."

speaker: Lasher
text: Lasher stares at you, stupefied. "Tell me, dost thou know what a unicorn is?"

speaker: Lasher
text: Lasher stares blankly at you. His mouth hangs open. "Very well. Then I shall tell thee what a unicorn is."

speaker: Lasher
text: Lasher shakes his head sadly. "No, thou merely thinks thou dost know what a unicorn is, but I shall tell thee the truth."

speaker: Lasher
text: "A unicorn is one of a family of nature spirits that were once called upon to aid a very powerful wizard many, many years ago."

speaker: Lasher
text: "Oh, do not be coy with me, Avatar. Thou dost know very well the purpose of a unicorn. "

speaker: Lasher
text: "We are foolproof virgin detectors!"

speaker: Lasher
text: "I do not remember the wizard's name, for much time has passed since then, but suffice it to say that he was a royal bastard. Anyway, for one reason or another, the chieftain of our clan, who at that time was a horse's ass named Sharp-Hoof, decided that rather than heed this wizard's rightful and properly performed ritual of calling, he was going to take the herd and chase after this bevy of really fine fillies."

speaker: Lasher
text: "Where was I? Oh, yes, Sharp-Hoof! The next morning, after we had had our way with these fillies, this wizard called us again. This time Sharp-Hoof realized that we had best answer, and were we sorry that we did! The wizard was horribly angry! And, well, I will just say that our agreements with such people are very, very binding."

speaker: Lasher
text: "Not only were we bound in service to this wizard for a thousand years, but he also placed a dreadful curse upon us."

speaker: Lasher
text: "As it fell out, we did not actually have to serve the wizard for a thousand years. He reduced the time by a few weeks after placing that curse on us." Lasher snorts sarcastically, "I was heartbroken."

speaker: Lasher
text: "We nature spirits used to be renowned for our randiness, and this wizard had called upon us to assist him in the seduction of some maiden. When we stood him up... Well, let us just say that he was one magician who was having a problem convincing his magic wand to work. Anyway, in a pathetic attempt to bolster his diminished feelings of manhood, he ruined us with an awesomely powerful Curse of Chastity."

speaker: Lasher
text: "It was a terrible curse. First, it drove us to kill all of the female members of our clan. Then it afflicted us with the particular sensitivity for which we have become known."

speaker: Lasher
text: "That is correct. So sensitive are members of my race to all forms of sexual energy that we can only tolerate physical contact with one who has not yet had any experience in that form of procreation - or recreation, if thou dost prefer."

speaker: Lasher
text: "Yes, I find it most unpleasant to actually come into physical contact with anyone who is not a virgin, and I will avoid doing so whenever possible."

speaker: Lasher
text: "Yes, well, I did not wish to get this personal with thee, but if thou does not mind, art thou a virgin?"

speaker: Lasher
text: "I thought as much!" Lasher starts to pace nervously. "If thou wouldst not mind standing back a bit, I would be most appreciative."

speaker: Lasher
text: Lasher slowly shakes his head. "Thou dost not have to brag in order to impress me, or fear any sort of verbal chastisements, honestly. By the way, I have an itch right betwixt my shoulder blades. Wouldst thou mind scratching it for me?" Lasher stretches out toward you. "Thank thee so much."

speaker: Iolo
text: "There's no shame in it, milord," says Iolo, looking very serious.

speaker: Shamino
text: "No, it is perfectly understandable. Thou hast been so busy lately," says Shamino. You sense he is struggling to maintain a straight face.

speaker: Dupre
text: "Why dost thou not go and pet the nice horsey. We would do it, but I think he prefers thee." With that, you hear an explosion of snorts and giggles.

speaker: Lasher
text: "I beg thy pardon, but perhaps thou shouldst go to the Lycaeum and have someone look up the definition of the word 'virginity' for thee. Wouldst thou mind stepping back, please?! Thou dost make me nervous."

speaker: Lasher
text: "Yes, I could tell the answer to my question before thou didst even speak it. Art thou a virgin by choice or by circumstance?"

speaker: Lasher
text: "Surely, Avatar, thou knowest that thou dost magically regain thy virginity each time upon returning to Britannia! Hast thou remained a virgin since then by choice or by circumstance?"

speaker: Lasher
text: "Well, I am sure thou wilt find the right person one day."

speaker: Lasher
text: "That is too bad, I am very sorry. I would love to be able to help thee, but that is no longer my purpose."

speaker: Lasher
text: "Oh, I do not know. It has been so long since I was personally involved in such matters. Art thou seeking love or art thou seeking lust?"

speaker: Lasher
text: "Hmmm, love is usually a very elusive quarry. I suppose that thou canst try thy luck in the city of Cove. It is a city of lovers, or so I have heard."

speaker: Lasher
text: "If quenching thy lust is thine only concern, then thou shouldst find satisfaction at the Baths, in Buccaneer's Den. But be sure to take a full purse."

speaker: Lasher

text: "Thank you, Fellowship members of Trinsic, for attending our meeting this evening."

text: "I am certain you are all sorely aware of the crimes that have been committed in our city. Now is a time to mourn those whom we have lost. speaker: Klog
text: "The Fellowship was created to advance a philosophy, a method of applying an optimistic order of thought to one's life. How dost thou follow this method? By applying the Triad of Inner Strength to thy life. The Triad is composed of three principles that, when applied in unison to thy life, can soothe the fever of a society that teaches thee to accept failure and banishes the destructive illusory thoughts and feelings from thy spirit."

speaker: Klog
text: "The first principle is to Strive For Unity. This means that we should reject divisiveness, put aside our differences and work together for the good of us all."

speaker: Klog
text: "The second principle is to Trust Thy Brother. Trust is essential, for what will you accomplish if you must be divided by constantly watching each other?"

speaker: Klog
text: "The third and final principle is Worthiness Precedes Reward. One must strive to be worthy of the rewards each of us seeks, for if one is not worthy of reward, why should you believe they should receive it?"
